deb_ex.sum: Reflects on the grief of baby loss, calls for better mental health support for bereaved families, and advocates for early specialist intervention after a first miscarriage to prevent further losses.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees early intervention after one miscarriage could prevent 10,000 losses annually, welcomes Northern Ireland's paid leave and baby loss certificate scheme, and calls for similar measures across the UK.

deb_ex.t: will the Prime Minister explicitly state today whether he intends permanently to lock Northern Ireland into foreign laws under an unelected European court
deb_ex.sum: Raises alarm about further EU alignment locking Northern Ireland into foreign laws and calls on the Prime Minister to restore the Acts of Union and the UK internal market.

deb_ex.sum: Urges that specialist care be offered after a first miscarriage rather than only after three, citing evidence it could prevent around 10,000 baby losses a year.

deb_ex.t: Bridlington Town FC will take on Curzon Ashton in the FA trophy first round proper—the first time the club has reached that stage of the competition in 22 years
deb_ex.sum: Congratulates Bridlington Town FC on reaching the FA trophy first round and requests a debate on the importance of sports clubs to local communities.

deb_ex.t: how do the Government plan to reach people who are digitally excluded, and will they be distributing printed resources?
deb_ex.sum: Opposition spokesperson broadly welcomes the campaign but presses the Minister on risk prioritisation, costs, digital exclusion, vulnerable people, devolved coordination, emergency alerts and cyber threats to critical infrastructure.

deb_ex.t: Will the Leader of the House join me in thanking every landlord and landlady across the country for all their hard work
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates the reopening of the Seabirds pub in Bridlington and his local Pub of the Year competition, thanking landlords and landladies across the country.

deb_ex.t: Fiscal responsibility means living within our means. Every household across East Yorkshire and up and down the country knows that we cannot spend more on the family credit card tha
deb_ex.sum: Attacks the Government's fiscal record, arguing borrowing and debt are rising unsustainably, and highlights civil service away-day spending as evidence of broken promises on wasteful expenditure.

deb_ex.sum: Cites 10,000 heat-related deaths in five years and presses the Government on what steps it is taking to future-proof homes, workplaces and communities against extreme heat.

deb_ex.t: Will he ensure rapid access to therapeutic support? We know that it is incredibly difficult, both for adoptees and for women and those who were girls
deb_ex.sum: The APPG chair thanks the Prime Minister, highlights 185,000 affected families including in her constituency, and presses for rapid therapeutic support and consideration of babies brought from other jurisdictions.

deb_ex.t: The reforms are not going to deliver accountability. They are going to weaken it, and as a result we will see more requests for investigations into patient safety.
deb_ex.sum: Concurs with the critique of the Dash reforms and warns that the Health Bill's accountability changes will weaken rather than strengthen the NHS accountability system, risking more safety failures.

deb_ex.t: What steps he is taking to support low-income households with increases in energy prices.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the government is taking to support low-income households with rising energy prices.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Minister for his answer. Preparedness for the sharp increase in domestic energy costs is vital, with 13.5 million homes expected to be paying more than 10% of their hou
deb_ex.sum: Highlights alarming figures on households facing energy poverty this winter and presses the Minister to go further by expanding the warm home discount, removing levies and introducing social tariffs.

deb_ex.t: Will the Minister urgently review her plans and take water back under public ownership, so that we can clean up this dirty business?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the River Ouse as the second worst for sewage pollution and calls on the Minister to go further by taking water companies into public ownership.

deb_ex.t: VAT is the problem, and it is calling for the Government to support a 10% cut in VAT to enable its hospitality businesses to flourish
deb_ex.sum: Highlights SPARK incubator's call for a 10% VAT cut for hospitality businesses and requests a Treasury statement on its impact for community interest companies.

deb_ex.t: will the Minister ensure greater accountability to young people across the country, through local panels that will hold local authorities to account for their actions?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the 30 by 30 plan and, drawing on a youth environment conference in York, calls for local youth panels to hold local authorities accountable on climate and nature action.

deb_ex.t: It is important that funding accompanies the modern service framework, so that we have an invest-to-save model moving forward
deb_ex.sum: Argues that funding must accompany the modern service framework for palliative care and requests a ministerial meeting to explore an invest-to-save model.

deb_ex.t: I congratulate my hon. Friend, but I want to ask about pharma in the light of the US-UK pharma deal. When I met academics yesterday, they expressed a concern that if we were to cha
deb_ex.sum: Labour backbencher asks whether a potential renegotiation of the US-UK pharma deal could require reopening the Switzerland agreement, citing academic concerns about costs and lives.

deb_ex.t: Q11. Before coming to this House, the Prime Minister and I attended the launch of my uncle’s book. It was entitled “Fine Lines and Distinctions”. Clearly, sometimes we have had tho
deb_ex.sum: Asks the outgoing PM to leave a note for his successor Andy Burnham to enact her legislation licensing short-term holiday lets to protect communities and keep housing costs down.

deb_ex.t: I welcome my right hon. Friend to his role. Ten months ago, my constituents were promised a public inquiry into our mental health trust, after 10 years of campaigning for it. Peopl
deb_ex.sum: Raises the delayed public inquiry into a mental health trust after ten years of campaigning and deaths in the interim, and urges the PM to extend devolution of scrutiny as well as power.

deb_ex.t: automatic recall often means that people who miss a probation appointment end up in prison, often for months on end.
deb_ex.sum: Raises concerns that automatic recall for minor breaches such as missing a probation appointment can lead to months in prison, and asks the Secretary of State to review the process to favour support outside custody.

deb_ex.t: will the Minister meet those Members to discuss further issues that were not raised during the debate?
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister to meet Members who could not speak in the debate so further issues can be raised and discussed.

deb_ex.t: Will the Minister meet me and the leader of City of York council? The fair funding formula is not working for our city because it does not use the lower-tier data with regard to th
deb_ex.sum: Asks for a meeting with the Minister and the leader of City of York council to address what she says is a flawed fair funding formula that leaves York as the worst-funded local authority.

deb_ex.t: the Government have not been able to get money out of the door, so can the Minister say more about how she will invest and spend that money?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights cross-party support for BioYorkshire but presses the Minister on why funding has not yet been released and how the government will invest more effectively.

deb_ex.t: so much significant, unaccountable power is being held that we, as Members of Parliament, cannot even deliver for our constituents
deb_ex.sum: MP raises her new clause on NHS accountability, arguing that significant unaccountable power in the NHS prevents MPs from delivering for constituents and asks the Minister to work with her before the Bill goes to the Lords.

deb_ex.t: York hospital was heralded as a cheap build, but we are paying a heavy price today. We know that heat in that hospital will have an impact on clinical outcomes
deb_ex.sum: Raises York hospital's poor build quality and heat-related clinical risks, asks the Secretary of State to consider a new hospital co-located with the university, and flags innovative primary care prevention work in York.

deb_ex.t: I led the independent commission on palliative care, and the data shows a worsening of palliative care; 170,000 people do not have access to the care that they need, and even those
deb_ex.sum: As chair of an independent palliative care commission, she intervenes to stress that palliative care is worsening, with 170,000 lacking access, and urges recognition of specialist skills gaps as well as access failures.

deb_ex.t: I refer Members to my entry in the Register of Members’ Financial Interests. Last week, I visited a prison with the University and College Union to look at the prison education ser
deb_ex.sum: Calls on the Minister to bring privatised prison education contracts in-house and to work across departments to ensure education meaningfully reduces reoffending.

deb_ex.t: the levies raised in York must stay in York—not move into wider North Yorkshire. Will the Minister ensure that the levy is hypothecated to the place where it is raised
deb_ex.sum: Supports the levy but urges the Minister to guarantee that money raised in York stays in York and is ringfenced for local tourism investment.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the Government’s ambition to have free personal care and to keep the triple lock for the duration of this Parliament. However, the Secretary of State will know that I hav
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Government's ambitions but presses for stronger action to end pensioner poverty this Parliament and for an impact assessment of the proposals.

deb_ex.t: poverty is still embedded in our communities. Could the Leader of the House say what the Government are doing to ensure that Departments come together to address poverty?
deb_ex.sum: Marks 125 years since Rowntree's poverty study by referencing a new York University report showing poverty persists, and asks the Government to coordinate across Departments and engage with lived-experience-led work.

deb_ex.t: we could do so much more to lift their confidence in their professional skills
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the statement and the Prime Minister's interest in care co-operatives, and asks the Minister to work with the Co-op party to empower staff and service users.

deb_ex.t: If he will take steps to help ensure Post Office provision in every community.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the minister what steps will be taken to ensure post office provision in every community.

deb_ex.t: I need a solution now. What steps will the Minister take to ensure that we have a temporary solution before we get our sustained outcome?
deb_ex.sum: Raises the closure of York's Crown post office and urges the minister to find an immediate temporary solution for the city centre.

deb_ex.t: What steps she is taking with Cabinet colleagues to regulate funeral services.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the minister what steps are being taken with Cabinet colleagues to regulate funeral services.

deb_ex.t: Will the Government meet me and funeral directors so that we can prevent the York site from operating and set high regulatory standards
deb_ex.sum: Highlights concerns about poor practice at low-cost mass storage facilities, citing a proposed York site, and calls for a ministerial meeting to prevent it operating and set high standards.

deb_ex.t: recorded crime figures in York Central reached an 11-year high this summer. About a third of those were antisocial behaviour offences, and retail crime reached its highest level
deb_ex.sum: Maskell flags that recorded crime in York Central hit an 11-year high, with antisocial behaviour and retail crime surging, and asks what steps the minister is taking to ensure York is properly resourced to tackle offending.

deb_ex.t: we have a challenge in the way the funding works for people with no local connection
deb_ex.sum: MP highlights York's success in tackling rough sleeping but asks how funding will follow people with no local connection to the area where they choose to stay.

deb_ex.t: Will the Minister set out how the application of the duty of candour and the prevention of carve-outs will be applied to the work of the Northern Ireland Legacy Commission
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill and praises the Prime Minister's commitment, but presses the Minister on oversight mechanisms, Northern Ireland legacy proceedings, and the Tees Esk and Wear Valleys mental health inquiry.

deb_ex.t: I congratulate the Prime Minister on taking office and thank him profoundly for his tribute to the Cleveland police officers, PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough, who were so tragi
deb_ex.sum: McDonald congratulates Burnham and welcomes his remarks on public control of utilities, urging him to commit to insourcing public services and ensuring the new public interest test delivers economic transformation.

deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to the officers and praises community solidarity, but highlights that Cleveland has the highest crime rate and largest proportional officer cuts, and calls for urgent and permanent correction of the resource deficit.

deb_ex.t: I rise as the chair of the all-party parliamentary group on spinal cord injury to speak to amendments 103 and 104, new clause 160 and amendment 105 in my name. I thank the Minister
deb_ex.sum: Speaks to amendments on spinal cord injury services, seeking ministerial clarification on how national standards, workforce capacity and specialist centres will be protected as commissioning responsibilities transfer under the Bill.

deb_ex.t: surely the already granted licences for arms used in the occupation should be suspended
deb_ex.sum: McDonald commends the statement but urges immediate suspension of already-granted arms licences used in the now-acknowledged illegal occupation.

deb_ex.t: the duty actually bites when the risk of genocide is known, not at the determination of legal processes? That is when the United Kingdom has a duty to act.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that the UK's duty to act on genocide arises when the risk is known, not only after formal legal determination, while welcoming steps taken so far.

deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Secretary of State but warns that reassuring veterans risks undermining victims' families' confidence, and presses the Government to reconsider new clause 50 on Attorney General consent.

deb_ex.sum: Asks the same question as the previous member about the Bill's impact on access to justice for victims and survivors.

deb_ex.t: the police funding formula is simply not fit for purpose, especially when Cleveland has the highest level of crime and the poorest level of resources
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the £5.2 million for Cleveland police but argues the funding formula is unfit for purpose and that the situation cannot be resolved without a complete reconfiguration of policing.

deb_ex.t: If she will make a statement on her departmental responsibilities.
deb_ex.sum: Opens topical questions by inviting the Secretary of State to make a statement on her departmental responsibilities.

deb_ex.t: Will the Secretary of State meet with recognised trade unions to develop a Department for Transport insourcing strategy, including across rail and other transport services
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the First Secretary's insourcing unit announcement and asks the Secretary of State to meet trade unions to develop a Department for Transport insourcing strategy covering rail and other services.

deb_ex.sum: Criticises Conservative plans as Trussonomics 2.0 and argues the inheritance tax system is unfair because the wealthiest avoid it through complex planning while ordinary families pay the headline 40% rate.

deb_ex.t: I hope we can agree that there is a problem because the wealthiest people can avoid inheritance tax through various loopholes
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges that households and businesses feel heavily burdened and agrees the core problem is that the wealthiest can avoid inheritance tax through loopholes.

deb_ex.t: We have one of the highest headline rates of inheritance tax in the OECD, yet only 4% of estates end up paying it
deb_ex.sum: Argues the UK's complex tax code forces people into expensive advice, and proposes reforming inheritance tax fairly while opposing a mini-Budget-style approach, instead favouring income tax cuts funded through EU growth.

deb_ex.t: Yes. Of all political parties represented in this Chamber, the official Opposition will know that the leader of the Liberal Democrats was an excellent climate Minister in the coali
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Lib Dem leader's economic credentials and contrasts the party's plan to cut income tax for 30 million people against the Conservatives' inheritance tax cut benefiting only 30,000, funded through EU growth.

deb_ex.t: rebuilding our relationship with Europe is the single biggest lever available to increase economic growth, to boost living standards and to cut personal tax
deb_ex.sum: Argues that rebuilding the relationship with Europe is the single biggest lever for growth, living standards and tax cuts, and attacks the Conservatives as anti-growth for refusing to acknowledge this.

deb_ex.t: I can tell the hon. Member that, based on the statistics, the thing that would bring the biggest amount of growth would be having a closer relationship with Europe. He will know th
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates that closer EU ties would generate the greatest growth and links that dividend directly to income tax cuts for workers, attacking the Conservatives' unfunded promises.

deb_ex.t: scrapping taxes in an unfunded way is not the way to reform tax in this country, and it is certainly not the way to run the economy
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges unfairnesses in inheritance tax but insists scrapping it in an unfunded way is irresponsible, and promotes the Lib Dem growth plan as the credible alternative.

I welcome the Minister for Veterans and People to his new role. He will be interested to know that my Gosport constituency has the highest proportion of veterans in the country. A
deb_ex.sum: Argues that Operation Valour improves visibility but does not invest in core services like housing and healthcare, and asks how it will avoid being mere window-dressing.

deb_ex.t: I know that the Minister cares deeply about increasing sporting participation, so she must be as disappointed as I am that the Government’s rhetoric just does not match the facts.
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Minister by listing cuts to school sport funding, business rate rises forcing fee increases, council facility closures and poor UK expenditure rankings, arguing Government rhetoric does not match reality.

deb_ex.t: It is a pleasure to follow my hon. Friend the Member for Droitwich and Evesham (Nigel Huddleston) in welcoming our hon. Friend the Member for Reigate (Rebecca Paul) to her role—I k
deb_ex.sum: Supports the Bill, highlights the UK's soft power through sport, but gently criticises the Government for failing to match rhetoric with action on soft power strategy and the Soft Power Council.

deb_ex.t: I am grateful to the Secretary of State for her statement, but I have to confess to being a bit more confused now than I was when I walked into the room. When it comes to Hampshire
deb_ex.sum: Dinenage expresses confusion about whether the Hampshire decision is a pause or cancellation, attacks the costs imposed on councils already under financial strain, and demands reimbursement and a clear timetable.

deb_ex.t: MPs across the Solent region were scrambling for reliable information with complete radio silence from the Home Office
deb_ex.sum: Hampshire coastal MP criticises the lack of Home Office communication with local MPs during the Portsmouth incident, questions the adequacy of policing resources, and demands better intelligence-sharing and assurances about future incidents

deb_ex.t: I also warmly welcome this announcement. The sheer number of young people whose lives have been impacted by this issue is a damning indictment of a collective failure to keep child
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the announcement but criticises tech companies for innovating fast on products while moving slowly on safety, and asks how compliance will be monitored and what sanctions will apply.

deb_ex.t: the funeral sector was nothing better than a lawless wild west with no mandatory qualifications to practise, no accreditation for professionals, no licensing of businesses
deb_ex.sum: Calls for urgent statutory regulation of funeral directors via new clause 41, citing the Hull case of 67 charges for decomposing bodies and arguing the sector remains a lawless wild west with no mandatory qualifications or licensing.

deb_ex.t: Families have already waited years and cannot be expected to wait indefinitely.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the majority of funeral directors are professional but warns the government's vague promise of proposals 'in due course' is unacceptable; new clause 41 would extend the Human Tissue Authority's remit to cover the whole sector.

deb_ex.t: It feels like the Government agree, so I ask the Minister to tell the House exactly when a statutory scheme will be brought forward
deb_ex.sum: Calls on the Government to commit to a timetable for statutory regulation of the funeral sector, arguing all parties agree and the regulatory black hole must be closed.

deb_ex.t: As the Minister knows, technology is being used in many different forms to threaten women. A Gosport domestic abuse survivor, Harmony Hayman, is still living in fear of a former pa
deb_ex.sum: Raises the case of Gosport constituent Harmony Hayman, a domestic abuse survivor still threatened by a former partner using a prison mobile phone, and urges the minister to review domestic abusers' eligibility for early release.

deb_ex.t: I must admit that I am really puzzled by the Minister’s statement. The visitor levy is not going to be ringfenced for tourism, so how does he know that it will go to its intended d
deb_ex.sum: Dinenage questions the lack of a ringfence, the absence of a cap, and the evidence base for growth claims, warning that hospitality businesses already struggling will not survive another tax.

deb_ex.t: In Gosport, the number of young people not in education, employment or training has gone up by 23% under this Government.
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Secretary of State for ignoring rising NEET figures under this government, blames business taxes for youth unemployment in Gosport, and presses him on what Milburn's report will actually deliver.

deb_ex.t: no one from the Home Office had the courtesy to contact me before, during or after those 150 people were landed on the shores of my constituency
deb_ex.sum: Raises alarm that French smugglers have shifted to a Normandy–Solent route, describes 150 people landing in her constituency without prior Home Office notice, and demands the government explain what it is doing to shut down this new route.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Minister for updating the House. I have had so much casework on this, as she will know, with some really heartbreaking stories. The fact is that the backlog, including
deb_ex.sum: Presents a constituent with a life-threatening condition still waiting five months for payment, criticises the lack of hard timescales, and demands clarity on sanctions, Capita's future contracts, clawback, and compensation.

deb_ex.t: The climate crisis is upon us. We in the UK are now in the midst of our third heatwave in less than three months. Communities have endured sweltering conditions that have put huge
deb_ex.sum: Opens the debate by linking the climate crisis and heatwaves to the construction sector's carbon footprint, arguing that embodied carbon is a critical gap in UK climate policy that the Government has so far ignored.

deb_ex.t: we need to recognise that we should be reusing buildings as much as possible. We should be reducing the destruction caused by a failure to reuse
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the intervention and argues that regulations requiring whole-life carbon assessment are needed to ensure buildings are reused rather than demolished, applying the waste hierarchy to construction.

deb_ex.t: I could not agree more with the hon. Gentleman. Since I entered this place, I have been campaigning for homes and buildings that are truly fit for the future. We need to take this
deb_ex.sum: Extends her argument that the Government's inaction is creating a fragmented patchwork of local rules that burdens industry, and calls on the Minister to provide national leadership and a clear regulatory pathway aligned with international

deb_ex.t: national regulation on embodied carbon will reduce complexity for the construction industry, not increase it. It will replace fragmentation with consistency
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the use of article 4 to prevent demolition as a last resort and reiterates the case for national regulation to replace the current fragmented local approach, directly challenging the Government's inaction.

deb_ex.t: this is not regulation that industry fears; it is regulation that the construction sector is asking for
deb_ex.sum: Quotes a now-senior minister's own past support for embodied carbon regulation to press the Government to act, and calls for use of the UK net zero carbon buildings standard as a fast-track compliance route.

deb_ex.t: Does she not recognise that Government is the institution that can provide exactly the consistency that the sector requires?
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Minister to acknowledge that Government is the institution best placed to deliver the consistency that the sector is calling for, challenging the case for further delay.

deb_ex.t: The Minister has outlined the complexities of regulating in this area as in any other area, and I am glad to hear her say that this does not mean the Government will do nothing. Th
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Minister's complexity argument by pointing out that hundreds of industry experts have already created a regulatory framework ready for Government adoption, asking her to acknowledge this preparatory work.

deb_ex.t: Heatwaves, which are becoming more frequent and more severe due to the climate crisis, create a health crisis. We see that in excessive temperatures in our hospitals and other heal
deb_ex.sum: Links the NHS heat crisis to the broader climate emergency, calls on the Minister to support a maximum workplace temperature Bill and push for a government-wide adaptation and resilience plan.

deb_ex.t: What support she plans to provide to local authorities to help them adopt new technologies for tackling potholes and road defects.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what support the government plans to give local authorities to adopt new technologies for tackling potholes and road defects.

deb_ex.t: Why not equip them with cameras and AI-enabled technology, so that they can spot, map and log potholes immediately, as soon as they appear?
deb_ex.sum: Proposes equipping bin lorries with AI cameras to spot and map potholes in real time, urging cross-departmental coordination and funding to roll this out nationally.

deb_ex.t: Will he ban trade in goods, services and investment in both directions immediately, because the facts on the ground are changing now, at pace and faster than ever before?
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the government for more hand-wringing delays and demands an immediate ban on trade in goods, services and investment in both directions, arguing that facts on the ground are changing at pace right now.

deb_ex.t: will he rule out Rosebank and Jackdaw, because the climate damage they would create hugely outweighs any possible benefit
deb_ex.sum: Chowns highlights record heat and harvests as evidence of the climate crisis and presses the Prime Minister to honour his manifesto pledge by ruling out new oil and gas licences including Rosebank and Jackdaw.

deb_ex.t: I would like to speak to amendment 15 and new clause 30, tabled in my name, and to new clauses tabled by other colleagues from across the House. First of all, I welcome the new Min
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes steps in the Bill but argues it must go much further on dirty money, disinformation and structural democratic reform, urging the Minister to encourage the Prime Minister to initiate a national commission on electoral reform.

deb_ex.t: I was speaking in relation to the title of the Bill.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly defends her remarks as relevant to the Bill's title before being ruled out of order again.

deb_ex.t: We have to take big money out of politics, take the poison of disinformation out of politics, and fix our political system once and for all.
deb_ex.sum: Calls for a total ban on corporate donations and annual campaign expenditure limits, arguing big money and disinformation are loopholes the Bill must close completely.

deb_ex.t: the climate damage created by Rosebank and Jackdaw will hugely outweigh any potential economic benefits and therefore rule them out
deb_ex.sum: Argues that climate breakdown already far outweighs any economic benefit from Rosebank and Jackdaw and urges the Minister to rule both fields out entirely.

deb_ex.t: we cannot get good growth unless it is both green and fair. We will not build sustainable prosperity by trashing nature and the climate
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the government's continuity with the previous Chancellor, demanding action to bring water into public hands, tax wealth fairly, and ensure growth is green and fair.

deb_ex.t: waiting another six to nine months to implement these sanctions is still too long? We must speed up.
deb_ex.sum: Warmly welcomes the settlement trade ban but presses the Foreign Secretary to implement sanctions faster than the proposed six-to-nine months, given the ongoing conflict in Gaza and the West Bank.

deb_ex.t: Capita promised to have this resolved, with all bereavement cases done by the end of August. It broke that promise. This week, she is still waiting.
deb_ex.sum: Describes a bereaved constituent waiting 11 months for a death-in-service payment after Capita broke its promise, and calls for Capita to be barred from future contracts of this kind.

deb_ex.t: the wildfires and droughts we saw this summer and the impending extreme El Niño show that we cannot wait that long
deb_ex.sum: Chowns argues that waiting until 2028 for the next national adaptation programme is too long given this summer's wildfires and droughts, and calls for urgent action to build resilience for farmers and communities now.

deb_ex.t: I was disappointed that the talks convened in July did not involve all the parties that had previously been involved in the existing cross-party social care talks
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Prime Minister's commitment to cross-party social care talks but expresses disappointment that July's talks excluded some previously involved parties, asking for a timetable and genuine cross-party inclusion.

deb_ex.t: No doubt inadvertently, that is misleading because no such invitation was ever issued to the Green party.
deb_ex.sum: Raises a point of order claiming the Leader of the House gave a misleading answer about smaller parties being invited to cross-party social care talks, and asks how to get the record corrected.

deb_ex.t: Hereford sixth-form college has told me that 21 young people dropped out last year because of transport problems
deb_ex.sum: Raises transport costs as a key barrier to post-16 education access in her rural constituency and calls on the Secretary of State to work with Cabinet colleagues to implement free bus travel for all young people.

deb_ex.t: I will use my contribution to do two things: first, to reiterate that international law and human rights are absolutely critical, and secondly, to reflect on the responsibilities t
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Government's recognition of the ICJ ruling and the settlement trade ban but argues the UK remains complicit while F-35 components are still exported to Israel, and calls for full consistency with international law.

deb_ex.t: I am requesting that he cites his sources for the claims he has made as to the reserves of shale gas in this country.
deb_ex.sum: Asks Richard Tice to provide sources for his claims about shale gas reserves in the UK.

deb_ex.t: Fundamentally, however, there is one key reason why we must have a full ban on fracking, which is that we must keep fossil fuels in the ground.
deb_ex.sum: Backs a full statutory ban on fracking on climate grounds and asks the Minister to confirm the energy independence Bill will include a ban covering existing licences.

deb_ex.t: Fossil fuels are traded globally. If we open up new production of fossil fuels, the reality is that that will do nothing for bills, do almost nothing for energy security and be a c
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the energy security argument for fracking, saying new fossil fuel production will not cut bills or improve security and distracts from renewable investment.

deb_ex.t: We know, for example, that Jackdaw would generate 27 jobs—the number of people who fit on the top of a double-decker bus.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects Tice's characterisation and highlights that Jackdaw would generate only 27 jobs, undercutting the employment case for fossil fuel development.

deb_ex.t: Yes, seriously. I can give the hon. Member the reference, unlike for the extraordinary statistics he cited in his speech, which apparently have no basis in actual evidence. Fundame
deb_ex.sum: Offers to provide a reference for the Jackdaw jobs figure, criticises Tice's unsourced statistics, and reiterates the need for a full ban on fracking.

deb_ex.t: It is indeed true that there is considerable public subsidy for oil and gas, as well as revenues from the windfall taxes. As the hon. Member for Alloa and Grangemouth pointed out,
deb_ex.sum: Confirms public subsidy for oil and gas, highlights fossil fuel companies' enormous profits, and asserts renewables are the cheap clean energy of the future.

deb_ex.t: No, the argument that there is commercially viable production is a nonsense. The hon. Member should look at the information from the British Geological Survey.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the claim of commercially viable shale gas in the UK and directs opponents to the British Geological Survey.

deb_ex.t: I have already given way to the hon. Gentleman and several other people, so I will move to my conclusion. Fundamentally, we are living in a burning world. The 11 hottest years on r
deb_ex.sum: Concludes by citing accelerating climate change and wildfire damage to UK communities, and presses the Minister to confirm the energy independence Bill will include a full statutory ban covering existing licences.

deb_ex.t: There are currently no commercially proven reserves of shale gas in the UK, and yet he is suggesting that there are tens of billions at hand just to be plucked.
deb_ex.sum: Challenges Tice's claims about shale gas reserves, noting there are no commercially proven reserves in the UK, and asks him to cite sources for his assertions.

deb_ex.t: the climate crisis is one of the biggest international challenges facing us, that it requires us to keep fossil fuels in the ground
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the PM's acknowledgement of Brexit's damage but criticises the absence of any mention of the climate crisis, urging the government to rule out Jackdaw and Rosebank ahead of COP31.

deb_ex.t: There is nothing pragmatic about pouring more fuel on the fire of the climate crisis. Does the Secretary of State still agree with herself?
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the government by quoting the Secretary of State's own past statements opposing new fossil fuel development and demands the government rule out Rosebank and Jackdaw.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the Government’s stated commitment to tackling the crisis in social care. It does pensioners no favours if we kick the can down the road and continually fail to address i
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the social care commitment but warns the funding gap is urgent and the 2030 timetable too slow; argues that fixing social care also requires fairly taxing wealth.

deb_ex.t: we need to ensure that care is locally provided but nationally funded, and will she lobby her colleague the Chancellor
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the statement but calls for an end to the postcode lottery, the life lottery and catastrophic care costs, advocates nationally funded locally provided care, and asks the Minister to push the Chancellor to consider fair taxation of

deb_ex.t: Last week I was contacted by a constituent who faces a £300 a month shortfall between her rent and her local housing allowance. She is deeply concerned about the rent arrears and t
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent facing homelessness due to a £300 shortfall between rent and local housing allowance, cites a JRF report on rent controls, and calls for a debate on unfreezing LHA and introducing rent controls.

deb_ex.t: The Minister knows, because I wrote to him the day after this latest SFI shambles, that farmers in North Herefordshire are livid about the problem. Farmers in Ocle Pychard, Pudlest
deb_ex.sum: Conveys the distress and anger of North Herefordshire farmers excluded from the scheme and demands direct answers on why funding is lower, why last year's lessons were not applied, and how the government will own the problem.

deb_ex.t: does she agree that social care needs to be locally delivered, but nationally funded?
deb_ex.sum: Calls for an end to the postcode lottery in adult social care, citing the King's Fund report, and asks whether social care should be nationally funded and locally delivered.

deb_ex.t: The Energy Secretary herself has admitted that Jackdaw will not bring down bills and will create only 27 jobs. The 2024 Labour manifesto said that the climate crisis is the greates
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Prime Minister on the Jackdaw approval, citing its minimal job creation and energy bill impact, and invokes the UN climate warning to argue fossil fuels must stay in the ground.

deb_ex.t: On 14 October, the UN’s international commission of inquiry on the OPT and Israel published its latest report. I quote paragraph 43, which concludes that “Israeli military operatio
deb_ex.sum: Quotes the UN commission of inquiry's finding that Israeli military operations constitute a widespread and systematic attack on civilians, and presses the Secretary of State on whether he recognises these conclusions and how the UK can avoi

deb_ex.t: Flooding is no longer something that people talk about as a freak event or a piece of bad luck; increasingly, they expect it to happen again.
deb_ex.sum: Opens debate by sharing a constituent's flooding ordeal and argues the government must invest now in flood resilience before costs and climate impacts escalate further.

deb_ex.t: Absolutely, and that is a point I will return to later in my speech. There is a huge benefit-cost ratio for early investment in flood resilience—it pays back many times over. Let u
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the previous intervention and reinforces the economic case for early flood resilience investment, noting annual flood costs could rise to £4.5 billion by mid-century.

deb_ex.t: Once again, the hon. Member’s point is that as we face increasing frequency and severity of floods, existing problems are going to become worse, so we need to invest to protect com
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the previous intervention that increasing flood frequency makes existing problems worse and that early investment is cheaper than later costs.

deb_ex.t: Natural flood management has got to be a core element of our response to flood risk.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that natural flood management must be central to the government's response and personalises the issue through accounts of flooded families, farmers and business owners.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman’s point about co-ordination between agencies is absolutely crucial; it is another point that I will be coming to in my speech. This is an issue that crosses boun
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the need for joined-up cross-agency coordination, raises the flood recovery framework, planning standards for sustainable drainage, and asks the Minister when schedule 3 of the Flood and Water Management Act will be commenced.

deb_ex.t: I am always in favour of Government making it easier for local authorities to unlock funding, as well as Government providing more funding to enable the good things, like natural f
deb_ex.sum: Supports easier local authority access to funding, asks whether farmers providing flood risk reduction should be rewarded, questions plans for water storage, and calls for action at the scale the climate crisis demands.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend makes an excellent point. The Government have a crucial role to play in supporting farmers to put in place the measures that are so helpful for our long-term resilie
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the call for better support for farmers, highlights that 58% of England's best agricultural land lies in floodplains making this a food security issue, and sets out the strong benefit-cost ratios for flood resilience investment.

deb_ex.t: The responsibility of Government is not simply to respond to flooding after it happens, but to build the resilience our communities will need in a rapidly warming climate.
deb_ex.sum: Concludes by challenging the government to act at the scale the flood resilience challenge demands, not merely respond after the fact.

deb_ex.sum: Asks what mechanisms the Timms review has put in place to ensure young people with cancer and other disabilities are properly heard and accounted for.

deb_ex.sum: Argues for consistency in applying international law and trade restrictions to Israeli settlements, as has been done with Russia.

deb_ex.t: if large-scale new oilfields are granted at Rosebank or Jackdaw, for example, there could be emissions equivalent to 28 low-income countries from just one oilfield
deb_ex.sum: Green MP welcomes the statement but warns that approving new oilfields like Rosebank or Jackdaw would produce emissions equivalent to 28 low-income countries and undermine climate and nature goals.

deb_ex.t: we could have a No. 10 for the future in the form of a climate protection unit in the Cabinet Office, which is needed to drive the cross-Government approach
deb_ex.sum: Points to extreme heat, drought and wildfires this summer and calls for a climate protection unit in the Cabinet Office to drive a cross-government approach, beyond the No. 10 North model.

deb_ex.t: Does the Secretary of State accept that local government funding is extremely stretched, especially for councils that run services such as SEND and social care
deb_ex.sum: Warns that further instability will worsen already-stretched council finances, particularly for SEND and social care, and argues that any reorganisation must come with proper local government funding.

deb_ex.t: To cease the statutory functions of Healthwatch without a suitable alternative in place…is to risk another major failing in patient safety and scrutiny
deb_ex.sum: Quotes Healthwatch Norfolk's warning that scrapping Healthwatch risks patient safety and asks whether the Government is reconsidering its plans.

deb_ex.t: During one of the summer heatwaves, a hospital serving my constituency—the Norfolk and Norwich university hospital—had to switch off its MRI scanners, resulting in hundreds of peop
deb_ex.sum: Raises the case of Norfolk and Norwich hospital switching off MRI scanners during a heatwave, causing hundreds of lost appointments, and urges investment plans to address keeping equipment and staff safe in extreme heat.

deb_ex.t: the window 2 debacle shows the level of interest there is, and that far more funding is needed in the SFI funding pot
deb_ex.sum: Agrees certainty is vital and argues the window 2 debacle demonstrates that far more funding is needed in the SFI pot to support nature-friendly farming.

deb_ex.t: What steps her Department is taking to prepare communities for flooding in winter 2026-27.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Government what steps are being taken to prepare communities for flooding in winter 2026-27.

deb_ex.t: How is she working across Government to ensure that preparedness for flooding risks this winter are stepped up, to keep our communities safe?
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Minister on cross-government coordination to step up flood preparedness given unprecedented climate impacts and the forecast super El Niño bringing a colder, wetter winter.

deb_ex.t: The Minister is right to highlight the growing risk of the loss of services and utilities in emergencies. Preparedness needs to be driven at a national level, but much of it needs
deb_ex.sum: Supports the national approach but presses the Minister on whether local resilience forums are adequately funded and whether every part of the UK has a local resilience plan.

deb_ex.sum: Argues that slow bureaucratic processes delay countryside stewardship payments to farmers ready to create wetlands and restore floodplains, and calls on DEFRA to properly resource Natural England and the Rural Payments Agency.

deb_ex.t: What are the Government doing to make it easier for survivors of abuse to cope with a system that often seems to add insult to injury?
deb_ex.sum: Commends the Bath charity Voices and asks what the government is doing to make it easier for survivors to cope with a court system that often compounds their trauma.

deb_ex.t: Women are waiting on average nine years for a diagnosis, and research like that is crucial to helping them access support much sooner.
deb_ex.sum: Congratulates Bath's Royal United Hospital on pioneering endometriosis research that could cut the average nine-year diagnosis time and asks the Leader of the House to join in that recognition.

deb_ex.t: organised crime gangs are then moving with impunity online, where enforcement is a lot less rigid. What is the Home Office doing to stop making it so easy to move
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the unit as a step to remove illegal vapes but warns that organised crime gangs are moving online where enforcement is less rigorous, and calls for action there too.

deb_ex.t: Dorothy House runs spaces called bereavement help points, where people who are grieving can meet others who are grieving. The service relies entirely on volunteers. The trauma of b
deb_ex.sum: Raises the example of Dorothy House bereavement help points run entirely by volunteers, arguing that bereavement support for baby loss should be an essential part of trauma care, not optional.

deb_ex.t: What steps her Department is taking to help tackle the use of illegal and non-compliant e-bikes.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the Department is taking to tackle illegal and non-compliant e-bikes.

deb_ex.t: Riders in the gig economy in particular ride fast and dangerously. What steps are being taken to tackle the demands of illegal bikes in the gig economy?
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent's near-miss on a cycle path with an illegal e-bike and asks what steps are being taken to tackle dangerous illegal e-bike use, particularly in the gig economy.

deb_ex.t: The women only find out once the videos have been shared 100,000 times and more, and they do not know what to do.
deb_ex.sum: Raises the problem of women being secretly filmed and videos shared online, calling on the PM to support ending the practice and to consider making misogyny a hate crime.

deb_ex.t: will the Minister do the bold thing, which is to get rid of business rates and replace them with a commercial landowner levy?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the 20% rate cut but calls on the government to fulfil its manifesto pledge of a full business rates overhaul, specifically suggesting replacement with a commercial landowner levy.

deb_ex.t: Q4. Community energy is a fantastic way of empowering communities and helping with both energy security and the cost of living. The Energy Security and Net Zero Committee recently
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that complex market regulations prevent households near community energy projects from buying locally generated electricity, using a Bath school as an example, and urges faster market reform.

deb_ex.t: What support her Department provides to help colleges and training providers develop international skills partnerships.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what support the Department provides to help colleges and training providers develop international skills partnerships.

deb_ex.t: Will he work with the British Council to build on its international skills partnership programme so that providers such as Bath college can access funding and support?
deb_ex.sum: Praises Bath college's collaboration and urges the Minister to work with the British Council to expand international skills funding, and suggests the issue be raised at the upcoming EU summit.

deb_ex.t: In the spirit of co-operation, even if we did this test, could he explain the damage and disruption that would be caused to communities in the UK if we tried on the scale that the
deb_ex.sum: Challenges Tice to explain how UK fracking could avoid the community disruption that is manageable in the vast empty spaces of the US.

deb_ex.t: Is it not true that our energy bills are subsidised, and that we are subsidising the oil and gas industry?
deb_ex.sum: Points out that oil and gas already receive public subsidies, undermining the argument that renewables are uniquely expensive and fracking is a cheaper alternative.

deb_ex.t: Is it not true that fracking is a massive scar on the countryside and is far more visible and disruptive than, for example, an onshore wind turbine?
deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to highlight that fracking causes far greater landscape damage than onshore wind turbines, undermining pro-fracking arguments from those who oppose renewables on countryside grounds.

deb_ex.t: I congratulate my hon. Friend the Member for Thornbury and Yate (Claire Young) on securing this important debate and on her excellent introduction. I am in full solidarity with the
deb_ex.sum: Calls for a complete permanent ban on fracking, arguing the energy independence Bill must close all loopholes, cover existing licences and put the ban in statute rather than relying on a reversible moratorium.

deb_ex.t: It is incomprehensible that in 2026 it is not banned outright.
deb_ex.sum: Argues fracking is unsustainable, unsafe and incompatible with net zero, and urges the Government to honour its manifesto pledge by enacting a full statutory ban covering all existing licences and closing all loopholes.

deb_ex.t: Would the hon. Member give us some figures or comparisons of how much fracked fuel we can produce in this country compared with the United States?
deb_ex.sum: Challenges Tice to provide comparative figures on how much fracked gas could realistically be produced in the UK versus the US.

deb_ex.t: Is it not true that delaying the transition—the hon. Lady does not want to accept a delay until 2050, but whatever the delay may be—will make energy more expensive for our citizens
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the shadow minister's defence of delayed energy transition, arguing it will make energy more expensive for citizens and is therefore irresponsible.

deb_ex.t: The Government have committed themselves to making misogyny an aggravated offence, but will the Minister go further and commit herself to making misogyny a hate crime?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the surge in covertly filmed nightlife videos shared with misogynistic abuse and calls on the government to go further by making misogyny a hate crime.

deb_ex.t: Every local area should have a youth hub—the benefits are so very clear.
deb_ex.sum: Endorses youth hub expansion but presses the Minister to confirm when Bath will receive one.

deb_ex.t: can he outline his ambition for negotiating cuts to the red tape and endless paperwork for businesses across the board
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the damage Brexit red tape has done to small businesses in Bath and asks the PM to outline his ambition for cutting paperwork across all business sectors.

deb_ex.t: Last week I held my regular roundtable for local domestic abuse organisations in Bath. There was fear—real fear—among the organisations that represent survivors and victims about t
deb_ex.sum: Reports real fear among Bath domestic abuse organisations about early releases and asks how the government will assess whether Avon and Somerset police have the capacity to support victims.

deb_ex.t: details are still not forthcoming. Will the Minister set out a timeline to give community energy projects the clarity that they have so long been waiting for?
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Government to publish a timeline for local energy trading, arguing community energy projects have been waiting too long for clarity.

deb_ex.t: jobs that will be directly created by Jackdaw and otherwise would not exist
deb_ex.sum: A Lib Dem MP voices the disappointment of climate campaigners and young people and challenges the Government to specify how many direct jobs Jackdaw will actually create.

deb_ex.t: we do not know the reasons why there was a withdrawal because the data is not held centrally
deb_ex.sum: Raises the lack of centrally held data on outcome 16 withdrawals from sexual abuse investigations and calls for a debate to understand why victims withdraw and help them access justice.

deb_ex.t: What steps are the Government taking to ensure that more customers and householders can have access to water butts?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the role of rainwater run-off reduction and community water butt schemes, and presses the Government to ensure more householders have access to water butts.

deb_ex.t: How is this policy going to be visibly enforced, so that public transport users in Bath can be sure that something is happening?
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges Liberal Democrat influence on the policy but presses the minister on how enforcement will be made visible to passengers in Bath.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes removal of clause 3 but announces he cannot support the Bill, arguing it transfers the Crown court backlog to an already overwhelmed magistrates court and that clauses 1, 2 and 6 remain deeply problematic.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that requiring judges to give reasons will increase appeals, contrasting this with jury verdicts which require no reasons and are rarely subject to public scrutiny.

deb_ex.t: we have to be very careful about what measures we take in this place in trying to support the pubs that we care for and love.
deb_ex.sum: Praises contributions from all sides but cautions that Parliament must think carefully about what measures will genuinely help pubs, arguing that a pub's true value lies in its community role far beyond its physical fabric.

deb_ex.t: In every neighbourhood you go to in Stevenage, you will find a pub—or a former pub, and that is the point.
deb_ex.sum: Notes that Stevenage's founders placed pubs at the heart of every neighbourhood within 15 minutes of homes, but acknowledges that many of those pubs have since been lost, illustrating the difficulty of protecting them.

deb_ex.t: ensuring that pubs survive is really difficult.
deb_ex.sum: Describes the rich pub heritage of Stevenage's old town, including coaching inns and a pub that was once a Napoleonic prison, but warns that pubs across the new town have been lost, showing how difficult it is to ensure pub survival.

deb_ex.t: we have buildings that were used for other purposes but are now pubs.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that communities need places to come together and highlights the flexibility of buildings in Stevenage that have switched between uses, including a former snooker club now operating as a microbrewery taproom.

deb_ex.t: we do not always have to introduce new laws in this place; we should think about how we can better implement the laws that already exist.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the Bill's 150-year threshold is poorly framed and argues Parliament should focus on better implementing existing laws rather than introducing new ones, before turning to local heritage examples in Stevenage.

deb_ex.sum: Notes Oasis's origins in a Stevenage pub and uses it to argue for recognising heritage spanning decades, not just centuries.

deb_ex.sum: Presses the Minister to agree that men who enter Britain illegally and need guidance not to commit rape should be deported immediately.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Secretary of State to state her red lines on experimenting on children regarding gender decisions, pressing her after the previous night's vote on puberty blockers.

deb_ex.t: today, will they put the interests of women before those of the Labour party?
deb_ex.sum: Moves a motion condemning the Government's plan to house illegal migrants at MOD Bicester and calls for ECHR withdrawal to enable deportations, directly challenging Labour MPs to prioritise women's safety.

deb_ex.t: This issue is not just in that area, either, but across the country. It is affecting women and girls in constituencies everywhere across the UK.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the previous intervention and broadens the concern to women and girls across the whole UK, not just the Bicester area.

deb_ex.t: men from cultures where women are treated worse than animals; men who the Government have decided need a leaflet asking them not to rape women and girls
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on leaving the ECHR and deportation, describing the migrant men as coming from cultures hostile to women and criticising the Government's leaflet approach.

deb_ex.t: did the Government agree that men entering this country illegally from countries such as Eritrea, Afghanistan and Sudan pose a direct threat to the safety of women and girls
deb_ex.sum: Responds to the Labour intervention by citing her own visit to Stoke and presses the Government on whether it agrees illegal migrants from certain countries pose a threat to women and girls.

deb_ex.t: The women of Linton-on-Ouse in North Yorkshire are worried about the 1,200 men who are about to descend on their community.
deb_ex.sum: Backs the previous intervention and highlights other communities facing large numbers of asylum-seeking men, praising local MPs battling the Home Office and councils.

deb_ex.t: it is not just a case of their values being different from ours; it is a case of their taking advantage of our nature, our culture and our values.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the previous intervention and adds that migrants exploit Britain's open and welcoming culture.

deb_ex.t: why not one member of the Labour party has responded to the women of Piddington who have written to them about this issue
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the Labour challenge by invoking new Conservative leadership and presses the point that Labour MPs have not responded to women of Piddington.

deb_ex.t: That technique was used to silence rape gang victims in our cities and towns, and it is appalling that Labour has not learnt from that scandal.
deb_ex.sum: Accuses the Government of using class as a weapon to silence communities' safety concerns and draws a parallel with the failure to act on rape gang victims.

deb_ex.t: why the use of houses in multiple occupation for asylum accommodation has increased by 12% since this Government took over
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the intervention by questioning the rise in HMO asylum accommodation under this Government and demanding a transparent long-term solution.

deb_ex.t: You have made an excellent point, which I will bring up later in my speech.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the HMO transparency point and says she will return to it later in her speech.

deb_ex.t: These are just a few examples.
deb_ex.sum: Recounts multiple specific cases of sexual violence committed by asylum seekers housed in taxpayer-funded accommodation to argue the Government's approach puts women and girls at risk.

deb_ex.t: men who should have been deported before they could roam our streets and forever change the lives of young women and girls
deb_ex.sum: Argues the men described should have been deported before committing crimes and that Government leaflets are no substitute for enforcement.

deb_ex.t: They are suffering because we are not deporting illegal migrants, and that is why we need to leave the ECHR.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that Piddington village will face serious safeguarding risks from the proposed asylum camp with no extra police provision, and calls for leaving the ECHR to enable deportations.

deb_ex.t: We Conservatives are committed to leaving the ECHR, so that we can deport foreign nationals who come here illegally within a week.
deb_ex.sum: Endorses leaving the ECHR as the Conservative solution to enable rapid deportation of illegal foreign nationals within a week.

deb_ex.t: I will give way after I make some progress. I have mentioned just a few of the horrific crimes committed by illegal migrant men—men who should have been deported before they could
deb_ex.sum: Accuses Labour of dismissing women's legitimate safety concerns, refusing to publish crime data on asylum seekers, and being ideologically captured on multiculturalism at the expense of community safety.

deb_ex.t: Why will they not give us the data on crimes committed against women and girls by men with active asylum claims?
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses Labour's counter-arguments as scripted lines, demands publication of crime data on asylum seekers, and sets out the Conservative plan to leave the ECHR and establish a removal force.

deb_ex.t: There may be some buyer’s remorse across Oxfordshire; I could not possibly say. I will say that we Conservatives have a very different view from the Liberal Democrats on open borde
deb_ex.sum: Calls for immediate action on illegal immigration, urges leaving the ECHR, and pledges the Conservative plan of automatic deportation, a removal force, and a ban on asylum claims for illegal arrivals.

deb_ex.t: My right hon. Friend makes an excellent point. The shadow Home Secretary has already made the point that we need sanctions and proper ways of enforcement for countries that refuse
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that sanctions against countries refusing to accept returnees are needed and defers to the shadow Home Secretary to elaborate on enforcement mechanisms.

deb_ex.t: I would point out that when the right hon. and learned Lady was Home Secretary, in charge of all of these things and making these key decisions, immigration was at record levels. I
deb_ex.sum: Deflects Braverman's challenge by noting immigration rose to record levels under her tenure, then closes by pledging the Conservative party will listen to and act for women concerned about their safety.

deb_ex.t: the first community that opened their hearts and their doors to me were my friends in the West Indian Caribbean community in west London
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to the Minister's work across communities, shares her own story of being welcomed by the West Indian Caribbean community in west London, and celebrates black community leaders.

deb_ex.t: When the Windrush arrived in 1948, the men and women on board did not just come to work; they built churches and social clubs
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to community organisations and reflects on the Windrush generation's role in building churches and social clubs despite hostility.

deb_ex.t: All of us have wonderful constituents who represent our communities and raise their concerns
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the hon. Member for Croydon East for her intervention and reaffirms the importance of community leaders across all constituencies.

deb_ex.t: black communities show that we can be an integrated, cohesive and multiracial Britain. We can celebrate the same values and be proud of who we are
deb_ex.sum: Congratulates the new Mayor of Ealing, reflects on her own grassroots community work and pays tribute to black Britons in her constituency including the Isaiah family.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the exploitation of women globally through international surrogacy arrangements and asks when legislation will come before the House to address this.

deb_ex.sum: Argues the BNO route's effectiveness must be judged by safety not visa numbers, and challenges the Government's failure to place the CCP in the enhanced tier of FIRS or to publish the overdue annual report.

deb_ex.sum: Argues nobody asked for reorganisation, that Rutland council excluded opposition councillors, and calls for a delay to ensure all councillors across Leicestershire and Lincolnshire have genuinely been engaged.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes government funding for the A605 and Tinwell A1 junctions but urges the government to use it for slip road widening rather than traffic lights, which National Highways itself considers inappropriate.

deb_ex.t: when will Ministers stop hiding behind a dead-end Metropolitan police investigation and do something to deter future hostilities in the UK?
deb_ex.sum: Presses Ministers to act over Chinese embassy guards using prohibited electroshock weapons against peaceful demonstrators, accusing the government of hiding behind a police investigation.

deb_ex.t: for survivors this feels like a form of early release. Mark Sanders should not be in our communities—which he now is—after serving only a quarter of his sentence
deb_ex.sum: Kearns raises the case of convicted child rapist Mark Sanders, who was moved to an open prison after two years of a near-ten-year sentence, and criticises the Government for failing to respond to her earlier written representations.

deb_ex.sum: Warns that NATO's threshold for responding to Russian airspace violations is too high, encouraging Russian recklessness and miscalculation, and calls for more Article 4 referrals.

deb_ex.t: living in a perpetual state of torture cannot be right, and we cannot allow people to wait longer.
deb_ex.sum: Drawing on her own near-death experiences, she urges undecided Members to vote for the Bill, arguing that laws cannot be written in hope of miracles that will not come for most dying people.

deb_ex.t: does she recognise that if some Members of this House think certain amendments are crucial to the Bill, they can do so?
deb_ex.sum: Raises the procedural option of 'suggested amendments' under Erskine May, noting it hasn't been used since 2004, and asks whether members could use it to add amendments they consider crucial.

deb_ex.t: the Government are imposing the least popular option on our communities
deb_ex.sum: Presents a petition with over 8,500 signatories opposing the Government's forced local government reorganisation plans for Rutland, Stamford and surrounding rural communities, arguing the least popular options are being imposed.

deb_ex.sum: Adds that the Government has also closed the Cabinet Office atrocity prevention centre, which she spent two years establishing, and argues this is alarming given rising global conflict.

deb_ex.sum: Presses the Minister for a long-overdue answer on why a paedophile was moved to an open prison just two years into a ten-year sentence, saying survivors have been ignored since May.

deb_ex.sum: Urges the Secretary of State to use pandemic-era evidence of women being mistreated in maternity services to overcome internal NHS resistance to reform.

deb_ex.t: They refused to come to an agreement about what was safer for my baby, and they said that I had to make that decision
deb_ex.sum: Shares a personal emergency birth experience where an obstetrician and midwife refused to agree on a C-section decision, forcing her to choose, illustrating the danger of professional rivalry.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Members who secured this debate, and all the families who have, in their darkest moments, raised their voices so that we can support them and, it is to be hoped, p

deb_ex.t: it should be mandatary to teach cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or CPR, for babies before they are discharged
deb_ex.sum: Calls for mandatory baby CPR training before hospital discharge and updated RCOG guidance on blood clots, sharing personal experiences of both issues to underscore their life-or-death importance.

deb_ex.t: My request to the Health Secretary is to roll out the app across every single hospital. We have proven that it works
deb_ex.sum: Endorses opening forced adoption records, calls for a national rollout of the Tommy's AI clinical decision support app across all NHS maternity units, and urges the Government to act on proven life-saving tools.

deb_ex.sum: Shares her own experience of placenta accreta and an 11% chance of dying in childbirth, stressing that inadequate attentive care affects high-risk as well as standard pregnancies.

deb_ex.sum: Condemns the energy ceasefire as a farce that protects Russian refineries while Ukraine's power grid is destroyed, and demands large-scale generators for Ukraine and a chapter VII Houthi terrorist designation.

deb_ex.sum: Attacks the Government for scrapping powers to close Confucius institutes and demands they be reinstated, while also calling for expulsion of Iranian intelligence-linked officials and a freeze on Russian and Belarusian tourist visas.

deb_ex.sum: Warns that over-reliance on Chinese-processed materials for renewables is as dangerous as dependence on petrochemical dictators, and links energy policy failures to the malign influence of Iran and Russia.

deb_ex.sum: Concludes by repeating that Iran's malign influence directly affects UK security, that the welfare bill must be cut to fund defence, and that failed programmes like Ajax must be recognised and scrapped.

deb_ex.sum: Argues that vague government statements on oil and gas are insufficient, and demands exploitation of North Sea resources to deliver genuine energy security.
