Opposition Members genuinely wish the whole Transport team well ahead of the weekend and next week—although if they are moved up, along or down, at least they will not have to answ
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the government's ZEV mandate as unachievable, arguing last year's targets were only met through compliance credits bought from Tesla and BYD rather than genuine consumer demand.

deb_ex.t: British vehicle manufacturers are expressing the view, with increasing urgency, that the ZEV mandate has simply become an ideological shibboleth of the Secretary of State for Energ
deb_ex.sum: Accuses the government of treating the ZEV mandate as ideological dogma, calls on the Secretary of State to listen to industry and motorists, and demands the mandate be scrapped to save over 100,000 jobs.

deb_ex.t: In London boroughs and cities across the country, council-wide 20 mph speed limits are causing havoc. In Wales, councils are desperately trying to unpick the last Welsh Labour Gove
deb_ex.sum: Attacks council-wide 20 mph speed limits as a failed Labour-driven policy that harms motorists and rural communities, comparing them to the discredited Welsh Government approach.

deb_ex.t: will she make a statement tomorrow so that questions can be asked then, rather than during a Second Reading debate?
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Secretary of State to make a formal statement tomorrow so that all Members can ask proper questions about the NATS outage rather than raising it during a Second Reading debate.

deb_ex.t: Before I turn to the Bill, let me comment on the events of the last 24 hours, which have shown just how important effective oversight of our aviation sector is. The shocking failur
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the Government for not making a formal statement on the NATS outage today, questions why Labour whipped against a review of airport drop-off charges in the Lords, and raises soaring charges at Gatwick and Luton.

deb_ex.t: If he does not want to answer the questions, we will have to drag him to the House tomorrow.
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Government frontbench to answer questions about the NATS outage from the Dispatch Box rather than from a sedentary position, threatening to compel a statement the next day.

deb_ex.t: If the Minister would like to speak, he can stand at the Dispatch Box. No, he does not want to do that—fine. We will have him here tomorrow, then, as we were told today that our ur
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill's stated aims but criticises it for lacking vision on growth, workforce development and pilot shortages, challenges soaring airport business rates, and questions whether no DfT Minister attended Farnborough airshow.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Lady makes a very clear case for why such a review of airport parking charges is necessary. One has not happened for a decade. It was great to get the support of the Liber
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the Lords amendment requiring a review of airport drop-off charges, warns against the Government removing it, and links soaring charges to surface access targets that lack viable alternatives for passengers.

deb_ex.t: Where are the measures to ease the burdens surrounding apprenticeships, an issue raised with me directly by the apprentices I met at Heathrow recently?
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the Bill for lacking measures on workforce, apprenticeships, pilot shortages and single-aisle aircraft manufacturing, and accuses the Government of treating aviation as a tax source rather than an engine of growth.

deb_ex.t: I just wanted to make it very clear that I was in no way questioning what Mr Speaker decided. When he spoke to me, he made it very clear that his understanding was that the Governm
deb_ex.sum: Disputes the Minister's characterisation of his remarks, asserting he was told by Mr Speaker that the Government intended to make a statement on the NATS failure.

deb_ex.t: Thank you very much, Madam Deputy Speaker. The point I was making was that I was basically being accused by the Minister of saying something that I had not said. I just wanted to m
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies he was correcting a mischaracterisation by the Minister, insisting the real issue is one of parliamentary scrutiny of the NATS failure.

deb_ex.t: Members have not had the chance today to properly raise the NATS blackout, which has affected over 100,000 passengers and cost UK aviation tens of millions of pounds
deb_ex.sum: Raises a point of order seeking guidance on how Opposition Members can obtain a government statement on the NATS blackout affecting over 100,000 passengers.

deb_ex.t: Where are the safeguards against higher charges for motorists? The Minister does not know.
deb_ex.sum: Closes speech by demanding to know what safeguards exist against higher motorist charges, accusing the Minister of ignorance about his own Bill.

deb_ex.t: Clauses 33 and 81 could lead to road charging schemes right across the country. The Minister seems not to have read his own Bill.
deb_ex.sum: Argues clauses 33 and 81 open the door to nationwide road charging, accuses the Minister of not reading his own Bill, and announces a reasoned amendment to defend motorists against unlimited tolls.

deb_ex.t: the Bill allows for exactly what we see in France, which is toll roads across the entire strategic road network
deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to press the Liberal Democrat speaker to accept that the Bill permits French-style tolls across the entire strategic road network.

deb_ex.t: rejects the sweeping powers the Bill would grant Ministers to impose new road-charging schemes across England through secondary legislation
deb_ex.sum: Moves the reasoned amendment declining Second Reading, arguing the Bill grants sweeping ministerial powers to impose road charging across England with minimal parliamentary oversight and that the Government cannot be trusted to deliver the

deb_ex.t: We are discussing legislation that will enable the biggest road infrastructure project that this country has done in decades, but where is she today?
deb_ex.sum: Responds on the London bridges point, then criticises the absence of the Secretary of State from a debate on the country's largest road infrastructure project in decades.

deb_ex.t: look at the road projects that we were putting forward under the last Government and at the projects that have already been cancelled under this Government
deb_ex.sum: Deflects by pointing to road projects advanced under the last Government and schemes cancelled by the current one, promising to address this later in his speech.

deb_ex.t: all the planning has already gone through, as the Minister said. That is what the last Government were doing—getting us to exactly to this point.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that the previous Government had already completed all the planning for the lower Thames crossing, contrary to the implication from the Labour benches.

deb_ex.t: the Minister has already contradicted her. She should have listened to his speech.
deb_ex.sum: Points out that the Minister's own speech contradicted the Labour backbencher who shook her head at his claim about the previous Government's planning work.

deb_ex.t: Would the Minister like to intervene on me to say if any companies have been lined up and who is looking forward to funding this project under the proposed legislation?
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the concern about unknown funders and invites the Minister to intervene and name any companies lined up to finance the project, noting he declines to do so.

deb_ex.t: I have just given way several times, so let me make a little progress before I give way again. The Secretary of State is too busy to bother about motorists until they become useful
deb_ex.sum: Accuses the Government of being anti-motorist, detailing a long list of cancelled road schemes and arguing the Bill's open-ended powers could expose the entire road network to charging.

deb_ex.t: My right hon. Friend makes a good point. The Government have devised a new cunning plan. They are not just banning diesel—oh no; they are banning hydrotreated vegetable oil. You he
deb_ex.sum: Criticises National Highways for banning diesel and hydrotreated vegetable oil on lower Thames crossing construction sites, arguing this drives up costs that will ultimately be passed on to toll-paying motorists.

deb_ex.t: The last Government fought tooth and nail through the courts to deliver the scheme and get the planning consents all the way through
deb_ex.sum: Disputes the Government's credit for planning consent, argues costs are being built into the scheme from the start, and calls for withdrawal from the Aarhus Convention to reduce legal challenge costs on infrastructure.

deb_ex.t: We are totally against opening up the entire strategic road network to charging, which is what this piece of legislation does.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies the Conservative position is not against tolls per se but firmly against the Bill's powers to extend road charging across the entire strategic road network.

deb_ex.t: Nowhere in this legislation is there any talk of the exact price that people will have to pay to cross the river. There is no idea of who is going to build the crossing, the cost o
deb_ex.sum: Argues the Bill leaves key questions entirely unanswered — cost, builder, and toll price — and calls for withdrawal from the Aarhus Convention to cut the hundreds of millions spent defending legal challenges to road projects.

deb_ex.t: How far have we drifted when our rules make special provision for polygamy or incest to be recognised in the benefit system?
deb_ex.sum: Moves to bring in a Bill prohibiting recognition of polygamous and incestuous overseas marriages in the social security system, arguing the current rules are indefensible and urging the Government to support the Bill.

deb_ex.t: Does she agree with herself, the Prime Minister or her junior Minister?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights contradictory statements from the Secretary of State, Prime Minister and a junior Minister on Heathrow expansion, questioning the coherence of the Government's position.

deb_ex.t: When will this Transport Secretary listen to British business, the unions and British drivers and scrap the zero emission vehicle mandate
deb_ex.sum: Cites Chancellor Merz's move to scrap the EU combustion engine ban and calls on the Government to scrap the ZEV mandate, which he argues is costing British jobs and taxpayers.

deb_ex.t: I really welcome the Government’s U-turn on adopting Conservative policy and deciding to review airport drop-off charges, but in response to my written question, the Minister did n
deb_ex.sum: Sarcastically welcomes the review as adoption of Conservative policy but challenges the Minister to confirm that business rates increases, employment taxes and anti-car targets will also be included in the inquiry.

deb_ex.sum: Questions whether the Bill's delay is due to the resignation of the former Armed Forces Minister and suggests the Government should pause for thought.

deb_ex.sum: Questions whether the House deserves to hear the new Prime Minister's views on the unfolding crisis before recess.

deb_ex.t: 4. What steps he is taking with Cabinet colleagues to strengthen Wales’s place in the Union.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Secretary of State what steps he is taking with Cabinet colleagues to strengthen Wales's place in the Union.

deb_ex.t: A strength of the Union is unity in diversity. Notwithstanding much progress since 2010, the last two years have seen a diminution in the number of Welsh speakers in Wales, particu
deb_ex.sum: Notes a decline in Welsh speakers, particularly among young people, over the last two years and presses the Minister for a plan to reverse the trend.

deb_ex.t: This Bill responds to the widely held view that services for infants, prospective parents and parents of young children are somewhat vulnerable when they rely largely on non-statutory guidance
deb_ex.sum: Introduces his private Member's Bill, explaining its purpose of placing infant and early-years services on a statutory footing and making them accountable to Parliament rather than reliant on non-statutory guidance.

deb_ex.t: This Bill is quite deliberately written at a higher level. It does not specify what the services should be; it empowers Ministers to regulate and make provision for those services.
deb_ex.sum: Walks through the Bill's six clauses, explaining how each places duties on the Secretary of State to define, assess, provide and report on early-years services, and defends the deliberately high-level drafting.

deb_ex.t: The Government removed the requirement to ringfence the funding for Sure Start, and because local authorities were not required to spend that money in that way, they made their cho
deb_ex.sum: Concedes that the removal of ringfenced Sure Start funding was the wrong priority and accepts responsibility on behalf of the previous government.

deb_ex.t: I remember with respect to my own children the importance of a visit by the midwife, even after birth
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the importance of home visits, drawing on personal experience of midwife visits after birth, and briefly explains clause 1's duty on the Secretary of State to define services.

deb_ex.t: today we are putting these services on a statutory footing. Of course subsequent Governments can change statutes, but this Bill makes it an explicit decision of this House and Parliament
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Bill places services on a statutory footing, making any future removal an explicit parliamentary decision, and runs through clauses 2 to 6 covering need assessment, provision, annual reporting and interpretation.

deb_ex.t: Let us hope that we have begun a process today with this legislation that will have as profound an impact.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks Members for contributions, offers places on the Standing Committee, and expresses hope the Bill will have as profound an impact as the 1944 Education Act.

deb_ex.t: I am delighted by the reprieve—the New Forest was to be split, and part of it swallowed by Southampton. Will the Secretary of State accept my representation that we want the integr
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the pause as a reprieve for the New Forest and presses the Secretary of State to preserve the integrity of the New Forest rather than allowing it to be absorbed by Southampton.

deb_ex.t: Last week, the Prime Minister boasted in the same breath that we had the fastest growth in the G7 and that the decade of slow growth was caused by Brexit. If we are ahead of the pa
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the logical consistency of the Government's claim that the UK has the fastest G7 growth while also blaming Brexit for a decade of slow growth.

deb_ex.t: I join that long list of UK Ministers who have raised, at the very highest level in Israel, the most egregious practices in the west bank, designed specifically to prevent a two-st
deb_ex.sum: Draws on personal ministerial experience of repeatedly raising west bank abuses with Israel at the highest level only to be rebuffed, and congratulates the Foreign Secretary for now acting.

deb_ex.t: Just how confident is the Minister that this was not a cyber-attack? How confident is he of the resilience of the system in the event of such an attack
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Minister on whether this was a cyber-attack, questions the resilience of systems against such attacks, and asks about the Government's willingness to retaliate as a deterrent.

deb_ex.t: If the hoteliers of Bournemouth are gagging to pay this tax, I can assure the Minister that those in hospitality in the New Forest are not. The Minister said that everybody will be
deb_ex.sum: Swayne contradicts the Bournemouth hoteliers' backing cited earlier by noting New Forest hospitality is firmly against the levy, and challenges the Minister's claim that everyone will win given the lack of detail on rates and coverage.

deb_ex.t: the financial damage of not addressing it is that we will all pay higher mortgages and endure higher costs
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the Budget as politically calculated to avoid tough choices until an election, arguing it fails to address debt, productivity or the structural question of taxation versus benefits.

deb_ex.t: I believe that this is the cut-and-run Budget.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the Budget as a cynical pre-election exercise, suggesting even the Liberal Democrats are preparing for a snap December election on the back of its populist measures.

deb_ex.t: Were he to consult a map, the Minister would understand that the Creator’s purpose in placing the estuary of the Test was to prevent, for government purposes, the eastern part of t
deb_ex.sum: Uses dry wit to argue that the New Forest's eastern area should not be treated as part of Southampton, implying the Government's reorganisation proposals ignore natural geographic boundaries.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out government action to drive growth and jobs across Scotland, highlighting the local growth fund and the push to decentralise economic power beyond Holyrood.

deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms government commitment to Grangemouth reindustrialisation, citing the £120 million chemicals plant commitment and work to unlock £200 million from the national wealth fund.

deb_ex.t: While our Prime Minister is determined to end rough sleeping, in Scotland it is on the rise, and that is not good enough.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges housing is devolved but highlights concern about rising rough sleeping and children in temporary accommodation in Scotland, contrasting with UK government action in England.

deb_ex.t: This Government are committed to supporting a competitive and sustainable steel sector across the United Kingdom, with Scotland a vital part of that. The UK’s first-ever steel stra
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's commitment to a sustainable steel sector, highlighting the new steel strategy and Scotland's role within it.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is a powerful advocate for those she represents, and I know she discussed the situation at Dalzell works with the Prime Minister when he was in Motherwell recently.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the seriousness of Liberty's failure to pay Dalzell workers and confirms the government is looking at the situation closely and will continue to work with the MP.

deb_ex.sum: Rejects Conservative criticism on energy policy, blaming them for the Jackdaw delay and defending the government's clean-energy approach as the route to lower bills.

deb_ex.t: We are cutting red tape and striking new trade deals around the world to drive up exports, and boosting the role of Scottish small and medium-sized enterprises
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's pro-business agenda, citing trade deals, red tape reduction and support for Scottish SMEs in defence and energy.

deb_ex.t: it is time for us to have an honest conversation with the country about our broader relationship with Europe. That stands to benefit Scotland in many ways
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach to EU relations as beneficial to Scotland while attacking the Conservatives over the Truss mini-Budget and its economic damage.

deb_ex.t: There are now 12 youth hubs open in Scotland, with a further 27 planned across our nation. Each will provide a range of services to our brilliant young people
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the new West Dunbartonshire youth hub and highlights the expansion to 12 open youth hubs in Scotland with 27 more planned.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the rough sleeping investment but highlights that those with no recourse to public funds in Ealing Southall are excluded, and asks for ministerial meetings to ensure they are not left behind.

deb_ex.t: Does he agree that the steps this Government are taking will help to ensure that there is room in our prisons for those who are making life a misery
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the introduction of respect orders in Ealing Southall and asks the Secretary of State to confirm that prison places will be available for persistent antisocial behaviour offenders.

deb_ex.t: many of our rough sleepers do not have the right to stay or work in the country, so the council cannot legally help them off the streets.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that many rough sleepers in Ealing Southall have no right to remain, meaning the council cannot legally help them, and asks the Secretary of State to meet her to find ways to help this group return home with dignity.

deb_ex.t: weekly drop-in they run to help rough sleepers without the right to stay in this country and advise them on how to reconnect with family and go home with dignity
deb_ex.sum: Highlights a Sikh gurdwara in her constituency that helps rough sleepers reconnect with family, and asks the Secretary of State to congratulate the organisation and support similar groups.

deb_ex.t: all the changes that she is bringing in through the Bill, including those discussed today, will help us to bring down those waiting lists even further
deb_ex.sum: Highlights improved waiting list performance in her area and expresses confidence the Bill's changes will drive further improvement.

deb_ex.t: her announcement today will not just help the NHS to beat the heat, but help us to save money that we can spend on patient care
deb_ex.sum: Highlights Ealing hospital's solar and heating investment as evidence that the Government's capital programme both addresses heat resilience and saves money for frontline care.

deb_ex.t: Many people in my constituency work at the nearby Heathrow airport, so it is extremely important for jobs, but for many other constituents the noise of the airport can be annoying
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether airspace modernisation will reduce aircraft stacking and noise over west London and whether local people will retain a say on airspace decisions.

deb_ex.sum: Costigan welcomes the Elizabeth line but raises overcrowding as a problem for constituents travelling to Heathrow, particularly in rush hour with luggage.

deb_ex.sum: Argues that after 14 years of austerity and centralisation, No. 10 North is worth the cost if it genuinely benefits left-behind communities like her own.

deb_ex.t: this Bill strikes the right balance between continuing social mobility for long-standing tenants while protecting homes for those most in need
deb_ex.sum: Highlights 3,000 families in temporary accommodation and 9,000 homes lost to right to buy in Ealing, and asks whether the Bill strikes the right balance between social mobility and protection of housing stock.

deb_ex.t: it was his party, the Liberal Democrats, in coalition with the Conservatives, that massively increased the discounts for right to buy
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Liberal Democrat speaker by pointing out that his party in coalition with the Conservatives substantially increased right-to-buy discounts, contributing to the very problem he criticises.

deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to credit community organisations like the Hanwell Friends of Sabastiya with influencing the Government to take its recent robust steps on Israel and Palestine.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the new respect orders and asks the Minister to ensure courts have guidance ready before their introduction on 26 October so police and courts can act immediately.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the levy and notes local businesses in Southall support it, but presses the Minister to ensure London's unique governance structure means boroughs can jointly shape how the levy operates.

deb_ex.t: black mothers face up to a 40% higher risk of miscarriage than white mothers
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Amos report but urges the taskforce to address the double jeopardy facing black and Asian families in maternity services, and calls for language support and recognition of siblings as bereaved family members.

deb_ex.sum: Cites research showing disabled claimants prefer employment support to cash benefits and presses the Minister to use tailored support to reduce the welfare bill while helping those who want to work.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the shadow Secretary of State by arguing the Conservatives' own legacy Act gave no real protection to veterans' families as it was found to be unlawful.

deb_ex.t: more money to be spent where it matters—on teaching and learning?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights Great British Energy solar panel investment in three local schools and asks whether the resulting savings will free up money for teaching and learning.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the national care service as beneficial for unpaid carers and families in her constituency, while affirming the state pension will continue to rise.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the closure of Southall police station and calls on the Prime Minister to back her campaign to reopen it as part of efforts to revive the town centre.

deb_ex.sum: Labour backbencher welcomes the fair pay agreement investment but presses the Minister on how far the half a billion pounds will go in properly valuing care workers.

deb_ex.sum: Celebrates the Bill as completing the legacy of Catholic emancipation and invokes Daniel O'Connell, while noting there is still no statue or portrait of O'Connell in the House.

deb_ex.t: this Bill is about removing discrimination in elected office and not about inherited office
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the Bill concerns discrimination in elected office, not inherited office.

deb_ex.t: she is the first Somali-born hijab-wearing woman to hold that position
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the hon. Member for her tributes and asks her to join in congratulating Councillor Faduma Mohamed, the first Somali-born hijab-wearing Mayor of Ealing.

deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to her late constituent Eric Huntley, celebrating his founding of Bogle-L'Ouverture Publications and the Ealing bookshop as a landmark of black community resilience and education in the face of violent racism.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the investment and local decision-making powers, and asks the Minister to work with Ealing council and a local charity to address the high proportion of rough sleepers with no recourse to public funds in the constituency.

deb_ex.sum: Draws parallels with constituents in Hanwell Locks stuck in a battle with Bellway over remediation, and asks whether the compliance plans and financial penalties in the Bill will make a real difference.

deb_ex.sum: Liberal Democrats support the SI but argue it does nothing to catch criminals already operating outside any permit system, calling for higher fixed penalty notices, better resourcing and genuine enforcement against organised gangs.

deb_ex.t: the growing number of short-term lets is displacing local families and workers from the rented sector, hollowing out our rural communities
deb_ex.sum: Raises the impact of short-term lets on rural communities, asking what specific steps will protect rural rented stock from being lost to the market.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights the severe impact on Somerset and Devon farmers, long vaccine waiting lists and rising fallen stock costs, and presses the Minister to accelerate vaccination, provide financial assistance and remove surveillance barriers.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Minister to explain how the growth agenda will reach rural areas like Glastonbury and Somerton, citing a large productivity gap.

deb_ex.sum: Supports amendment 19 and promotes her own new clause 120 for a farmer-friendly GP scheme, urging the Government to treat the upcoming chief medical officer rural health report as a genuine test of action.

deb_ex.t: Government buying standards for food still do not mandate local or British sourcing, leaving farmers in Glastonbury and Somerton locked out of supplying local schools.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the new school food standards but presses the Government to strengthen buying standards to require local sourcing and to back her Good Food Bill.

deb_ex.sum: Warns that British food security is endangered by worsening extreme weather and presses the Minister on what discussions have taken place with DEFRA to strengthen farm resilience.

deb_ex.sum: Argues the government is diverting hundreds of millions from rural to urban councils, leaving Somerset £21 million worse off, and demands remoteness funding be restored in the December settlement.

deb_ex.t: heating oil has no price cap to protect them. The sector simply is not working for consumers
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that heating-oil householders face doubled bills with no price cap protection, and calls for the cap to be extended to off-grid homes, asking for an urgent ministerial meeting.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the end of first-come-first-served but argues the pot remains too small, cites a constituent facing financial hardship, and calls on the Minister to press the Chancellor for an extra £1 billion a year.

deb_ex.t: Those who can afford an adviser are waved through the farm gate, while those who cannot are left out in the field.
deb_ex.sum: Closes for the Liberal Democrats, detailing the unfairness of the window closure, highlighting that DEFRA's own forecasts predicted it yet did nothing, and exposing a two-tier system favouring land agents over family farmers.

deb_ex.sum: Presents a constituency petition urging the Government to publish its assessment of Capita's performance, set firm deadlines for clearing outstanding claims, prioritise bereavement cases, and strengthen oversight of outsourced contracts.

deb_ex.sum: Describes a constituent who has had to withdraw her retirement application twice due to Capita's failure to provide a pension quotation, and asks the Minister to intervene personally and give a date for payment.

deb_ex.sum: Lib Dem spokesperson welcomes the commitment but highlights past broken pledges, raises concerns about the tight eight-week timeframe for councils, rural homelessness, and the need for long-term social housing investment.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights Somerset aerospace and defence firms at risk from UK exclusion from the SAFE defence fund and presses the Minister to commit to securing UK participation on fair terms.

deb_ex.t: he cannot fathom why Governments have not yet fully implemented those recommendations. Does the hon. Gentleman share that frustration?
deb_ex.sum: Shares a constituent civil servant's bewilderment that IICSA recommendations have not been fully implemented, expressing solidarity with that frustration.

deb_ex.t: we are not spending sufficiently on defence. I want to challenge the hon. Member for Alloa and Grangemouth
deb_ex.sum: Challenges a colleague's opposition to defence spending and asserts that the UK is not spending sufficiently on defence, arguing preparedness failures invite conflict.

deb_ex.t: I fear that the Prime Minister has been sent naked into the Ankara conference chamber. The defence investment plan is indeed a skinny dip
deb_ex.sum: Argues the Prime Minister has been sent inadequately resourced to NATO, the defence investment plan falls short, and calls for faster progress towards higher GDP spending on defence by 2030.

deb_ex.t: Conflict does not necessarily begin when a missile is fired or a border is crossed. It can begin when public trust is systemically eroded
deb_ex.sum: Urges the Government to treat warfighting readiness as a whole-of-society endeavour including countering disinformation and information warfare, not just platforms and procurement.

deb_ex.t: despite covering less than 1% of the ocean floor, seagrass beds are responsible for 15% of its total carbon capture
deb_ex.sum: Raises the potential of ocean-based carbon capture, specifically seagrass, as an additional solution to land-based tree planting.

deb_ex.t: does the Secretary of State share my view that it was cynical of the Conservative party to develop a shadow petition to gather voter intention data?
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that Natural England's proposals concerned overgrazing broadly and notes ponies' positive role, then condemns the Conservatives for using a shadow petition to gather voter data.

deb_ex.t: What steps he is taking to improve UK-EU foreign and security co-operation.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the government is taking to improve UK-EU foreign and security cooperation.

deb_ex.sum: Asks the Foreign Secretary to support an EU initiative by four member states to seize immobilised Russian state assets for Ukraine's self-defence.

deb_ex.t: will the Secretary of State please consider the greater costs associated with delivering in the countryside, such as rural Devon?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the pause on Devon's reorganisation review and asks the Secretary of State to factor in higher rural delivery costs during the rapid review.

deb_ex.t: Ottery St Mary primary school is fundraising for air conditioning. Will the Secretary of State talk to her counterparts at the Department for Education
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the hospital cooling funding but raises school overheating, citing two primary schools in his constituency forced to close or fundraise for air conditioning, and asks the Secretary of State to engage the Department for Education.

deb_ex.sum: Raises reduced train services on the west of England line due to dry embankments and calls for a debate on adapting rail infrastructure to climate change.

deb_ex.t: The EU still gets 12% of its gas imports from Russia. While this is down from 45%—the level before the full-scale invasion—the proceeds are still fuelling the Russian war machine.
deb_ex.sum: Notes that the EU still imports 12% of its gas from Russia and urges the Secretary of State to maintain European unity and press EU partners to cease all Russian gas imports.

deb_ex.t: Does the Minister think that, as well as attenuation ponds and SUDS, people should be encouraged to store water in their own gardens using such things as water butts?
deb_ex.sum: References devastating flooding from Storm Chandra in his constituency and asks the minister whether household-level measures such as water butts should be more actively encouraged alongside SUDS and attenuation ponds.

deb_ex.sum: Rejects equivalence between Israel and Hamas but insists the Government must go further to fully match its stated commitments to international law and a two-state solution.

deb_ex.t: There is a real danger that investment in fracking will be a catastrophic mistake, as the fuels, facilities and resources become stranded assets.
deb_ex.sum: Argues against fracking and expanded fossil fuel extraction, warning of stranded assets as renewables advance. Also warns that Conservative support for fracking is politically damaging.

deb_ex.t: Will the UK step up investment in clean, domestic renewable energy production, as well as in the grid to distribute it?
deb_ex.sum: Citing repeated energy shocks and the National Security Adviser's warning of winter hardship, urges the government to step up investment in domestic clean energy and grid infrastructure.

deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister what steps are being taken to improve reoffending reduction programmes.

deb_ex.sum: Links early release reoffending rates to housing instability using a constituency case and asks what housing schemes support rehabilitation beyond the initial release period.

deb_ex.sum: Raises concerns from Devon businesses including a named cottage operator about reduced tourist footfall and argues the levy is designed for cities with wealthy overseas visitors, not rural areas.

deb_ex.t: Why does the Prime Minister think that his predecessors have been so reluctant to speak about Russian attempts to interfere in the referendum?
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Prime Minister on why his predecessors refused to publish an unclassified summary of the intelligence assessment into Russian interference in the EU referendum, as recommended by the ISC six years ago.

deb_ex.sum: Asks the Home Secretary to credit a member of the public for alertness in the RAF Fairford plot and calls for more whole-of-society security engagement.

deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to note that a Devon constituent suffered from sudden SFI withdrawal the previous year, questioning whether DEFRA is capable of learning from repeated mistakes.

deb_ex.sum: Notes the Minister's admission that Jackdaw will not reduce bills and asks for more detail on Government plans to remove or reform standing charges on gas bills.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the specific retention issue of Barnstaple staff redeployed to Exeter being charged £20 a day for parking, asking the Minister to address retention alongside recruitment.

deb_ex.sum: Supports the previous speaker by citing a village in his constituency that petitioned to keep its postie, emphasising the welfare role postal workers play in rural communities.

deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituency case of a constituent who lost PIP and UC and has received no substantive response from the Department for six months, asking whether individual cases can inform systemic improvements in communication.

deb_ex.sum: Praises the Home Secretary but argues hotel closures will fail without genuine deterrence, asking what plans exist to prevent small boat arrivals from settling in British society.

deb_ex.sum: Raises concern that rural areas like the New Forest and Waterside would lose local representation if absorbed into a unitary authority dominated by Southampton and Eastleigh.

deb_ex.sum: Asks the Prime Minister to clarify exactly how he believes Russia was able to alter the result of the referendum, challenging a claim the PM appears to have made.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the front-bench statements but warns that signals sent by the Chagos deal undermine Falklands deterrence, and urges the Minister to give Argentina an unambiguous warning that military action will be met with overwhelming force.

deb_ex.sum: Lewis questions why suspects in an Iranian-backed attack were released on bail and raises concern about foiled terrorist plots by people who entered the UK illegally across the channel.

deb_ex.sum: Warns that illegal small boat arrivals include would-be terrorists, citing a foiled Manchester synagogue attack, and urges remedial action before an atrocity occurs.

deb_ex.sum: Lewis argues the Government's claimed record defence increase is misleading given cold-war spending levels of 4.5–5% of GDP, and warns that creative accounting will undermine the NATO 3.5% core target.

deb_ex.sum: Raises distressing reports of care home deaths from heatstroke and a specific case she has written about, asking what plans exist to improve heatstroke awareness among the care home workforce and how the CQC will assess compliance.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the unjust prosecution of parents whose children with unmet SEND needs are absent, and asks for a review of the issue ahead of the education for all Bill with the aim of ending the practice.

deb_ex.sum: Argues the current moratorium is insufficient and calls on the Government to define fracking by intent rather than fluid volume, closing the legal loophole and enacting a full permanent ban in law.

deb_ex.t: The tremor that shook Lancashire, felt across the area at a magnitude of 2.9, came in the days after a stage that used just 142 cubic metres of fluid.

deb_ex.sum: Presses the inconsistency of opposing renewables while supporting fracking on countryside grounds, and calls for investment in clean energy including nuclear at Oldbury, urging the Minister to close the loophole.

deb_ex.t: Fracking will never shift a price set on global markets and it will never be worth the earthquakes, the polluted water and the broken trust it leaves behind.

deb_ex.sum: Warns that rumoured cuts to the DESNZ budget could undermine both critical energy infrastructure security and the government's ability to reduce household energy bills.

deb_ex.sum: Raises constituent cases of months-long delays in DWP responses, including an 18-month Child Maintenance Service failure, and calls for a ministerial statement on improving response rates.

deb_ex.t: I want to use this debate to call again for Ofcom to properly regulate the Royal Mail or be replaced.
deb_ex.sum: Argues Ofcom must be given proper powers to investigate local failures or be replaced by a new regulator, and presses the Minister to reveal what further measures the Government will take if Royal Mail does not improve.

deb_ex.t: the Prime Minister stated that if Royal Mail does not improve, further measures will be taken. Can the Minister now reveal what those measures are
deb_ex.sum: Argues regulation has not truly been tried properly yet and presses the Minister to reveal what serious consequences Royal Mail will face for continued failure.

deb_ex.sum: Uses a constituent's absurd experience of Capita accessing a shared spreadsheet to mock claims of technological improvement and questions whether Capita can ever safely deliver an AI-enabled service.

deb_ex.sum: Presses the Government to go further by allowing patients to hold small reserves of prescription medicines, and asks how access to essential medications will be guaranteed during widespread disruption.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights that whistleblowers often face unfair treatment after initially coming forward and presses the minister for stronger ongoing protections.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the government to go beyond containment and build a coalition to defeat the Houthis outright, arguing that Iran is directing their aggression to disrupt global shipping lanes.

deb_ex.t: Britain has a debt problem, Britain has a defence problem, Britain has a growth problem, and apparently, as we learned yesterday, there is nothing the Chancellor can do.
deb_ex.sum: Attacks the Budget as failing on defence, debt, growth and taxes, arguing it ducks every major challenge facing Britain.

deb_ex.t: If time allows, I will be very happy to go into great detail about our record on defence. When Russia invaded Ukraine, we were proud to stand with the people of Ukraine, and to reb
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Conservative record on defence and accuses the Chancellor of failing his own test by not properly funding armed forces in this Budget.

deb_ex.t: I should make some progress, and we have got plenty of time to talk about defence
deb_ex.sum: Deflects further intervention and signals intention to move on to other Budget issues.

deb_ex.t: No, no. I have a very good answer. In 2010, the Defence Secretary’s party wanted to reduce and cut further our armed forces. We were the party that will always stand behind our arm
deb_ex.sum: Asserts the Conservative Party opposed Labour cuts to armed forces in 2010 and has always stood behind them.

deb_ex.t: Let me make some progress, because this debate is about the whole Budget. There will be plenty of opportunities to talk about defence, which we can come back to. Let me give the Go
deb_ex.sum: Condemns the Budget for raising taxes, failing on welfare reform, running up debt and threatening living standards, calling it a missed opportunity.

deb_ex.t: The Labour Whips have clearly been doing their history lessons, but history lessons are not going to defend our country. The threat is real. The Defence Secretary is running around
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses Labour's history lesson as irrelevant and presses that the Chancellor failed his own test on defence funding.

deb_ex.t: Not properly funding our armed forces is not going to scare anyone in Moscow and it will not deter Tehran.
deb_ex.sum: Argues the failure to properly fund defence leaves Britain exposed and calls on the Chancellor to resign, accusing Labour of breaking promises to the armed forces.

deb_ex.t: I read that the Budget had the most measures in it of any Budget, but also that they were the most inconsequential. I will try to crack through a few other things. [ Interruption.
deb_ex.sum: Accuses the Government of handing money to trade unions, failing on welfare, raising taxes and presiding over falling living standards, calling the Budget historically inconsequential.

deb_ex.sum: Speaks as an NUJ group secretary and personal SLAPP victim to urge faster, broader legislation, welcoming Government engagement but pressing for swift action beyond the narrow 2023 Act provisions.

deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister to extend the disposal notification window to include community land trusts and housing co-ops so that homes in rural areas do not leak into the private sector and become second homes.

deb_ex.sum: Presses the speaker good-humouredly to actually name the pub he should have visited, noting the question was not yet answered.

deb_ex.sum: Celebrates his identity as a black British man with English roots, honours the contributions of those who came to the UK to work and serve, and notes he is the first black MP to represent a seat anywhere in the west midlands.

deb_ex.t: I say that because I do not want anyone else to have to say it
deb_ex.sum: Explains he raises his historic first not out of vanity but because he hopes no one will ever have to say it again about their own seat.

deb_ex.t: black history is British history. I am tired of people who should know better—some who sit in this House—who appear determined to tear our communities apart
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates black British history as inseparable from British history and attacks those who seek to divide communities along racial lines, drawing on his own mixed heritage and the contributions of post-war black Britons.

deb_ex.sum: Encourages local authorities and organisations such as the Staffordshire Black Business Network to engage in marking the 40th anniversary of Black History Month.

deb_ex.sum: Thanks the shadow Minister for her thoughtful speech and for highlighting a story that supports arguments made from the Government benches about black British history.

deb_ex.sum: Corrects the Minister on the name of his constituency and invites her to meet the Staffordshire Black Business Network in Newcastle-under-Lyme.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees with his colleague's point on ceramics and pushes back against narratives that young people are unwilling to work.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the need for sensible transport policy from the county council and criticises it for road closures and poor communication, noting 22 unhelpful letters from county hall.

deb_ex.sum: Argues the county council is failing to deliver services people pay for and calls on it to either fix roads properly or stand aside, before citing the King's Trust as an example of best practice.

deb_ex.sum: Praises the King's Trust, local jobs fairs, Keele University and Newcastle college's advanced manufacturing technical excellence college status, and calls for a mayoral strategic authority to unlock investment and jobs.

deb_ex.sum: Calls on the Minister to address rural employment, prioritise a mayoral authority over local government reorganisation, improve cross-departmental working and align skills provision with employer needs, welcoming existing investment but ask

deb_ex.sum: Urges the Minister to send Hansard to the Chancellor so that Staffordshire's case for skills and employment investment is reflected in the Budget speech.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms the government will do all necessary to protect the Falkland Islands and looks forward to commemorating the 45th anniversary of the conflict.

deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Minister for remarks on Nepal floods, then asks what work is being done across government to tackle online disinformation from bad state actors.

deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Prime Minister for visiting Harlow and asks him to condemn the Russian incident at Leipzig airport and express solidarity with Germany.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes government investment but urges that the charity and voluntary sector be properly funded and supported long-term rather than treated as a cheap alternative.

deb_ex.sum: Briefly intervenes to welcome work experience students in the Gallery, implicitly endorsing youth engagement with politics.

deb_ex.sum: Thanks NHS staff in Harlow, welcomes wave 2 new hospital programme inclusion for Princess Alexandra, but presses for emergency interim capital funding given the ageing estate.

deb_ex.sum: Shares good news about the Golden Valley development breaking ground, promising 12,000 cyber and tech jobs, and invites ministers to visit.

deb_ex.sum: Blames Conservative-negotiated Brexit for the EES queues, criticises the Government for diplomatic failures, and calls for an immediate Commission meeting and joining the single market and customs union.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights that asylum accommodation contract costs more than tripled and asks whether the incoming Prime Minister's stated ambition to activate break clauses will lead the Government to rip up the agreements.

deb_ex.t: Does the Home Secretary agree with her decision? What is the Home Office doing about the abuse and misinformation on X?
deb_ex.sum: Notes the Culture Secretary's departure from X over misinformation and abuse, and asks whether the Home Office agrees and will also leave the platform.

deb_ex.t: It is horrifying that three politicians have been murdered in this country in the past decade. Clearly, there is more work to be done.

deb_ex.sum: Interrupts the shadow Home Secretary to probe whether UK membership of the ECHR affects the ability to deport people to the countries he cited.

deb_ex.t: I was quite taken aback by the passion that the shadow Home Secretary showed for wiping out many decades of hard-won human rights that we all enjoy.
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the shadow Home Secretary for wanting to discard decades of hard-won human rights that protect everyone, not just asylum seekers, and corrects the claim that all rights are relative.

deb_ex.sum: Concludes the Bill is rhetoric over substance, will not stop small boats or cut accommodation costs, and calls for a proper EU asylum agreement instead.

deb_ex.t: I wonder whether the Secretary of State or a Minister can tell me why so many trains due to terminate at Cheltenham unexpectedly terminate at Gloucester?
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent frustration about Cheltenham trains unexpectedly terminating at Gloucester rather than their scheduled destination, asking Ministers for an explanation.

deb_ex.sum: Praises the doctors and donors behind a £17.5 million cancer centre appeal in Cheltenham and urges the Leader of the House and the local council to support the project.

deb_ex.t: The proposals are not the result that I wanted for my constituency or Gloucestershire. However, I am a reasonable man, and I am willing to take the Secretary of State at his word.
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the single unitary outcome for Gloucestershire but presses for assurance on financial sustainability from day one and asks whether the Golden Valley can be designated for retained council tax to keep the proceeds of growth locally.

deb_ex.sum: Warns that funding pressures may lead to overnight closure of Cheltenham West fire station, and asks the minister to help secure support for Gloucestershire's fire service.

deb_ex.t: is she in the business of overturning the political consensus across party locally in Gloucestershire? If not, will she just let us get on with it
deb_ex.sum: Questions whether the Secretary of State intends to overturn the cross-party local consensus in Gloucestershire, and urges her to let councils get on with delivering for residents.

deb_ex.sum: Lib Dem spokesperson questions why police had no advance intelligence and why no arrests were made, criticises Reform MPs for inflaming tensions, and calls for the UK to join EU migration and asylum pacts.

deb_ex.t: The Secretary of State’s mention of prevention was welcome: that means keeping people cool in their own homes. For those who live in a conservation area or a listed building, howev
deb_ex.sum: Argues that conservation area and listed building rules are preventing residents, especially older people and parents with young babies, from installing cooling measures, and calls on the Secretary of State to lead reform of planning rules.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the Golden Valley cyber-security development in Cheltenham and asks the government to extend the designated area so proceeds can be retained locally, and to restart stalled talks with local authorities.

deb_ex.sum: Argues that the EU asylum and migration pact meets the government's own stated goals and is cheaper than bilateral agreements, questioning why it is not being considered.

deb_ex.sum: Wilkinson welcomes the security review but presses for additional police funding around military bases, accelerated security measures at RAF Fairford, and asks what action is being taken against Iranian operatives.

deb_ex.t: What is the rate of women in the UK who report being sexually harassed in public?
deb_ex.sum: Probes the Conservative speaker's use of statistics by asking what the equivalent rate of sexual harassment in the UK is, implying the comparison may not be as stark as claimed.

deb_ex.t: I will indeed respect the amount of time for the third party, which I understand is 10 minutes.

deb_ex.sum: Rejects the ECHR withdrawal argument, argues leaving would not stop a single small boat crossing and would damage law enforcement co-operation, while criticising Conservatives for chasing Reform's agenda.

deb_ex.sum: Raises constituent concerns about the persecution of Christians in Nigeria and calls on the Church of England to do more in speaking out and providing solidarity globally.

deb_ex.t: stand-alone sixth-form colleges, which fall between the cracks of FE and sixth-forms in multi-academy trusts when it comes to capital funding
deb_ex.sum: Urges the Minister to release V-level qualification guidelines earlier, address the capital funding gap for standalone sixth-form colleges, and ensure bus routes serve college locations.

deb_ex.t: keeping artisan skills and abilities alive is proving difficult. May we have a debate in Government time about how we keep skills alive
deb_ex.sum: Highlights H & E Smith, a century-old tile manufacturer in his constituency, and asks for a debate on preserving skills in declining traditional manufacturing industries.

deb_ex.sum: Opens the debate by welcoming the £120 million government support package for ceramics, while noting ongoing work is needed to deploy the funding effectively.

deb_ex.t: we cannot make steel in this country without ceramics, so everything that the sector does contributes towards the greater good of UK plc.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the economic significance of the ceramics sector—20,000 jobs, £2 billion output, £600 million exports—and stresses its indispensable role in wider manufacturing.

deb_ex.t: I agree with my hon. Friend, who has been pursuing that for a long time. The ceramics industry is a great example of where procurement rules could be geared more towards supporting
deb_ex.sum: Calls for procurement rules to require Homes England-funded housebuilding to source bricks from British manufacturers, framing it as environmentally and economically sound.

deb_ex.t: There are many wonderful 10-minute rule Bills and private Members’ Bills that support the ceramics sector, and my hon. Friend’s back British bricks Bill is one of them. More to the
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the back British bricks Bill, highlights ceramics' role in defence, advanced manufacturing, biomedical and green technology, and presses for ceramics' full inclusion in the supercharger scheme.

deb_ex.t: it costs three times as much today to fire a product, whether it be a brick or a plate, as it did in 2019.
deb_ex.sum: Continues pressing for full ceramics inclusion in the supercharger scheme, explaining the structural unfairness whereby excluded energy-intensive firms subsidise those inside the scheme.

deb_ex.t: access to bus franchising, the adult skills agenda and spatial planning is the real victory that we look for
deb_ex.sum: Asks for clarity on when strategic authority decisions and mayoral elections will be made, so areas like Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent can access devolved powers on buses, skills and planning.

deb_ex.t: It is quite something to listen to a shadow Secretary of State whose party oversaw a net migration increase of 2.5 million in four years, and who has the brass neck to lecture the
deb_ex.sum: Attacks the shadow Home Secretary's credibility on immigration given his party's record of record net migration, accusing him of seeking social media clips.

deb_ex.t: Is the Leader of the House able to confirm what that SI is about? Will he give us hope that the IRGC will finally be banned tomorrow?
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Leader of the House to confirm that tomorrow's national security statutory instrument will proscribe the IRGC, arguing it is behind anti-Jewish hatred and is deeply destabilising.

deb_ex.t: can the Minister commit that once the independent inquiry has completed, the report is brought to the House so that we can discuss the outcome with the same prominence
deb_ex.sum: Asks what public education is planned to help consumers reduce demand during peak periods, and requests that the inquiry report be brought formally before the House once completed.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right about the malign influence. Following some of the attacks in Iran and the Iranian people seeking to change their leadership, he will have seen th
deb_ex.sum: Cites evidence that Iranian-linked X accounts promoting far-right and Scottish independence content went silent when Iran cut its domestic internet, urging the House to address state-backed bot operations in the UK.

deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that Iranian state-sponsored bot farms pump out political points to stimulate dissent rather than genuine discussion, amplifying the concern about foreign interference.

deb_ex.t: Longton station in my constituency was allocated money from the transforming cities fund to have a lift installed. Unfortunately, that money was reallocated by the city council tow
deb_ex.sum: Raises that funding for a lift at Longton station was reallocated by the city council to other projects, and asks for a departmental meeting to restore and protect funding for the lift.

deb_ex.t: I say to the Minister that we should never apologise for taking bold action that protects well-paid, unionised jobs in this country and is crucial to the reindustrialisation of our
deb_ex.sum: Snell backs the nationalisation and urges the Government to extend the range of steel grades produced domestically to supply manufacturers in his constituency who cannot currently source what they need.

deb_ex.t: why he did not use the opportunity to make some of the very small consequential changes to the southern boundary of places such as Stoke-on-Trent
deb_ex.sum: Broadly supports the Staffordshire proposals but presses the Secretary of State on why minor southern boundary adjustments were not made and raises concern that his constituents face a council tax rise rather than a cut.

deb_ex.t: I congratulate the Prime Minister and welcome him to his place. I also welcome what he said about serving British food across the public estate in this country, but may I push him
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the commitment to British food across the public estate and urges the Prime Minister to go further and faster on public procurement to benefit British industries and jobs.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges McVey's position by pointing out the inconsistency of allowing overseas citizens to vote by citizenship while denying the same right to 16-year-olds who live and contribute in the UK.

deb_ex.sum: Snell welcomes devolution ambitions but presses the Secretary of State for clarity on the timetable for mayoral combined authorities for Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent, where current opportunities fall short of local aspirations.

deb_ex.t: Not everything is about the south or the north. There is a swathe of counties that form a band of engineering and manufacturing prowess in this country
deb_ex.sum: Advocates for the midlands as overlooked in the north-south growth narrative and raises specific sector concerns around REACH regulation, steel tariffs and energy scheme access.

deb_ex.t: it is not fine for those who work shifts or who work a job that takes them out of their home. There is a structural barrier to lower-paid people
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that lengthy online queues disadvantage shift workers and lower-paid people, creating a structural barrier to arts and cultural access for working-class communities.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Home Secretary for her statement and recognise the dignified way in which she, as a woman of colour, carries out her duties in trying to help and support all of us, hav
deb_ex.sum: Snell praises the Home Secretary but presses for stronger state action against perpetrators of violence and extremism, arguing that protection of victims alone is insufficient.

deb_ex.t: he will know that it was introduced in 1986 under Mrs Thatcher. Did he think it was a spiteful tax when she introduced it?
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the shadow Chancellor by pointing out that the inheritance tax relief he criticises was introduced under Thatcher in 1986, asking whether he considered it spiteful then.

deb_ex.t: he failed to declare that one of the biggest beneficiaries of his policy would be JCB, which just happens to have given him £30,000 over the last year.
deb_ex.sum: Raises a point of order suggesting the shadow Chancellor should have declared a donation from JCB before speaking in favour of a policy that would benefit the company.

deb_ex.t: Under the Conservatives, about 1,400 migrants were living and dispersed in my city, but that number has fallen significantly under this Government.
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the motion's premise by noting migrant numbers in his city fell under this Government and questions the Conservatives' own record of engagement with affected communities.

deb_ex.sum: Asks whether asset recovery powers are sufficient to ensure crime does not pay and how they are currently being deployed.

deb_ex.sum: Accepts the energy security case but presses the Minister on gas-intensive industries such as ceramics that have no alternative to gas and have been excluded from industrial competitiveness schemes.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the union learning fund but urges the Minister to ensure adult reskilling keeps pace with technological change for Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent's ageing workforce.

deb_ex.sum: Calls on DWP to relax apprenticeship provider registration restrictions and the £100,000 subcontracting de minimis so more Stoke employers can take on apprentices.

deb_ex.t: could the hon. Gentleman set out by how much he thinks the minimum wage should be cut?
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the previous speaker to state explicitly by how much he thinks the minimum wage should be cut.

deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's record, reaffirms the pledge to reduce energy bills, highlights renewables as the quickest route, and points to warm home discount benefits in the questioner's own constituency.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees heat networks are vital to clean power targets, points to the green heat network fund already in operation, and commits to looking at further support.

deb_ex.t: we took an average of £150 off energy bills, which is now factored into our bills for years to come, and we have also expanded the warm home discount.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government action including the £150 reduction in energy bills at the last Budget and expansion of the warm home discount.

deb_ex.t: We are preparing for every contingency and looking at the support that may be required in the autumn and winter. The significant increase in the warm home discount has obviously be
deb_ex.sum: Assures that the government is preparing for autumn and winter contingencies and points to the significant increase in warm home discount recipients in the Member's constituency as evidence of action.

deb_ex.t: This is nonsense. That was set up by an arm’s length organisation set up by the previous Government. It is not something that the Government are funding. In so far as that refers t

deb_ex.t: They can already access grants through the warm homes plan, and they will soon be able to receive loans.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms constituents can already access warm homes plan grants and that loans will follow soon.

deb_ex.t: Every wind turbine we turn on and every solar panel that we deploy helps to push gas off as the price-setter.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that expanding renewable generation is the most effective way to decouple electricity prices from gas, noting that every new turbine or solar panel reduces gas's role as the price-setter.

deb_ex.t: My understanding is that just over £1 million of the £10 million in the fund has been distributed.
deb_ex.sum: Encourages more people to claim the heating oil support and notes that only just over £1 million of the £10 million fund has so far been distributed.

deb_ex.t: We are also undertaking the cost allocation review, which deals with those issues.
deb_ex.sum: Offers to share details of the schemes with the MP and points to the ongoing cost allocation review as the broader vehicle for addressing standing charge issues.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's three-part position: a commitment to ban shale gas fracking via legislation, distinction from low-volume hydraulic fracturing, and the case for clean energy over fossil fuels.

deb_ex.t: I agree with much of what the hon. Gentleman said. I would also say that we are not Pennsylvania or Texas; we are the United Kingdom, and we will operate on the basis of our nation
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies the technical distinction between high-volume shale gas fracking and low-volume hydraulic fracturing used in conventional operations and geothermal, emphasising the robust regulatory regime that applies.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for her question. In her introduction to the debate, the hon. Member for Thornbury and Yate raised the point about geothermal. The specific issues relating t
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the House there is no loophole allowing shale gas fracking to resume, reaffirms the moratorium, and confirms no new onshore licences will be issued.

deb_ex.t: Absolutely not. As I said a moment ago, we are not the United States; we are not Pennsylvania or Texas. It is a different energy market. There is nothing to suggest that the extrac
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the US gas price comparison as irrelevant to the UK market and reiterates that neither shale fracking nor additional North Sea extraction would reduce domestic energy costs.

deb_ex.t: That is a different argument to the one the hon. Member for Boston and Skegness was making. What is clear is that it will not directly reduce the cost of energy in this country. Re
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the government's evidence-based position: maintaining the fracking moratorium, ending new licences, and accelerating clean energy transition to protect jobs, consumers and climate commitments.

deb_ex.t: We took VAT off electricity bills from October and we took £150 out of costs last year.
deb_ex.sum: Minister highlights VAT removal from electricity bills, warm home discount, and ongoing work to decouple energy prices from gas as support for struggling households.

deb_ex.t: we are already providing air defence support to Saudi Arabia through the defence partnership.
deb_ex.sum: Minister reaffirms solidarity with Saudi Arabia and Yemen's recognised government, confirms air defence support is being provided, and commits to discuss Houthi proscription with Foreign Office officials.

deb_ex.t: It is our belief that that will help to drive down the cost of fuel.
deb_ex.sum: Minister points to fuel finder transparency measures and support for rural households via heating oil assistance and the boiler upgrade scheme rather than extending rural fuel duty relief.

deb_ex.t: More extraction of oil and gas from the North sea will not reduce prices for consumers across the country, and it will keep us hooked on volatile fossil fuels.
deb_ex.sum: Minister rejects calls for more North Sea extraction, arguing it will not lower consumer prices and would keep the UK dependent on volatile fossil fuels, reaffirming the shift to renewables.

deb_ex.t: We have already had about £100 billion of investment into renewable energy in the UK since 2024.
deb_ex.sum: Minister highlights £100 billion of renewable investment since 2024 as evidence of the government's commitment to reducing dependence on foreign energy sources.

deb_ex.t: our priority is having free flow through the strait of Hormuz, and that is what we have been working on with our allies and partners globally.
deb_ex.sum: Minister reassures the House that free flow through the strait is the priority, confirms air defence support to Saudi Arabia, and declines to comment on detailed operational matters.

deb_ex.t: Fuel supplies to the UK have remained resilient since the start of the conflict. As people across the country would expect, the Government will mitigate where possible the potential impacts
deb_ex.sum: Minister condemns the Houthi attack, outlines the pipeline closure situation, reassures that UK fuel supplies remain resilient, and sets out government plans for contingency planning and supporting households.

deb_ex.t: I will endeavour to answer all the hon. Gentleman’s questions, but if there are any that I do not answer, I will follow up on them in writing. Let me begin with the discussions tha
deb_ex.sum: Minister details diplomatic engagement with Saudi Arabia, reassures on UK energy supply resilience, defends the warm homes plan funding and heating oil support, and argues the UK must move away from fossil fuel dependency.

deb_ex.sum: Minister agrees that the crisis reinforces the case for clean power and domestic renewables to control both price and supply, and accepts the invitation to visit the constituency.

deb_ex.t: We will not rush this process; we will do things properly in order to ensure the best outcome for people across the country, including workers in the North sea.
deb_ex.sum: Minister confirms diplomatic engagement with Saudi Arabia, defends the quasi-judicial process on Jackdaw and Rosebank, blames the previous government for the judicial review, and reaffirms oil and gas will remain part of the energy mix.

deb_ex.t: the purpose of that mission is to ensure that we have renewable sources of generation, so that we control the supply and the price of energy
deb_ex.sum: Minister praises Vince's constituency advocacy, points to the clean power mission and renewable generation as the answer, and highlights the VAT removal from electricity bills and the £150 energy cost reduction already announced.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Father of the House for his question. We are still extracting oil and gas from the North sea. We have a supply coming from the North sea every day. We have that energy
deb_ex.sum: Minister confirms ongoing North Sea extraction, agrees oil and gas will remain part of the energy mix, but stresses the basin is in long-term decline and a responsible government must invest in the renewables transition.

deb_ex.t: It is important that we have a diverse energy mix across the country, including renewables, so that we in this country have the most secure and resilient supply of energy.
deb_ex.sum: Minister explains that site choices are a national decision for NESO and Ofgem, and reaffirms the importance of a diverse energy mix for resilient supply.

deb_ex.t: Let me take that in two parts. First, this is obviously a decision that has to be taken carefully. The Secretary of State has to a make an assessment and a judgment. The hon. Membe
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends the careful decision-making process on Jackdaw and Rosebank, reiterates that North Sea extraction continues and will do so for decades, and reaffirms the transition planning.

deb_ex.t: The CMA raised concerns, though, about the impact of a potential price cap. This market does not operate in the same way as the traditional gas and electricity market.
deb_ex.sum: Minister points to the CMA report on heating oil, acknowledges the market is not working properly, notes complexity around a simple price cap, and promises a government response to CMA recommendations shortly.

deb_ex.t: As I said in response to previous questions, we are exploiting the resources in the North sea; we are extracting oil and gas from it. We will make a decision on Rosebank and Jackda
deb_ex.sum: Minister confirms ongoing North Sea extraction, states decisions on Rosebank and Jackdaw will come in due course, and argues that investment in renewables is essential alongside oil and gas for energy and national security.

deb_ex.t: I always enjoy it when Reform use “socialist” like it is a bad word and not a badge of honour. As I have said in response to previous questions, we are using the resources from the
deb_ex.sum: Minister dismisses Tice's ideological attack with light humour and reaffirms that North Sea oil and gas extraction is ongoing and will remain part of the energy mix for years to come.

deb_ex.t: I was not expecting to have an ideological debate on a Tuesday afternoon. I have said, and I repeat again, that we are using the resources from North sea oil and gas and we will co
deb_ex.sum: Minister rejects the ideological framing, reaffirms continued North Sea production, and warns that abandoning renewables in favour of oil and gas alone would be a road to nowhere for energy and national security.

deb_ex.t: The warm homes plan will ensure that cooling measures, as well as heating measures, are available for the most vulnerable homes.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms that the warm homes plan will cover cooling as well as heating measures, and highlights the expanded boiler upgrade scheme now including air-to-air heat pumps.

deb_ex.t: I can give the hon. Gentleman that assurance. He will know that we are currently reviewing part O of the Building Regulations on overheating in order to ensure that, in the future,
deb_ex.sum: Gives the requested assurance and notes the government is reviewing building regulations on overheating to ensure buildings can adapt to future climate conditions.

deb_ex.t: I will be meeting the relevant bodies soon, and we hope to be able to unlock this at pace.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the hon. Member for his collaborative pressure on accreditation bodies and confirms the Minister will be meeting them soon to unlock progress.

deb_ex.t: We fully support the warm homes plan and the boiler upgrade scheme. We have had a record-breaking year on the boiler upgrade scheme, with over 8,000 applications in July, which is
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms full government support for the warm homes plan and boiler upgrade scheme, citing record application numbers and continued expected uptake.

deb_ex.t: The warm homes plan is already delivering in communities across our country, and last month the Secretary of State announced the devolution of that plan. Giving power to local lead
