deb_ex.t: no individual can ever again be released unless the very next day they are being deported from this country
deb_ex.sum: Calls for a law change ensuring that convicted offenders are deported immediately upon release, arguing some crimes forfeit the right to legal protections.

deb_ex.t: money and corruption always find a way. Would it not be better to have an overall cap for all donations, foreign or domestic?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the statement but expresses concern that money and corruption will always find workarounds, and asks the minister to consider an overall cap on all donations, domestic as well as foreign.

deb_ex.t: it is important not just that the hotels are reduced, but that the dispersal accommodation that has overburdened communities, like mine in Hartlepool, is also reduced
deb_ex.sum: Backs the Bill wholeheartedly but presses the Home Secretary to also reduce dispersal accommodation that has overburdened communities like his in Hartlepool.

deb_ex.t: will he now commit to attacking the problem and replacing the hated council tax system that hammers towns like mine?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the PM's criticism of council tax as regressive and presses him to go further by committing to replace the system, citing Hartlepool's band D rate of £2,556 versus Westminster's £1,048.

deb_ex.t: That was 6,780 days ago—more than 18 and a half years—and yet he remains in prison.
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent's case of 18 and a half years in prison on a one-year-and-126-day IPP tariff and presses the Justice Secretary to ensure a fair, transparent and rehabilitative route to release.

deb_ex.t: The lawlessness that we are seeing in certain parts of our communities did not happen overnight. It is the consequence of systemic underfunding of our police and our fire service.
deb_ex.sum: Pays personal tribute to PC Blades, links the lawlessness to systemic underfunding, and calls for a long-term funding formula fix for both police and fire services.

deb_ex.t: Will the Minister take the message back to her Department that we must approve Jackdaw and Rosebank and go further to expand drilling in the North sea
deb_ex.sum: Calls explicitly for approval of both Jackdaw and Rosebank and urges the Minister to take back to the Department a message to expand North Sea drilling further.

deb_ex.t: rebuilding strong, trusted local government must be central to rebuilding trust in politics
deb_ex.sum: Brash urges that rebuilding trusted local government be central to restoring faith in politics, and asks for a meeting to discuss simplifying high-street rental auctions for councils like Hartlepool.

deb_ex.t: the Falkland Islands will remain British
deb_ex.sum: Argues that whatever positions Trump or Argentina take, they make no difference because the Falkland Islands will remain British.

deb_ex.t: Like parents and grandparents in Hartlepool, I find it incredible that technology companies even had to be asked to put software in place that protected against child sexual abuse.
deb_ex.sum: Expresses disbelief that tech companies had to be asked and refused, and argues the Government should assume their moral bankruptcy and legislate immediately rather than asking.

deb_ex.t: Politics is ultimately about confidence. Leaders cannot lead without the confidence of their party, a Government cannot govern without the confidence of this House, and legislation
deb_ex.sum: Conditionally supports the carry-over but warns the Bill still lacks veterans' confidence, and signals he will withdraw support if veterans in his constituency cannot make their views heard before the Bill proceeds.

deb_ex.t: is it not also incumbent on our local councils to do the exact same thing in order to honour our veterans who receive military compensation?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the national campaign but also calls on local councils to disregard military compensation in locally administered benefits, citing his own motion in Hartlepool as a model.

deb_ex.t: What steps he is taking to help increase investment in jobs and skills in the defence sector in the north-east.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the minister what steps are being taken to increase investment in jobs and skills in the defence sector in the north-east.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the investment outlined by the Minister, but as a north-east MP, I always want to see more.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the investment but calls for more support to help north-east SMEs navigate defence procurement, and requests a ministerial meeting about Steel Benders UK in Hartlepool.

deb_ex.t: New drilling in the North sea is good for energy security, national security and jobs, including jobs in my constituency of Hartlepool and in the supply chain.
deb_ex.sum: Warmly welcomes the Jackdaw decision for its benefits to energy security, national security and jobs including in Hartlepool, and criticises populist politicians for prioritising ideology over facts.

deb_ex.t: Kevin Brown committed eight burglaries in Hartlepool, targeting businesses and charities like Alice House hospice and Cornerstone homelessness charity. The court handed him a suspended sentence.
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituency case of a repeat burglar who received only a suspended sentence, and calls on the Minister to build more prison places so such individuals are locked up.

deb_ex.sum: Presents a 15,000-signature petition calling for maternity services to be reinstated at North Devon District Hospital and urging the government to improve staffing, local resilience, and prevent emergency suspensions.

deb_ex.sum: Argues the diversion to Exeter is dangerous given the distance and road quality, questions the trust's definition of birth incidents, and calls for honest data from the Minister.

deb_ex.sum: Calls for Ofcom to be given stronger enforcement powers and presses the Minister with specific questions on enforcement capability, postcode-level performance data, staffing accountability and consumer remedies.

deb_ex.sum: Marks the funeral of Sir Billy Boston, rugby league's first knight, and asks the Leader of the House to join in paying tribute and sending condolences to his family.

deb_ex.t: will he at least commit to kicking off a national commission on electoral reform?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Prime Minister's support for political reform but presses for a specific commitment, either to change the voting system before the next election or to launch a national commission.

deb_ex.t: not a penny of this grant should reach him. Neither should any other taxpayer funding, and that has to include what happens at the end of his life
deb_ex.sum: Supports the grant's purpose and the planned reduction but calls for stronger transparency and reporting requirements, and explicitly demands confirmation that no public money will fund any ceremonial honours for Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

deb_ex.t: devolution cannot simply mean transferring responsibilities from Whitehall without the funding necessary to deliver them
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes devolution in principle but presses for councils to get proper funding alongside powers, calls for stronger national resilience preparedness, digital sovereignty, and further electoral reform including donation caps and fairer voti

deb_ex.t: attempting to legislate for linguistic purity in a language that, for over a millennium, has borrowed vocabulary ad hoc from other languages
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the shadow minister's proposal to restrict campaign material to British languages by pointing out the irony that English itself borrows extensively from other languages, including words used in the Bill itself.

deb_ex.t: big money is infiltrating our politics, with millions of pounds paid to politicians, uncapped donations and direct payments for inflammatory social media posts. It is totally disfiguring our politics.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill as a step forward but argues it does not go far enough on big money in politics, calling for a royal commission on donation caps and tighter restrictions on foreign-linked donations.

deb_ex.t: Until this House finds the courage to give people a Parliament that actually reflects how they vote, we will not have restored trust in our democracy.
deb_ex.sum: Expresses frustration that proportional representation is out of scope, argues fairer votes are essential to restoring trust in democracy, and says the Liberal Democrats will support the Bill only as a first step.

deb_ex.t: It is welcome that the Government have asked the Electoral Commission to look at spending limits. I love a task-and-finish group almost as much as I love a taskforce or a sub-commi
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Electoral Commission review of spending limits but presses the Minister for concrete timing on donation caps and whether reforms will be in place before the next general election.

deb_ex.t: I look forward to seeing how our noble friends in the other place can make it even stronger.
deb_ex.sum: Announces Liberal Democrat support for the Bill while highlighting its imperfections and calling for further work on donation limits and proportional representation.

deb_ex.t: One of the many horrifying things when considering online safety is the number of abuse perpetrators who themselves are children.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights cases where children are perpetrators as well as victims, citing a local example of a nudifying app, and asks what is being done with the DfE to support schools and families.

deb_ex.t: I must confess that I am a little frustrated, because I think this is the third time that the ventilation system at Stepping Hill hospital has been announced by a Minister—and it i
deb_ex.sum: Expresses frustration that ventilation funding for Stepping Hill has been announced before without new money, points to a £138 million repairs backlog, and invites the Secretary of State to visit the hospital.

deb_ex.t: when an MP is financially rewarded by an algorithm for their political output, it crosses the line into financial influence
deb_ex.sum: Argues current lobbying laws are too narrow, citing MPs earning large sums from X posts as a financial influence loophole, and calls for updated ethics and lobbying rules.

deb_ex.t: Last week, Channel 4 showed senior figures from Reform UK discussing how money from an American donor could reach the party through his UK-based son. Do the Government agree that c
deb_ex.sum: Raises Channel 4 reporting on Reform UK and overseas finance, argues the Representation of the People Bill does not go far enough and calls for a cap on all political donations.

deb_ex.t: self-employed adopters are not eligible for the support for which birth parents and employed adopters are eligible. Is his review looking at closing that gap
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether the ongoing parental leave and pay review will close the gap that leaves self-employed adopters ineligible for support available to birth parents and employed adopters.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the Home Secretary’s announcement of the independent review of protective security provided by the state to those in public life. The statement mentions former MPs and pa
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the review and extension of Operation Ford to councillors but argues the operation is inconsistent and asks how the Government plans to strengthen it so elected councillors receive the protection they deserve.

deb_ex.t: may I encourage him to look at a cap on political donations to limit the influence of ultra-wealthy individuals and potential foreign interests?
deb_ex.sum: Raises concerns about foreign interference in elections and asks the PM to review campaign finance rules, including introducing a cap on political donations to limit ultra-wealthy and foreign influence.

deb_ex.t: It cannot be acceptable in 2026 that someone who holds the confidence of this House should be barred from part of their job because of their faith.
deb_ex.sum: Liberal Democrats support the Bill as a necessary modernisation removing anti-Catholic and antisemitic restrictions, but urge the Government to go further on broader constitutional and democratic reform.

deb_ex.t: I encourage the Government to go further, faster—an encouragement that the Liberal Democrats always give when they are on their feet talking about political and constitutional reform.
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms Lib Dem support for the Bill but presses the Government to treat it as a starting point and go further faster on wider political and constitutional reform.

deb_ex.t: Will she confirm if that is new, new money, or if it is money that has already been allocated to our schools, or already allocated to tackling antisemitism?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the review but presses the Secretary of State on the role of school governors and asks whether funding announced is genuinely new money or already allocated.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Minister for advance sight of her statement and for the briefing last week. Since the last ministerial statement in July, Capita is reported to have met its own Septemb
deb_ex.sum: Lib Dem spokesperson highlights a constituent quoted £14,000 less than expected after 14 months, presses for clearer accountability, debarment consideration, and inflation-linking of outstanding payments.

deb_ex.t: What recent discussions he has had with European allies on tackling foreign interference in democratic processes internationally.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Foreign Secretary what recent discussions he has had with European allies on tackling foreign interference in democratic processes.

deb_ex.t: I am grateful to the Foreign Secretary for those remarks, but with Russian-linked interference operations continuing to target democratic elections across Europe, does he feel that
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Foreign Secretary's remarks but presses him on whether current arrangements are sufficient and urges full UK involvement in the European democracy shield and proposed European centre for democratic resilience.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Minister for advance sight of his statement. Let me place on record our thanks to the emergency services, volunteers and communities who respond to civil emergencies, b
deb_ex.sum: Lib Dem spokesperson welcomes the campaign but pushes for a formal civil volunteer reserve, better maintenance of the priority services register, coordination with utility companies, and a digital sovereignty strategy to address cyber threa

deb_ex.t: We know that more can be done on transparency around lobbying and will present our response to Parliament in due course.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the commission's work, acknowledges more transparency is needed on lobbying, and promises a parliamentary response in due course.

deb_ex.t: We certainly recognise that the current system of transparency around lobbying does not have widespread support; it is not good enough.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the current lobbying transparency system is inadequate and commits to carefully considering legislative reform in response to the commission's report.

deb_ex.t: We will, of course, consider that in the response to the EIC.
deb_ex.sum: Warmly acknowledges the question from the hon. Member for Strangford and commits to considering Northern Ireland in the government's response to the commission.

deb_ex.t: I take very seriously, as I am sure Members across the House do, the issues of outside earnings by Members, and particularly potential undue influence.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to consider outside earnings and undue influence as part of the commission response, and shares concerns about financial influence via social media platforms.

deb_ex.t: all critical decisions should be taken by Ministers who are directly accountable to Parliament and the public.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress: all 306 arm's length bodies reviewed, reform commitments for over a third, with a policy of devolution by default to increase democratic accountability.

deb_ex.t: devolution by default means restoring powers to where they should be, with democratic accountability.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's review, reiterating that 306 bodies are covered and over a third are being reformed, and argues the devolution by default approach restores democratic accountability.

deb_ex.t: I was pleased that the Federation of Small Businesses welcomed our social value changes over the summer.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government action on SME procurement including ambitious spend targets, strengthened late payment policy, and raised social value thresholds, noting FSB approval.

deb_ex.t: I would be more than happy to meet him to discuss how, as we develop this agenda, we can make it work for communities like ours.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the hon. Member's local campaigning and offers a meeting to discuss how the procurement agenda can be tailored to benefit communities like his.

deb_ex.t: I commend my hon. Friend for his remarkable stamina over the summer, with more than 80 visits across his constituency—the largest in England. He is certainly a passionate campaigne
deb_ex.sum: Praises the MP's constituency engagement, outlines social value procurement reforms aimed at local food production and accepts the invitation to visit a local farm.

deb_ex.t: I am of course happy to meet him to discuss the issue further.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the MP's campaigning for British bus manufacturing and agrees to meet to discuss raising social value procurement requirements further.

deb_ex.t: I assure her of the seriousness with which we take that issue and broader procurement issues, and I would be happy to meet her
deb_ex.sum: Ferguson affirms the seriousness with which the government treats procurement issues and offers to meet the MP to discuss the specific case.

deb_ex.t: We are committed, and the Cabinet Secretary is committed, to conducting a full review of the civil service.
deb_ex.sum: Ferguson defends the ongoing civil service review as committed and serious, noting that decisions on powers ultimately rest with the Prime Minister.

deb_ex.t: Its purpose is to remove the restrictions that prevent a person who professes either the Roman Catholic or Jewish faiths from advising the sovereign on Church appointments.
deb_ex.sum: Explains the operative effect of both clauses, noting the Bill removes restrictions preventing Roman Catholics and Jews from advising on or making Church appointments, and that it commands broad consensus.

deb_ex.t: this is a narrowly focused Bill without knock-on consequences. The temporary arrangement in respect of the Lord Chancellor will be brought to an end once this Bill has been passed
deb_ex.sum: Closes the debate by welcoming cross-party support, affirming the Bill is narrowly focused with no wider constitutional consequences, and confirming temporary Lord Chancellor arrangements will end once the Bill passes.

deb_ex.t: We have been trapped in a vicious economic circle for decades, and that vicious circle is underpinned by our dependence on fossil fuels, which means lower growth, higher inflation
our affordability and security crises are intertwined, and that they lean on each other
deb_ex.sum: Argues that the Iran war demonstrates the link between energy security and domestic affordability, and calls for investment in clean energy and good jobs to make Britain more resilient and united.

deb_ex.t: Iran struck a tanker, and that led to the end of the ceasefire.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms condemnation of Iran, notes it struck a tanker ending the ceasefire, and appeals for cross-party unity to meet the current crisis.

deb_ex.t: we have to tell the public both that war is on our doorstep and that resilience is now far more important
deb_ex.sum: Argues the public are increasingly aware of security threats and sets out a two-track policy of making life affordable and defending the nation, including investment in clean energy.

deb_ex.t: there is a clear commitment on the Labour Benches to fund the defence investment plan
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's commitment to fund the defence investment plan and argues the defence economic strategy must also focus on scaling up industrial capacity for conflict.

deb_ex.t: A House divided against itself cannot stand, and nor can our nation.
deb_ex.sum: Expresses confidence in funding the defence plan and warns against members of the House who seek to divide the country and weaken it, calling for unity to meet the moment.

deb_ex.t: In areas such as mine in the east midlands, growth has been too low because spending has been too low.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that low spending has caused low growth in east midlands areas like Loughborough, and asks the Minister to explain how making life affordable will raise growth locally and nationally.

deb_ex.t: Residents in Gardner Way in my constituency are stuck. They are subject to an Act from 1925 and a rent charge that makes it incredibly difficult for them to sell their homes, becau
deb_ex.sum: Raises constituents trapped by a 1925 rent charge that risks repossession and prevents home sales, urging the owner to allow a deed change and asking for confirmation that planned legislation will address the practice.

deb_ex.t: we are making a choice to use some of that money to help cut bills for people in our constituencies across our country.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Budget as reflecting Labour's founding values of shared prosperity, contrasting it with Conservative and Reform approaches, and argues windfall taxes on banks and oil companies are fair and effective.

deb_ex.t: What steps her Department is taking to help tackle violence against women and girls.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the Department is taking to tackle violence against women and girls.

deb_ex.t: only 3% of reported rape cases ever make it to trial, and of the few who ever get their day in court after distressing delays, just 53% see a conviction.
deb_ex.sum: Raises the dire rape prosecution statistics in Sussex, highlights low conviction rates and stalled progress on Operation Soteria, and presses the Minister for specific action to improve investigation and prosecution of rape cases there.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Liberal Democrat position opposing military escalation, calling for diplomacy to return the US and Iran to the negotiating table, and urging the Government to protect shipping and reduce household energy costs.

deb_ex.sum: Argues a diplomatic settlement is the only way to sustainably protect shipping, and calls for concrete domestic measures such as cutting fuel duty and investing in energy resilience to ease household costs.

deb_ex.t: No British national should be used as a bargaining chip in a geopolitical stand-off.
deb_ex.sum: Asserts all proposals are fully costed and raises the case of British nationals Lindsay and Craig Foreman detained in Evin prison, calling for urgent diplomatic action to secure their release.

deb_ex.sum: Liberal Democrats support the regulations but note they are overdue, and press the Minister on resources for enforcement, prosecution of offenders, protection of at-risk communities, and the need for a wider counter-disinformation strategy.

deb_ex.t: The European Union and the United States have taken steps to sanction Mr Ivanishvili. When will the UK Government follow suit?
deb_ex.sum: Notes EU and US sanctions on Georgian oligarch Bidzina Ivanishvili following arrests of protesters and calls on the UK Government to follow suit.

deb_ex.sum: Asks the Secretary of State to clarify whether the East Sussex boundary discussion will be reopened as part of the review, referencing constituents' concerns about Brighton and Hove's proposed expansion.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the air defence pledge but presses for more NATO coordination on interceptors, criticises the pace of defence spending increases, promotes Liberal Democrat defence bonds, and calls for tougher sanctions on Russian fossil fuels.

deb_ex.sum: Argues the Government lacks a serious national framework for civilian resilience and proposes a dedicated civil defence office and volunteer reserve covering cyber-security and emergency response, citing Finland as a model.

deb_ex.t: can the Defence Secretary explain to me and the people of Portsmouth why he is considering handing operation of this critical sovereign capability to the US?
deb_ex.sum: Raises concerns about US interference in allied military satellite communications via Starshield and challenges the government over reports it is considering a US bid to operate Skynet, risking sovereign capability and jobs in Portsmouth.

deb_ex.sum: Proposes expanding cadet and reserve forces into a voluntary civilian resilience strand covering cyber-defence and emergency response, and calls for a new civil defence office.

deb_ex.sum: Supports the defensive RAF assistance but presses the minister on the expected duration, safeguards against prolonged involvement, and diplomatic efforts to maintain freedom of navigation through the Bab al-Mandab strait.

deb_ex.t: No Government can meet a 1,000-day deadline on a funding plan that does not exist. That is why we Liberal Democrats have proposed defence bonds.
deb_ex.sum: Argues the government's 3% defence target cannot be met without funding decided now, and proposes defence bonds to raise £20 billion within the Defence Secretary's own 1,000-day deadline.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Foreign Secretary's earlier 4% figure as inclusive of non-core spending, acknowledges Europe's reliance on the US, and presses her to concede that further defence increases will be needed.

deb_ex.t: if energy costs in particular stay as they are, there are future disasters ahead
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Lords amendments and the prospect of job security for Scunthorpe constituents, but flags that uncompetitive energy costs remain a serious ongoing threat to steel and heavy industry.

deb_ex.sum: Uses the Minister's visit to Immingham to press for a direct train service from King's Cross to his constituency and invites the Minister to join his campaign.

deb_ex.t: will he acknowledge that energy costs must be dealt with before that investment will follow?
deb_ex.sum: Vickers expresses no ideological objection to nationalisation but argues it is only a short-to-medium-term fix and presses the Minister to acknowledge that energy costs must be resolved before private investment will follow.

deb_ex.t: parks need support from our local authorities, and it is important that sufficient resources are made available.
deb_ex.sum: Congratulates two parks in his constituency on green flag awards and calls for a statement on local government finance to ensure sufficient resources for parks and community facilities.

deb_ex.sum: Raises a concern from Gibraltar's opposition leader about future constitutional changes and asks for a guarantee that Gibraltarians will have the final say on any such changes.

deb_ex.t: If NHS England proceeds to break up our current footprint, it will directly undermine the viability of Scunthorpe and Grimsby general hospitals.
deb_ex.sum: Raises concerns about NHS England's proposed integrated care board boundary changes in the Humber region, arguing they will undermine Scunthorpe and Grimsby hospitals and harm 300,000 patients.

deb_ex.t: Grimsby and Cleethorpes comprise one of the largest urban areas in the entire country that does not have a direct link to our capital city.
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Government to restore direct train services from Grimsby and Cleethorpes to London, arguing Ministers could do so simply by signing an order.

deb_ex.t: If the Prime Minister could give us an early win, it would be a victory for me in 15 years but he could deliver it in 15 weeks.
deb_ex.sum: Uses humour to press the PM for an early win on restoring a direct London to northern Lincolnshire rail service after fifteen years of campaigning.

deb_ex.t: could he give an assurance that he will look at the case and do all he can to ensure that this individual is not released
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent's case where a convicted knife attacker facing a new rape charge received a letter saying he would be released, and asks the Lord Chancellor to intervene.

deb_ex.t: As we heard a short while ago from the Father of the House, my right hon. Friend the Member for Gainsborough (Sir Edward Leigh), Lincolnshire county council welcomes the review, bu
deb_ex.sum: Reports cross-party and council-leader support for the status quo in north Lincolnshire's two unitaries and urges the Secretary of State to take an early decision to preserve it.

deb_ex.t: the decision to allow doctors to help bring about the death of a human being crosses a major moral threshold
deb_ex.sum: Opposes the Bill on the grounds that it lacks sufficient safeguards, drawing on personal experience of his parents' deaths and the palliative care his father received. Argues the Bill would lessen the value society places on human life.

deb_ex.t: moves to legislate for assisted dying would be yet another step that lessens the value that we as a society place on human life
deb_ex.sum: Uses his mother's death to reinforce the value of hospice care, and argues the Bill lacks necessary safeguards and would diminish the value society places on human life.

deb_ex.t: if assisted dying is legalised, we will be poorer as a society. We will have crossed a line.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that legalising assisted dying would make society poorer, cross a fundamental line and undermine the doctor-patient relationship by introducing doubt about whether a clinician is wholly committed to preserving life.

deb_ex.sum: Flags his attendance at the British Steel development board in Scunthorpe and asks the Secretary of State for any positive news to pass on.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the danger of pavement parking to guide dog users and disabled people, notes the Government's view that further legislation is needed, and asks for a ministerial statement ensuring local authorities have resources to act.

deb_ex.sum: Supports the Bill and the principle that the Prime Minister of any faith should have an input into senior Church of England appointments.

deb_ex.sum: Raises a pilot scheme fitting air filters in classrooms with reported health benefits and potential cost savings, and asks for a debate or ministerial statement on the Government's position.

deb_ex.sum: Asks for assurance that any EU reset will not undermine the operation of the Humber freeport established as a Brexit benefit.

deb_ex.sum: Praises local hospices and Hospice UK research showing modest extra funding could save NHS money, and requests a debate on the hospice movement's financial case.

deb_ex.sum: Asks whether the Government have plans for modest electrification linking seaports such as Immingham to the main line to improve rail freight distribution.

deb_ex.sum: Notes that both unitary authorities and all four local MPs in North Lincolnshire and North East Lincolnshire support the status quo, and questions why the Minister is prolonging uncertainty after his predecessor's assurance.

deb_ex.t: the use by the IDF of artificial intelligence machine guns, which are trained on people using sponge-tipped bullets and tear gas, is a way of dehumanising Palestinian people
deb_ex.sum: Urges action against IDF use of AI-guided weapons in civilian spaces, arguing it is a deliberate strategy to dehumanise Palestinians and force them from their homes.

deb_ex.t: If it is good enough for other countries, and if it is now good enough for the EU, it should definitely be good enough for the UK
deb_ex.sum: Points to the EU's consideration of a trade ban as evidence that if it is good enough for European partners it should be good enough for the UK.

deb_ex.t: a Labour MP has undermined the four councils against the will of the councils, which have been democratically elected, and without discussing it with any of the MPs
deb_ex.sum: Raises a rumour that a Labour MP acted against the wishes of four democratically elected councils to block a Wessex combined authority, and asks the Minister to deny it.

deb_ex.t: Will she pause any new approvals until their impact beyond 2050 has been fully assessed, and done so in the light of the seventh carbon budget?
deb_ex.sum: Liberal Democrat MP raises a specific incinerator proposal in her constituency that draws waste from outside the local area and asks the Minister to pause new approvals pending assessment against the seventh carbon budget.

deb_ex.t: the Ministry of Defence is in the High Court, fighting for them not to have rights under the duty of candour
deb_ex.sum: Raises the Chinook crash victims' family, noting the MoD is in the High Court resisting duty of candour rights, and urges the Minister to intervene and ensure full public investigation.

deb_ex.t: an insufficient provision of safety measures poses a daily risk to all pedestrians, including the hundreds of school children who traverse this road
deb_ex.sum: Presents a constituent-led petition calling for a pedestrian crossing and refuge on Wimborne Road near Knobcrook Bridge, citing risks to schoolchildren, elderly residents and the wider community.

deb_ex.t: Dunyeats Road in my constituency is suffering from multiple issues that are causing people and traffic to collide. Will she consider allowing councils to bring forward those crossings?
deb_ex.sum: Notes that side road zebra crossings are already permitted in Manchester, London and Wales but not the rest of England, and urges the Secretary of State to allow councils to introduce them.

deb_ex.t: for young carers summer can be more like groundhog day, as children as young as five have to support their family.
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to young carers and advocacy organisations, highlights her young carers champion Bill, and asks for a Government-time debate on better support ahead of the autumn education Bill.

deb_ex.t: Will the FCDO work with Cabinet colleagues to ensure that the public are educated, and will it consider funding a national programme of public information
deb_ex.sum: Calls for public education on climate change and asks whether the FCDO will fund a national public information programme to build trust in climate data.

deb_ex.t: We have had the hottest summer on record, and we have had an exceptionally high number of tragic deaths in the rivers and seas around the country. At the same time, so many childre
deb_ex.sum: Slade links tragic drowning deaths to pool closures and calls on the PM to fund leisure centres so every child can learn to swim.

deb_ex.t: When the Justice Committee visited a young offenders institute earlier this year, we found that most of the young people were not able to access even a minimal amount of education
deb_ex.sum: Slade draws on the Justice Committee's visit to a young offenders institute to highlight that lack of education and training increases reoffending, and asks what the Lord Chancellor is doing to improve access.

deb_ex.t: it is the structure of business rates that is causing the decline of our high streets and the decimation of our hospitality sector
deb_ex.sum: Seeks clarification on devolved business rates retention, warning that simply allowing councils to cut rates shifts the financial burden from businesses to statutory services.

deb_ex.t: Wareham is fortunate to be served by the fantastic Rex cinema, which is Dorset’s oldest cinema and one of the oldest in the country, and it is volunteer led. It shows two films eve
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the plight of a historic volunteer-run cinema needing £400,000 for roof repairs and asks the Minister to extend cultural capital grants to community cinemas.

deb_ex.t: We need a review of this huge housing target, so that it is based on need in the local community, with a requirement for the infrastructure to come first.
deb_ex.sum: Describes communities in Dorset doubling in size without roads, GPs or water treatment, with new homes lying empty and unaffordable; calls for a review of housing targets based on local need with infrastructure delivered first.

deb_ex.t: What additional measures are being considered to make sure we do not end up with a two-tier system between those with an HRA and those without?
deb_ex.sum: Raises the problem facing councils like Dorset that have no HRA because they sold their stock, warning of a two-tier system and asking what measures will prevent it.

deb_ex.t: What message does it send to our brave RNLI rescue crews if the police stand aside during these events while they put their lives at risk day and night?
deb_ex.sum: Raises repeated targeting of the RNLI in Poole by far-right groups and questions what message is sent to rescue crews when protesters cause injuries and criminal damage without arrest.

deb_ex.t: In Dorset, we have lost 44 dentists in the last five years, and there has not been a single new contract for 10 years
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that Dorset has lost 44 dentists in five years with no new contracts, and asks whether better reporting would expose and help reverse such gaps.

deb_ex.t: I join the thanks to the Government for these actions, but am deeply concerned about the fear that the shadow Foreign Secretary’s comments may have caused. The Foreign Secretary ma
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the settlement sanctions but raises constituent concerns sparked by the shadow Foreign Secretary's remarks, and seeks reassurance that life-saving drugs manufactured within green-line Israel will not be affected.

deb_ex.t: charities such as the RNLI are now having to ask people to take real action on their personal safety and their privacy
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes government action on child safety but raises the doxxing of RNLI rescuers on Meta and X and asks what more the Government can do to hold tech companies to account over posts that endanger individuals.

deb_ex.sum: Commends specialist school staff for rebuilding pupils' confidence and asks how parents, young people and teachers can influence qualification choices when funding constraints currently limit options.

deb_ex.sum: Supports restricting or banning airport drop-off charges until genuine public transport alternatives are provided, citing Bournemouth airport where charges rose to £8 despite virtually no bus service.

deb_ex.t: removal of that phrase is key to changing passenger rights
deb_ex.sum: Slade shares her personal experience of airlines falsely citing 'extraordinary circumstances' to deny compensation and urges that removing that phrase is essential to genuine reform.

deb_ex.t: if the delay goes one day past that, rather than amending the figures, the system has to start all over again
deb_ex.sum: Slade raises a constituent's case where a system flaw forces the entire pension process to restart for a single day's delay, and proposes a simple technical fix to save both Capita and claimants significant difficulty.

deb_ex.sum: Raises ongoing failures of the Child Maintenance Service and calls on the Leader of the House to ask the relevant minister to update Parliament on what action will be taken following Lords' recommendations.

deb_ex.sum: Broadly welcomes the Government's stance as close to getting the balance right but urges that further measures remain on the table if Israel does not change course, and raises concerns about proscription law and its inconsistent application

deb_ex.sum: Presents a 900-signature petition from constituents opposing a 1,200-home development on green belt land between Bearwood and Merley, urging the Government to call in and reject the planning application.

deb_ex.sum: Lib Dem MP highlights families without school places and long diagnosis delays, urging the Government to consider early neurodivergence screening to plan provision properly.

deb_ex.sum: Raises as a parent the hidden cost of interest accruing before repayment begins, adding thousands to borrowing, and asks whether the Committee examined this specific issue.

deb_ex.t: When most children go home from school, they bury their head in a book, grab a football or turn on the TV, but for young carers, home time looks very different. They carry burdens
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the educational disadvantages faced by young carers and calls on the government to legislate for a Young Carers' Champion in every school in England, backed by a 4,000-signature petition.

deb_ex.t: will the hon. Member join me in calling for the menB vaccine to be repeated for teenagers next year and every year until all children are protected
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the disproportionate sepsis risk to children from meningitis and calls for the menB vaccine to be repeated annually for teenagers until all children are protected.

deb_ex.t: What a hero. What an incredible man to do that every time a similar case happens.
deb_ex.sum: Pays personal tribute to Lord Mackinlay for visiting young sepsis survivor Hamish during his recovery, calling him an incredible man.

deb_ex.t: I was really disappointed that the Department for Education did not think it was necessary to add meningitis awareness into the personal, social, health and economic education programme
deb_ex.sum: Asks the shadow Minister to support adding meningitis awareness to the PSHE curriculum in secondary schools, citing the Department for Education's refusal to do so.

deb_ex.t: A few weeks ago, I visited Margaret Green Animal Rescue in Wareham, where I was told that the rescue takes in animals when pet owners are prosecuted for animal welfare offences, bu
deb_ex.sum: Raises the welfare of animals taken in by rescues during lengthy prosecution delays and asks the Minister to look at enabling rehoming before cases are resolved.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the closure of the Poole–Cherbourg Barfleur ferry route as a direct consequence of Brexit red tape, urging the Prime Minister to include UK ports in the UK-EU summit agenda.

deb_ex.t: a young man travelling from Kent to Dorset every week to follow his level 2 barbering course, because there were no courses anywhere else
deb_ex.sum: Highlights a 30% drop in hair and beauty apprenticeships, false self-employment pressures, a critical shortage of providers, and requests a meeting with the Minister and sector representatives.

deb_ex.t: Several constituents who have been in touch with me are victims of domestic abuse and desperately need to move. Emotional support and safety planning are cold comfort when offender
deb_ex.sum: Raises constituency cases of domestic abuse victims who face danger from early-released offenders cutting tags and making threats, and asks what the Ministry of Justice is doing with local authorities to prioritise their rehousing.

deb_ex.t: a rural speed limit of 40 mph would better suit the countryside where the roads simply were not built for the level of traffic
deb_ex.sum: Highlights multiple road deaths on Dorset's rural roads and calls for a debate on reducing rural road deaths, arguing a default 40 mph rural speed limit would save lives more effectively than the current 60 mph limit.

deb_ex.sum: Lib Dem MP calls for Richard's law — mandatory DBS registration, minimum training and a national carers register — to be incorporated into the national care service reforms.

deb_ex.t: will the Government consider limiting their online sales using the Product Regulation and Metrology Act 2025
deb_ex.sum: Raises constituents' concerns about unsafe high-powered e-bikes, e-scooters and conversion kits sold online and calls on the Government to consider limiting their online sales using the 2025 Act.

deb_ex.sum: Recalls the Prime Minister's pledge to Chinook families and asks the Secretary of State to facilitate the long-delayed meeting between those families and the Prime Minister.

deb_ex.t: Does the Minister think that it is acceptable for it to take four months to put a stamp on a letter and send it?
deb_ex.sum: Uses a constituent's bereavement case to challenge the Minister over a claim that is accepted but has apparently been awaiting dispatch for four months, asking if she finds that acceptable.

deb_ex.t: young people in supported housing and foyers dread the cliff edge of their 18th birthday because it can mean eviction, as benefits assume that young people are living at home
deb_ex.sum: Raises the cliff-edge risk for care leavers at 18 and calls for the full universal credit rate to be extended to them in collaboration with DWP.

deb_ex.t: The issue of electronic monitoring does not concern only those on early release. Michele, a victim of domestic abuse, has a restraining order against her ex-partner until 2036 that
deb_ex.sum: Raises the case of a domestic abuse victim whose ex-partner still had no tag ten days after release, leaving her and her children housebound in fear, and presses the Minister to prioritise serial domestic abuse victims for early tagging.

deb_ex.t: an ethical wall needs to be created between developers and inspectors, with proper enforcement and mandatory Housing Ombudsman Service membership for developers
deb_ex.sum: Uses a constituency case in Wimborne to argue for an ethical wall between developers and building inspectors, with proper enforcement and mandatory Housing Ombudsman membership for developers.

deb_ex.t: it is the erasing of the next generation in Gaza. That must surely constitute a war crime.
deb_ex.sum: Raises the destruction of reproductive healthcare facilities causing miscarriages and infant deaths, describing it as erasing the next generation and potentially constituting a war crime.

deb_ex.t: Will the Leader of the House arrange for a ministerial update on the corporate blockers stopping people improving their own homes
deb_ex.sum: Raises cases where developers and housing associations are blocking residents from installing solar panels and EV chargers, and requests a ministerial update on corporate blockers.

deb_ex.t: the 20% VAT rate on salons is viewed by the sector as a penalty for employment and growth as, for businesses operating on narrow margins
deb_ex.sum: Presents a petition calling on the government to introduce a permanently lower 10% VAT rate for hair and beauty services, citing an 84% fall in apprentice starts and a looming 93% employment collapse.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the nuisance caused by illegal racing vehicles and modified cars in her constituency and asks about progress on acoustic devices to help police act.

deb_ex.sum: Raises constituent concerns and references the APPG report on shell companies and proxy donors linked to Russia, pressing the Minister to confirm the new measures will permanently close those funding routes.

deb_ex.t: She was told in October, after a long battle, that nearly £15,000 would be paid within 28 days. She still has not received a penny.
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent promised nearly £15,000 within 28 days who has still received nothing, and presses the Minister to confirm bereavement cases remain a priority and that Capita is adequately resourced.

deb_ex.t: how the different agencies with responsibility for waste should be working more effectively together
deb_ex.sum: Raises a local fire at Hathernware industrial estate as evidence of harm and urges better multi-agency co-ordination and accountability beyond the Environment Agency.

deb_ex.t: the importance of sorting out the courts so that immediate action can be taken when problems are identified
deb_ex.sum: Highlights a two-and-a-half-month delay in obtaining a court order to stop a repeat offender at a local illegal fire site, urging faster court action.

deb_ex.t: there is a strong desire to see independent patient voice maintained outside the system; of course, Healthwatch was established due to issues within health structures
deb_ex.sum: Intervenes before HSSIB is discussed to put on record concerns about the abolition of Healthwatch and the need to maintain an independent patient voice outside the system.

deb_ex.t: I have sat through the debate, and I do not believe that community pharmacy or independent prescribing have been mentioned. Does my hon. Friend, with his experience as a GP, endors
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether community pharmacy and independent prescribing could help relieve GP and A&E pressure, endorsing the Government's moves to expand pharmacist roles.

deb_ex.t: keep funding urgent and emergency care, keep the pressure on trusts that are lagging behind, and keep listening to Back Benchers
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes Government transparency measures and investment including a new urgent treatment centre at QMC, but flags a recent critical incident with 188 patients in A&E and asks the Minister to keep funding urgent care and pressure on lagging

deb_ex.t: I thank the Minister for all the work that he has done, especially on the co-production front, which has been so important to disabled communities. One of my constituents had his P
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituency case of a constituent denied PIP for two years before winning at tribunal at the highest rate, and asks what reassurances the Minister can give that such dehumanising failures will not recur under the new system.

deb_ex.t: when so many constituents are moved to act, the least that we can do is make progress on ending trade with illegal settlements
deb_ex.sum: Highlights intense constituent pressure, including personal visits to Parliament, as justification for making progress on ending trade with illegal settlements.

deb_ex.t: many residents are concerned that decisions affecting their community will be taken solely by a large unitary authority, leaving local voices further removed
deb_ex.sum: Presents a petition from West Bridgford residents calling for a new town council, arguing the area lacks local democratic representation as unitary reorganisation concludes.

deb_ex.t: What steps his Department is taking to help oppose the expansion of illegal settlements in the west bank.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the government is taking to oppose illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank.

deb_ex.t: The UK told the Security Council on 29 June that more than 6,000 settlement housing units had already been approved this year, alongside the declaration on 24 June of a further 465
deb_ex.sum: Cites alarming statistics on settlement expansion and argues current UK measures are failing, calling for a trade ban as the necessary next step.

deb_ex.t: Will the Prime Minister confirm that it is his intention to make rural areas a priority during his premiership?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Prime Minister's farm visit and asks him to confirm that ending the rural penalty — higher costs and weaker services in rural areas — will be a priority of his premiership.

deb_ex.t: will the Secretary of State meet me and the Mayor of the East Midlands, Claire Ward, to look at the investment that needs to go into that site
deb_ex.sum: Raises the National Water Sports Centre in his constituency as a venue needing investment for a potential northern Olympics bid, and requests a ministerial meeting.

deb_ex.t: The Secretary of State moved on from this quickly earlier. I wanted to talk specifically about transport arrangements, as in my constituency, we have three international venues in
deb_ex.sum: Raises the need for local councils to have enforcement powers over transport plans around major venues, drawing on his constituency experience of three international venues in close proximity.

deb_ex.t: does he agree that using sport as a regeneration and visioning tool is an excellent way to bring everybody together in a cross-party way to secure long-term benefits
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that using sport as a long-term regeneration and visioning tool, as being developed in the Trent Sports District, is an effective cross-party way to secure lasting benefits.

deb_ex.t: LGR is extremely complex but extremely important. It therefore did not need to be a term-one priority for this Government, and I remain of that view
deb_ex.sum: Questions whether LGR needed to be a first-term priority and asks how Rushcliffe and Nottinghamshire residents who felt ignored will be properly consulted in the new approach.

deb_ex.t: the midlands is being squeezed from the north and from the south. Will she help me to revisit the limit, resurrect the previously canned scheme on the A46
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes growth rhetoric but presses the Minister on the lack of midlands investment, asking her to revisit funding limits and meet to discuss a specific road scheme.

deb_ex.t: Will she commit today to ensuring that older, rural areas are prioritised and that her team look at East Leake health centre?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Government's approach to capital investment but raises the specific case of East Leake health centre, a deteriorating 1960s building with holes in the roof, and asks for rural areas to be prioritised.

deb_ex.t: One thing that has changed over time is the fact that there is now so much emphasis on live performance for musicians to be able to make an income. Perhaps my hon. Friend agrees th
deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to argue that streaming services have distorted the market and that this must be examined alongside ticketing reform, since musicians now depend so heavily on live touring income.

deb_ex.t: Could the Secretary of State confirm the specific measures that he will take to ensure that UK-based drone companies stay and manufacture here in our country?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights constituent drone company Skycutter being encouraged to move to the US after winning a US government contract, and asks what specific measures will keep UK drone manufacturers in Britain.

deb_ex.t: we cannot treat stock transfer as virtuous and that we have to get to the point where housing revenue accounts are not treated and talked about as being traditional debt
deb_ex.sum: Raises the case of Rushcliffe borough council which transferred all its stock in 2003 and built none since, and argues housing revenue account borrowing should not be treated as traditional debt.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the Bill and the Government’s commitment to a decade of renewal for social and affordable housing. I will use my time to speak on behalf of the villages in my Rushcliffe
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill and the rural right-to-buy exemption but presses the Minister to introduce a local replacement guarantee for rural stock disposals, place rural exception sites on a statutory footing, and create a dedicated rural affordabl

deb_ex.t: if we are serious about a decade of renewal that reaches every postcode, rural Britain cannot be an afterthought
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates the need for the Bill to address rural communities specifically and calls on the Minister to adopt the Labour Rural Research Group's recommendations so rural Britain is not left behind.

deb_ex.t: Farmers are trying to invest in proper water management, as she is describing, but they often need more than three years to do so.
deb_ex.sum: Urges the minister to consider extending environmental land management scheme funding beyond three years so farmers can make the longer-term investments in water management that are needed.

deb_ex.t: With 59% of musicians saying that EU touring is no longer viable, will the Prime Minister commit to putting visa waivers for this specific purpose on the table
deb_ex.sum: On behalf of a Musicians' Union member, urges the PM to commit to visa waivers for EU touring at the November summit, given 59% of musicians find EU touring unviable.

deb_ex.t: acknowledging a problem is where fixing it must begin, and we need to see the co-design of a new system very quickly
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes Government acknowledgement of SFI failings but presses for co-designed reform, RPA IT improvements, a clear SFI27 timetable, and reconsideration of the 3 hectare minimum.

deb_ex.t: The aim is a countryside where farms are less dependent on subsidy and scheme windows, and more independent, resilient and sustainable
deb_ex.sum: Agrees simpler systems cost less to administer, stresses farming profitability as the essential mission, and calls for accelerated implementation of the Batters review.

deb_ex.t: we need to fix the SFI system, and I am pleased that the Government have given indications of how they plan to do that
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes Government indications on SFI reform, calls for ending first come first served, and urges collective action on farming profitability.

deb_ex.t: I think the hon. Gentleman missed out SFI window 1 in his description.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly intervenes to note that Farron's account omitted the first SFI window earlier in the year, implying the government's record is more complete than presented.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Conservative speaker by asking whether it is better to close an overspent scheme or to underspend the DEFRA budget by £358 million, defending the government's record.

deb_ex.t: most items, including public guardian letters and NHS letters, come via Whistl and UK Mail, which means that they do not actually get included in the universal service data
deb_ex.sum: Points out that most important letters travel via Whistl and UK Mail and are excluded from universal service data, and calls for updated measurement of postal performance.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights a rise in acquired brain injuries among young people from e-bike accidents at a Nottingham hospital and calls for more resources for police to tackle the problem.

deb_ex.sum: Recalls meeting the family of Amanda Walker, who took her own life due to the cladding scandal, and asks the Secretary of State to consider Amanda's five specific asks including closing loopholes for non-qualifying leaseholders and an indus

deb_ex.sum: Introduces a ten-minute rule Bill to address £9 billion in unspent developer contributions sitting in local authority accounts, arguing the money should be spent on schools, GP surgeries and roads rather than left idle and devalued by infla

deb_ex.t: He wrote again to No. 10 in March, and I wrote to the Health Secretary in July. There have been no responses
deb_ex.sum: Raises constituent Matthew Cox's unanswered correspondence with the Prime Minister and Health Secretary, asking the Minister to take his case away and ensure an accessible, timely reply.

deb_ex.t: LGR is extremely complicated, should never have been a term-one priority, and has destabilised the very organisations on which we rely
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes fair consideration for Nottinghamshire but argues LGR should not have been a first-term priority and is destabilising councils; asks whether 'minded to' could mean reorganisation does not proceed.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the new drone facility coming to Swindon but argues the DIP funding is insufficient and presses the Minister on whether the procurement model needs urgent reform under new leadership.

deb_ex.t: It is not enough to say that the Government plan to insource more contracts—they cannot insource everything.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the statement but presses the Government on whether it is doing enough to ensure Whitehall gets better value from procurement and project management beyond just insourcing more contracts.

deb_ex.t: a man with his head full of rubbish is a fitting representative of the mainstream parties in this House
deb_ex.sum: Criticises all parties except Reform for fielding a comedian candidate in the Clacton by-election and presses the PM to clarify who he wants to win there.

deb_ex.t: in his time as Mayor of Greater Manchester youth employment did not improve. In fact, it got worse and no amount of taxpayer-funded support is going to fix that
deb_ex.sum: Attacks the PM's record on youth employment in Greater Manchester and argues that tax cuts for business, not taxpayer-funded support, are the way to get young people into work.

deb_ex.t: I want to be constructive because I welcome the creation of a stronger centre, with a proper political centre in No. 10 and a corporate HQ for the non-political functions. My quest
deb_ex.sum: Broadly welcomes the creation of a stronger centre but presses the minister on the residual purpose of the Cabinet Office and Cabinet Secretary in the new structure.

deb_ex.t: the Bill is not concerned with those questions. The claim is made that the Bill will defend democracy, but it is actually a flagrantly partisan attempt to kneecap Reform UK
deb_ex.sum: Attacks the Bill as partisan legislation designed to harm Reform UK while exempting trade union donations to Labour, and defends donors to Reform UK as legitimate British citizens exercising their democratic rights.

deb_ex.t: there are now 2.5 million Commonwealth citizens resident in this country who are entitled to vote in our elections who are not citizens of the United Kingdom. That is wrong
deb_ex.sum: Argues that 2.5 million Commonwealth citizens resident in the UK who are not UK citizens should no longer be entitled to vote in UK elections, calling this an anomaly that must be corrected.

deb_ex.t: How can we integrate genuinely? How can we bring our divided country together if we do not do our democracy in the same language?
deb_ex.sum: Argues the Bill should require election materials to be in English only, restrict proxy voting, and enforce individual secret voting, framing these as making formerly implicit democratic principles explicit.

deb_ex.t: the Cabinet Secretary is proposing to take new powers to direct permanent secretaries of Government Departments. Will the Minister confirm whether legislation is planned
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Minister to confirm whether legislation is planned to change the statutory basis of the civil service and whether the Cabinet Secretary should have power to direct permanent secretaries.

deb_ex.t: There is what might be an important innovation in the text of this year’s sovereign grant annual report and accounts, which the Bill refers to and which the Minister is describing.
deb_ex.sum: Raises the omission of 'defender of the faith' from the annual report and asks the Minister to confirm no alteration to the monarch's role is implied and that any such change would be debated in Parliament.

deb_ex.t: whether the introduction of VAT on school fees has led to an increase in the number of in-year moves, especially among service families?
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the government by asking whether the introduction of VAT on private school fees has increased mid-year school moves for armed forces children with SEND, and calls for published research on this.

deb_ex.t: In the seven years that I have been a Member of this House, I do not think that I have been in a more respectful, positive and high-quality debate. There have been some absolutely
deb_ex.sum: Kruger argues the Bill fails on a core moral principle by not addressing the structural imbalance that places the legal burden almost entirely on veterans while paramilitaries received amnesties, and calls for stopping all future prosecutio

deb_ex.t: the actual practice of repeat prosecutions on the scale that we have seen—not the threat, but the reality—is unacceptable.
deb_ex.sum: Kruger argues the British Army won the military conflict but accepted the unjust exposure to prosecution as the price of peace, and that repeat prosecutions on this scale were never anticipated.

deb_ex.t: We are very familiar with that argument. I do not think this is the time to have that debate, but I am confident—and there has been a lot of learned advice to this effect—that it i
deb_ex.sum: Kruger asserts it is possible to withdraw from the ECHR while maintaining Good Friday agreement obligations, defending that position against challenge.

deb_ex.t: it is absolutely scandalous that non-essential training has been suspended across large parts of the British Army because there is no money
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Secretary of State over reports that non-essential Army training has been suspended due to lack of funding and demands to know when training on Salisbury Plain will resume.

deb_ex.t: Does he agree that the Prime Minister has a function to play in the advice given to the sovereign, or does he think this is purely a procedural matter
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister to clarify whether the Prime Minister plays a substantive advisory role or merely a procedural transmitting role in conveying Church appointment advice to the sovereign.

deb_ex.t: the value of this Bill is that it could strengthen the Church of England and reconnect it with the political community of which it is properly a part
deb_ex.sum: Supports the Bill but argues it should strengthen rather than diminish the Church of England's role in political life, and warns against leaving episcopal appointments solely to Church House bureaucrats.

deb_ex.t: What we do not want bureaucrats in the Church of England appointing each other, which is what we have at the moment—that is why they are all left wing.
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the preceding speaker's scepticism, arguing that 20th-century Prime Ministers took their Church appointment responsibilities seriously and calling for a genuinely broad church rather than appointments controlled by Church House.

deb_ex.t: will he approve more North sea exploration and, while he is at it, speed up the roll-out of nuclear as well
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether Budget calculations assume Rosebank approval and presses the Prime Minister to approve more North Sea exploration and accelerate nuclear roll-out.
