Non-consensual intimate images, and the kinds of images that the hon. Lady talks about, are absolutely disgusting. This Government have taken action to ensure that they will be tak
It does not keep a single victim safe if we have nowhere to lock up offenders.
deb_ex.sum: As Minister for Victims, pays tribute to grooming gang survivors, outlines the Government's actions including record convictions and the Longfield inquiry, and defends early release as necessary to maintain prison capacity.

deb_ex.t: This Government have been absolutely clear that we will ensure there will always be prison cells for people when they are convicted and sentenced to custody.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies there is no specific grooming gangs offence and reaffirms the Government's commitment to ensuring prison cells are always available for those sentenced to custody, contrasting with the Conservatives' prison-building record.

deb_ex.t: I want to ensure that I can look them in the eyes and know that when offenders are convicted and sentenced to custody, there are prison cells for them.
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms that the Government always listens to victims but insists prison capacity must be maintained so that convicted offenders can always be imprisoned.

deb_ex.t: grooming has been made a clear aggravating feature. However, I would be happy to meet the hon. Lady to discuss this point if she would find that useful.
deb_ex.sum: Explains that grooming is now an aggravating factor in sentencing but that judges retain discretion over the final sentence, and defends the Government's prison-building record against Conservative criticism.

deb_ex.t: I will ensure that the Under-Secretary of State for Justice, my hon. Friend the Member for Rother Valley (Jake Richards), writes to the hon. Lady.
deb_ex.sum: Commits to ensuring the Prisons Minister writes to the Lib Dem MP with an update on HMP Dartmoor.

deb_ex.t: Conservative Members have talked many times in this debate about how we got here, but they have not been honest about how we got here.
deb_ex.sum: Signals intent to address Conservative Members' account of how the prison crisis arose, implying it has been dishonest.

deb_ex.t: I did work experience with the police as a teenager, back when this country had a Labour Government who were recruiting thousands of additional police officers.
deb_ex.sum: Begins to contrast her own professional experience with the criminal justice system under Labour and Conservative governments to contextualise the prison capacity crisis.

deb_ex.t: That is not a coincidence; it is a choice, repeated by successive Governments for 14 years.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that 14 years of Conservative-led government choices—delayed courts, shuttered courts, reckless probation privatisation—created the prison capacity crisis that necessitates the early release scheme.

deb_ex.t: I am going to continue to make some progress, but I will give way shortly.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly signals she will continue making her case on the origins of the prison crisis before taking further interventions.

deb_ex.t: If prisons run out of space, courts cannot sentence anyone to custody. If courts cannot sentence anyone to custody, they cannot function.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the full scale of Conservative cuts to police, courts, probation and prisons over 14 years, arguing this left prisons at 99% capacity and that without early release the entire justice system risked total breakdown.

deb_ex.t: release does not mean freedom. We are delivering tougher punishment outside prison. We are ramping up tagging to monitor offenders
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends the government's early release policy, emphasising public protection measures including tagging, probation funding, and licence conditions, while contrasting the record favourably against the Conservatives.

deb_ex.t: this Government are deporting such offenders in greater numbers than ever before
deb_ex.sum: Minister summarises backbench contributions on criminal justice, defending the government's record on foreign national deportations, court sitting days, and reducing reoffending.

deb_ex.t: I will not give way. A number of hon. Members have spoken passionately about victims, and rightly so. We understand that these issues will be difficult and upsetting for many victi
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends the government's communication with victims through the victim contact scheme, contrasting it with what she describes as chaotic Conservative handling of early releases.

deb_ex.t: Victims were told only days before their offenders were let out, and in some cases they were not told at all.
deb_ex.sum: Minister sets out licence conditions including exclusion zones and a new dedicated helpline for victims, criticising the previous government for informing victims only days before offenders' release.

deb_ex.t: when public bodies fail, the response is candour, not cover-up
deb_ex.sum: Introduces the Bill on Report, describing it as a landmark shift requiring honesty and transparency from public bodies toward bereaved families rather than institutional cover-up.

deb_ex.t: families have had to fight for the truth and their trust in the state to be forthcoming and truthful has been shattered
deb_ex.sum: Credits the Hillsborough families and a wider coalition of campaigners for driving the Bill, stressing it belongs to all families who have fought institutions for the truth.

deb_ex.t: I will make some progress, and then I will take interventions. Many have graciously—often at huge personal and emotional cost—shared their experiences with us to shape the Bill. Th
deb_ex.sum: Thanks campaigners, predecessors and ministers for shaping the Bill, and explains why the Government paused to address Manchester Arena families' concerns about intelligence services.

deb_ex.t: we are clear that the Bill needs to apply across the United Kingdom, and we are working with devolved nations to ensure that happens
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House that the Bill is intended to apply across the whole United Kingdom and that work with devolved nations is ongoing.

deb_ex.t: We are seeking a full culture change, and are trying to prevent any kind of attitude of covering things up
deb_ex.sum: Responds by affirming the Bill seeks a full culture change against cover-ups and offers to meet the hon. Member to discuss the specific Stakeknife case.

deb_ex.t: where information can be disclosed, it should be disclosed, while ensuring that proper protections are in place
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government amendments ensuring compliance directions apply to individual intelligence officers and establishes secure disclosure procedures, while protecting national security.

deb_ex.t: I am very happy to meet the hon. Member and others, specifically in relation to the Ministry of Defence
deb_ex.sum: Offers to meet the hon. Member to discuss how the duty of candour can apply to MoD cases safely.

deb_ex.t: If it is specifically in relation to security services, and to security at the moment—
deb_ex.sum: Begins to conditionally offer to take the intervention, limiting it to security services matters.

deb_ex.t: a public servant does not have to come forward until it is safe to do so, but steps must be taken without delay
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the Bill does not override existing law including the Official Secrets Act, sets out protections for intelligence officers, and announces secondary legislation to extend the duty further.

deb_ex.t: It is absolutely right that recommendations are tracked and that we ensure there is a clear way of giving everyone confidence
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Cabinet Office is working to ensure inquiry recommendations are tracked and offers to brief the hon. Member on progress.

deb_ex.t: The Government have already taken steps to improve transparency in response to inquiry recommendations, including launching the new gov.uk dashboards
deb_ex.sum: Points to new gov.uk dashboards tracking inquiry recommendations and welcomes the Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee's scrutiny work.

deb_ex.t: there is clearly work to be done in relation to inquests and in relation to inquiries and their recommendations
deb_ex.sum: Notes ongoing work by the Chief Coroner on prevention of future deaths reports and acknowledges further work is needed on inquests and inquiry recommendations.

deb_ex.t: the largest expansion of legal aid in a generation, granting access to non-means-tested legal aid to families at any inquest where a public authority is an interested person
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges public confidence in handling recommendations is being actively considered and outlines the legal aid expansion as the largest in a generation to rebalance families against public authority legal teams.

deb_ex.t: we would hope that, in general, one legally aided advocate would be sufficient to support each family through an inquest hearing
deb_ex.sum: Responds to concerns about legal aid advocacy by explaining the expansion, noting one legally aided advocate should generally suffice, but commits to continuing to look at the issue as the Bill progresses.

deb_ex.t: my hon. Friend assists me in finding my place in my notes again, so I thank her
deb_ex.sum: Briefly thanks a colleague for helping her find her place in her notes.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend has been a passionate advocate in relation to legally aided work, and I know that she will take every opportunity to raise concerns about the rates. The amendments m
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges concerns about legal aid rates, sets out Government amendments on archivists, devolved Government provisions and Scottish legal aid, and commits to publishing a clear implementation timeline.

deb_ex.t: The Bill allows a Minister to extend the duty and allows the flexibility to apply it to reviews where it would be most beneficial. I know that my hon. Friend has campaigned long on
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Bill allows Ministers to extend the duty of candour to reviews where beneficial, offers to discuss this further, and pays tribute to bereaved families who campaigned for the legislation.

deb_ex.t: This Bill will finally put that imbalance right. It shifts the system away from secrecy and defensiveness towards openness, honesty and accountability.
deb_ex.sum: Closes the debate as a minister, defending the Government amendments on national security, explaining existing safeguards remain intact, and affirming the Bill will apply to maternity scandals and strengthen accountability across public ins

deb_ex.t: We are clear that we will apply the duty of candour to the Leeds and Sussex maternity reviews.
deb_ex.sum: Responds to specific points on national oversight, maternity reviews, whistleblowing and water companies, confirming the Government's commitments and willingness to work further on outstanding concerns.

deb_ex.t: Restriction zones reverse that burden by confining offenders to specific areas. Will the Justice Secretary be more ambitious about the use of restriction zones
deb_ex.sum: Atkinson welcomes the victims hotline being brought forward and asks the Justice Secretary to be more ambitious in using restriction zones to curtail offenders' freedoms rather than victims'.

deb_ex.t: Last month I visited HMP Foston Hall to see the work it was doing giving catering and hospitality experience to women there, but when so many in our prisons are on remand, waiting
deb_ex.sum: Describes her visit to HMP Foston Hall and argues that remand and recall prisoners are a barrier to rehabilitation, calling for a debate on education, training and work in prisons.

deb_ex.t: Thank you, Mr Speaker. The Government’s progress on deporting foreign national offenders is welcome, but how will the Minister work with the Home Office to ensure that receiving co
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes government progress but presses the minister to ensure receiving countries are informed of offenders' convictions, especially for violent or sexual offences, to protect public safety abroad.

deb_ex.t: more than 5,000 people who should have been monitored were not tagged—that equates to 15% of all people with an electronic tagging order.
deb_ex.sum: Raises Justice Committee and Institute for Government findings that thousands of offenders were not tagged or had faulty tags, and presses the minister for specific figures on tagging timeliness and day-one tagging.

deb_ex.t: When I first put on my barrister’s robes and horse hair wig nearly 20 years ago, victims and defendants were not commonly waiting years for trial, victims of rape and serious sexua
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the removal of the Crown court bench division and increased resources for magistrates courts, but warns of a gathering storm in magistrates courts and calls on the Minister to set capacity targets matching the accelerated timeline.

deb_ex.t: Accelerating reforms means accelerating the strain on our magistrates court, so will the Minister bring forward target dates to match the accelerated timeline?
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the lawyer shortage problem and expresses concern about insufficient numbers entering criminal practice; calls for review of allocation guidelines if the right to elect is removed.

deb_ex.t: I am very conscious of the time available for this very important legislation, so I am turning the page to conclude. To return to where I started, I welcome the Government’s commit
deb_ex.sum: Concludes by welcoming the Government's commitment to reducing the backlog but warns that simply shifting cases to magistrates courts without adequate support will continue to fail victims and defendants.

deb_ex.t: around 1,000 people a month left prison homeless. Will the Minister work with the MOJ to use this investment to go beyond the target
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the funding but urges the Minister to go beyond halving homelessness among prison leavers and presses for quarterly rather than annual reporting of accommodation figures.

deb_ex.t: Victims should not have to make their lives smaller, looking over their shoulder because offenders are free to roam; it is the offender whose freedoms should be limited.
deb_ex.sum: Calls on the government to be more ambitious in using restriction zones to limit offenders' movements, and presses for tags to be fitted at the prison gate rather than weeks later, asking whether this will be in place by January.

deb_ex.t: this is a brilliant example of our Government rebuilding British industry and working alongside business to deliver skilled jobs
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates the £2.5 billion Rolls-Royce investment announced in the Budget as a brilliant example of the Government rebuilding British industry and creating skilled jobs.

deb_ex.t: It is very clear that the Minister agrees that the infected blood scandal is a tragic disaster and a failure of public service. The Government must ensure that it never happens aga
deb_ex.sum: Argues the Government must prevent future failures by introducing a robustly enforced duty of candour on all public officials, as called for by survivors.

deb_ex.t: Will the Government introduce mutual ownership of water companies, professionally managed, to put customers and the environment first?
deb_ex.sum: Raises repeated sewage dumps in his constituency rivers and calls on the Government to introduce mutual ownership of water companies to prioritise customers and the environment.

deb_ex.t: What steps have the Government taken to make independent domestic advisers mandatory in family courts, to help deliver justice?
deb_ex.sum: Calls for independent domestic violence advisers to be made mandatory in family courts and presses the government on what action has been taken since a junior minister said warm words were not enough.

deb_ex.t: 74 sewage spills, for a duration of 684 hours. That means that Thames Water dumped sewage for the equivalent of 456 football matches
deb_ex.sum: Highlights 74 sewage spills totalling 684 hours in Wokingham in 2025 alone, reinforcing the call for stronger government action on Thames Water.

deb_ex.t: How will the cancer manuals support earlier diagnosis, and will they include specific guidance to improve outcomes for children and young people?
deb_ex.sum: Asks how the cancer manuals will support earlier diagnosis and whether they will include specific guidance to improve outcomes for children and young people.

deb_ex.t: I congratulate the Minister for Veterans and People, the hon. Member for Leyton and Wanstead (Mr Bailey) on his recent promotion. Most Members will agree that the repression of Ira
deb_ex.sum: Condemns Trump and Netanyahu's illegal war on Iran as reckless and driven by ego rather than diplomacy, warns of rising costs for UK families from strait of Hormuz instability, and calls for fuel duty cuts and closer EU defence partnership.

deb_ex.t: I urge the Government to back the Liberal Democrat proposal for a new growth and defence partnership with the European Union
deb_ex.sum: Urges the Government to back a new EU growth and defence partnership and to press the US and Iran to return to negotiations and restore stability in the strait of Hormuz.

deb_ex.t: If this summer’s free bus travel scheme for under-15s proves successful, will the Minister look to extend it for the future? It would help hard-working families in Wokingham make t
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether the government will extend the free summer bus travel scheme beyond this year if it proves successful, citing benefits for families in Wokingham.

deb_ex.t: Nearly a thousand families of children with special educational needs and disabilities are supported by Camp Mohawk and its fantastic daycare centre in my constituency.
deb_ex.sum: Praises Camp Mohawk in his constituency for providing daycare and support to nearly a thousand families of children with SEND, and asks the Leader to recognise the invaluable role such charities play.

deb_ex.t: extremism can take many forms, but its goal is always the same: to intimate, divide and undermine our democracy
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to Sir David Amess and Jo Cox, warns about toxic political discourse and online misinformation, and calls for elected representatives at every level to be able to serve safely without fear.

deb_ex.t: what steps will the Government take to ensure that Wokingham receives a fairer settlement and can provide the services that residents deserve?
deb_ex.sum: Raises Wokingham borough council's chronic underfunding and asks what steps the Government will take to ensure a fairer settlement for local services.

deb_ex.t: Can the Minister confirm that the Government are reviewing the military infrastructure and surveillance capabilities on the islands in response to Argentina’s announced plans to bo
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister to confirm whether the Government is reviewing military infrastructure and surveillance on the islands in response to Argentina's announced military build-up.

deb_ex.t: there is a very real concern that progress on cancer outcomes risks being deprioritised amid the competing priorities of a Department facing many external pressures
deb_ex.sum: Warns that the Bill removes the statutory requirement to prioritise cancer outcomes and seeks ministerial assurance that the national cancer plan will remain a priority despite the restructuring.

deb_ex.t: What steps she is taking with Cabinet colleagues to make it easier for people with accessibility needs to contact Government Departments.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the minister is taking with Cabinet colleagues to improve accessibility for people with accessibility needs when contacting government departments.

deb_ex.t: Does the Minister agree that adjustments must be applied consistently by Departments and contractors? What action will be taken when they are not?
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent's case where agreed accessibility adjustments were removed and telephone appointments were arranged despite a hearing impediment, and presses for consistent enforcement.

deb_ex.t: Brexit has created a web of red tape preventing businesses in Wokingham from developing relationships with European partners.
deb_ex.sum: Jones argues Brexit has created red tape harming businesses in Wokingham and calls on the government to negotiate a growth and defence partnership with the EU.

deb_ex.t: Everyone had concerns about NHS workforce shortfalls blocking the progress of the national cancer plan
deb_ex.sum: Reports cancer charities' and clinicians' concerns about NHS workforce shortfalls blocking the national cancer plan and calls for a debate on the investment needed.

deb_ex.t: Can the Secretary of State confirm that this support will continue even if the USA, under President Trump, backs away even more from supporting Ukraine?
deb_ex.sum: Reflecting concerns of Ukrainian constituents in Wokingham, asks whether UK support will continue even if the USA under President Trump withdraws further from backing Ukraine.

deb_ex.t: requiring pension scheme surpluses in defined-benefit schemes to be used to improve pensions for members before surplus funds can be released
deb_ex.sum: Asks the government to assess requiring DB scheme surpluses to benefit members before being released to employers.

deb_ex.t: nothing in law stops the Government requiring pre-1997 pensions to be restored before surplus goes back to employers
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Minister by arguing that nothing in law prevents requiring pre-1997 pension restoration before surplus goes to employers, implying the government has chosen not to act.

deb_ex.t: 13,000 people every day are left stranded in hospital beds, unable to leave because their care packages have not been put in place
deb_ex.sum: Lib Dem MP welcomes the statement but highlights the scale of the crisis — thousands stranded in hospital, spiralling costs, and struggling councils — and sets out three tests the reforms must meet.

deb_ex.t: The Liberal Democrats have set the Government three tests for the social care reforms.
deb_ex.sum: Lib Dem MP sets out three tests for the reforms — carers' rights, universal free personal care, and protection from catastrophic costs — and urges cross-party engagement.

deb_ex.t: many carers are pleading for urgent action to help resolve the high vacancy rate and to incentivise people to stay in the sector
deb_ex.sum: Urges urgent action beyond the government's workforce plan commitment to address high vacancy rates in social care, and requests a debate on skills and professional development for the sector.

deb_ex.t: If he will list his official engagements for Wednesday 21 October.
deb_ex.sum: Asks a routine engagements question as a precursor to a substantive follow-up.

deb_ex.t: Like you, Mr Speaker, I have recollections of Aberfan and being at primary school myself at that time. Too many patients are suffering because of treatment delays and having their
deb_ex.sum: Urges the Prime Minister to support his private Member's Bill requiring annual parliamentary reports on cancer diagnosis and outcomes.

deb_ex.t: Five months into the review process, only about 1% of cases have been reassessed.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the slow pace of carer's allowance case reassessments and calls for a government statement on accelerating reviews, compensation, and ending the earnings cliff edge.

deb_ex.t: My 80-odd-year-old mum was recently admitted to Airedale hospital with acute respiratory issues. She had to wait in a chair for over 12 hours
deb_ex.sum: Shares a personal family experience of an elderly relative waiting 12 hours in undignified conditions and asks whether neighbourhood health teams could prevent such admissions.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely agree with my hon. Friend that it is not about fixing the problem at the front door; it is about fixing the problem at the back door. Does she agree that closer integr
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the back door is the key problem and urges the Minister to consider her Health Bill amendment on health and care integration as part of the solution.

deb_ex.t: I commend the organisers of the national emergency briefing, which I attended last year, as well as the local organisers of the people’s emergency briefing in Shipley. The climate
deb_ex.sum: Praises the national emergency briefing and raises the growing threat of upland moorland wildfires in her constituency, pressing the Minister for further action to protect peatland moors.

deb_ex.t: we need to take further steps to ensure that all candidates feel secure and able to stand for public office at all levels
deb_ex.sum: Promotes her new clause 81 to make all candidates' addresses automatically anonymous, asking the previous speaker to agree that further steps are needed to keep candidates safe.

deb_ex.t: If I see you in public, I will try my best to kill you. I will work hard to find out where you live, and I will kill you there.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill's democratic reforms but urges the Government to adopt her new clause making non-publication of candidates' home addresses the default, citing a personal death threat against her.

deb_ex.t: other groups, such as those with learning disabilities, also face barriers in participating in elections, and that further work should be done
deb_ex.sum: Supports accessible voting for blind people and urges further work to remove barriers for people with learning disabilities.

deb_ex.t: It is a fantastic opportunity to build housing around Shipley station, which is close to the recently refurbished Shipley market.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the fast-track development commitment near transport hubs and invites the Secretary of State to visit Shipley station to see its potential for affordable housing and high street regeneration.

deb_ex.t: we need a stronger duty to co-operate, both within the NHS and between the NHS and local authorities
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether her colleague agrees that a stronger duty to co-operate between the NHS and local authorities, as proposed in her new clause 106, is needed.

deb_ex.t: I worked as a civil servant for the coalition Government, and I saw at first hand some of the duplication and confusion caused when NHS England was set up, so I welcome this Bill a
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill and NHS England abolition but argues that integration of health and social care needs stronger statutory obligations, illustrated by two constituency cases where disjointed care caused serious harm.

deb_ex.t: the ethnic inequalities we see in cancer outcomes and access to cancer treatment such as radiotherapy should also be included in the suggested review
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether ethnic inequalities in cancer outcomes and access to radiotherapy should also be included in any proposed review.

deb_ex.t: there can be no choice until hospice and end-of-life care are properly funded
deb_ex.sum: Dixon, as APPG chair, argues that with 170,000 people dying each year without palliative care access, genuine choice cannot exist until hospice funding is properly secured.

deb_ex.t: Three quarters told us that the claims process itself had been distressing or retraumatising.
deb_ex.sum: Presents the Public Accounts Committee's findings on government compensation schemes, highlighting delays, complexity, distress caused to claimants, and calling for fairer, timelier, victim-centred schemes.

deb_ex.t: We urge the Government to make sure that is much more timely in future.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Committee did not examine index-linking but agrees delays are too long and urges the Government to make compensation more timely.

deb_ex.t: As an officer of the all-party parliamentary group on patient safety, I am very well aware that the Hughes report is still in the Government inbox, awaiting a response. I also have
deb_ex.sum: Notes the Hughes report is still awaiting a Government response and expresses hope that a co-designed compensation scheme for pelvic mesh victims will be brought forward swiftly.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Gentleman, and I guess I return the compliment—although I am not sure I always enjoy his contributions to the Public Accounts Committee! However, I certainly recog
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that lessons must be learned about why the underlying scandals occurred, not just how compensation is delivered.

deb_ex.t: I agree with my hon. Friend—another colleague on the Public Accounts Committee. The report is very clear that much more needs to be done to try to reach victims; there is a concern
deb_ex.sum: Agrees outreach must improve, warns the LGBT veterans scheme is closing with victims still unreached, and calls for lower evidential burdens alongside fraud protections.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for being such a champion for those in her constituency who suffered from the decisions that impacted on the Windrush generation. She is absolutely right. We
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that legal support for Windrush claimants was inadequate and endorses the call for clearer, more consistent access to legal assistance in future schemes.

deb_ex.t: I commend my hon. Friend for all her years of work on the Public Accounts Committee and for her leadership and foresight in making sure that the work was done by the National Audit
deb_ex.sum: Points to the infected blood scheme's relative independence as a positive example and calls for future schemes to prioritise co-design, timeliness and fairness for victims.

deb_ex.t: He remains in prison with no set release date, despite having passed his mental health tribunal.
deb_ex.sum: Raises the case of a constituent serving an IPP sentence since 2007 with no release date despite passing a mental health tribunal, welcoming the review but pressing for specific support for autistic prisoners.

deb_ex.t: we also need to look at NHS Resolution, the clinical negligence scheme, and stop making it a fight for parents to get answers
deb_ex.sum: Calls for reform of NHS Resolution and the clinical negligence scheme so that bereaved families are not forced into long adversarial legal battles to get answers.

deb_ex.t: in the NHS staff survey only four in 10 midwives say that their organisation would address concerns if they were raised.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that only four in ten midwives believe their organisation would act on concerns raised, and urges more action to build a safe staff speaking-up culture in maternity units.

deb_ex.t: 10. What recent progress she has made on improving the UK’s resilience to the impacts of climate change.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the same question as the previous member about progress on improving UK climate change resilience.

deb_ex.t: As hon. Members have said, we endured one of the hottest summers on record, with 10 days reaching 35°, which is double the previous record. We also saw deaths from extreme heat. Wh
deb_ex.sum: Notes record heat deaths this summer and presses the Minister to explain what the government is doing to ensure new homes are designed to protect against extreme heat.

deb_ex.t: What steps she is taking to help increase prosecutions for non-domestic stalking.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the government is taking to increase prosecutions for non-domestic stalking.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Attorney General for her response. I recently spoke to two of my constituents, Julie and Jodie, about the repeated harassment they had experienced at the hands of a for
deb_ex.sum: Raises constituents' case where police failed to identify a pattern of stalking and urges the Attorney General to urgently improve CPS and police training and standards.

deb_ex.t: how the Government will ensure that the national care service gives peace of mind to families and carers that care and support will be there when they need it
deb_ex.sum: Labour MP and APPG carers chair asks how the national care service will give families peace of mind regardless of finances or location.

deb_ex.t: Does my hon. Friend agree that we need supportive local government to help to implement these policies?
deb_ex.sum: Agrees communities should be able to take over heritage buildings but raises a local example of a pool struggling without council support, arguing supportive local government is essential for these policies to work.

deb_ex.t: it links up with local heritage pubs around Saltaire so that they are part of the wider festival.
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates the Bradford beer festival run by CAMRA, noting how it links with local heritage pubs in Saltaire and supports local breweries and heritage pubs such as Fanny's Ale House and the Beehive.

deb_ex.t: Sadly, it is now a pubco and is seeking a tenant for its ongoing use, which shows some of the challenges for our pubs.
deb_ex.sum: Raises the historical example of Saltaire, where no pub was built by Sir Titus Salt, noting that the resulting Victoria pub is now a pubco seeking a tenant, illustrating ongoing challenges for heritage pubs.

deb_ex.t: As the Minister acknowledged, Yorkshire is now in drought, and at least part of the blame must be with the water companies such as Yorkshire Water who have failed to prioritise any
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister to agree that the upcoming water Bill must be used to fundamentally change how water companies are run, prioritising citizens over profit.

deb_ex.t: local planning authorities already have powers to create local lists for buildings of local historic importance, and those can include heritage pubs.
deb_ex.sum: Notes that local planning authorities already have powers to create local lists covering heritage pubs and asks whether existing provision is sufficient.

deb_ex.t: One of the pubs in my constituency, the Woolpack in Esholt, was the pub used for the filming of “Emmerdale”, if there are any fans of that show here. Although the building itself m
deb_ex.sum: Cites the Woolpack in Esholt, used for filming Emmerdale, as an example of a pub with strong cultural heritage value that may not qualify under purely architectural criteria.

deb_ex.t: I wonder whether my hon. Friend is aware of the Society of Independent Brewers and Associates’ campaign “Drop the Tap Tax”, which seeks to lower the alcohol duty on beer sold in pu
deb_ex.sum: Draws attention to CAMRA's 'Drop the Tap Tax' campaign seeking lower alcohol duty specifically on draught beer sold in pubs, and invites the speaker to raise it with the Chancellor.

deb_ex.t: I would like to understand how we can preserve the interiors of heritage pubs
deb_ex.sum: Strongly backs the Bill, describes cherished historic pubs in Shipley, and presses for provisions to protect pub interiors as well as exteriors, while calling for fairer relationships between tied pubcos and independent breweries.

deb_ex.t: those heritage pubs are not only part of the local community, but also provide a fantastic resting place for visitors to our areas who enjoy walking
deb_ex.sum: Endorses saving heritage pubs, noting they serve not just local communities but also walkers and visitors, and cites Dick Hudsons in Bingley as an example.

deb_ex.t: 84% of people said that since the pub had been taken into community ownership, it was a better place to live
deb_ex.sum: Cites evaluation evidence from a community-owned pub showing strong social benefits and asks whether the case for community ownership of heritage pubs is proven.

deb_ex.t: The excellent Saltaire Blonde, brewed in my constituency and named after the fantastic world heritage site village of Saltaire, is distributed nationwide.
deb_ex.sum: Takes the opportunity to promote Saltaire Blonde ale brewed in her constituency and asks whether it has found its way into Collinge's local heritage pubs.

deb_ex.t: As a member of the APPG on beer, could my hon. Friend recommend his favourite beer?
deb_ex.sum: Intervenes playfully to ask the speaker's favourite beer, keeping the warm tone of the debate.

deb_ex.t: I am still waiting in suspense to learn what his favourite beer is. Could he please put me out of my misery?
deb_ex.sum: Playfully presses the speaker to finally reveal his favourite beer after repeatedly deferring the answer.

deb_ex.t: These disruptions can have a significant economic impact on our heritage pubs
deb_ex.sum: Supports the previous speaker's point by citing a road closure near a historic pub in her constituency that harmed trade, urging councils to manage roadworks better.

deb_ex.t: the tramshed itself is a heritage space where SALT is now producing fantastic, excellent local beers
deb_ex.sum: Cites the SALT brewery in a converted tramshed in her constituency as an example of heritage space not clearly covered by the Bill's definition.

deb_ex.t: we have had repeated undertakings from Capita that improvements were imminent. Despite that, many of my constituents are still waiting for quotes and pension payments.
deb_ex.sum: Commends the Minister but, as a Public Accounts Committee member, notes that repeated Capita commitments have not been delivered, and asks whether the Minister agrees Capita should pay for its failures.

deb_ex.t: I also commend the Committee for its deliberative work and the innovative way it is taking evidence on this subject. When the Public Accounts Committee, of which I am a member, did
deb_ex.sum: Raises the vulnerability of migrant care workers tied to single employers under the skilled worker visa scheme and asks whether the Committee will take evidence from overseas care workers and consider sector-wide sponsorship.

deb_ex.t: police are often powerless to pursue them. Will the Minister look again at guidance for police forces and ensure they have the resources they need
deb_ex.sum: Calls on the Minister to review guidance for police and ensure forces have resources including drones and off-road bikes to enforce action against illegal e-motorbikes.

deb_ex.t: this Chancellor and this Budget got that balance right, delivering security at home, with better public services, and security from threats abroad
deb_ex.sum: Dixon welcomes Budget measures on energy bills, the carer's allowance taper, social care ambitions and defence spending, arguing the Chancellor struck the right balance between fiscal discipline and public investment.

deb_ex.t: schemes needed to be designed with the victims, and that there should be independence, just as there is in the case of infected blood
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the Public Accounts Committee report recommending compensation schemes be designed with victims and administered independently, and urges the Minister to follow that model.

deb_ex.t: Will she confirm that business rates relief will not apply to the vape shops that are popping up on our high streets and blighting them?
deb_ex.sum: Asks the minister to confirm that business rates relief will not be extended to vape shops, which she regards as blighting high streets.

deb_ex.t: run by two inspiring brothers who came to the UK as child refugees from Myanmar. Will the Leader of the House join me in congratulating Sizzling Lounge
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates Sizzling Lounge from Bingley winning at the National Curry Awards and highlights the contribution of curry restaurants, especially in Bradford, to local high streets.

deb_ex.t: Like my hon. Friend, I have small breweries in my own constituency, including the Saltaire Brewery, the Goose Eye Brewery and SALT. Does she agree with me that, with rising energy
deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to welcome the £10 million annual alcohol duty relief for small brewers as particularly timely given rising energy costs facing small breweries.

deb_ex.t: the new low-income tax-free allowance for pensioners, which will ensure that they can keep their state pension and hard-earned pension
deb_ex.sum: Invites the Lib Dem speaker to welcome the Chancellor's new low-income tax-free allowance for pensioners as a positive Budget measure.

What steps he is taking with Cabinet colleagues to support the creation of jobs for young people.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the same question as the previous member about steps being taken with Cabinet colleagues to support youth job creation.

deb_ex.t: I played my part in the creative industries by playing in bands with names as louche as Street Lethal and Cheap Sweeties.
deb_ex.sum: Offers a humorous personal anecdote about playing in bands as a schoolboy as a prelude to his main question.

deb_ex.t: I’ve got it! In the modern era, that all important first job is increasingly hard to find because of the Chancellor’s jobs tax and the massive 330-page Employment Rights Act 2025.
deb_ex.sum: Argues the Chancellor's jobs tax and the Employment Rights Act are making it harder for young people to find work, and urges the Secretary of State to press the Chancellor to cut the burden on industry.

deb_ex.t: Politicians salami-slicing sentences is a betrayal. It is a betrayal first and foremost of victims.
deb_ex.sum: Uses Scotland's SNP early release plans as a cautionary tale, argues loss of liberty is the core of justice and that politicians who salami-slice sentences betray victims, police and the public.

deb_ex.t: rather than warm words about an EU reset, we had the French ambassador in for an interview sans café
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the damage to perishable seafood exports from Dover delays and calls for the French ambassador to be summoned rather than relying on warm words about an EU reset.

deb_ex.t: refused to put vital public funds into defence firms that have legitimate commercial relationships with our ally Israel
deb_ex.sum: Praises Scotland's military and industrial defence contributions but attacks the Scottish Government for refusing public funds to defence firms with ties to Israel, calling the First Minister a 'fifth columnist' damaging NATO.

deb_ex.t: my constituents want to know whose hand is on the tiller and what course will be set. Is that so unreasonable?
deb_ex.sum: Accuses the Government of brazenly avoiding scrutiny and questions why the new Prime Minister cannot come to the House to explain his plans.

deb_ex.t: As a member of the Business and Trade Committee, it is a delight to see the fruits of Brexit being brought home. Will the Minister confirm that the deal is not contingent on us tak
deb_ex.sum: Conservative member welcomes the deal as a Brexit benefit and asks the Minister to confirm there is no submission to Swiss courts or regulatory alignment, while questioning why similar boldness is not shown with the EU.

deb_ex.t: The Prime Minister’s warm words about rural and coastal communities will be seen, I am afraid, like the chocolate Freddo bar that he said he could not affect the price of: sweet, b
deb_ex.sum: Cooper dismisses the Prime Minister's warm words about rural and coastal communities as insubstantial and ridicules the triple-helix growth theory, demanding much more detail and concrete action.

deb_ex.t: for millions of Britons, vehicles are lifelines not luxuries. The imminent rise in fuel duty comes as tankers are ablaze in the strait of Hormuz
deb_ex.sum: Condemns fuel duty as a revenue grab, argues vehicles are lifelines not luxuries, and questions how family budgets can survive a duty hike alongside rising prices from the Strait of Hormuz conflict.

deb_ex.t: benefit crime has effectively been decriminalised, and the Scottish Conservatives have raised the case of people being coached on how to fiddle
deb_ex.sum: Raises the effective decriminalisation of benefit fraud in Scotland and complaints that DWP disclaims responsibility, arguing there is a moral imperative to act.

deb_ex.t: I have had farmers weeping, too—men in their 80s, with hard knocks enough for many lifetimes under their belts.
deb_ex.sum: Describes the emotional impact of agricultural property relief changes on farming families in rural Scotland, argues inheritance tax is double taxation, and outlines the Conservative plan to abolish it on family homes and restore full agric

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend, who speaks to farmers far more than Labour Front-Bench Members ever do. Indeed, he knows that this is about fairness. We Conservatives believe in rewarding
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on fairness grounds and raises the practical hardship caused by high interest rates on late tax payments and the illiquidity of farm assets when meeting inheritance tax deadlines.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Gentleman for his intervention, but he is talking about adding yet more costs on to businesses. I have heard from farmers who tried inheritance planning but were t
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the life insurance suggestion as an additional cost burden, highlights practical banking obstacles to inheritance planning, and calls on the Government to halt the family farm tax immediately.

deb_ex.t: it seemed to come as a shock to them that it would put as much as £70 or £80 on a tonne of fertiliser
deb_ex.sum: Expresses surprise that the Government did not anticipate the carbon border adjustment mechanism's significant impact on fertiliser costs when it focused on cement and steel.

deb_ex.t: Food security is national security, as the mantra from the Government Benches goes. Yet the reality, I am afraid, is that it is much spun and little done. The family farm tax sent
deb_ex.sum: Condemns the Government's family farm tax, fertiliser tax and red diesel costs as proof of an urban-centric disconnect from rural Britain, and dismisses EU re-entry as no solution for Scottish farmers.

deb_ex.t: One of the great sports in this place is who has the best constituency. Well, National Geographic magazine’s verdict is in and the only place in the UK to get a mention in its “Bes
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates Dumfries and Galloway's inclusion in National Geographic's best places to travel in 2027 and asks the Leader of the House to encourage VisitBritain to promote it.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's commitment to growing cadet forces, especially in underserved communities, and mentions strengthening links with employers to expand opportunities including in Bracknell Forest.

deb_ex.sum: Minister points to existing RAF Cadets cyber-programme being expanded across all cadet forces as evidence the government is already addressing civilian cyber-resilience needs.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms ongoing diplomatic engagement with regional allies through the Foreign Office minister and offers to provide further detail in writing.

deb_ex.sum: Declines to confirm future proscription measures but says all options are being considered and offers the member a meeting with the FCDO minister.

deb_ex.sum: Points British nationals to FCDO consular advice and defends the technical clarity of 'defensive counter air' as established military doctrine.

deb_ex.t: We urge the Houthis to return to a UN-led political pathway, and we will continue to work with regional allies.

deb_ex.t: I can speak here with great comfort, knowing that we will ensure that those processes are met, and that our rules and values are upheld by our allies and partners.

deb_ex.t: Providing defensive counter air to prevent attacks on airports and civilian structures is a fairly significant offering.

deb_ex.t: our military commanders are content that they can meet the deployment and the other tasks that we have set out for them.

deb_ex.t: we do not discuss the assessments that are made, which could impact the safety and security of our military personnel.

deb_ex.t: The Prime Minister has said that we will take a pragmatic approach, and oil and gas will remain part of our future
deb_ex.sum: Repeats the Government's pragmatic position on oil and gas but declines to comment on the specific decisions pending the process.

deb_ex.t: Oil and gas will be part of our energy mix, and the environmental impact assessment that is taking place will take account of Scope 3 emissions
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges oil and gas will remain in the energy mix and confirms Scope 3 emissions will be part of the environmental impact assessment.

deb_ex.t: reducing venting and flaring would represent a cost and efficiency saving. We should be using our energy efficiently
deb_ex.sum: Agrees methane reduction is important for efficiency and the environment, and says she is working domestically and internationally to address venting and flaring.

deb_ex.t: Scope 3 emissions will be part of the environmental impact assessment, which will be given to the Secretary of State and will feed into her decision-making process
deb_ex.sum: Offers to review the BBC report and confirms Scope 3 emissions will be included in the environmental impact assessment informing the Secretary of State's decision.

deb_ex.t: we have expanded the North sea jobs service to support workers. He is right that there is a huge crossover between renewables and oil and gas workers
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the Government's expanded North sea jobs service and agrees the Secretary of State will factor in the crossover between oil and gas and renewables workers.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Lady for her question. I admire her trying to lure me into a conversation on independence and devolution. I am afraid that that is not part of the scope of the dis
deb_ex.sum: Declines to be drawn on devolution or a specific timeline, prioritising the robustness of the process and reaffirming commitment to a just transition for Scottish workers.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for his excellent analysis of why we have ended up here; he is absolutely right. It is on all of us to respect the process. I think that the feeling of the H
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the previous speaker's analysis blaming the Conservatives and defends the need for a robust process before announcing a decision.

deb_ex.t: we also need to make sure that we have other sources of energy. That is why record investment in clean energy has been secured
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the declining basin argument but pivots to highlight government investment in clean energy as the broader solution.

deb_ex.t: we are, at the moment, a price-taker on the international fossil fuel markets, which has an impact on our constituents
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that fossil fuel price volatility harms constituents and highlights the Secretary of State's focus on energy affordability as the Government's response.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Lady for her question and for her passion on this topic. The environmental impact assessment that has been part of the process will take account of Scope 3 emissio
deb_ex.sum: Notes that the environmental impact assessment includes Scope 3 emissions and signals the Government's serious commitment to climate change without pre-empting the decision.

deb_ex.t: we know that climate change is a key issue. We saw the wildfires this summer and, only this week, we saw the Prime Minister talking in his first interventions
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms that process robustness must be respected and that climate change is a central concern, citing the Prime Minister's COP commitment.

deb_ex.t: it was only in August that these consultations closed. There is a lot of interest in this place and outside, and our Secretary of State wants to consider things properly
deb_ex.sum: Defends the pace of decision-making by noting consultations only closed in August and insists proper process is needed to avoid further legal challenges.

deb_ex.t: I cannot make any further comments on these particular projects because of the robust regulatory process that is under way
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member for his views but declines to comment further on the specific projects given the ongoing regulatory process.

deb_ex.t: nobody would say that this Government have not moved at pace in terms of our clean energy mission
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the charge of slow decision-making, noting the consultation only closed in August, and highlights the Government's overall pace on the clean energy mission.

deb_ex.t: I appreciate the strength of feeling—I can hear the strength of feeling on both sides of this House
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the strength of feeling on both sides but declines to comment further on the specific decisions, reaffirming the Government's commitment to an efficient energy system.

deb_ex.t: Getting into any defence of specific areas may lead me to potentially say things that I should not say as it is a decision for the Secretary of State
deb_ex.sum: Declines to defend or challenge any specific element of the Rosebank case and notes the Secretary of State will consider the full environmental impact assessment.

deb_ex.t: I note my hon. Friend’s opinion. As I say, there is a strength of feeling on the different sides of the House. We are noting that, but I will make no comment. On her question about
deb_ex.sum: Notes the range of views without pre-empting the decision and condemns the Conservative suggestion to repeal the Climate Change Act as baffling.

deb_ex.t: The Secretary of State has put energy affordability at the heart of our agenda, and we will continue to do that
deb_ex.sum: Points to the Secretary of State's long-standing commitment to tackling fuel poverty and the Government's record investment in warm homes as the answer to energy affordability concerns.

deb_ex.t: we are very much in favour of evidence-based policymaking
deb_ex.sum: Minister briefly reassures the House that the government is committed to evidence-based policymaking on the fields.

deb_ex.t: the robustness of this process is key. We need to ensure that we respect the process, which will lead to clarity on the decision
deb_ex.sum: Minister welcomes the suggestion about scrutiny and emphasises that the robustness of the process will lead to clarity on the final decision.

deb_ex.t: the Secretary of State will make a decision in due course, taking account of the new evidence that she has received
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges the North Sea's wide impacts on jobs, investment and communities and confirms the Secretary of State will make a decision in due course based on new evidence.

deb_ex.sum: Outlines government steps including launching a climate and nature security taskforce and an upcoming wildfire summit, framing the summer's extreme weather as vindicating the need for action.

deb_ex.t: We are indeed living through extremes of climate change, and we felt that so intensely this summer. This should encourage us all to accelerate our efforts to mitigate, but also to
deb_ex.sum: Outlines government plans to introduce passive cooling measures in capital funded schemes including solar shading, shutters and cooler building materials under the warm homes plan.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is a long-standing champion of retrofitting and of new build. We on this side of the House are proud of the future building standards, which require all new homes to
deb_ex.sum: Defends the future building standards requiring new homes to be zero carbon-ready and reduce overheating risk, and notes a full technical review is under way to keep regulations fit for the future.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Gentleman for that question; I am a little unsure how it relates to this question grouping. We are looking at how to ensure we align the— [ Interruption. ] I am sp
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the question while explaining that solar farm policies are being aligned with DEFRA's land use framework to deliver clean power alongside nature restoration.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Lady for her very important question. This is one of the reasons why, before this summer, we launched the climate and nature security taskforce. As I said, sadly i
deb_ex.sum: Points to the climate and nature security taskforce as the vehicle for addressing food security impacts of extreme weather and confirms close joint working with DEFRA on cascading climate and nature risks.

deb_ex.t: all eligible households can benefit from the expanded boiler upgrade scheme, which now includes air-to-air heat pumps that can heat and cool our homes
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government action on the warm homes plan, including expanded boiler upgrade scheme covering air-to-air heat pumps for heating and cooling.

deb_ex.t: We want to go faster to make sure that new homes are built to resilient standards. That is why we have committed to the net zero standards
deb_ex.sum: Outlines planned passive cooling measures, devolved delivery of the warm homes plan, and commitments to net zero standards and overheating building regulations to make homes fit for the future.

deb_ex.t: we are working with many heritage organisations to determine the best way to do that. We are constantly learning to make sure that there is mitigation and adaptation
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the challenge of retrofitting harder properties and says the government is working with heritage organisations to find solutions, promising to keep the Member updated.

deb_ex.t: if we want to tackle the climate crisis and to protect the people and places we love, at some point we have to stop releasing polluting gases
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that this summer's weather brought the climate crisis home to many UK residents and firmly reaffirms net zero as the Government's goal.

deb_ex.t: We have strong protections in national planning policy that guide developers to avoid peatland and, where that is not possible, to mitigate.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the questioner and sets out the government's position: peatlands are vital habitats and strong national planning protections exist, with further work ongoing with DEFRA.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the importance of peat, highlights the £47 million restoration announcement, and commits to following up with DEFRA to review policy options while keeping the questioner informed.

deb_ex.sum: Declines to comment on the specific planning application but affirms the government's commitment to minimising environmental impacts of all clean energy infrastructure.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights the role of peatland restoration in slowing waterflow and reducing flood risk, citing Moors for the Future projects, and asks the Government to continue supporting healthy peatlands.

deb_ex.sum: Condemns the auto-commencement clause as reckless and argues the Bill's safeguards against coercion are inadequate, with the assessment focused on medical prognosis rather than social and psychological vulnerability.

deb_ex.sum: Catalogues decades of failed Conservative promises on social care reform and urges the Minister to commit to fully implementing Baroness Casey's report when published.

deb_ex.sum: Supports Clause 17 repealing the presumption of contact, paying tribute to Claire Throssell, citing 68 children killed over 30 years, and warning that judicial culture must also change alongside the law.

deb_ex.sum: Blames privatisation for Royal Mail's decline and argues vulnerable constituents in Calder Valley are hardest hit. Welcomes the Minister's efforts but says the service is still not good enough.

deb_ex.sum: Cites research showing death rates among young adults in the north are 42% higher than in the south and asks whether the Prime Minister's growth-in-every-postcode pledge will extend to health outcomes.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the statement and cites cases of fatal domestic abuse to press the Lord Chancellor on how changes will better protect victims and ensure psychological harm including coercive control is properly recognised.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights Portsmouth's deprivation and cultural assets, and champions its bid to become UK city of culture, calling for the first such city in the south of England.

deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to highlight that parental leave is effectively a class privilege, with 90% taken by the top half of earners, pricing lower-paid workers out of bonding with their babies.

deb_ex.sum: Argues Portsmouth has been overlooked in investment decisions and asks the Minister to ensure the city is central to growth plans.

deb_ex.t: Argentina was defeated and, above all, the Falkland Islanders have made their choice: they want to remain British.
deb_ex.sum: Speaking for Portsmouth constituents with deep connections to the 1982 conflict, insists the issue is settled by the islanders' choice and demands Argentina and Trump stop treating the Falklands as a bargaining chip.

deb_ex.t: the focus is too often on what young people are doing, rather than on the adults who are grooming and coercing them
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the announcement but presses the Secretary of State to say more about work to identify and disrupt adults who groom and coerce children online.

deb_ex.sum: Supports the call for regulation, noting that reputable funeral directors themselves want robust oversight.

deb_ex.t: I know that this Government do not believe there is any equivalence between the lawful service of our military personnel and indefensible acts of terrorism.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill and the Government's amendments on veteran protections, rejects Braverman's characterisation of armed forces confidence, and defends the Government's record of support for service personnel.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the announcement as measured and responsible, asks how energy independence will feed into national resilience planning and seeks assurance the Warm Homes Plan will not be slowed.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights the Children's Commissioner finding Portsmouth is one of the worst places to be a child and access post-16 education, calling it a wake-up call for the local Lib Dem council.

deb_ex.sum: Describes constituents driven into debt and mental distress by Capita's failures and presses the Minister on what consequences Capita has already faced and whether further failure will bring further penalties.

deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to note that Barclays' profits are up, implicitly defending the bank surcharge against Conservative claims it will damage the banking sector.

Around 59% of children in the most deprived areas reach a good level of development by the time they start primary school compared with 79% in the least deprived areas. Babyzone is
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the development gap between deprived and affluent areas and praises Babyzone charity for opening a hub in Easterhouse, calling for a debate on closing that gap.

deb_ex.t: Around 59% of children in the most deprived areas reach a good level of development by the time they start primary school compared with 79% in the least deprived areas.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the development gap between deprived and affluent children, praises Babyzone's work opening a hub in Easterhouse, and calls for parliamentary time to debate closing that gap.

deb_ex.t: What steps he is taking with Cabinet colleagues to support regeneration in Scotland through the Pride in Place programme.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the minister what steps are being taken with Cabinet colleagues to support regeneration in Scotland through the Pride in Place programme.

deb_ex.t: the key strength of the Pride in Place programme is not only that it is investing £20 million in long-forgotten places, like Springburn, Barmulloch and Balornock
deb_ex.sum: Praises the Pride in Place programme and highlights local leader Jim Hope BEM as an example of trusting communities to shape their own futures in Springburn, Barmulloch and Balornock.

deb_ex.t: What steps he is taking to support young people into employment.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the government is taking to support young people into employment.

deb_ex.t: The Prime Minister hit the nail on the head when he said that too many young people have been failed by a schools system that focused too much “on the university route, and not eno
deb_ex.sum: Argues that investing in young people's skills and opportunities is preferable to leaving them on benefits, citing young constituents' desire for work and purpose.

deb_ex.t: Q11. A recent BBC “Disclosure” documentary exposed violence, open drug dealing, child exploitation, and a staggering 1,200 sexual offences recorded in Glasgow city centre in the ye
deb_ex.sum: Raises serious public safety issues in Glasgow city centre including violence and sexual offences and calls for a co-ordinated government response, while criticising SNP underfunding and Reform's exploitation of the situation.

deb_ex.t: Royal Mail was once widely respected and trusted, but it is now too often a cause of frustration and anger for our constituents. Year after year, Royal Mail is falling short of the
deb_ex.sum: Recounts constituent harm from missed NHS appointments and failures of the NHS barcode workaround in Scotland, urging Royal Mail management to take real responsibility and meet its targets.

deb_ex.t: I hope that the promise from management to meet targets by early next year is signed for and delivered on time.
deb_ex.sum: Urges Royal Mail management to take responsibility rather than blame external factors, highlights rising stamp prices and poor worker conditions, and calls for the promised improvements to be delivered.

deb_ex.t: Will the Prime Minister accept my invitation to return to FARE with the Work and Pensions Secretary to discuss making that principle a guide for supporting young people
deb_ex.sum: Draws on personal experience of Easterhouse deprivation to urge the Prime Minister to adopt FARE Scotland's personalised approach as a national guide for supporting young people.

deb_ex.t: his three-year-old daughter was involved in a terrifying near-miss with a recklessly ridden e-bike. The unsafe use of these vehicles is a growing threat to public safety.
deb_ex.issue: illegal use of e-bikes and e-scooters
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent's near-miss involving a recklessly ridden e-bike and calls for a debate on cross-border cooperation between Scottish and UK governments on dangerous e-bike use.

deb_ex.t: Will the Government ensure that there are criminal sanctions on officeholders who fail to whistle blow when they know or become aware of political interference or wrongdoing?
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister to consider establishing an office of the whistleblower with legal protections and criminal sanctions on officeholders who fail to report known political interference or wrongdoing.

deb_ex.t: Last month, the High Court issued its judgment permitting the development of 119 homes in a flood risk area in the village of Yatton in Somerset. The site had failed the flood risk
deb_ex.sum: Raises a High Court judgment permitting development on a flood-risk site in Yatton that failed the sequential test, and urges DEFRA and MHCLG to jointly assess its potentially precedent-setting national impact.

deb_ex.t: If Defence Secretaries are misled by their Departments, I do not really understand his faith in leaders of intelligence services and others not being able to hide the truth
deb_ex.sum: Questions the shadow Secretary of State's faith in intelligence service leaders by citing a former Conservative colleague who believes he was misled by his own Department when Defence Secretary.

deb_ex.t: the Ministry of Defence is in the High Court in London, trying very hard to silence the Chinook families by saying that they are out of time
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the irony that the MoD is in court trying to silence the Chinook families on the very day Parliament debates a duty of candour, arguing the Bill must cover the MoD.

deb_ex.t: If the rates of the specialists and professionals who are supporting the public bodies came down, and matched the rising rate of legal aid for the support of those individuals
deb_ex.sum: Argues that true equity of arms requires legal aid rates for families to match those of public bodies' specialists, making investigations simpler for courts and inquests.

deb_ex.t: would-be passengers could not find any details or get through to the operator, and they were left standing in extreme heat at the roadside
deb_ex.sum: Raises a case where passengers were left stranded due to poor information about a replacement shuttle bus, and calls on the Minister to ensure operators and local authorities provide clear, timely information during disruptions.

deb_ex.t: I herald the passage into law of the Public Office (Accountability) Bill, but many will be disappointed that the judge in Tuesday’s High Court hearing had to rule, under current le
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Public Office (Accountability) Bill but urges the incoming Prime Minister to ensure victims of cover-ups can discover and challenge them in time, citing the Chinook families' High Court defeat.

deb_ex.t: May I encourage the Church Commissioners to support the Church in facilitating community events? Wells cathedral and Wells bishop’s palace are at the centre of an amazing programme
deb_ex.sum: Raises a local issue about a stop notice served on a family farm in Wells that has supported community events at the bishop's palace, asking the Church Commissioners to intervene.

deb_ex.t: this is just opportunistic profiteering at the expense of people who are vulnerable, and actually, when people have died, the families really are catastrophically affected
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituency case where a property has been unsellable since 2022 due to landlord restrictions, exit fees and age requirements, describing it as opportunistic profiteering against vulnerable people.

deb_ex.t: One of the retirement buildings in my patch has just been offered the repainting of its windows for £240,000. I think that works out at over £5,000 per flat.
deb_ex.sum: Seeks clarification that management companies such as FirstPort will be captured within proposed legislation, citing an extreme example of a £240,000 window repainting quote.

deb_ex.t: what assessment has the Secretary of State made of issuing alerts on a regional or county basis for important but more local emergencies, such as bluetongue outbreaks
deb_ex.sum: Munt asks what assessment has been made of issuing regional or county-level emergency alerts for localised events such as bluetongue outbreaks in rural areas.

deb_ex.t: Suicide is the leading cause of death among under-35s. After nearly 30 years, Papyrus, the national youth suicide prevention charity, went into administration two days ago
deb_ex.sum: Marks World Suicide Prevention Day and raises the sudden collapse of Papyrus, including the closure of its 24/7 crisis HopeLine, sharing a constituent's fear for their young adult child, and urging immediate government action on crisis supp

deb_ex.t: What steps she is taking to improve the student loan system.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Secretary of State what steps she is taking to improve the student loan system.

deb_ex.t: Young constituents tell me that they cannot trust the fees system when a change of Government can mean a change to the terms of their loans.
deb_ex.sum: Argues the frozen repayment threshold, high living costs and lack of trust in the system are harming disadvantaged students, and calls for uprating thresholds, restoring maintenance grants and creating an independent watchdog.

deb_ex.t: the NHS maternity survey says that 18% of parents reported that their concerns during labour and birth were not taken seriously.
deb_ex.sum: Raises constituents' experience and cites NHS data showing 18% of parents felt their concerns during labour were not taken seriously, pressing for staff to listen and act on parental concerns.

deb_ex.t: Two weeks ago, the Liberal Democrats were clear that if Iran or the IRGC were confirmed to be behind the plot at the RAF base at Fairford, every Iranian diplomat who assisted in ac
deb_ex.sum: Presses the government on why, given confirmed Iranian involvement in the Fairford plot, Iranian diplomats up to and including the ambassador have not been expelled.

deb_ex.t: Its business rates liability this year has increased by almost 2,700%, from £1,070 per annum to £28,820 per annum, with no meaningful warning
deb_ex.sum: Raises the case of a Somerset camping business facing a near 2,700% business rates increase and asks for a ministerial meeting to discuss the impact on rural hospitality businesses.

deb_ex.t: Metachromatic leukodystrophy, known as MLD, is a devastating genetic disease that progressively destroys the nervous system. Children born apparently healthy lose their ability to
deb_ex.sum: Describes the devastating impact of MLD on children and calls for newborn heel-prick screening to be extended to include the condition at just 17p per test, requesting a ministerial meeting with DHSC.

deb_ex.t: most agents actually only managed to get in eight, nine or 10 applications in the very short window that was available
deb_ex.sum: Raises barriers facing farmers including poor broadband and limited agent capacity, and presses the Minister to commission a high-speed review by the RPA before 2027.

deb_ex.t: I submitted a written parliamentary question to the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs on 28 April. I am awaiting a response.
deb_ex.sum: Raises a point of order about an unanswered written parliamentary question submitted to DEFRA on 28 April and asks the Speaker for advice on how to obtain a response.

deb_ex.t: Will he accelerate the decoupling? Can he offer a timetable in which he will do that?
deb_ex.sum: Calls on the Minister to accelerate decoupling of electricity prices from wholesale gas prices and asks for a firm timetable.

deb_ex.t: This affects children, directly and cumulatively, and indicates a lamentable lack of care and compassion for young people.
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituent's case of £29,000 in written-off child maintenance arrears and calls on the Leader of the House to urge a full review and reform of the Child Maintenance Service.

deb_ex.t: what specific political and diplomatic conditions would need to be met for the Government to withdraw this defensive support, and how will Parliament be kept informed on progress?
deb_ex.sum: Asks the minister what specific political and diplomatic conditions would trigger withdrawal of defensive support and how Parliament will be kept informed.

deb_ex.t: The Church’s lead safeguarding bishop has said that mandatory reporting should take precedence over confidences passed under the seal of confession, which is to be lauded. Confessi
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the lead safeguarding bishop's position that mandatory reporting should override the seal of confession, and presses the minister to confirm what concrete steps the Church will take to act on this.

deb_ex.t: Royal Mail is advertising for more posties but applicants do not even need to provide a CV. These people would be expected to deliver documents of prime importance
deb_ex.sum: Raises concerns about Royal Mail advertising for posties without requiring CVs, given the sensitive documents they handle, and supports calls for better practice.

deb_ex.t: I applaud what the Secretary of State is doing. However, would it not be sensible to stop the business of fire engineers, paid for by the building owners, using PAS 9980 to sign of
deb_ex.sum: Broadly supports the Secretary of State but argues that fire engineers paid by building owners should not be able to use PAS 9980 to sign off dangerous cladding as acceptable.

deb_ex.t: Community transport minibuses, such as Mendip Community Transport, are a lifeline for rural communities, but the minibus driving test is costly—it costs up to £2,000 per volunteer—
deb_ex.sum: Raises the high cost and difficulty of the minibus driving test for volunteers and asks the Minister to meet her and recognise the sector's own driver awareness scheme as a licensing route.

deb_ex.t: With just 23% of adults in Somerset having seen an NHS dentist in the last two years
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that only 23% of Somerset adults have seen an NHS dentist recently and calls on the Government to reform dental services and end the south-west's dental desert.

deb_ex.sum: Supports new homes but presses for guarantees that GP provision will keep pace with development, citing Barking Riverside where GPs already serve 20% more patients than average.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Minister for her statement and agree that London is indeed a powerhouse for growth. However, as a Member of Parliament for an outer London borough, I know, and she will
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the growth agenda but asks the Minister to confirm that job creation and industrialisation priorities will reach outer London constituencies such as hers.

deb_ex.t: Safe and secure housing is the foundation of a good life, and the availability of social and affordable housing plays an important part in the provision of housing in this country,
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill's right-to-buy reforms, including the 35-year exemption for new social homes and 100% retention of receipts by councils, drawing on her experience as a council leader.

deb_ex.t: record interest rates, which completely decimated housing revenue accounts for councils up and down the country
deb_ex.sum: Explains that record interest rates undermined councils' housing revenue accounts and that the Conservative measure did not go as far as the current proposals, also welcoming domestic violence protections in the Bill.

deb_ex.t: a shared ownership property that is categorised as affordable has become unaffordable for many of my constituents
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill and its shared ownership review, sharing constituency cases where shared ownership charges have made supposedly affordable homes unaffordable, and expresses broad support for more social and affordable housing.

deb_ex.t: What support her Department provides to councils for SEND services.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what support the Department provides to councils for SEND services.

deb_ex.t: Creating additional SEND spaces is critical for my constituency as we have had a 100% increase in education, health and care plans and an extra 1,000 students now need special educ
deb_ex.sum: Highlights a 100% rise in EHC plans in her constituency and calls for the Schools Bill to include compulsory SEND training for mainstream teachers.

deb_ex.t: does she agree that building a national care service means that we can improve care for older people but also create rewarding career pathways for young people
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister to confirm that the national care service will create rewarding career pathways for young unemployed people, drawing on high youth unemployment in her constituency.

deb_ex.t: What steps his Department is taking to oppose the expansion of illegal settlements in the west bank.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the Department is taking to oppose illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank.

deb_ex.t: Thank you, Mr Speaker. I welcome the Government’s new sanctions to address illegal settlement expansion in the west bank. We have all watched in great horror as Palestinians face i
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Government's sanctions but calls on the Secretary of State to go further by sanctioning Israeli Defence Minister Katz and Major General Bluth, who are implicated in war crimes in the West Bank.

deb_ex.t: that around £1 billion of surplus that is locked up in the scheme is used to give members a new bonus pension now

deb_ex.t: I do not think that anybody could explain to a retired miner in Mansfield why his bonus should be less secure than the one paid to someone he worked alongside

deb_ex.t: Those on the Conservative Benches spent five years doing nothing for mineworkers.

deb_ex.sum: Puts four specific questions to the Minister on surplus sharing, bonus pension protection, timely payout of surpluses and the long-term future of both schemes, and calls for action before more pensioners die.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights that around 15% of Derby South households are in fuel poverty and asks the Secretary of State for reassurance that as much help as possible is coming.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that the Bill strengthens the Church of England by bringing in more voices and thanks the Minister for the legislation.

deb_ex.t: families have seen inquiries established, reports published and recommendations accepted, only for the same failures to recur again and again. We must break this cycle
