deb_ex.t: it just adds to the weight of evidence showing that we need urgent and immediate action. We cannot wait. We cannot let those families down.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that the case raised is representative of far too many families, reinforcing the need for urgent and immediate action.

deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to bereavement charities while noting they are often filling gaps the NHS should cover, and stresses the need for personalised, family-centred care that treats every patient as an individual.

deb_ex.t: When a mother or parent says that something is wrong, that concern must be taken seriously.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that listening to mothers and families is the defining feature of good maternity care and calls for a national action plan setting out entitlements covering safety, dignity, informed choice and compassionate communication.

deb_ex.t: No healthcare professional should be forced to choose between remaining silent about unsafe care and risking their livelihood by raising it.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the point about care not being available when most needed and signals he will outline the full package of support required.

deb_ex.t: Families have heard promises before, they have watched recommendations accepted, and they have been assured that lessons would be learned, only to see another family experience the same failures.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes Royal Marines action against shadow fleet vessels but presses the Secretary of State on whether the UK has the capability to intercept drones launched from them.

deb_ex.t: T4. I was pleased to see co-operation with the Netherlands on a new amphibious fleet in the defence investment plan. I spent two years of my career working alongside the Dutch mari
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Anglo-Dutch amphibious fleet co-operation in the defence investment plan and presses for a timeline on when operational amphibious ships can be expected given HMS Albion and HMS Bulwark are out of service.

deb_ex.t: Do you think we are closer to a nuclear negotiation today than we were back then? Do you think that negotiating at the start would have been a better approach
deb_ex.sum: Asks the shadow minister whether she believes nuclear negotiations are closer now than at the time of the JCPOA and whether earlier diplomacy would have been preferable.

deb_ex.t: I thank the right hon. Lady. She talks about the UK’s military support in the conflict. I wonder whether she is suggesting that we should have provided support to the Americans dur
deb_ex.sum: Asks the shadow minister to clarify whether she is advocating direct military support to the US during initial strikes or some other form of military assistance.

deb_ex.t: President Milei has coupled his renewed sovereignty claim with an increase in defence spending and plans to expand the naval base at Tierra del Fuego.
deb_ex.sum: Notes Argentina's increased defence spending and naval base expansion alongside its sovereignty claim, and asks whether threat assessments have been updated and defences are adequate.

deb_ex.t: Will the Foreign Secretary now make it clear that such threats will not stop the UK upholding international law and the right of people to self-determination
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the sanctions as the right moral response and asks the Foreign Secretary to make clear that Israeli threats about the Falkland Islands will not deter the UK from upholding international law.

deb_ex.t: 500 civilians were killed in a strike on a single Hamas target. To give a UK example, something similar happened against three former British servicemen at the World Central Kitchen
deb_ex.sum: Raises the 'NAZA' documentary on IDF targeting systems in Gaza and asks for Government accountability on the killing of British World Central Kitchen workers.

deb_ex.t: Two hundred and sixty-four members of our armed forces were murdered by terrorists. They had their unresolved cases terminated by the 2023 legacy Act.
deb_ex.sum: Supports the carry-over motion, sharing harrowing stories of Troubles victims still seeking justice, and argues the legacy Act must be replaced to give families a chance at truth.

deb_ex.t: are the Government considering taking this step against the Houthis, or are they looking at proscribing the organisation as a terrorist group?
deb_ex.sum: Ballinger welcomes the IRGC designation and asks whether the government is considering proscribing the Houthis as a terrorist organisation given their Iranian-backed attacks.

deb_ex.t: is the asset of community value not a better mechanism for doing that than the Bill we are debating?
deb_ex.sum: Suggests that assets of community value are a better mechanism than the Bill for communities wishing to repurpose or protect heritage pubs.

deb_ex.t: I would also like to congratulate the organisers of the Halesowen beer, cider and gin festival at Halesowen cricket club.
deb_ex.sum: Congratulates the Warrington Oktoberfest organisers and adds praise for the Halesowen beer, cider and gin festival in his own constituency as another example of community-building through local hospitality events.

deb_ex.t: Does she agree that the steps that the Chancellor is already making to reduce business rates for pubs will help publicans and heritage pubs in particular to continue?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the burden of energy costs and business rates on publicans and supports the Chancellor's steps to reduce business rates for pubs, calling for further reform shifting rates from high streets to large online businesses.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is giving an important speech. I was reflecting on the town of Stevenage only being 80 years old. In the Bill, heritage pubs are defined as those that are more than
deb_ex.sum: Points out that the Bill's 150-year age threshold would exclude new town pubs like those in Stevenage, arguing the Bill is exclusionary of newer communities with their own heritage.

deb_ex.t: I share his outrage and that of the communities he mentioned. I notice that there have been difficulties with the process of getting it rebuilt.
deb_ex.sum: Expresses solidarity with the outrage over the Crooked House demolition and probes the promoter on the timeline for rebuilding the pub.

deb_ex.t: That is a sensible suggestion. I like the hon. Gentleman’s proposal that the public should be informed about a potential sale—or, indeed, about any other changes listed in the Bill
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the public notification proposal but probes how residents without internet access would be informed about a potential sale.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member is being very generous with interventions; I do appreciate that. I thank him for recognising that the national policy planning framework has made positive changes t
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the promoter for acknowledging NPPF improvements but asks whether the Bill addresses upwards-only rent reviews, which create financial pressure on pub operators.

deb_ex.t: because there has been such a reduction in number of people who are smoking, especially at a younger age, in due course it may become a benefit for pubs
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Tobacco and Vapes Act and the rising age limit, and suggests that as smoking declines among the young, the loss of indoor smoking may eventually cease to be a drag on pub trade.

deb_ex.t: There are real challenges with rogue developers, not just in the Crooked House case, but across the board.
deb_ex.sum: Raises a constituency case of a collapsed supporting wall and rogue developer inaction, and asks whether the Government could do more to challenge such situations.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is making an excellent speech. I am reflecting on my experience in Halesowen; it is a built-up area rather than a residential area, but unfortunately, we have had re
deb_ex.sum: Argues that years of cuts to local government have made pubs and other community spaces even more vital, making their continuation more important than ever.

deb_ex.t: Those fantastic names that have lasted for years and years and years should continue; pubs should not be rebranded with random generic chain names.
deb_ex.sum: Raises concern about pubs losing their historic names to generic chain branding, arguing that the heritage of pub names is as important as the buildings themselves.

deb_ex.t: Will my hon. Friend give the House an answer as to which Miliband he supported?
deb_ex.sum: Playfully asks the hon. Member to reveal which Miliband he supported in the 2010 Labour leadership election.

deb_ex.t: Warrington might be very similar to the Black Country, in that canals were historically used to pass barrels of ale from brewery to pub.
deb_ex.sum: Draws a connection between Warrington's canal network and the Black Country, asking whether the Sankey Canal was historically used to transport beer from breweries to pubs.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend continues to make an excellent speech. On the subject of planning systems and frameworks, does she share my concern that, despite the good intentions of this Bill, t
deb_ex.sum: Expresses concern that additional layers of bureaucracy created by the Bill could cause more friction for pub owners and planning authorities than intended.

deb_ex.t: it is being repurposed to be a community centre by an excellent community group called Stepping Out, which supports young disabled people
deb_ex.sum: Cites a derelict pub in Halesowen being converted into a community centre for disabled young people as a positive example of heritage building reuse.

deb_ex.t: the opportunity for them to engage with their Member of Parliament, in a space that they are comfortable in and among their community, is vital
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the point about pubs as community engagement spaces, noting their value for reaching disillusioned voters in deprived areas.

deb_ex.t: there seems to be a gap in education—in giving the community the tools to enable them to do that
deb_ex.sum: Suggests local government should do more to educate communities on tools like assets of community value to help save pubs and community spaces.

deb_ex.t: What a magnificent story! I just want to reflect on the community value that pubs and breweries can add, on top of their location and heritage. In my constituency, the Hunting Tree
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the Hunting Tree pub in his constituency as an example of community value generated through new ownership and charitable activities.

deb_ex.t: the third-best cider pub in the country is found in Halesowen
deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to praise cider options at a pub in Halesowen and broaden the discussion to the range of drinks available in pubs across the country.

deb_ex.t: the new powers that the Prime Minister has given to restrict places such as vape shops and betting shops on the high street
deb_ex.sum: Notes the Government's new high street powers and asks the speaker to comment on the positive impact of microbars opening in empty shops.

deb_ex.t: I strongly welcome new clause 32, which requires the commission or any inquest to take into account the context in which soldiers are operating.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Bill and government amendments, particularly new clause 32 protecting veterans' context and amendment 192 preventing repeat investigations, drawing on conversations with ICRIR officials.

deb_ex.t: the same preparations will help folk in the UK be prepared for both those attacks and natural disasters.

deb_ex.sum: Corrects the previous speaker by pointing out that the Budget includes a 4% reduction in heating oil tariffs and a £100 payment for heating oil users this winter.

deb_ex.t: the Chancellor he did commit to reaching 3% of GDP by 2030. Can the right hon. Gentleman say when the Conservatives reached 2.7% of GDP on defence
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the shadow minister by pointing out the Chancellor did commit to 3% of GDP on defence by 2030 and asks when the Conservatives themselves reached 2.7%.

deb_ex.t: British attitudes survey, which in 2024 found that 73% of the British public supported assisted dying and have done so over the last 20 years
deb_ex.sum: Edwards disputes the polls cited by Shannon, pointing to the British Attitudes Survey showing 73% public support over 20 years and criticising the methodology of opposing polls.

deb_ex.t: I will give way to my hon. Friend the Member for Hackney South and Shoreditch
deb_ex.sum: Edwards gives way to Dame Meg Hillier.

deb_ex.t: I am asking Members of this House to send the Bill back to the House of Lords so that they can continue their important work
deb_ex.sum: Edwards clarifies the Bill incorporates two previously agreed amendments and asks Members to send it back to the Lords so they can continue scrutiny and amendment.

deb_ex.t: Her engagement with those from all sides of the debate, particularly in Committee, delivered a stronger Bill
deb_ex.sum: Edwards agrees it would set a dangerous precedent and pays tribute to Kim Leadbeater's work on the previous Bill, noting it produced stronger safeguards and prompted action on palliative care funding.

deb_ex.t: Everybody should have access to good-quality palliative, hospice and end-of-life care in their final moments
deb_ex.sum: Edwards agrees improving palliative care is a priority supported by the Prime Minister and argues all constituents deserve access to good end-of-life care.

deb_ex.t: organisations that provide that care, though, their services cannot address pain and suffering in all circumstances
deb_ex.sum: Edwards notes that even organisations providing palliative care acknowledge it cannot address all pain and suffering, citing testimony from medically expert Members during the Bill's previous passage.

deb_ex.t: cancer having eaten away at their carotid artery. We felt their frustration when the maximum dose of sedatives could not alleviate the choking
deb_ex.sum: Edwards recounts harrowing cases of terminal patients—including those facing faecal vomiting, arterial bleeding while conscious, and suffocation—to argue they deserved choice and a dignified death.

deb_ex.t: we can, and must, both improve palliative care and support assisted dying
deb_ex.sum: Edwards argues both improving palliative care and legalising assisted dying must be pursued together to create a holistic end-of-life care system offering choice and dignity.

deb_ex.t: the four-year implementation period provided for at the end of the Bill would give us the opportunity to work together to improve palliative care
deb_ex.sum: Edwards responds that the Bill's four-year implementation period would provide time to improve palliative care alongside assisted dying, creating the holistic system she advocates.

deb_ex.t: nobody would be receiving assisted dying until 2031 at the earliest. That would be too late for many people, but it would be plenty of time
deb_ex.sum: Edwards notes no one would receive assisted dying until 2031 at the earliest, providing ample time to improve palliative care in parallel.

deb_ex.t: as the time of death gets closer, the accuracy of the diagnosis is increased
deb_ex.sum: Edwards explains the six-month threshold was drawn from international evidence showing prognosis accuracy increases as death approaches, reducing the risk of misdiagnosis.

deb_ex.t: now it is time for us to send this assisted dying Bill back to the House of Lords, so that it can finish what it started
deb_ex.sum: Edwards calls on the House to send the Bill back to the Lords to complete scrutiny, praising the robust but courteous debate of the previous Session.

deb_ex.t: The Government have been clear, as the Government of the previous Prime Minister were, that they remain neutral on assisted dying
deb_ex.sum: Edwards states the Government remains neutral on assisted dying but is committed to ensuring workable legislation, pointing to assurances given at Third Reading of the previous Bill.

deb_ex.t: I am asking Members today to start the process of sending this Bill back to the House of Lords, so that they can continue their important function
deb_ex.sum: Edwards concludes by urging Members to vote to send the Bill to the Lords so peers can fulfil their constitutional role of scrutinising and refining legislation.

deb_ex.t: Members should be in no doubt that the Bill we sent the Lords last year was robust.
deb_ex.sum: Asserts that the Bill sent to the Lords last year was robust and Members should have no doubt about that.

deb_ex.t: The Bill was expertly drafted by the Office of the Parliamentary Counsel and developed with comprehensive technical advice from officials
deb_ex.sum: Emphasises that the Bill was expertly drafted by the Office of the Parliamentary Counsel with comprehensive technical advice from DHSC and MoJ officials.

deb_ex.t: I am confident in saying to this House that the Bill before us today is a well-designed, safe piece of legislation.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges government neutrality on assisted dying but argues the Bill before the House is well-designed, safe and legally robust.

deb_ex.t: the Bill is explicit that it does not apply to people with a disability.
deb_ex.sum: Responds to the equality concern by pointing out that the Bill explicitly states it does not apply to people with a disability.

deb_ex.t: It is important that we are giving disabled people the same rights as other people.
deb_ex.sum: Argues there is no uniform view among disabled people on assisted dying and that the Bill gives disabled people the same rights as others, while being clear it applies only to terminally ill adults with six months to live.

deb_ex.t: No, I will not give way. I will make some progress
deb_ex.sum: Declines further interventions and signals intention to continue making progress with the speech.

deb_ex.t: As has been mentioned, the Bill has been subject to hundreds of hours of scrutiny, and amendments have been made to strengthen its safeguards, but that does not mean it cannot be s
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges hundreds of hours of scrutiny and amendments already made, while welcoming the prospect of further amendments in the Lords including on eating disorders and matters raised with medical and hospice bodies.

deb_ex.t: All I am asking the Chamber to do today is to send the Bill back to the House of Lords so it can continue its work
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the claim that amending a Bill means it is deficient, and explains the aim is simply to send the Bill back to the Lords to continue interrupted scrutiny.

deb_ex.t: There were a number of amendments around points of clarification—some external organisations wanted some words made a little clearer, although they seem robust to me—that I certain
deb_ex.sum: Indicates some Lords amendments sought clarificatory wording changes which she views as robust but believes could be made in the Lords stage.

deb_ex.t: Taking the approach I have outlined respects both the will of this House, as expressed in June 2025, and allows the usual parliamentary processes to continue.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that proceeding as outlined respects the will of the House as expressed in June 2025 and allows normal parliamentary processes to continue.

deb_ex.t: That is a part of our usual parliamentary process and the hon. Lady is right to raise that point. By sending the Bill back to the Lords as it stands, we will prevent that same smal
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the procedural point on suggested amendments and argues that sending the Bill as it stands will prevent the same peers from filibustering it again.

deb_ex.t: peers in the House of Lords will accept that important distinction between their Chamber and ours, and fulfil their role in the usual way.
deb_ex.sum: Expresses hope that Lords will accept their constitutional role and return an amended Bill for a final Commons vote before Royal Assent.

deb_ex.t: a small number of unelected peers filibustered legislation that was supported by this Chamber. That is not how our democracy is supposed to function.
deb_ex.sum: States she would accept the Bill being voted down through proper democratic process but cannot accept unelected peers having filibustered legislation supported by the elected Chamber.

deb_ex.t: a multidisciplinary panel of people with different perspectives who were trained in spotting coercion—a psychiatrist, a legal expert and a social worker
deb_ex.sum: Explains that the judicial safeguard was replaced by a multidisciplinary panel including a psychiatrist, legal expert and social worker specifically trained to detect coercion, arguing this is a stronger not weaker protection.

deb_ex.t: It is not acceptable that the outcome of those deliberations has not been respected. We owe it to the people we represent to find a resolution
deb_ex.sum: Appeals to the House to respect the outcome of Members' careful deliberations over nearly a year and insists a resolution must be reached within this Parliament.

deb_ex.t: There was a Committee that had hundreds of hours of scrutiny and properly kicked the tyres on the robustness of this legislation.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the call for further Commons Committee scrutiny, arguing the House has already done its job through hundreds of hours in Committee and the Bill should now return to the Lords to complete their scrutiny.

deb_ex.t: people who are themselves terminally ill and who, due to the passage of time, may never get the opportunity to choose a dignified death
deb_ex.sum: Edwards urges the House not to lose sight of terminally ill people in the gallery who are relying on this legislation and may never benefit from it themselves.

deb_ex.t: If I had known that assisted dying was an option, a weight would have been lifted from my mind for the last 10 years.
deb_ex.sum: Edwards shares the personal story of Christie Arntsen, a terminal cancer patient, to illustrate the fear caused by the absence of an assisted dying option.

deb_ex.t: the fear and worry for those who know that palliative care may not be enough to avoid a difficult and painful death
deb_ex.sum: Edwards argues that the status quo imposes fear and suffering on the terminally ill and that voluntary assisted dying systems abroad show a better way.

deb_ex.t: the Bill allows them not to be involved in the process if they do not wish to be
deb_ex.sum: Edwards responds that opinion is divided in the palliative care community and that the Bill already allows clinicians to opt out.

deb_ex.t: they cannot understand how, having secured the support of the people they elected to represent them, the issue that is so important to them has been frustrated
deb_ex.sum: Edwards closes by quoting Elise Burns, a terminally ill constituent who has since died, and calls on MPs to assert the Commons' democratic will by supporting the Bill's Second Reading.

deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the Department is taking with the beauty industry to provide accessible routes into employment and training for young people.

deb_ex.sum: Celebrates British Beauty Week and local businesses in Weston-super-Mare, and asks for more detail on how the youth guarantee will support small businesses in his area.

deb_ex.t: Thousands across my constituency and millions across the country still struggle to get online, to stay online and to be safe online.
deb_ex.sum: Marks Get Online Week by highlighting the digital exclusion of millions and calls for more parliamentary debate and resources to tackle the problem.

deb_ex.t: What steps she is taking to help reduce sewage discharges into waterways.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister what steps are being taken to reduce sewage discharges into waterways.

deb_ex.t: I am deeply concerned about the impact of sewage pollution and will always urge the Government to go faster and harder to tackle the crisis.
deb_ex.sum: Cites a report alleging 50,000 unreported sewage spills and calls on the Government to go faster and harder to hold water companies to account, particularly for coastal communities.

deb_ex.t: 400 posties are leaving every week. Our posties and Royal Mail workers deserve proper support, staffing levels and working conditions to deliver the service people expect.
deb_ex.sum: Defends postal workers facing abuse and poor conditions, highlights that 400 posties leave every week, and calls on Government and Ofcom to act decisively on the Committee's six-month deadline recommendation.

deb_ex.t: I am frustrated that our regulatory system has not evolved to deal with the level of corporate gaslighting that seems to run roughshod over worker and customer interests.
deb_ex.sum: Echoes the Committee's call for decisive Government and Ofcom action within the six-month deadline, warning that corporate statistics obscure the lived reality of workers and customers.

deb_ex.sum: Raises the operational concern that hostile states could exploit the humanitarian defence by setting up shell charities, and asks whether the government can detect and stop such activity.

deb_ex.sum: Uses Devon's seasonal tourism economy to illustrate how rising taxes and costs are destroying summer jobs for young people, and calls tackling youth unemployment a priority.

deb_ex.sum: Provocatively asks whether Andy Burnham endorses the government's plans, implying internal Labour division on the policy.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Government to publish figures on small boat arrivals who abscond or go missing, arguing the Home Office holds the data needed for proper parliamentary scrutiny of the problem.

deb_ex.sum: Argues reorganisation is consuming council bandwidth and presses the Minister on whether the incoming Labour leader Andy Burnham agrees with the proposed timelines for Devon.

deb_ex.t: services delivering NHS-level care should not depend on public generosity to survive
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that air ambulance charities receive no direct government funding while facing rising costs, and calls on the Minister to assess how to support their sustainability.

deb_ex.sum: Questions how the Foreign Secretary is reassuring international partners about Britain's finances amid rising bond yields and Middle East inflationary pressures, and asks whether he is warning against fresh non-essential spending.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights a voluntary breastfeeding support group in his constituency that struggles for funding and calls on the Government to properly support such organisations through the Bill.

deb_ex.t: Building 1.5 million new homes and doing LGR at the same time was clearly bonkers.
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the decision to pursue reorganisation alongside a major housebuilding programme as misguided, cites over £1 million already spent by local councils in Devon, and demands clarity on Devon's elections and timeline.

deb_ex.sum: The Con MP asks the Government to publicly name the state responsible for the JLR cyber-attack and explain what repercussions have followed, arguing a national conversation is needed.

deb_ex.sum: Asks the PM to confirm which country was responsible for the Jaguar Land Rover hack and what repercussions have followed.

deb_ex.sum: Raises awareness of musculoskeletal conditions during Bone and Joint Week, drawing on his own debilitating ankle injury to argue for earlier intervention, better NHS access and recognition of the enormous economic cost of inaction.

deb_ex.t: I will come on to the points that the hon. Gentleman has made, but he is completely right. We must look at these problems in the round, because this is an issue of not just physica
deb_ex.sum: Continues his personal account of living with osteoarthritis to make the case that early intervention is a sound economic investment and that equitable access to timely MSK care must not depend on ability to pay.

deb_ex.sum: Raises concern about the future of HMS Protector as Britain's only naval ice patrol ship and questions whether a single replacement can sustain presence at both poles alongside maintenance requirements.

deb_ex.t: What assessment her Department has made of the adequacy of access to NHS dentists.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Department to assess the adequacy of access to NHS dentists.

deb_ex.t: someone took a trip of more than 130 miles because no local practice would take them as a patient.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights severe local access problems with 86% of survey respondents unable to get an NHS dentist, and asks the Minister to examine the lack of catchment areas for dental practices.

deb_ex.t: people in Pinhoe in my constituency are receiving letters only once every two to three weeks
deb_ex.sum: Reports ongoing unacceptable delivery failures across his constituency seven months after raising the issue in a Westminster Hall debate, and calls for Parliament to turn debate into real action.

deb_ex.t: From the numbers for Royal Mail, it looks like asset stripping is going on, so we can understand why those posties are having a difficult time.
deb_ex.sum: Defends posties, suggests Royal Mail's financial trajectory looks like asset-stripping, and highlights the particular importance of letters for elderly constituents.

deb_ex.t: Royal Mail clearly says that it is now a parcel company that still delivers letters, and that is an issue
deb_ex.sum: Agrees letters are being deprioritised, notes Royal Mail now self-identifies as a parcel company, and calls for the universal service obligation to be made fit for purpose with real penalties.

deb_ex.t: letters relating to their cancer treatment have been arriving late. For patients already facing the anxiety and uncertainty of cancer treatment
deb_ex.sum: Describes rural-urban service disparities, highlights a constituent whose cancer treatment letters arrived late, condemns the trend toward asset-stripping, and asks the Minister to address economy access mail and Ofcom's regulatory effectiv

deb_ex.t: we have to really dig into the universal service obligation and make sure that there are significant penalties if Royal Mail does not do what it has signed up to
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the need for significant penalties within the universal service obligation to ensure Royal Mail fulfils its commitments.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend hits the nail on the head. If we look at those numbers again—losses of £400 million three years ago and then £200 million, followed by a £14 million profit—they show
deb_ex.sum: Agrees fines are being baked into the operating model, calls for penalties unacceptable to shareholders, and asks the Minister whether Ofcom's regulatory approach is effective.

deb_ex.t: Will the Minister touch on the points that I raised about deferred mail? There should be more transparency over the economy service that Royal Mail offers. Constituents are receivi
deb_ex.sum: Asks the Minister to address deferred or economy-class mail and calls for greater transparency so constituents know when public bodies have chosen cheaper delivery options.

deb_ex.sum: Challenges the government's reluctance to publicly attribute state-sponsored cyber-attacks, citing the Jaguar Land Rover incident, and calls on the Foreign Secretary to name the state responsible.

deb_ex.t: if the Government are going to ask people to stock up on tinned food and wind-up radios, they must be honest when we are attacked.
deb_ex.sum: Supports the Be Ready campaign but presses the Minister to be transparent about threats and to tell the House which state was responsible for the Jaguar Land Rover cyberattack.

deb_ex.sum: Argues the UK is out of step with European partners and calls for a comprehensive ban across all goods and services from settlements, noting existing restrictions have been neutralised by Israeli reimbursement schemes.

deb_ex.sum: Asks whether the Lord Chancellor or Judicial Appointments Commission should have input into the first appointments to the new authority to better guarantee independence.

deb_ex.sum: Cites poor NHS, housing and ferry performance under the SNP to argue the Scottish Government should focus on delivery rather than independence.

deb_ex.sum: Recalls that a Labour-led Scottish Government introduced free personal care in 2002 and asks the Secretary of State to confirm Barnett consequentials will be available for Scotland to spend on social care.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Government's fireworks consultation but presses for a timeline for the response and warns that next year's bonfire season must see real change given ongoing antisocial fireworks use in communities like Knightswood.

deb_ex.t: What steps he is taking to protect British interests in the High North.
deb_ex.sum: Asks the minister what steps are being taken to protect British interests in the High North.

deb_ex.sum: Endorses British leadership of the Joint Expeditionary Force and asks the minister for an update on recent JEF meetings in Iceland and major regional exercises.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is being very generous with his time this evening. As he knows, I went to school next door to the art school, and it has always held a special place in my life. Does
deb_ex.sum: Draws a personal connection to the school and links its restoration to the wider regeneration and economic recovery of Glasgow's Sauchiehall Street area.

deb_ex.sum: Highlights the preventability of skin cancer and calls for a debate on reducing VAT on sunscreen to make it more affordable as a public health measure.

deb_ex.t: delays in the postal service can have particularly serious knock-on consequences for people in those communities
deb_ex.sum: Draws on Scottish Affairs Committee findings to highlight how postal delays hit remote Scottish communities hardest, and asks the Minister to ensure reporting covers rural Scotland and to clarify NHS barcode uptake.

deb_ex.t: just 54% of stamped and metered first-class mail reached the Outer Hebrides the next working day and the figure for Lerwick in Shetland was only 25%
deb_ex.sum: Highlights that Scotland-wide averages conceal dire performance in islands, calls for granular rural reporting, and raises health and safety concerns for posties handling large parcels in offices built for letters.

deb_ex.t: Scotland will receive a disproportionately small share of the total UK fund. Our Committee questions
deb_ex.sum: Presents the Scottish Affairs Committee report on maximising Scotland's benefit from increased defence spending, highlighting skills shortages and calling for greater apprenticeship investment and joint UK-Scottish Government planning.

deb_ex.t: apprenticeships will also come through our further education colleges, and it is important that they are given the resources to benefit
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the call for continued inter-governmental cooperation and stresses further education colleges also need resources to support the defence and clean energy sectors.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges disruption to defence sector recruitment while drawing encouragement from apprentices at BAE Systems who informally advocate for their work.

deb_ex.t: I very much hope that the Government take our point that they need to engage with the financial services sector to address that.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees there is widespread misunderstanding of the defence sector's importance and urges the Government to engage with financial services to address debanking problems.

deb_ex.t: The myths about those trades have been busted by the academy. It is wonderful to see young people so enthusiastic about the jobs and the future
deb_ex.sum: Praises the BAE Systems skills academy for addressing the welding skills gap and challenging stereotypes about industrial trades, highlighting the enthusiasm of young workers.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that the benefits of defence spending should extend to logistics and service roles, not just technical jobs, and urges Government action to widen opportunities through the supply chain.

deb_ex.t: reform is coming, because under this Labour Government we are reforming the social security safety net

deb_ex.t: If settlements are illegal, why are we still treating their products as legitimate? Every shipment from a settlement carries a human cost in the displacement, deprivation of income and death
deb_ex.sum: Condemns the Government's inaction as hollow given its own acknowledgement that settlements are illegal, detailing surging settler violence and land seizures and demanding an end to all trade with settlements.

deb_ex.t: Condemnation without consequence is nothing less than complicity. Israeli settlers, aided and abetted by the IDF and the Israeli Government, have taken away the rights of the Palestinians
deb_ex.sum: Argues the UK has a legal obligation to prevent genocide and condemns successive governments for trading with Israel and settlements despite condemnation, accusing the government of complicity.

deb_ex.t: this issue is not just about products coming from settlements to the UK, but companies in the UK trading in goods and services in the settlements
deb_ex.sum: Argues that the trade ban debate must also cover services, not just goods, pointing to companies like Airbnb and Booking.com selling tourism in occupied territories.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the Minister’s response so far, amid the shocking allegations that staff covered up the greater risks of power blackouts during the recent heatwave, but it is not just he
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Minister's responses but asks what steps the Department is taking to ensure rapid AI data centre expansion does not compromise energy security, increase blackout risks or burden local communities.

deb_ex.t: Will he, for instance, consider revoking regulation 45 of the Council Tax (Administration and Enforcement) Regulations 1992
deb_ex.sum: Raises the scale of council tax debt and bailiff use and calls on the Prime Minister to consider revoking the relevant regulation and introducing a duty of care to protect debtors.

deb_ex.t: Does the hon. Member agree that most parents want to provide that support for the children, but given where we are economically in our country, many are unable to do so due to the
deb_ex.sum: Intervenes to stress that economic pressures stop many willing parents from giving adequate support, calling for the joined-up early years approach being discussed.

deb_ex.t: To extend that point, does the hon. Gentleman agree that the use of screens by adults or people in the room with the child can also have an adverse impact? It is almost like second
deb_ex.sum: Extends the screentime point to include adult screen use around children, comparing it to second-hand smoke and calling for education on this.

deb_ex.t: The House will agree that we believe that all children should be born equal. However, we are here today because we also know that in the fifth or sixth richest country in the world
deb_ex.sum: Strongly endorses the Bill, stressing health inequalities, ethnic disparities in infant mortality, and the need for the annual report to drive real improvements for disadvantaged and minority communities.

deb_ex.t: I wholeheartedly agree with the hon. Lady. It is important for parents, mothers and families to know that Government policy is free from commercial influence, not just in this spac
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with calls for tighter formula regulation, argues the MHRA should regulate nutritional content and marketing of substitute breast milk, and urges that government policy be free from commercial influence.

deb_ex.t: If we are serious about giving the Bill meaning beyond good intention, the resources required to deliver it must follow.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees there should be no postcode lottery in maternity care, warns that health visiting caseloads have become unsustainable, and insists that proper resources must follow the Bill's ambitions.

deb_ex.t: after Brexit it lost a lot of its export business. What are the Government going to do to support furniture, upholstery and supply chain manufacturers in Dewsbury and Batley
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the post-Brexit export losses for furniture and manufacturing businesses in Dewsbury and Batley and asks what the Government will do to support them.

deb_ex.t: it is akin to an abusive relationship. Will the Minister unequivocally confirm that Britain will not tolerate intimidation and blackmail by the US, Israel or others
deb_ex.sum: Characterises the UK-US relationship as akin to an abusive one under Trump and demands an unequivocal statement that Britain will not tolerate intimidation from the US, Israel or others.

deb_ex.t: Will the Foreign Secretary explain why it has taken the Labour Government so long to act?
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the government for the change in policy but presses the Foreign Secretary on why action took so long after the ICJ opinion, and calls for full compliance with international law and a review of past non-compliance.

deb_ex.t: Meta has just agreed to pay $18 billion in a legal settlement in the US, so will the Government pursue similar robust enforcement against such companies?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the statement, highlights existing hardware-level child protection technology, and urges the Government to pursue Meta-style financial enforcement against harmful platforms.

deb_ex.t: On the subject of a sovereign wealth fund, would the right hon. Gentleman comment on the fact that under the Tories we sold off our national treasures in North sea oil and gas? We
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the previous Conservative government for selling off North Sea oil and gas assets rather than investing them in a sovereign wealth fund as Norway did.

deb_ex.t: Will the hon. Gentleman share his assessment of the impact of increasing the retirement age to 66 and 67, with a target of 70, on the availability of junior jobs for young people t
deb_ex.sum: Asks the speaker to assess whether raising the retirement age reduces entry-level job opportunities for young people.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the Government’s announcement that they will reduce the deposit for first-time buyers. Does the hon. Gentleman agree that the price of housing is so extortionate that, on
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the reduced deposit for first-time buyers but warns that house prices are so high that mortgages will last decades and young buyers may never pay them off before retirement.

we need to commit to both, not as optional extras, but with long-term ringfenced funding, so that we do not lose another generation to the streets
deb_ex.sum: Highlights cuts to neighbourhood policing and youth services as drivers of rising youth crime, and calls on the Prime Minister to commit to long-term ringfenced funding for both.

deb_ex.t: Children are being exposed daily to horrific, violent content online. Ofcom’s own research shows that nearly a quarter of 11 to 17-year-olds have seen violent content in just four
deb_ex.sum: Highlights alarming Ofcom data on children's exposure to violent algorithmic content, notes little improvement since the Act's duties came into force, and calls for Ofcom to be given immediate enforcement tools.

deb_ex.t: should the rules be applied equally to Israeli diplomats in this House? When China banned our elected Members, the Speaker banned the Chinese ambassador
deb_ex.sum: Argues that speaking against alleged war crimes is a badge of honour and calls on the Speaker to ban the Israeli ambassador from Parliament, as was done with China.

deb_ex.t: On the issue of disarmament, should we not also be calling for Israel’s disarmament, given the atrocities that have been committed? Previous Governments have intervened in the midd
deb_ex.sum: Calls for Israel's disarmament and raises the possibility of military action against Israel in response to alleged atrocities, drawing a parallel with past international interventions.

deb_ex.t: unless America takes action, Israel is not going to back off from the atrocities it is carrying out
deb_ex.sum: Argues that without the United States backing the peace plan, Israel will not change course, and urges the Government to push harder on all levers to bring America on side.

deb_ex.t: It is brilliant to see an example in the interim report of a young woman who taught herself Shopify in order to start a business. This Government have prioritised growth, which com
I am delighted to present this petition on behalf of Walton-le-Dale residents in my constituency regarding the potential felling of the 18 royal lime trees that have stood for 112
I am grateful for the opportunity to debate Government support for private investment in Lancashire this evening. Lancashire is my home. It is also the home of some of the most pow
urge the Government to direct NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria Integrated Care Board to commit to a full reopening of the hospital
deb_ex.sum: Presents a petition with over 3,000 signatures calling on the government to direct the local ICB to fully reopen Longridge Community Hospital and address fire safety concerns with a clear timeline.

deb_ex.t: even though the evidence is there a million times over, sometimes getting the political will is even harder.
deb_ex.sum: As chair of the APPG on babies, enthusiastically backs the Bill, marshals evidence on brain development and early intervention savings, and pays tribute to those who built Sure Start.

deb_ex.t: it will be critical for this Government to research why parents rely so much on screentime, and how we can support parents not to have to do so
deb_ex.sum: Agrees screentime research is needed and calls on the Government to investigate why parents rely on it and how to reduce that reliance.

deb_ex.t: Women in this country will not accept the industrialisation of our bodies. This Labour Government have promised neighbourhood and preventive healthcare
deb_ex.sum: Pushes back against calls to consolidate and close maternity units, urging the Minister to ensure maternity care remains community-based and women-centred rather than industrialised.

Can he give me an assurance that this policy is only the start of solving a problem that can often involve a complex set of individual circumstances?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the commitment to end rough sleeping by Christmas, thanks local charities in Southend, and asks for assurance that the policy is just the beginning of addressing complex homelessness.

deb_ex.t: I am extremely grateful for the opportunity to speak in this debate, because at the end of the day, nothing matters more than protecting our democracy. It is the bedrock of our soc
deb_ex.sum: Endorses votes at 16, welcomes measures against online disinformation and crypto donations, and emphasises the importance of protecting democracy from intimidation and digital harms.

deb_ex.t: Will the Foreign Secretary assure me that the Government will continue to work towards greater community cohesion in this country
deb_ex.sum: Burton-Sampson welcomes the measures but presses the Foreign Secretary to assure that the government will continue working for community cohesion and protection of both British Jews and British Muslims.

deb_ex.t: T5. This summer saw the first hosepipe ban imposed by Essex and Suffolk Water on my constituency since 1997. However, some Opposition Members would deny that what we are seeing is
deb_ex.sum: Cites the first hosepipe ban since 1997 in his constituency as evidence of climate change and calls for net zero to remain a government priority.

deb_ex.t: biodegradable does not necessarily mean flushable, and even plastic-free wipes are made of tougher fibres that do not break down
deb_ex.sum: Introduces a Bill to regulate the labelling, sale and marketing of wet wipes, arguing that even plastic-free wipes cause serious sewer blockages and sewage discharges, and citing local water summits and constituency evidence to make the cas

deb_ex.t: As his plaque behind me says, may his light remain.
deb_ex.sum: Marks the fifth anniversary of Sir David Amess's murder in his constituency and invites the Leader of the House to celebrate the Children's Parliament, a project Sir David founded.

deb_ex.t: people of my colour are made by some to feel like we do not belong in this country, but we have built and we have protected this country
deb_ex.sum: Shares his family's wartime service to Britain and challenges those who make black Britons feel they do not belong to withdraw from that rhetoric.

deb_ex.t: Last night, I joined the 1987 Committee, set up by the fantastic Fatima Kamara and her team. As hon. Members can tell from its name, it recognises the year—that historic year—in wh
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the 1987 Committee, which helps young black people enter politics, and congratulates its founders for their work inspiring the next generation.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend the Member for Redditch (Chris Bloore) for securing the debate and my hon. Friends the Members for Lichfield (Dave Robertson) and for Corby and East Northamp
deb_ex.sum: Describes Southend as the original optimised delivery model pilot where failures were ignored before national rollout, but notes a promising local CWU-backed trial of a rebalanced round system now being rolled out across the sorting office.

deb_ex.t: We have to fight against that. The service is vital across the country, and we have to do everything we can to ensure that we do not lose it.
deb_ex.sum: Shares concerns about managed decline and welcomes the Government's action on bogus self-employment, arguing Royal Mail must not be dragged down to the level of companies that deny workers statutory rights.

deb_ex.t: Royal Mail has shown some desire to move towards that, but, like many others, I am concerned about the speed with which that will happen
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes signs of progress in Southend but urges Royal Mail to move faster on contract harmonisation and to listen to posties, unions and residents to find a route to genuine improvement.

deb_ex.t: It was a great pleasure to visit my hon. Friend and announce our procurement reforms at Griffon Marine in her constituency. The Prime Minister has been repeatedly clear that more p
deb_ex.sum: Affirms the government's commitment to greater public control of the water industry and promises reform plans will be set out shortly.

deb_ex.t: I will, of course, raise that with DEFRA and look into the specific issue on his behalf.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the member for his constructive contribution and commits to raising the controlled burning concern with DEFRA.

deb_ex.t: Whitehall and the Government as a whole have been told in no uncertain terms that they will now be required to justify why policies are not devolved
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that Whitehall culture must change and outlines the government's devolution-first principle, requiring justification when policies are not devolved.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Gentleman raises a number of really important and interesting issues that will be considered as we look to greater public control of our energy system. Local and com
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the issues raised and says local and community control is central to the government's vision for public control of the energy system.

deb_ex.t: The Mayor of London has been involved in continued talks through No. 10 North on the devolution settlement. We will continue to consider what further powers and resources London deserves.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Mayor of London is involved in talks on the devolution settlement and that the government will continue to consider further powers and resources.

deb_ex.t: The Prime Minister has been clear repeatedly that we stand against Scottish independence and against an independence referendum. We will continue to make the case for the Union.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees fully, reaffirms the government's opposition to Scottish independence and an independence referendum, and notes the Minister for Intergovernmental Relations holds this responsibility closely.

deb_ex.t: May I be absolutely clear that the service levels for the civil service pension scheme following the move to Capita have been completely unacceptable? Our immediate priority is to
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges that service levels following the Capita transition have been unacceptable, outlines commercial levers being used to hold Capita to account, and promises an update from the Parliamentary Secretary.

deb_ex.t: Cobra is the right team within the Department to co-ordinate activity across Government. We have worked closely with the Environment Agency, the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the new normal of extreme weather and says Cobra is the right coordinating mechanism, noting close working with the Environment Agency, DEFRA and the Met Office.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right to champion that important development. I would be delighted to facilitate a meeting for him in No. 10 North.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the development and agrees to facilitate a meeting at No. 10 North.

deb_ex.t: I will take that point away. We have already made significant progress in our review on closing or merging arm’s length bodies, including NHS England and the Advisory Committee on
deb_ex.sum: Notes progress already made closing or merging arm's length bodies and commits to writing to the member on the specific organisations he raises.

deb_ex.t: It is fantastic to hear my hon. Friend’s enthusiasm. We have set ourselves such a tight deadline exactly to ensure that we fill in the map of the whole of England and do not lose t
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the enthusiasm, highlights the tight deadline set to complete the English devolution map, and agrees to meet Thames Valley leaders and MPs.

deb_ex.t: We have awarded £100 million to the fire service and will co-ordinate a wildfire summit on where we need to go further
deb_ex.sum: Expresses sympathy for those affected and outlines government actions including £100 million for fire services and an upcoming wildfire summit.

deb_ex.t: We will ensure that their voice is central to the work we do as we prepare for future summers.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks firefighters for their efforts over the summer and commits to ensuring their voice is central to future preparedness work.

deb_ex.t: The £100 million has already been allocated, so that will have been done under the existing funding formula. Future allocations will be determined at the Budget.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the £100 million has already been allocated under the existing funding formula and that future allocations will be determined at the Budget.

deb_ex.t: We are removing the veto on decision making for transport infrastructure and devolving a number of powers under the Transport and Works Act 1992
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the importance of integrated transport and confirms powers under the Transport and Works Act will be devolved to speed up mass transit delivery, citing commitments to Leeds and Bristol.

deb_ex.t: We will reduce the size of the central civil service, shift power and resources out of Whitehall and speed up decision making.
deb_ex.sum: Rebuts concerns by asserting the reforms will reduce the central civil service, shift power from Whitehall and speed up decision making.

deb_ex.t: ensuring that non-elected bodies that are not accountable to politicians are not given free rein to make decisions. I will, of course, take away that issue.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees unelected bodies should not make unchecked decisions and commits to taking away the issue of R&D funding balance.

deb_ex.t: The staffing of No. 10 North has been done on an interim basis to get it set up and running. We will recruit permanently and, of course, those roles will be based in Manchester.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that No. 10 North staffing is interim and that permanent roles will be based in Manchester.

deb_ex.t: Through double devolution closest to the ground, we will ensure that the CVS is properly utilised and funded.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that the charity and voluntary sector should be properly funded and empowered, and states double devolution will ensure this.

deb_ex.t: I will take away the wider point and establish what work needs to be done to ensure that properly dealing with neurodiversity is embedded across the whole of Government.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the importance of the point and commits to establishing what work is needed to embed proper handling of neurodiversity across government.

deb_ex.t: I encourage him to raise it with the Leader of the House so that we have proper time in the Chamber to debate the issue.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the point and directs the member to raise it with the Leader of the House for proper debate time.

deb_ex.t: As the hon. Lady knows, the Prime Minister said yesterday that we will be hosting a National Economic Council with the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in or
deb_ex.sum: Points to the forthcoming National Economic Council with devolved First Ministers as the forum where such devolution questions will be addressed.

deb_ex.t: They will not have any difference in altering the level of business rates, but they will be incentivised and be able to keep a share of them.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that devolution concerns retention of business rates growth rather than altering rate levels, while reaffirming the Prime Minister's commitment to cutting rates for pubs and hospitality.

deb_ex.t: we are now preparing for flooding, and we are making extensive preparations for a wide range of scenarios ahead of winter
deb_ex.sum: Expresses sympathy and confirms extensive government preparations for flooding ahead of winter, promising a ministerial meeting to address the constituency's needs.

deb_ex.t: I can assure her that these issues will be considered by the wildfire summit, which I agree will need a bigger room at this rate.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the points are important and assures the MP the issues will be considered at the upcoming wildfire summit.

deb_ex.t: we will be hosting a meeting of the National Economic Council with the First Minister. The Prime Minister has already met him and is committed to devolving power
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government by noting fire services are devolved in Scotland and highlighting the Prime Minister's commitment to meet the First Minister and devolve power beyond Holyrood.

deb_ex.t: the Prime Minister set as his priority reducing burdens and cutting taxes for businesses—hospitality businesses in particular—in the first days of his premiership
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the burdens on small businesses and points to the Prime Minister's stated priority of reducing burdens and cutting taxes, including for hospitality businesses.

deb_ex.t: the Communities Secretary will determine next steps on local government reform by the end of October 2026
deb_ex.sum: Promises to pass the concerns to MHCLG and confirms the Communities Secretary will determine next steps on local government reform by end of October 2026.

deb_ex.t: The Cabinet Office supports the wider civil service and still fulfils a number of incredibly important functions, including cross co-ordination of governmental priorities. The Cabi
deb_ex.sum: Defends the continuing role of the Cabinet Office in cross-governmental coordination and affirms the Cabinet Secretary will always be needed to run the civil service.

deb_ex.t: I cannot imagine there are many people in this House who have not been touched by suicide in one way or another. I certainly have, in my close family.
deb_ex.sum: Responds with personal empathy, agrees the issue could and should be fixed through better joined-up governance, and accepts the invitation to meet.

deb_ex.t: We are already pursuing a number of reforms, including the abolition of NHS England, to ensure that decisions can be made democratically at the centre of Government
deb_ex.sum: Points to NHS England abolition and devolution reforms as the mechanism for directing decisions and resources locally, and agrees to raise the Blackburn case with the Health Secretary.

deb_ex.t: We are incredibly conscious of the historical underfunding of fire services across the country. That is why the previous Administration committed an additional £100 million to loca
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges historical underfunding and points to the £100 million committed to local fire and rescue services, noting future decisions will be for the Budget.

deb_ex.t: The Prime Minister has been clear that we do not want to impose anything centrally on areas that do not want to combine areas.
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates that the government does not want to impose central solutions and offers to facilitate discussions to find the right authority and powers for the area.

deb_ex.t: Fundamental to that negotiation will be reform of the decisions that Stormont makes and the way that the Executive have made decisions historically
deb_ex.sum: Points to the Northern Ireland Secretary's ongoing funding negotiations with Stormont and stresses that reform of Executive decision-making must accompany any new settlement.

deb_ex.t: fiscally devolving a share of income tax and business rates to mayors, giving local leaders greater power to attract private investment, create good jobs and deliver growth

deb_ex.t: I am determined that we have the data, the monitoring and the reporting to ensure that this scheme does work and is not a sticking plaster

deb_ex.t: local authorities could be given powers to use their resources to bring estates up to an adoptable level and then charge the developers for that work retrospectively
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on sewerage adoption and adds that local authorities should be empowered to bring estates up to adoptable standard and charge developers retrospectively to break the current deadlock.

deb_ex.sum: Raises a vehicle crash at a nursery in Ellesmere Port that injured children and asks for a ministerial statement on nursery security and safety standards.

deb_ex.sum: Describes a constituent whose portal showed only one year of service instead of 35 and argues that a competence test must be built into the public interest test to bar serial-offending companies from public contracts.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Government amendments resolving the security services impasse and asks the Minister to clarify how amendment 157 will operate in practice.

deb_ex.sum: Accepts the council notification point, confirms a lessons-learnt investigation is under way, and reiterates the government's commitment to commercial accountability and regular updates to local stakeholders.

deb_ex.sum: Defends the cancellations by blaming the previous Conservative Government for committing to more schemes than they funded, deflecting frustration back to the opposition.

deb_ex.t: the previous Government committed to far more schemes than there was funding for, so we had to evaluate which were the least value for money
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates that cancelled schemes were unfunded commitments by the previous Government, then sets out the £27 billion road investment strategy and explains the Bill's purpose in bringing in private finance.

deb_ex.t: the Bill means that roads operated under the new licensing regime can be held to the same standards as the rest of the strategic road network
deb_ex.sum: Responds briefly on automated vehicles, then explains the regulated asset base model, the regulatory role of the Office of Rail and Road, safeguards for road users and the rationale for the lower Thames crossing.

deb_ex.sum: Madders defends East West Rail as a priority project that will unlock growth, jobs and connectivity across the Oxford-Cambridge corridor, and commits to having the Rail Minister respond to Fuller's detailed questions in writing.

deb_ex.sum: Praises the Member's campaigning, acknowledges the misery caused and offers a cross-departmental ministerial meeting to explore how to tackle the issue.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees illegal e-bikes have no place on roads, outlines plans including a new cross-Government ministerial group and letters to retailers, and agrees to meet interested Members.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms cycling on pavements is an offence, notes new dangerous cycling offences in the Crime and Policing Act 2026, and says he has written to food delivery companies about rider conduct.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member makes a very fair point. One of the purposes of the cross-departmental working group is to work with Home Office officials and Ministers to understand the limitatio
deb_ex.issue: illegal use of e-bikes and e-scooters
deb_ex.sum: Explains the cross-departmental working group will engage the Home Office on police limitations and novel enforcement methods, and welcomes information from Essex police.

deb_ex.sum: Rejects the charge of compromising safety, cites statutory guidance published in January, notes the most problematic floating bus stop designs are no longer being built, and pledges to continue work on the issue.

deb_ex.t: We need to get this plague of illegal e-bikes sorted out once and for all, and this Government are determined to do that.
deb_ex.issue: illegal use of e-bikes and e-scooters
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House an action plan already exists, built on APPG recommendations and feeding into the cross-departmental group, and declares the Government determined to end the plague of illegal e-bikes.

deb_ex.t: I am grateful to Aura Mobility for engaging with the Department’s consultation, which we will respond to very shortly.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the company for engaging with the consultation and confirms the Government's response will be published very shortly.

deb_ex.t: We recognise that improvement is needed on the time taken to process medical driving licence applications, and plans are in place to address this.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out DVLA's headline transaction figures and acknowledges improvement is needed on medical driving licence processing times, noting plans are in place.

deb_ex.t: I recognise the hon. Member’s concerns, and I have asked for further information on some the matters he has raised. We are taking steps to tackle the issue. We have introduced a ne
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concerns raised, outlines steps taken including a new digital casework system and extra staff, and gives improving figures for medical licence processing times with a target of 45 days by March.

deb_ex.t: Well, if the agency was failing, then that was the condition we found it in when the hon. Member’s party left office. I am not entirely sure what he is complaining about. He is say

deb_ex.sum: Accepts the invitation to visit and acknowledges record road network investment, while noting funding is finite.

deb_ex.sum: Extends condolences to Shayan's family, accepts the meeting request and highlights the road safety strategy work, including engagement with bereaved families.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the difficulty of isolating noise in trials of acoustic devices and notes police already have powers, offering to write with further information.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the road's importance, says the Department is ready to proceed and joins the MP in calling on Reform-led East Sussex council to release the necessary funding.

deb_ex.t: the city economic drivers and the travel-to-work areas ought to have a voice in that
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the valid point that city economic drivers should have a voice in devolution structures even when reorganisation and devolution timelines diverge, and commits to taking the issue away.

deb_ex.t: With Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, and also with West Sussex, we are still earlier in the process, so we will confirm in writing what that will be. However, all decisions will b
deb_ex.sum: Confirms that Cambridgeshire and Peterborough decisions will be 'minded to' and notes the area is earlier in the process, while congratulating the member on his new appointment.

deb_ex.t: If there is new information that we have not considered, I would be happy to receive it
deb_ex.sum: Defends the 'minded to' process as the appropriate mechanism for receiving new representations and remains open to fresh information.

deb_ex.t: it should not be assumed that, just because areas were in previous batches, that will be the order in which we will take them
deb_ex.sum: Notes Hampshire decisions were withdrawn in September and will be reviewed, warning that previous batch order should not be assumed to determine future sequencing.

deb_ex.t: the idea that there should not be a democratic-mandate reset to negotiate that transfer just does not hold
deb_ex.sum: Defends holding district elections to avoid a democratic deficit during the reorganisation process and asset-transfer negotiations, with vesting day set for April 2029.

deb_ex.t: Now that the review has concluded, the individual meetings requested by a list of MPs will take place, and we will contact MPs in the usual way for those Monday sessions. Notwithst
deb_ex.sum: Confirms individual MP meetings will now take place following the review's conclusion, with the 'minded to' process allowing formal representations beyond that.

deb_ex.t: councils themselves determine what type or form of arrangement they want to put forward for their area
deb_ex.sum: Explains that councils submit their own financial assessments of transitional costs alongside boundary proposals, with those costs included in profiles sent to Government.

deb_ex.t: He cares about the place that he represents, and he wants devolution in Lancashire to be a success. In that, we are entirely as one
deb_ex.sum: Warmly praises the member's persistent advocacy for Lancashire and affirms shared commitment to making devolution there a success.

deb_ex.t: I tend to find that the truth is somewhere in the middle. I am trying to get a compromise that people accept
deb_ex.sum: Commits to reviewing both proposals and the consultation process for Hertfordshire with an open mind, seeking a compromise between large single unitaries and more local structures.

deb_ex.t: the invitation for areas to make submissions to the LGR process was entirely voluntary; there was no mandation
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the LGR process was entirely voluntary and council-initiated, while acknowledging the point about the impact on council staff and officers.

deb_ex.t: ensuring that the decision reflects community identity is definitely at the back of my mind
deb_ex.sum: Commits to looking at Hampshire afresh without predetermining outcomes, acknowledging that decisions should reflect community identity.

deb_ex.t: let us not detract from the benefit of this multibillion-pound investment to our communities
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the call for more consultation while defending the Government's engagement record and urging members to focus on the economic benefits the devolution investment brings.

deb_ex.t: I can announce to the House that the first phase of the review is now complete.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's position on local government reorganisation, announcing completion of the programme review and 'minded to' decisions for five areas, with a three-week representations period before final decisions.

deb_ex.t: I am playing this with an absolutely straight bat—I want to do this with integrity
deb_ex.sum: Defends the decision to pause and review the programme, explains the 'minded to' process, and pushes back on claims about abortive costs, arguing most spending was necessary regardless.

deb_ex.t: I can give an absolute assurance that even if we have to introduce new legislation to preserve that status, we will do whatever we have to do
deb_ex.sum: Confirms decisions for remaining areas will come in the new year, gives an absolute assurance that no city will lose its city status through reorganisation, and explains the logic of announcing decisions as soon as they are ready.

deb_ex.t: Working backwards, the reason we carried out the review was to ensure that we, as the Ministers who were making the decisions, were satisfied that the decisions were being made in
deb_ex.sum: Defends the thorough review process, explains why fresh ministerial decisions are needed, declines to publish legal advice in line with long-standing Government policy, and says Cambridgeshire and Peterborough's position in the queue is not

deb_ex.t: in two-tier areas, there is confusion about which council to hold to account for the delivery of services, and there is a duplication of services
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the case for reorganisation, arguing residents deserve clear accountability and that savings from reducing duplication should be redirected to frontline services.

deb_ex.t: All the local authorities that were engaged in LGR, whether they were part of the four subject to the court challenges or the one that we are withdrawing today, will receive a paym
deb_ex.sum: Confirms all local authorities engaged in the process, including Essex, will receive a payment for work done and that reorganisation will return to Hampshire, Essex, Norfolk and Suffolk.

deb_ex.t: there have to be fresh ministerial decisions that are objective and that we approach with an open mind
deb_ex.sum: Confirms councils do not need to develop new proposals and explains the 'minded to' process as a mechanism to rebuild good faith and allow further input before final decisions.

deb_ex.t: any decision of Government can be challenged in court, including the one in Gloucestershire
deb_ex.sum: Explains why a 2027 shadow unitary election in Gloucestershire is not feasible given the 'minded to' process timeline, risk of judicial review, and need for consistency across the country.

deb_ex.t: We have confirmed multiple times that the 500,000 population size was a guiding figure, and we were very mindful during the course of reorganisation that some councils went above t
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the 500,000 population figure was always a guide, not a fixed rule, and confirms the 'minded to' process will be open to tweaks but not entirely new proposals.

deb_ex.t: we will have a Monday evening surgery every two weeks from 7 pm to 9 pm
deb_ex.sum: Explains the meeting was held back pending the review and announces a fortnightly Monday surgery slot to accommodate the 40 to 50 MPs who have requested meetings.

deb_ex.t: One of the criteria for reorganisation is that it has to be compatible with devolution going forward
deb_ex.sum: Confirms devolution compatibility is a criterion for reorganisation, welcomes the 10 new devolution agreements announced the previous day, and agrees to meet the hon. Member.

deb_ex.t: I just do not agree with the analysis that we can stay as we are
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the suggestion that the status quo is viable, arguing financial pressures from social care and temporary accommodation mean reorganisation is necessary to redirect money to frontline services.

deb_ex.t: we are trying to get to the best possible solution in Gloucestershire, Worcestershire and all the other places that we have mentioned today
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach to reorganisation, acknowledging competing interests and the complexity of individual decisions, and invites representations during the 'minded to' process.

deb_ex.t: We published the criteria at the start of the process, and those criteria stand. They are unweighted; the idea is that they give us the freedom to take into account that England is
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the published criteria remain unchanged and that there is no additional window for modification proposals, while promising to write to Members about Cambridgeshire and Peterborough and West Sussex.

deb_ex.t: our view is that three weeks ought to be enough time to do so
deb_ex.sum: Defends the three-week 'minded to' window, explaining it is open to a wide range of stakeholders beyond councils, and maintains it is sufficient time for representations.

deb_ex.t: We cannot have elections being cancelled, creating a democratic deficit. Councils must have representatives around the table, with a mandate given to them by the public.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the need for clarity but defends confirming decisions area by area as soon as possible, and insists elections cannot be cancelled as councils must retain democratic mandates.

deb_ex.t: it would be wrong to predetermine it
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the suggestion that delay is purposeless, explaining that previous decisions are being withdrawn and remade from fresh proposals, and that it would be wrong to predetermine outcomes.

deb_ex.t: I can definitely commit to moving as quickly as possible. All the points she has raised—about identity, good public services and so on—are in our mind
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the hon. Member for her representations and commits to moving as quickly as possible, assuring her that concerns about identity and public services are being considered.

deb_ex.t: the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 requires us to bring forward neighbourhood governance arrangements before Christmas
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach, explaining that neighbourhood governance arrangements will be embedded in law to keep decision-making local, and corrects Farage's characterisation of the legal challenge.

deb_ex.t: securing devolution and investment for the counties of Leicestershire and Rutland could be transformational for their communities and their economy
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the impact of delays on council staff and officers and pledges to move at pace, highlighting the transformational potential of devolution for Leicestershire and Rutland.

deb_ex.t: The cost of transitioning from the two-tier system to new unitaries is covered by councils in their proposals. They tell us how they will finance the transitional arrangements that
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the framing of excessive costs, explaining that councils finance their own transitions and that the Government has introduced new funding of £900,000 per new unitary.

deb_ex.t: Obviously, we were delighted to announce the devolution agreement yesterday. That will definitely bring new resources and powers to my hon. Friend’s area, but it has to be built on
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the devolution agreement and explains that the 'minded to' process provides a window for MPs and interested parties to make representations on proposals.

deb_ex.t: As with LGR, devolution is locally led, so it is for local areas to come to Government to say, “We have a broad agreement that we want to be in talks about devolution.” We then bri
deb_ex.sum: Explains that devolution is locally led and sets out the timetable: consultation around December, local authority decisions in February-March, then statutory instruments brought to the House.

deb_ex.t: If we accept that as an argument and want to make a modification order, we will then need to go through a separate consultation process
deb_ex.sum: Explains that proposals will be taken as submitted but that the 'minded to' window allows representations for modifications, which may require a separate consultation if accepted.

deb_ex.t: the English devolution White Paper that was published in December 2024 invited councils to be part of the voluntary programme, and every one of the 21 outstanding counties applied
deb_ex.sum: Defends the pace of change as economically and socially necessary, and clarifies that all 21 counties voluntarily applied to the programme following the December 2024 White Paper.

deb_ex.t: At the moment, the proposal regarding the “minded to” decision is to expand the boundary of Brighton and Hove city council to include the communities of Saltdean and Peacehaven fur
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the 'minded to' decision on expanding Brighton and Hove's boundary and assures the hon. Member that the consultation window allows communities and MPs to make representations.

deb_ex.t: for Cornwall, we are working as hard as we can to recognise that different places are in different positions on devolution
deb_ex.sum: Confirms Cornwall's different position is being recognised and that the Government is working to complete the devolution map through foundation or mayoral strategic authorities.
