deb_ex.t: What vision does he have to include the voluntary sector in the crucial task of tackling rough sleeping?
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Prime Minister's work on rough sleeping and asks what vision he has for involving the voluntary sector in tackling it.

deb_ex.t: early intervention, early intervention, early intervention
deb_ex.sum: Raises the crisis in mental health and social care services in her constituency, highlighting delayed discharges, fragmented care pathways and lack of housing, and calls for early intervention and systemic reform.

deb_ex.t: Does the Chair of the Treasury Committee agree it is high time that the equality impact assessment was published by the Department?
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether the Committee Chair agrees it is overdue for the Department for Education to publish the equality impact assessment on plan 2 repayment thresholds.

deb_ex.t: It is a real pleasure to speak in this debate and to reflect on the question of inheritance tax brought to the House by the Conservative party. It affects about 4% of the populatio
deb_ex.sum: Argues the Conservative motion benefits only 4% of estates at a potential £10 billion cost, contrasts it with Labour's cost-of-living measures, and defends the government's record on growth and stability.

deb_ex.t: Those who earn a lot, whether through pensions, inheritance or other things, will be taxed proportionately, which sounds like a pretty fair principle to me
deb_ex.sum: Defends proportionate taxation of larger pensions and inheritances, welcomes IMF upgrade of UK GDP, and lists Labour measures on bus fares, school uniforms, business rates and procurement as evidence of progress.

deb_ex.t: We will get on with delivering the difficult decisions and the change that our communities are longing to see
deb_ex.sum: Briefly reaffirms the government will get on with delivering difficult decisions and change, declining to take further interventions due to time.

deb_ex.t: For me, it was solid but not flashy—it was from the man who has HP Sauce on his sandwich, rather than pesto alla Genovese
deb_ex.sum: Praises the Budget as solid and supportive of households and small businesses, welcoming housing investment, council fiscal devolution and measures tackling rough sleeping.

deb_ex.t: It is absolutely vital that victims are at the heart of our justice system. My Blaydon and Consett constituents know that for too long, the system has not been working for victims
deb_ex.sum: Affirms that victims must be at the heart of the justice system and asks what impact the early victims' right to review will have for rape and serious sexual offence victims.

deb_ex.t: What steps his Department is taking with international partners to help tackle climate change.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the Department is taking with international partners to tackle climate change.

deb_ex.t: how is climate change resilience being embedded directly into our core diplomatic and security strategy?
deb_ex.sum: Describes constituents' suffering from extreme heat disruption and presses the government on how climate resilience is being embedded into diplomatic and security strategy.

deb_ex.t: The Secretary of State will be aware of my constituents Gemma Chappell and Rachel Walls, the great-aunts of baby Maya, who died at the hands of her mother’s partner. I thank the Se
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Secretary of State and Prime Minister for reviewing the early release scheme to exclude the killer of baby Maya and asks how victims will be supported going forward.

deb_ex.t: What discussions the Church of England has had with the Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport on the second round
deb_ex.sum: Asks what discussions the Church of England has had with the Secretary of State regarding the second round of the places of worship renewal fund.

deb_ex.t: What discussions has my hon. Friend had with the Department to ensure that round 2 funding is targeted towards former industrial communities with larger conservation needs?
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the repair burden on historic parish churches in former industrial communities like Blaydon and Consett and presses for round 2 funding to be targeted at areas with greater conservation needs.

deb_ex.t: what is measured is addressed, so we need to give the same attention to mental health that we rightly give to physical health measures
deb_ex.sum: Calls on the government to accept new clause 159 requiring mandatory national waiting time standards for mental health services, arguing that statutory accountability is needed to turn parity of esteem from aspiration into reality.

deb_ex.t: In the UK, someone takes their own life every 90 minutes—the length of a football match.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the scale of suicide in the UK and welcomes campaigns like the Premier League and Samaritans partnership, calling for a government-time debate on suicide prevention.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for this report on redress schemes, which certainly reflects the experiences of my constituents who have been involved in some of those campaigns. I particul
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the recommendation for an independent oversight body and asks how responses to inquiries such as the Hughes report on sodium valproate, mesh and Primodos could be accelerated.

deb_ex.t: What steps he is taking to support young people into employment.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what steps the government is taking to support young people into employment.

deb_ex.t: Just last week, I had the privilege of visiting Derwentside college in my constituency to see the amazing work it does in linking to employers in a range of sectors across the regi
deb_ex.sum: Praises Derwentside college for linking qualifications to real employment opportunities and invites the Secretary of State to visit.

deb_ex.t: many unpaid carers struggle to balance their caring responsibilities with paid employment, with consequences for their household finances and future pensions
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Minister for workforce work but asks what steps are being taken to help unpaid carers balance caring responsibilities with paid employment and avoid financial hardship.

deb_ex.t: it is a double injustice—first, that the parents, Emma and Janet, had to fight to get recognition and change in the prescription of sodium valproate
deb_ex.sum: Describes the situation as a double injustice, in that affected families first had to fight for recognition and now must fight again for compensation.

deb_ex.t: we do not intervene on Front-Bench speeches. The odd thing is that we went through this scenario this time last year
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker intervenes to remind Members not to interrupt front-bench speeches, noting the same situation arose the previous year.

deb_ex.t: Mr Gareth Snell, moving three rows back does not mean I cannot see you or hear you. Let us try to simmer down
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker calls for order, asking a Member who has moved seats to stop causing disruption.

deb_ex.t: Before I call the Chancellor of the Exchequer, I remind hon. Members that copies of the Budget resolutions will be available to them from the Vote Office in Members’ Lobby at the e
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker sets out procedural rules for the Budget statement, including availability of resolutions and the ban on interventions during the Chancellor's speech.

deb_ex.t: Colleagues who are chuntering will need a lot of stamina as we have many hours to go. Let us keep the Chamber calm.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker calls for order among noisy Members during the Chancellor's statement.

deb_ex.t: Mr Bowie, you are sitting far too close to me to be that noisy.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker calls a specific Member to order for being too noisy during the Chancellor's statement.

deb_ex.t: Dr Luke Evans, you will have to write yourself a prescription to calm down.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker again calls the Chamber to order, naming a specific Member for disruptive behaviour.

deb_ex.t: Mr Cartlidge, I think you have spoken more words than the Chancellor during this statement
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker calls the Chamber to order, humorously noting a Member has spoken more words than the Chancellor, and calls the Chancellor back.

deb_ex.t: Order. I am sorry to interrupt the Chancellor again, but Mr Holmes, just like last year, your voice is carrying far too heavily across the Chamber, and the hon. Member for Bridling
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker calls two named Members to order for disruptive behaviour, referencing a promise made earlier in the day.

deb_ex.t: It is on this motion that the debate will take place today and on succeeding days.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker explains the procedural basis for the Budget debate and calls the Chancellor to move the Income Tax charge motion formally.

deb_ex.t: I call the Chair of the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, after which there will be a speaking limit of eight minutes.
deb_ex.sum: Chair of the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee is called to speak; an eight-minute speaking limit is announced.

deb_ex.t: if Members are leaving the Chamber, they should leave very quietly and very quickly
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker calls for order as members leave the Chamber noisily during the Leader of the Opposition's speech.

deb_ex.t: Behave better than your child
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker calls order on noisy Labour members, appealing to their better behaviour.

deb_ex.t: The Defence Secretary will have to have a lie down in a dark room if he carries on like that
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker calls order on the noisy Defence Secretary.

deb_ex.t: We have to showcase the best of ourselves. Our constituents are watching.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker calls order on rowdy Labour members on both sides.

deb_ex.t: yowling for so long will be very bad for your throat, so simmer down
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker calls order on a noisy Labour member.

deb_ex.t: I am surprised that the hon. Member failed to get the Chancellor to use the word “Harlow” multiple times during the Budget statement.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker wryly notes that Vince failed to get the Chancellor to mention Harlow during the Budget statement.

deb_ex.t: Interventions should be short and sharp, and questions should be to the point.
deb_ex.sum: Calls for interventions to be short and sharp and to the point.

deb_ex.t: there are many people hoping to contribute this afternoon, so I hope the shadow Chancellor will be concluding soon.
deb_ex.sum: Urges the shadow Chancellor to conclude so other members may contribute to the debate.

deb_ex.t: he has to be loud, because there is so much heckling. Can everybody just calm down a little bit?
deb_ex.sum: Calls for order and asks members to calm the heckling so the Defence Secretary can be heard.

deb_ex.t: Order. Mr Obese-Jecty, this is not good behaviour. After yesterday, Mr Cartlidge, I thought you would have had a much quieter voice. I cannot hear the Secretary of State. Can we ju
deb_ex.sum: Calls for order, singles out a noisy member and asks the chamber to let the Defence Secretary continue.

deb_ex.t: the statement concerns my constituency in East Sussex
deb_ex.sum: Briefly notes personal interest in the statement as an East Sussex constituency MP before calling the shadow Secretary of State.

deb_ex.t: there are many people wishing to contribute? Hopefully his speech will be coming to a conclusion shortly.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker intervenes to manage time in the debate, urging the Defence Secretary to conclude his speech given the number of Members wishing to contribute.

deb_ex.t: Order. Mr Farage, no “you” and “your”, because it is not me who is responding.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker intervenes to remind Mr Farage not to address the Chair directly with 'you' and 'your'.

deb_ex.t: Order. Before the Minister responds, let me say that I am not at the Dispatch Box. It is “the Minister”, not “you” and “your”. Back-Bench MPs should be speaking through the Chair.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker again reminds back-bench MPs to address remarks through the Chair rather than directly to the Minister.

deb_ex.t: I ask Members to please ask only one question each, because we need to get through this statement quickly.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker asks Members to limit themselves to one question each so the statement can proceed efficiently.

deb_ex.t: I need Members to ask much shorter questions, and I need the Minister’s answers to be on point as well.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker intervenes to ask Members to keep questions brief and the Minister to stay on point.

deb_ex.t: I am grateful to the hon. Member for Beaconsfield (Joy Morrissey) for securing this debate, and grateful to other hon. Members for their contributions. I will try to address the po
Illegal e-bikes have no place on our roads. My Department has published guidance to make it clear that e-bikes that exceed the legal power and speed limits are treated as motor veh
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's position that illegal e-bikes must be registered and insured and that sellers of conversion kits must inform consumers of the legal implications.

deb_ex.t: The Department for Business and Trade has consulted on new product safety regulations and sought views on the targeted regulation of some products, including e-bike batteries and conversion kits.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the hon. Member's advocacy and confirms DBT has consulted on regulating e-bike batteries and conversion kits, with a response expected in the autumn.

deb_ex.t: We have legislated to introduce numerous lane rental schemes and are devolving powers to establish future schemes to mayors.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government action on congestion, including lane rental schemes and devolved powers to mayors to enable local decision making.

deb_ex.t: I am sorry to hear about the issues facing my hon. Friend’s constituents; I know how much he does to promote their interests. This Government are investing record sums in road main
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the constituent issues raised, highlights record government investment in road maintenance and tougher rules on street works, and directs the member to press Essex county council.

deb_ex.t: I am sure that the Roads and Buses Minister would be happy to continue those discussions.
deb_ex.sum: Notes previous meetings with the hon. Member about road disruption in his constituency and offers further discussions with the Roads and Buses Minister.

deb_ex.t: National Highways is considering in detail with local partners the case for detrunking the A69 and trunking the A689.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges safety incidents on the A69 and confirms National Highways is working with local partners on the case for detrunking, promising an update in due course.

deb_ex.t: The Government are committed to improving transport connectivity across the country. Through the £2.3 billion local transport grant, Staffordshire will receive more than £96 millio
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the £2.3 billion local transport grant and Staffordshire's £96 million share, and agrees to meet the hon. Member to discuss local transport priorities.

deb_ex.t: I would, of course, be very happy to meet them to talk about what we can do to improve safety on that road
deb_ex.sum: Extends sympathies to the family and agrees to meet the MP and constituents to discuss improving safety on that road.

deb_ex.t: we have said in the cycling and walking investment strategy that we intend to legislate for them in future.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government's intention to legislate for side road zebra crossings as part of the cycling and walking investment strategy.

deb_ex.t: New powers in the Crime and Policing Act 2026 mean that the police can seize e-bikes classed as motor vehicles when they are being used antisocially
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern about illegal e-bikes and highlights new police powers under the Crime and Policing Act 2026 to seize them when used antisocially.

deb_ex.t: My Department has commissioned specific research into those issues so that we can better plan action to tackle that.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern about illegal e-bikes in the gig economy and confirms the Department has commissioned specific research to plan action.

deb_ex.t: I agree that this is not acceptable. We are working to improve the situation.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges DWP response times are unacceptable, explains increased volumes and complexity are the cause, and says additional resources and improved case management are being deployed.

deb_ex.t: we recognise that response times are not good enough, and I am putting extra resources in to improve them
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates that response times are being addressed with extra resources and offers to look into the specific cases raised by her colleague.

deb_ex.t: Given the upcoming Prorogation and state opening of Parliament, I thought it would be helpful to return to the House to provide an update on the progress the Government have made t
May I begin by saying that the hon. Member’s speech—not least the beginning, when he visibly enjoyed his jokes more than the rest of the House—shows that, for the Conservative part
As I have set out to this House on previous occasions, the Government are working to comply with the motion passed in February. I can reassure the House that this remains the case,
With permission, I would like to update the House on the Government’s response to the Humble Address of 4 February. Before I do, I think it is important for all of us to reflect ag
I thank Members from across the House for their contributions this afternoon and for sharing the condolences expressed by the shadow Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, the hon.
I see that the House has been waiting for me. I am starting to prepare myself for a quieter life, and it was nice to have the opportunity to start that this morning. On 11 March an
I begin by thanking my right hon. Friend the Prime Minister for the dedicated work that he has undertaken since becoming leader of the Labour party. Following the crushing defeat t
the privatisation of the Royal Mail and its separation from the Post Office was a mistake. The coalition Government got that wrong
deb_ex.sum: Drawing on his experience chairing the Business and Trade Committee, argues the privatised model is fundamentally broken and calls for renationalisation and reintegration with the Post Office.

deb_ex.t: a Royal Mail that is back in public hands, reintegrated with the Post Office network. That would be a tangible example of change in every postcode
deb_ex.sum: Responds that better market regulation is needed regardless of ownership and reaffirms his call for Royal Mail to be returned to public hands and reintegrated with the Post Office.

deb_ex.t: the Conservative party thinks that we should not be doing anything at all. I am pleased to see this Labour Government doing the right thing
deb_ex.sum: MP welcomes the funding and contrasts it favourably with the Opposition's apparent opposition, noting the spread of street homelessness into unexpected parts of his Bristol constituency, and asks how the pot will be allocated.

deb_ex.t: This Government are committed to delivering a truly national civil service, one that lives and breathes the communities that we represent across the UK. We have exceeded our target
that is something the Government are already taking many steps towards. We are looking at visa enforcements.
deb_ex.sum: Minister welcomes rare cross-party agreement, confirming the Government is already using visa enforcement levers against countries that refuse to take back their nationals.

deb_ex.t: We are undertaking a range of consultation and engagement on measures with those partners. The Albania agreement was important, but the Home Secretary is making a number of arrangements
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the Opposition's framing, defends the Government's ongoing international engagement on returns, and signals upcoming announcements from the Home Secretary.

deb_ex.t: I am going to move on. Forgive me. We have driven up removals to the highest level in a decade—an important point to stop and reflect on—because of the progress we are making, with
deb_ex.sum: Sets out Government achievements including record removals, reduced asylum hotel use and a £1 billion saving, and outlines the new Immigration and Asylum Bill as the route to a fairer system.

deb_ex.t: public safety is and always will be at the forefront of our thinking. If the site is taken forward, there would be specialist security onsite 24/7
deb_ex.sum: Defends using former military sites including MOD Bicester for asylum accommodation, outlines security measures planned, and rejects withdrawal from the ECHR as counterproductive to immigration control.

deb_ex.t: It was this Government who picked up the pieces after the general election, following years of inaction and ineptitude.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the scale of the asylum crisis inherited from the Conservatives, including 110,000 small boat arrivals and £4.7 billion annual spending, to contextualise the Government's reform programme.

deb_ex.t: Under the last Government, £9 million a day was spent housing people in 400 asylum hotels. That was costly and inefficient.
deb_ex.sum: Defends scrapping asylum hotels as a pull factor costing £9 million a day and dismisses the Rwanda scheme as a £700 million farce that sent only four volunteers.

deb_ex.t: I do not know how much good money the right hon. Gentleman wants to throw after bad, but £700 million on four volunteers was an incredible waste of money.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects Rwanda as good money after bad and sets out that the British public accept legal migration and genuine refugees but will not tolerate a chaotic, unfair and expensive asylum system.

deb_ex.t: It is only a Labour Government who will fix the broken system, restore control at our borders and bring back fairness to our public services.
deb_ex.sum: Asserts that only the Labour Government will restore fairness and control to the asylum system and signals she will outline concrete progress made in the last two years.

deb_ex.t: Thanks to the action the Labour Government are taking, the picture today is improving, with crossings down, removals up and the system now finally on a more stable footing.
deb_ex.sum: Draws on her experience closing Sangatte and introducing juxtaposed controls to underline Labour's track record, and credits Government action with cutting crossings by 40% and removals rising.

deb_ex.t: I appreciate the hon. Gentleman raising the point about deterrence. It is extremely important but, as I said, the Rwanda deterrent was not effective. [ Interruption. ] Millions of
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses Rwanda as an ineffective deterrent and highlights counter-terror powers, a 74% rise in organised immigration crime arrests, and new prosecutions for dangerous boat piloting as real deterrents.

deb_ex.t: I appreciate the hon. Lady. Of course, I will come on to Piddington—that is the content, the subject and the title of this debate—but it is really important to understand the peopl
deb_ex.sum: Promises to address Piddington but first sets out the Government's international partnerships and enforcement actions that have stopped over 50,000 channel crossing attempts and cut small boat arrivals by 40%.

deb_ex.t: we have made great progress in closing asylum hotels, and we are committing to doing that by the end of this Parliament. We have saved over £1 billion
deb_ex.sum: Turley agrees to meet the MP, highlights progress in closing asylum hotels, the commitment to close them by Parliament's end, and over £1 billion saved compared with the previous government's approach.

deb_ex.t: we have reduced the numbers of those crossing by boat by 40%, and deportations are up—we have removed over 80,000 people
deb_ex.sum: Turley confirms boat crossings have fallen 40%, over 80,000 people have been removed, and that these figures are reducing pressure on the asylum system.

deb_ex.t: This Government are proud to put fairness at the heart of our approach by moving to alternative accommodation, including former military sites
deb_ex.sum: Defends Wethersfield's safety record and argues the government is taking a fairer approach by moving to self-contained former military sites.

deb_ex.t: I would be happy to meet him to discuss it further and will look into it.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member for raising the cases and offers to meet to discuss them further.

deb_ex.t: we would introduce a new approach to refugee protection in the UK called core protection, which marks a shift to a more streamlined approach that meets our international obligations
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Home Secretary visited Denmark and introduced core protection, a streamlined approach meeting international obligations without over-interpreting them, embedded in the Immigration and Asylum Bill.

deb_ex.t: I would be happy to meet the hon. Gentleman and his colleagues. Home Office officials continue to engage with Scottish Borders council and other local partners on asylum accommodat
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to meet the Member and his colleagues, noting that Home Office officials continue to engage with Scottish Borders Council and local partners on asylum accommodation.

deb_ex.t: Since this Government came to power, we have removed over 11,700 foreign national offenders; that is up 41% on the two years before then.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's record, noting 11,700 foreign national offenders removed since taking power, up 41%, and states determination to remove more.

deb_ex.t: Our asylum Bill will fix the broken appeals system and close the human rights loopholes, so that they cannot be exploited.
deb_ex.sum: Responds to the case raised by pointing to the Immigration and Asylum Bill, which will close human rights loopholes and allow immediate removal after sentencing from early next year.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right. We remain firmly committed to the ECHR and the protections it gives us all, including the prohibition on torture, a right to life and protection
deb_ex.sum: Affirms commitment to the ECHR while explaining the government's aim to prevent over-interpretation and build public consent for the immigration and asylum system.

deb_ex.t: It is sad to see the Conservative party so spooked by the far right that they are trashing some of the finest work of their greatest Prime Minister, Winston Churchill. When he said
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the Conservative call to leave the ECHR, invoking Churchill's legacy, and defends the government's approach of reforming rather than abandoning the convention domestically and internationally.

deb_ex.t: I beg to move, That this House does not insist on its disagreement to Lords Amendment 2 but proposes Amendment (a) to the Lords Amendment.
I beg to move, That this House insists on its disagreement with the Lords in their Amendments 89B and 89C but proposes amendment (a) in lieu of those amendments.
Gas is currently setting the price 60% of the time, compared with 90% in 2020. We need to go further, but we are taking action to do that.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress on decoupling gas and electricity prices, noting gas now sets the price 60% of the time versus 90% in 2020, and promises further action through contracts for difference and clean power investment.

deb_ex.t: The answer to that is simple: yes, absolutely. Everyone can see with their eyes what is driving up energy bills: our acute exposure to global fossil fuel markets that we do not con
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the call to go further and faster, argues the solution is investing in home-grown renewables, and criticises the Conservatives for abandoning the cross-party consensus on clean energy.

deb_ex.t: We are proud that over the past two years we have unlocked £100 billion of investment in clean power.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that clean power is the route to lower bills, highlights £100 billion of investment unlocked over two years, and criticises the Conservatives for abandoning that direction.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member is completely right that our route out of this is through clean power, and we need to ensure that consumers and businesses feel the benefit through electrification.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the questioner that the government has a strategy, pointing to the warm homes plan for solar and clean heat access, and affirms that electrification is the way forward with European countries watching UK progress.

deb_ex.t: any decision I make will be compatible with our climate commitments. That is the first responsibility I have as Secretary of State
deb_ex.sum: Declines to discuss specific consenting decisions but assures the House that any decision will be compatible with the Government's climate commitments.

deb_ex.t: lowering bills for households and businesses is at the very heart of our agenda
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's broad energy agenda, emphasising affordability, clean power, the warm homes plan, and new public bodies to deliver energy security.

deb_ex.t: We are and have been clear that oil and gas will be part of our energy mix for years to come.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the Falklands decision is not the UK Government's to make and reaffirms commitment to managing existing fields while diversifying to clean power.

deb_ex.t: On his watch, from 2016 to 2024, 75,000 oil and gas jobs were lost, because the Conservatives had no plan.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the attack, noting 75,000 oil and gas jobs were lost under the Conservatives, and pledges a proper transition plan for workers.

deb_ex.t: We have a plan to tackle that; the Conservative party does not.
deb_ex.sum: Points to the £150 bill reduction already announced and argues that diversifying into renewables and nuclear is the only lasting solution to high energy costs.

deb_ex.t: Yes, I will meet my hon. Friend, who is a brilliant champion, and her constituent.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to meet the MP and her constituent to discuss the EnviroShip renewable energy transport proposal.

deb_ex.t: we are running up clean energy to reduce our exposure to global fossil fuel markets and rolling out the warm homes plan so that we can upgrade our homes.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government actions to reduce energy bills including scrapping VAT on electricity, the warm homes plan, and expanding clean energy to cut exposure to fossil fuel markets.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right to give the example of Octopus Energy in his constituency. Through the warm homes plan, we are investing record amounts—billions—in upgrading our homes, bec
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the example raised and outlines the warm homes plan investment in home upgrades, stating solar, batteries and insulation can save households £600 to £800.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend asks an important question. We are acutely aware that low-income families will be hit hardest by rising prices. We are working with others across Government, includi
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the pressure on low-income families, lists existing measures including VAT removal and the warm home discount, and reassures that the government is working across departments for further support.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Member raises an important point. We know that families in off-grid households are under huge pressure, and we are taking action to support them. We have put aside £
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges pressure on off-grid households and outlines existing support including £50 million for heating oil users and new regulation, while committing to do more.

deb_ex.t: We are providing breathing space and standing by people because we need to, but absolutely taking the hard long-term action so that we can fix this problem for good.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach, arguing clean energy and market reform are the long-term solution to reducing bills, while short-term breathing-space measures are already in place.

deb_ex.t: Let no one be in any doubt, however, that we understand that the status quo is untenable, and we will take the action that is necessary to drive bills down.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the government understands the winter pressure on families and reaffirms commitment to the warm home discount, home upgrades and further action to drive bills down.

deb_ex.t: I gently point out to the right hon. Member that less than 1% of the land will be taken up by solar farms, even under our most ambitious assumptions, but let us come back to the co
deb_ex.sum: Corrects the claim about solar farm land use and defends renewables as the route to affordable bills, contrasting the government's plan with the opposition's lack of one.

deb_ex.t: Their cheap power plan is based on dodgy numbers and, candidly, we do have a plan for how to get bills down.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the Conservative cheap power plan as based on dodgy figures and attacks the Conservatives' 14-year record of inaction on clean energy, defending the government's own plan.

deb_ex.t: I join the shadow Leader of the House in sending our deepest condolences to the people of Spain in the aftermath of yesterday’s horrendous train crash, taking the lives of 68 peopl
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Budget as providing a clear plan giving families and businesses breathing space, points to council tax payments, business rates relief, housing support, and challenges the Conservatives' economic record.

deb_ex.t: Not only do I join my hon. Friend in congratulating Connor on completing such an extraordinary adventure; I thank him for doing so for such a good cause.
deb_ex.sum: Joins in congratulating Connor McElwaine on his remarkable charity cycle ride and wishes him safe travels home.

deb_ex.t: I always find the hon. Gentleman’s comments both honest and brave, and admitting that he is a Tottenham Hotspur fan is characteristic of him. [ Laughter. ] I understand his frustra
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges frustration at the postponed AI debate, points to the Government's £700 million AI investment in the Budget and upcoming G20 presidency, and commits to finding time for a debate.

deb_ex.t: I join my hon. Friend in condemning the appalling incident in Wakefield and reaffirming that all forms of hatred and division have no place in our society.
deb_ex.sum: Condemns the Wakefield attack, reaffirms that hatred has no place in society, and commits to finding time for a future debate on social cohesion.

deb_ex.t: As ever, I thank the hon. Gentleman for the hard work he does as Chair of the Backbench Business Committee, and indeed the rest of the Committee for the work they do. I join him in
deb_ex.sum: Sends Diwali wishes to the Hindu community, commits to raising concerns about Hindus in Pakistan with the FCDO, and says the Government takes the treatment of minority faith communities very seriously.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely agree with my hon. Friend that we should all take pride in the success of the Lionesses. We are committed to supporting every aspect of women’s sport, with Sport Engla
deb_ex.sum: Expresses concern at the discriminatory FA criteria raised and offers to facilitate a meeting with Sport Ministers to pursue the matter.

deb_ex.t: I will take away his point, and I will do my very best to make sure that the announcement is made in the appropriate way.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern about how the Sea Link announcement is made and commits to ensuring it is handled appropriately.

deb_ex.t: I understand that he has a meeting with the Parliamentary Secretary for the Cabinet Office in his diary, and I hope that meeting will address his concerns.
deb_ex.sum: Points to a scheduled Cabinet Office meeting that should address the hon. Member's concerns about the Student Loans Company outsourcing.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Gentleman will know how difficult these decisions can be, and I know the concern that such matters raise in constituencies like his—let us be absolutely clear and ho
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the genuine local concerns and commits to raising them with the Home Secretary, stressing the importance of taking communities with them on difficult decisions.

deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government by pointing to the inherited backlog of 2 million awaiting reassessment and announces Budget plans to tackle work capability assessment delays.

deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's record, noting welfare grew faster under the Conservatives and citing universal credit reform, personalised employment support and the youth guarantee.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the frustration, credits her predecessor's efforts, and gives an undertaking to the House to drive progress on redress and all Hughes report recommendations.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms the DLA-to-PIP transfer age proposal is under consideration following the Green Paper consultation and pledges cross-government working.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's record on defence, citing increased spending, recruitment and morale, and commitment to warfighting readiness by 2030.

deb_ex.t: at the spending review next year, the Chancellor will set out the spending profile that takes us to 3% and 3.5%.
deb_ex.sum: Details the trajectory of defence spending from 2.3% to a planned 3.5% of GDP and lists new equipment investments including autonomous drones and a hybrid Navy.

deb_ex.t: Project Safari was delivered from start to finish in three months—it is a model for how I expect other companies to react to our move to warfighting readiness.
deb_ex.sum: Praises Project Safari as a model for industry collaboration, highlighting faster delivery and greater access for small businesses in test and evaluation.

deb_ex.t: the review is on and the elections are on, and I am ready to get on with it
deb_ex.sum: Rayner confirms the review and elections are proceeding and expresses willingness to work with the questioner to resolve uncertainty.

deb_ex.t: the timetable for devolution should not be affected. We need to make sure that we make the right decisions on local government reform
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the rapid review will not delay devolution and that the right decisions on local government reform will be made at pace.

deb_ex.t: I do not believe that is a waste of the time and resources that have been put in. I believe that local government reform is an opportunity for Norfolk
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the characterisation of waste, says she has reviewed decisions with respect for Norfolk's work, and commits to working with local leaders at pace to provide certainty.

deb_ex.t: Again, I say to my hon. Friend that I recognise the work that has gone in. That work is not wasted. The pause will be about working with local areas at pace to get this right, but
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the work done, says the pause is about getting things right quickly, and offers ministerial engagement to ensure the right devolution package for Lancashire.

deb_ex.t: I want to reassure the hon. Member that this is about getting the process right. I want him and those local organisations to get in contact with my officials
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the process is about getting things right, points to transition funding commitments, and invites affected organisations to contact the Department.

deb_ex.t: I am absolutely clear that I want to take this forward. Local government reform is a priority, and I want to undertake it at pace
deb_ex.sum: Provides reassurance that local work was not wasted, explains the review was necessary given judicial review advice, and reaffirms local government reform as a priority to be taken forward at pace.

deb_ex.t: I do know what I am doing. I know that this has been a disappointment for some areas. I do not make this statement to the House lightly
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the criticism with humour, insists she does know what she is doing, and expresses sincere commitment to getting the process right for Worcestershire and other areas.

deb_ex.t: devolution can happen at pace, and that it will unlock potential. I am sure that the Minister will be happy to meet him
deb_ex.sum: Agrees devolution can proceed at pace and offers a ministerial meeting with Staffordshire MPs to unlock the area's potential.

deb_ex.t: I gently say to the hon. Member that while I appreciate she uses language like “shock and anger”, it was important to me, as Secretary of State, to make the right decision, so I ca
deb_ex.sum: Gently pushes back on the language of shock and anger, reaffirms that reform will unlock potential for Hertfordshire, and points to transition funding and the opportunity to tackle adult social care.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely believe that local government is critical to ensuring that we get the devolution agenda right, and that we must build back resilience at a local level
deb_ex.sum: Affirms the importance of listening to local government, acknowledges the pressures on councils, and commits to building resilience at the local level through the devolution agenda.

deb_ex.t: I will not drop it, because I believe that the people of Essex and people all over England deserve good local services
deb_ex.sum: Refuses to drop the process, insisting Essex residents deserve improved local services, and offers to meet local leaders to progress reform.

deb_ex.sum: Responds warmly with humour about Sherwood Forest and her own hiking mishap, and offers a ministerial meeting to discuss devolution and local government progress for the area.

deb_ex.t: I am looking at the areas, and that I will look to ensure that all the consultation, information and advice is correct and that we are making robust decisions
deb_ex.sum: Assures the member she is reviewing all consultation and advice to make robust decisions, and invites further contact with herself or the relevant minister.

deb_ex.t: Again, I do recognise the frustration that my hon. Friend has expressed at parts of this process. I want to ensure that we take this forward and that it is robust, and that is why
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the frustration, explains the review is to ensure legal robustness, and invites the Member to meet ministers to resolve concerns.

deb_ex.t: I think it is fair to say that there is a very strong argument and rationale for it. I will make sure that the review happens speedily and that we can give those reassurances as pa
deb_ex.sum: Offers measured reassurance that there is a strong rationale for the Isle of Wight's position and commits to addressing it speedily in the review.

deb_ex.t: local government reform is challenging and complex, but the aim for me is to deliver better services for local people. That means building the homes that we desperately need
deb_ex.sum: Commits to engaging residents in the review process and reaffirms that LGR aims to deliver better local services, defending the decision to pause and get it right.

deb_ex.t: I pay tribute to the hon. Lady’s local leaders and the work that they are doing in local government. I recognise the challenges that they face, and I have outlined what has happene
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to local leaders, acknowledges the challenges, and explains that previous ministers requested more time to consider proposals now under the wider review.

deb_ex.t: Devolution is at the heart of our plans to rewire the state. I am making this statement today exactly to ensure that that happens.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms devolution remains central to the Government's plans and that the statement is intended to keep that on track.

deb_ex.t: I do not see local government reorganisation as a wasted endeavour. I have been really clear about the reason for the pause: to get the decision right.
deb_ex.sum: Defends LGR as worthwhile, explains the pause is to get decisions right, references transitional funding, and commits to working at pace for the area.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely want to reassure hon. Members that this is not the end of local government reorganisation, because I am absolutely committed to it. I commend my hon. Friend for his wo
deb_ex.sum: Reassures Members that LGR is not finished, commends collaborative work done so far, and commits to pressing ahead on a firm legal footing.

deb_ex.t: I want to reassure the hon. Member that we do not want to leave rural Devon behind, either. As the Minister, my hon. Friend the Member for Oldham West, Chadderton and Royton (Jim M
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that rural Devon will not be left behind, commits to arranging a meeting with the Minister, and reiterates the review is about ensuring people are heard.

deb_ex.t: We are committed to devolution and to devolving power. The Prime Minister has made it really clear that that is one of his priorities.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government's absolute commitment to devolution and stresses the aim is to give areas the resources and support they need to flourish.

deb_ex.t: I totally recognise that Cambridgeshire has a huge amount of potential, and we will absolutely ensure that a meeting is set up with myself or the Minister. I gently say that I unde
deb_ex.sum: Commits to arranging a meeting for Cambridgeshire, explains the review is to ensure decisions are correct, and expresses confidence in the area's potential.

deb_ex.t: I reassure the Member that I am going to review those issues and make sure that I am confident in the decision that is made, including within the boundaries, to ensure that any dec
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the Member that the review will cover boundaries and decisions, commits to consultation, and promises a confident, informed final decision.

deb_ex.t: This is not about overturning or overpowering local decisions. This is about me reviewing these decisions and making sure that there is a robust system
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies the review is not about overturning local decisions but ensuring robustness, and promises to complete the process within weeks.

deb_ex.t: I am not a big fan of referendums, if I am really honest. That is my personal opinion, but I am open to having discussions
deb_ex.sum: Rayner says she is personally not keen on referendums but is open to discussions on how to ensure local residents feel engaged in the LGR process.

deb_ex.t: I have asked the Minister for local government, devolution and regional growth to undertake a rapid review of the local government reorganisation programme.
deb_ex.sum: Rayner outlines the scope of the rapid review covering 18 decisions already taken and two remaining areas, and commits to reporting back to Parliament at the earliest opportunity.

deb_ex.t: This is a pause. It is a review—I have made that absolutely crystal clear—for me to consider the legal advice that was provided as part of the JR process, as well as for me to be a
deb_ex.sum: Rayner clarifies the process is a genuine pause and review in response to legal advice and the Prime Minister's direction, and directs councils with financial concerns to her Department.

deb_ex.t: I recognise the work that has gone in from her local area and those representatives, and I pay tribute to the work that they are doing.
deb_ex.sum: Rayner reassures the hon. Member that the review aims to get decisions right and recognises the work done locally, committing to weeks rather than months for the review.

deb_ex.t: I am sure that the Minister will set a meeting up in his diary as soon as possible, so that we expedite the process.
deb_ex.sum: Rayner thanks the hon. Member, commits to ensuring local representatives are heard, and says the Minister will arrange a meeting as soon as possible.

deb_ex.t: I say again that the review does not include the reorganisation of Surrey. Councillors have been elected and new councils go live from 1 April.
deb_ex.sum: Rayner clarifies that the review does not include Surrey, which is proceeding with new councils going live from 1 April.

deb_ex.t: The review does not include the reorganisation of Surrey. As I said, councillors have been elected already, and the new councils go live on 1 April 2027.
deb_ex.sum: Rayner reiterates that the review excludes Surrey, that new councils go live in April 2027, and expresses confidence they will deliver vital services across the area.

deb_ex.t: I appreciate the hon. Member’s frustration, but— [ Interruption. ]
deb_ex.sum: Rayner begins to acknowledge the hon. Member's frustration before being interrupted.

deb_ex.t: I do appreciate the frustration in Essex. In response to the right hon. Member, who was here a while ago and raised these issues, I made it really clear
deb_ex.sum: Rayner acknowledges frustration in Essex and begins to explain that LGR is about delivering for local people.

deb_ex.t: local government reorganisation is delivering for people across Essex. I understand the pressures on local services. Essex does have a need for more housing and more infrastructure
deb_ex.sum: Rayner affirms that LGR is delivering for Essex residents and that the Government will work with local people to address housing, infrastructure and reform needs.

deb_ex.t: 72 people, 18 of them children, died in the Grenfell Tower tragedy. It was a deadly betrayal and a national tragedy that must never happen again.
deb_ex.sum: Rayner introduces the Bill by citing the Grenfell tragedy and setting out the scale of unsafe cladding. She details Government action taken since 2024 including the remediation acceleration plan and new funding for social housing providers.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms cross-departmental investment in skilled workforce and references the national identification drive to understand the scale of unsafe cladding.

deb_ex.sum: Responds that the Bill introduces tougher consequences for those who fail to remediate, including fines up to £500,000 and criminal prosecution, and highlights progress from the national identification drive.

deb_ex.t: I am really sorry to hear about the situation in my hon. Friend’s constituency. Since the Grenfell tragedy, many hon. Members across the House have had similar experiences of fires
deb_ex.sum: Expresses personal concern about unsafe buildings and the fires that have occurred since Grenfell, and signals she will address waking watch costs later in her speech.

deb_ex.sum: States the Bill aims to close loopholes that allow manufacturers and developers to avoid responsibility, and reports that remediation has been completed on over 470 more buildings since the acceleration plan was published.

deb_ex.t: My officials will have heard that call, and I or the Minister for Homelessness, Democracy, Communities and Faith, who is in her place, will be happy to meet my hon. Friend. Coming
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to a ministerial meeting and sets out action on waking watches including £62 million for fire alarms and forthcoming secondary legislation to ban insurance commissions being passed to leaseholders.

deb_ex.sum: Explains that PAS 9980 will become the mandatory standard for fire risk appraisals of external walls, creating a single consistent assessment approach, and previews forthcoming leasehold reform legislation.

deb_ex.t: I am happy to continue the conversations with my hon. Friend to make sure that we get that balance right; that is what we want.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to continue discussions to get the balance of penalties right and reaffirms the Bill's goal of compelling responsible parties to remediate buildings.

deb_ex.t: We are working on that. PAS 9980 is the established approach used across Government remediation programmes. It provides a robust and proportionate way of identifying the risk of fi
deb_ex.sum: Responds that work is ongoing and defends PAS 9980 as a robust and proportionate method for identifying fire risk in external walls.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend’s intervention shows that the remediation Bill is crucial to us meeting our ongoing challenges with the remediation acceleration plan. The relevant Minister will be
deb_ex.sum: Agrees a ministerial meeting on fire safety regulations and sets out the Bill's key provisions: a register of medium-rise buildings, mandatory external wall assessment standards, a new legal duty to remediate and escalating penalties includ

deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to Amanda Walker's family, confirms she has written to Amanda's mother, and announces new grant funding for high-risk internal fire safety defects in collectively owned and enfranchised buildings to narrow the gap with protecte

deb_ex.sum: Sets out Government plans to extend leaseholder protections, investigate non-qualifying leases, and expand the portfolio protection from three to six properties, reaffirming manifesto commitments.

deb_ex.t: We are hoping to make sure that nobody is left out, or left feeling those pressures. My right hon. Friend makes an important point. I outlined before that many of the groups we hav
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the House that the Government intends no one to be left out, and invites Members to meet the Building Safety Minister to explore how far protections can be extended.

deb_ex.t: The new national planning policy framework, published on 17 August, includes a number of new policies designed to increase densification inside settlements, including by encouragin
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government measures in the new NPPF to increase densification, including upward expansion of homes and creation of new dwellings in existing plots.

deb_ex.t: We have not got it wrong: the new NPPF does prioritise urban development and densification.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's NPPF, stating it does prioritise urban development and that local authorities can justify lower targets based on local constraints, with green belt release only after exhausting other options.

deb_ex.t: The Government are undertaking a number of pieces of work to look at what more we can do to revitalise our high streets. The Secretary of State and I are looking specifically at wh
deb_ex.sum: Outlines government work to revitalise high streets and bring empty homes back into use, including arming local authorities with necessary powers.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges viability challenges for house builders and explains that the government brought forward an emergency package with the Mayor of London specifically to get stalled sites moving.

deb_ex.t: we provide direct financial support for essential infrastructure in areas of greatest housing demand through land and infrastructure funding programmes.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government policy: local authorities plan infrastructure via development plans and funding statements, backed by strengthened national planning policy and direct financial support.

deb_ex.sum: Defends existing developer contribution rules as legally binding and enforceable, passes on the devolution request to colleagues, and invites the MP to write with details of the specific case.

deb_ex.t: As I just said to a previous question, we are looking at what more we can do to give local authorities the powers they need to bring empty homes back into use. My hon. Friend will
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges work to give councils powers to bring empty homes back into use and points to section 106 agreements as the mechanism for securing infrastructure and affordable housing.

deb_ex.t: we have strengthened national planning policy to ensure that community facilities and public service infrastructure are brought forward.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's record, points to strengthened planning policy, developer contributions and direct infrastructure financing, and acknowledges more remains to be done.

deb_ex.t: We regularly speak to colleagues in other Departments, including the Department of Health and Social Care, to ensure that we get that infrastructure up front and alongside development.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the legitimacy of the concern, explains that infrastructure delivery involves both developer contributions and workforce challenges, and confirms regular cross-departmental talks with DHSC.

deb_ex.t: inappropriate development in it should not be approved unless justified by very special circumstances.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out that the NPPF contains strong green-belt protections and that local planning authorities are responsible for setting and reviewing green-belt boundaries.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges concerns about station-area development but defends the NPPF approach, noting that proposals must not prejudice long-term plans and must be scaled to available infrastructure.

deb_ex.t: We will continue to explore further ways in which we might support councils to expand their stock of social homes, including low-cost borrowing options.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government steps already taken to support council borrowing and investment, including right-to-buy reform and a 10-year rent settlement, and signals further exploration of low-cost borrowing options.

deb_ex.t: As I made clear, we have already acted to build capacity in the sector, and will continue to explore further ways in which we might increase the headroom available to councils and
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the government's commitment to the self-financing principle but acknowledges HRA debt pressures and pledges continued exploration of ways to increase headroom for councils, including low-cost borrowing.

deb_ex.t: 30% of the funding will go to London. That will allow London to deliver at least £6 billion of initial allocations, over half of which will be for council housing.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges London's housing delivery challenges and highlights that 30% of social and affordable homes programme funding will go to London, with over half earmarked for council housing, while offering further discussion.

deb_ex.t: We have made changes to help more councils access an HRA, raising the threshold from 200 homes to 1,000 homes to provide support in that area.
deb_ex.sum: Outlines the government's raising of the HRA threshold from 200 to 1,000 homes and signals consideration of further measures to ensure public control of registered providers, pointing to the Social Housing Bill.

deb_ex.t: As the hon. Gentleman is hopefully aware, we have already taken action to reduce maximum right-to-buy cash discounts. Through the Social Housing Bill—as I mentioned, it has its Sec
deb_ex.sum: Points to government action already taken on right-to-buy discounts and forthcoming Social Housing Bill measures, including a 35-year ban on right to buy for new build social homes, and invites the hon. Member's support.

deb_ex.t: The definition of “reasonable walking distance” is set out in the glossary of the national planning policy framework. For the purposes of policies relating to land around well conn
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's definition of reasonable walking distance as 800 metres or 10 minutes' walk under the national planning policy framework glossary.

deb_ex.t: these are some of the most sustainable locations for new housing in the country
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach, reaffirming the brownfield-first policy and the sustainability rationale for development near well-connected stations, while offering to discuss the constituency's specific concerns.

deb_ex.t: I want to ensure that every opportunity is taken to retain homes in the social housing sector.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern about housing association asset sales and assures the House that the Government is exploring further steps to protect social housing stock.

deb_ex.t: As I have said, there are strong protections in the national planning policy framework. It is for local authorities to decide whether exceptional circumstances exist for the releas
deb_ex.sum: Sets out existing NPPF protections for the green belt and reaffirms the Government's commitment to preserving it while allowing local authorities to assess exceptional circumstances.

deb_ex.t: Primary legislation was taken through by the previous Government, and we have a plan to switch on the necessary secondary legislation to ensure that we have transparency over build-out rates.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the claim that primary legislation is needed, noting the previous Government already passed it and that secondary legislation to deliver build-out transparency will follow soon.

deb_ex.t: I am always happy to meet my hon. Friend.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to meet the hon. Member and suggests the relevant Minister would lead but offers to join if housing matters arise.

deb_ex.sum: Reminds Places for People of its consumer standards obligations, highlights Awaab's law on hazard repair timescales, and offers to look into the specific development if further information is provided.

deb_ex.t: Homeowners should not be expected to shoulder the financial consequences of defective work.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees homeowners should not bear the cost of defective work, acknowledges the legal complexity of the Goodrich Mews case, and confirms willingness to meet the hon. Member again.

deb_ex.t: These measures are driving up the quality and the safety of homes, and we can do that while increasing supply.
deb_ex.sum: Defends minimum energy efficiency and decent homes standards as improving quality and safety while maintaining the Government's ambition to increase housing supply.

deb_ex.t: It is not a blanket policy; it relates to well-connected stations. I have set out the definition, with appropriate minimum densities to go with it.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the policy applies specifically to well-connected stations and is not a blanket rule, defending the Government's planning approach.

deb_ex.t: We take the hon. Gentleman’s planning policies about as seriously as the country took his conference.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses Reform UK's planning proposals with a sharp quip, implying they carry as little weight as the party's conference.

deb_ex.t: The Government remain fully committed to delivering nationally significant growth in Greater Cambridge.
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the Government's full commitment to nationally significant growth in Greater Cambridge through a centrally led urban development corporation working with local leaders.

deb_ex.t: At least 60% of that historic £39 billion will go to social rented homes. We have delivered the highest number of council homes since records began in 1991-92.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the charge of lacking ambition, highlighting that at least 60% of the £39 billion will go to social rented homes and that record council homes have been delivered.

deb_ex.t: I am more than happy to meet my hon. Friend about the issue.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to meet the MP to discuss the community-led housing problem in his constituency.

deb_ex.t: the applicant is separate from our Department; we are the stewards of the process and will make the determination on the basis of those criteria.
deb_ex.sum: Explains the Department will assess any Crown development application against set criteria on its merits, noting the applicant is separate from the Department.

deb_ex.t: I am more than happy to meet my hon. Friend and other colleagues.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to meet the MP and Cornish colleagues to discuss housing and devolution.

deb_ex.t: we want to better understand whether local authorities are making full use of existing powers, but I reassure my hon. Friend that we keep the matter under review.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges varied practice on HMO regulation, states the Government wants to check local authorities are using existing powers, and reassures the MP the matter is kept under review.

deb_ex.t: That is precisely why we have introduced strategic cross-boundary planning through spatial development strategies— [ Interruption. ] The hon. Member says that it is not working, bu
deb_ex.sum: Points to spatial development strategies introduced under the Planning and Infrastructure Act as the mechanism to address cross-boundary planning issues, and offers a meeting.

deb_ex.t: I think the hon. Lady is referring to unauthorised development. We have strengthened national planning policy in respect of intentional unauthorised development, making it harder t
deb_ex.sum: Explains the government has tightened national planning policy to make retrospective permission harder for intentional unauthorised development, and acknowledges a more structured pattern is emerging that the government is working across de

deb_ex.sum: Thanks his colleague and confirms final decisions on the seven proposed new town sites will be brought forward shortly following the earlier consultation.

deb_ex.sum: The Minister moves Second Reading, arguing the Bill will protect social housing stock, reform right to buy, strengthen domestic abuse tenant protections, and reduce bureaucracy to boost social housebuilding.

deb_ex.sum: The Minister confirms councils will be given flexibility, outlines the three core objectives of the Bill, and details the right to buy reforms including extending eligibility to 10 years and exempting new builds for 30 years.

deb_ex.t: I recognise the strength of feeling in the House on disposals. I want to ensure that every opportunity is taken to retain homes in the social housing sector.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister acknowledges the concern about disposals, outlines the new notification requirements in the Bill, and signals the Government is looking at further steps to retain social housing stock.

deb_ex.t: We want to see councils once again directly delivering homes at scale. We also want councils working in far closer partnership with housing associations
deb_ex.sum: The Minister agrees councils should directly deliver homes at scale and in partnership with housing associations, and outlines new disposal notification requirements to prevent social homes being lost to the private market.

deb_ex.t: It is disappointing to hear that my hon. Friend’s local authority is not interested in any way in trying to bring those homes back under local authority control. As I said, there a
deb_ex.sum: The Minister acknowledges limits on government action over independent housing associations but commits to extending the notification window before disposal and to exploring further measures to protect social housing stock.

deb_ex.sum: The Minister turns to the Bill's second objective, explaining that existing law fails domestic abuse victims in social housing and the Bill will provide legal mechanisms to remove perpetrators and allow victims to remain.

deb_ex.t: after years of marginalisation, this Government have emphatically and unashamedly asserted the necessity and value of social rented homes.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister concludes his opening speech, summarising the Bill's three objectives and commending it to the House as a landmark step in protecting and expanding social rented housing.

deb_ex.sum: The Minister invites engagement from all sides on improving the Bill and formally commends it to the House.

deb_ex.sum: Affirms the Government takes resilience seriously across all threats and indicates the Prime Minister will have more to say in due course.
