deb_ex.sum: Firmly rejects the charge of political bias, reminds the House the IOPC investigation is independent, and cautions against making findings of fact before the investigation concludes.

deb_ex.t: I also announce an independent, root-and-branch review of the protective security provided by the state to those in public life
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary sets out the government's response to terrorist and hostile state threats, announces an expansion of police protection to former MPs and public figures, and launches an independent review of protective security led by Sir

deb_ex.t: I do not believe that anything has happened in this investigation that is i
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary defends the bail decision as an operational police matter, declines to comment on intelligence, and says she does not believe information about Kerry's list was withheld inappropriately.

deb_ex.t: I will pick up those conversations with counter-terror policing and wider criminal justice system partners to ensure that we have stress-tested the robustness of our arrangements
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary responds to the Speaker's concern about information-sharing, commits to stress-testing arrangements with counter-terror policing, and pledges to update the Speaker and the House.

deb_ex.t: we must have a wider national conversation about the cultural changes we have seen. We need a wider societal response against antisemitism
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary highlights £250 million of new funding for Jewish community protection and agrees that a wider societal response against antisemitism is needed beyond physical security measures.

deb_ex.t: I am in good discussions with the Defence Secretary to ensure that all appropriate measures are being taken at our military bases
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary urges Members to model appropriate political behaviour, reaffirms close cooperation with the Defence Secretary on military base security, and offers to write to Wilkinson with an updated response.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for his question. The policies of another political party are a matter primarily for that political party, and I would expect it to have to explain the impac
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary puts responsibility on the Green Party to explain its motion, and reminds all councils that equality law applies fully to Jewish communities and cannot be overridden by political decisions.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely agree with the final remarks of the Chair of the Select Committee. None of us wants to be mourning another of our colleagues, either current or former, and that is why
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary acknowledges the protective security system is fragmented and has not kept pace with changes in political culture, and explains why the independent review and expansion of Operation Ford are necessary.

deb_ex.t: the Government have already allocated record funding of over £70 million for the protective security schemes for faith communities. That includes all faith communities
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary confirms over £70 million in protective security funding across all faith communities, including £40 million for mosques, and calls for wider societal change to reverse polarisation.

deb_ex.t: No one had or has diplomatic immunity—I can put that on the record immediately
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary categorically rules out diplomatic immunity for any suspect and defends the pace of information release as necessary to protect the integrity of a live investigation.

deb_ex.t: I will always keep these matters under review. It is important that we respect the right to protest and to political dissent
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary says police have powers to require removal of face coverings and pledges to keep the legislative framework under review to balance the right to protest against the freedoms of others.

deb_ex.t: Of course, I recognise the deep anxiety that will have been felt by the residents of Whelford; it must have been a terrifying experience for them. The hon. Lady will understand tha
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary acknowledges the distress caused to Whelford residents and offers to arrange a meeting between Savage and the Security Minister to address their concerns.

deb_ex.t: knife crime is down by 11%, knife homicides are down by 25% and knife-enabled robberies are down by 18%. That is huge progress, but we must do more.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out statistics showing knife crime down 11% since the election and outlines crackdowns in 230 affected areas alongside prevention work.

deb_ex.t: this Government stand ready to support them where we can.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the family's campaigning efforts, notes policing is devolved but confirms the Government stands ready to support the Scottish Government.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman is absolutely right. It is imperative that we get knives off our streets, and he will know that we have already taken 63,000 knives off our streets and banned ni
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the need to get knives off streets, cites 63,000 knives removed and ninja sword ban, and flags a forthcoming consultation on the wider sale of knives regime.

deb_ex.t: I have an excellent working relationship with EU partners, particularly with France, which has helped prevent over 50,000 crossings since the election. The EU asylum pact has yet t
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach by highlighting the Franco-British cooperation that has prevented over 50,000 crossings, while cautioning that the EU asylum pact is not a silver bullet.

deb_ex.t: I am not going to conduct a negotiation with the European Union from this Dispatch Box. The hon. Member will know, as I have said to Liberal Democrat Members before, that we are of
deb_ex.sum: Declines to negotiate publicly from the Dispatch Box but signals ongoing discussions on law enforcement and data sharing with EU partners ahead of the UK-EU summit.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right. That is why this Government have been working to reset our relationship with the European Union. Of course, our co-operation with France is central to our
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the bilateral Franco-British approach, citing the successor Sandhurst agreement and a 43% reduction in small boat numbers as evidence of its effectiveness.

deb_ex.t: On returns under the pact for the countries that are in it, those returns are not happening at scale.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the claim that joining the EU asylum pact would be a silver bullet, pointing out that returns within the pact are not happening at scale and that the UK achieved more removals through its French agreement.

deb_ex.t: Honestly, what absolute piffle from the hon. Gentleman. He will know that the Prime Minister has been discussing having an open debate; that is not the same as settled policy, as t
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the question as misrepresentation, clarifying that the Prime Minister's call for open debate is not settled policy and accusing the Liberal Democrats of cherry-picking on freedom of movement.

deb_ex.t: We are committed to working closely together to ensure that we do not allow any illegal entry, either from the United Kingdom into the Republic or vice versa.
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary says she regularly discusses the issue with Irish counterparts and affirms the government's commitment to preventing illegal cross-border entry in both directions.

deb_ex.t: I am surprised by the correspondence that the hon. Member has received. She is welcome to share that with me. That is absolutely not the case for the announcements made in Septembe
deb_ex.sum: Disputes the correspondence received by the Member and reaffirms that Afghan women and girls will be prioritised as announced in September.

deb_ex.t: there is a world of difference between someone selling books and enjoying the fruits of their labour and saying that they will use that money to fund a proscribed organisation
deb_ex.sum: Rebukes the Member for irresponsibility, distinguishing between selling books and directing profits to a proscribed organisation, and defends the legal process by which proscription occurred.

deb_ex.t: our modern slavery arrangements are subject to strengthening in the Immigration and Asylum Bill, which is currently going through this House
deb_ex.sum: Notes that the Immigration and Asylum Bill already strengthens modern slavery arrangements and offers a meeting to discuss further changes.

deb_ex.t: Last December, Henry Nowak’s life was cut short in a horrific and senseless act of violence. My thoughts today are with Henry’s family and friends, who have shown extraordinary cou
deb_ex.sum: Announces an independent review into the death of Henry Nowak, covering missed opportunities to intervene, family support, and police conduct, with an initial report due within five months.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend will know that we have made it easier for the police to seize e-bikes on the spot, and we have cut the timeframe for disposal to just seven days. Police forces are a
deb_ex.sum: Outlines new powers allowing police to seize and dispose of illegally used e-bikes within seven days, noting forces are already making use of them.

deb_ex.t: Let me confirm for the House that settlement will be earned, not be automatic.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the shadow Home Secretary's challenge, reaffirms that settlement will be earned not automatic, and confirms policy will be set out in due course following consultation.

deb_ex.t: As the right hon. Gentleman is well aware, it is long-standing policy not to comment on individual cases. He often brings such individual cases to the Dispatch Box, so he should kn
deb_ex.sum: Declines to comment on an individual case in line with long-standing policy and reaffirms that all individuals seeking entry must meet immigration rules.

deb_ex.t: Small boat returns under this Government are at a record high, and our Immigration and Asylum Bill will help us to remove people faster than ever before.
deb_ex.sum: Claims small boat returns are at a record high and that the Immigration and Asylum Bill will accelerate removals, contrasting government progress with the previous administration's record.

deb_ex.t: Under this Government, small boat returns have increased. This is a crisis that began on the Conservative Government’s watch and got worse under the Conservative party; this Govern
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's record on small boat returns and attributes the crisis to the previous Conservative administration.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right that we need to maximise the numbers we are returning from this country. He will know that asylum-related returns are at their highest level since 2010. Thi
deb_ex.sum: Confirms asylum-related returns are at their highest since 2010 and promises further progress on increasing removals.

deb_ex.t: We have been able to make more progress on returns as a Government while remaining within the ECHR, and we will continue that going forward.
deb_ex.sum: Defends remaining within the ECHR, distinguishing it from EU rules, and argues the government is achieving progress on returns without leaving the convention.

deb_ex.t: Let me take this opportunity to pay tribute to all our partners in Portsmouth—the local authority, the police and all others—for their co-operation in dealing with the crossings la
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to Portsmouth partners, acknowledges gang displacement to new routes, and assures residents the government will continue to pursue criminal gangs and reduce crossings.

deb_ex.t: It is absolutely right for a Government seeking a system based on order, control and the principles of fairness and contribution to look at both the legal and illegal migration sys
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach to both legal and illegal migration and says further announcements on indefinite leave to remain policy will follow in due course.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right: not only are small boat returns up and asylum-related returns at their highest level since 2010, but in our first two years in office, this Government have
deb_ex.sum: Confirms returns of foreign offenders are up 41% on the last two years of the Conservative government and highlights returns co-operation with countries of origin and appeals reform.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Lady knows that given that there are outstanding issues to be considered in this case, I cannot comment on the facts. She should know that, as a principle, anyone who rece
deb_ex.sum: Declines to comment on the specific case due to outstanding issues but restates the principle that anyone sentenced to 12 months or more who poses a danger will have their asylum claim rejected.

deb_ex.t: we need to get maximum benefit for the travelling public. I hope to have future discussions about future rounds of the Access for All scheme
deb_ex.sum: Minister confirms investment in station accessibility through the Access for All scheme, covering 31 stations, and signals future discussions on further rounds.

deb_ex.t: I am very grateful to my hon. Friend and her Committee for their interest in personal safety on the transport network, especially that of women and girls. We have an ambitious, evi
deb_ex.sum: Secretary of State outlines the Government's evidence-based programme to tackle VAWG on the transport network, including nine commitments and funding for CCTV connectivity.

deb_ex.t: I would be happy to meet my hon. Friend to discuss this issue. One of the key things that we are trying to do is improve public transport nodes
deb_ex.sum: Minister agrees to meet the MP and expresses interest in improving public transport nodes.

deb_ex.t: publicly owned operators are performing better, on average, when it comes to reliability and cancellations
deb_ex.sum: Secretary of State notes publicly owned operators are performing better on average and commits to seeking more information on the specific Fen line problems.

deb_ex.t: in the spending review the Chancellor allocated £57 million to deploy low earth orbit satellite technology on our mainline trains
deb_ex.sum: Secretary of State confirms procurement for enhanced wi-fi will begin later this year, backed by £57 million for low earth orbit satellite technology on mainline trains including LNER.

deb_ex.t: Let me take this issue away for her and talk to the Mayor of the West Midlands and all relevant parties to ascertain whether anything can be done
deb_ex.sum: Secretary of State expresses sympathy for affected businesses and commits to engaging with the Mayor of the West Midlands and relevant parties to explore mitigation measures.

deb_ex.t: there are currently no plans to expand that London-wide fare payment zone
deb_ex.sum: Secretary of State acknowledges the affordability concern but confirms there are no plans to expand the London-wide fare payment zone, while noting pay-as-you-go ticketing rollout in the south-east.

deb_ex.t: I do not have the specific answer he seeks, but I promise him that I will go away, find out and come back to him.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges she does not have the specific answer to hand but promises to investigate and respond to the Member directly.

deb_ex.t: I beg to move, That the Bill be now read a Second time. Today is an important day, as this Bill starts its Commons journey, but it is a hard day on which to talk about the critical
deb_ex.sum: Opens Second Reading by addressing the NATS outage, apologising to passengers, announcing an independent CAA review, and outlining the Bill's main provisions on passenger rights, airspace modernisation, slot reform and safety.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right to raise the impact on people who were caught up in this disruption. I have read reports of people having to sleep overnight in airports and people who have
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the serious impact of the outage on passengers, commits to leaving no stone unturned to understand what happened, and says tough questions must be asked about NATS system resilience.

deb_ex.t: The public would rightly expect the Transport Secretary, while standing at the Dispatch Box, to answer questions here and now, so I am happy to take any interventions.
deb_ex.sum: Declines to defer questions to tomorrow, invites interventions now, and explains that the Bill restores expired powers to update assimilated EU aviation law and outlines its enforcement and passenger rights provisions.

deb_ex.t: The Minister with responsibility for aviation, my hon. Friend the Member for Selby (Keir Mather), has kindly just said that he will be very happy to meet the hon. Gentleman to disc
deb_ex.sum: Confirms a ministerial meeting will be arranged on cabin air quality, outlines the Bill's accessibility commitments including scrapping the unfair compensation cap for damaged mobility equipment, and explains new CAA direct enforcement powe

deb_ex.t: We want to move swiftly on these issues, and the provisions in the Bill are designed to do just that.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Bill is designed to speed up regulatory processes, acknowledges Glasgow airport's economic importance and commits to supporting it further.

deb_ex.t: I can guarantee my hon. Friend that there will be meaningful consultation with local communities about airspace changes—this Bill does not change the processes around that.
deb_ex.sum: Guarantees meaningful local consultation on airspace changes, notes the proposed Heathrow night-time flight ban, and explains that modernisation is needed to prevent major flight disruption by 2040.

deb_ex.t: We need to find a simpler way of making these changes, because the previous mechanism was too cumbersome, and I believe that this is a sensible and proportionate change.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the noise threshold change as a sensible rebalancing between noise and emissions considerations, and continues explaining how the Bill enables more agile slot regulation following the loss of post-Brexit powers.

deb_ex.t: We have sought to prioritise work on airspace changes in the London region, given the benefits that it could bring to London and the south-east. I am aware that there has been agre
deb_ex.sum: Explains the priority given to London-region airspace changes while confirming agreement over the summer to resume work on Scotland's airspace modernisation.

deb_ex.t: This is not a blank cheque; it follows a well-established model in which trusted regulators make rules within boundaries set by Parliament.
deb_ex.sum: Offers to write with a timeline on the CAA priorities document, explains how safety rule-making is being handed to the CAA within parliamentary boundaries, and commends the Bill to the House.

deb_ex.t: I am sure I speak for the whole House when I say that our thoughts are with those affected by yesterday’s horrific train crash in Spain. Our Rail Accident Investigation Branch has
deb_ex.sum: Sets out a range of transport announcements from the Budget, including the fuel duty cut extension, EV charging costs, Leeds station investment, road resurfacing and the £2 bus fare cap.

deb_ex.t: Where insourcing drives better outcomes for passengers and better value for the taxpayer, we should undoubtedly look at it.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms she meets trade union leaders regularly and that insourcing has been raised at the Rail Engagement Group, signalling openness to insourcing where it delivers better outcomes.

deb_ex.t: It is entirely right that the Prime Minister wants to look closely at the detail of such a nationally significant project.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's position on Heathrow, saying it is carefully working through consultation responses and applying strict tests on climate, noise and air quality.

deb_ex.t: I say gently to the right hon. Gentleman that the ZEV mandate is the rarest of things: a policy brought in by his Government that I agree with. Sadly, after a good start, even they
deb_ex.sum: Defends the ZEV mandate as a rare good policy inherited from the Conservatives, points to rising EV sales as evidence it is working, and rejects any rollback.

deb_ex.t: I share the right hon. Lady’s disappointment in the decision of the Office of Rail and Road. It can independently make that decision. My had supported the application for that new
deb_ex.sum: Shares disappointment at the ORR decision, notes her department had supported the application, and commits to working with Network Rail and others to consider options for new direct services.

deb_ex.t: I agree with my hon. Friend that his constituents are right to expect a good service every day of the week, including Sundays. I assure him that the management of Northern is aroun
deb_ex.sum: Agrees constituents deserve a seven-day service and confirms Northern management is in talks with the RMT on a way forward.

deb_ex.t: Avanti West Coast is due to come into public ownership in March next year, and there is an opportunity to look again at the timetable over the course of the next few years. I recog
deb_ex.sum: Notes Avanti West Coast will enter public ownership in March and signals an opportunity to review timetables, acknowledging the importance of later services to west coast constituencies.

deb_ex.t: In this control period, we are spending over £2.5 billion on the railways to address climate change mitigation and adaptation.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights over £2.5 billion being spent on climate adaptation for railways, notes the ongoing RAIB investigation, and underlines that safety is paramount.

deb_ex.t: Having good mobile connectivity is something that people feel strongly about, and it could improve satisfaction with journeys.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the Member's campaigning on rail connectivity and commits to continuing cross-government discussions to improve mobile connectivity on GWR services.

deb_ex.t: the creation of Great British Railways will bring the management of track and train together, ending decades of fragmentation, and delivering better and more reliable services
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress on rail reform: six operators brought into public ownership, Great Western Railway renationalisation imminent, and Great British Railways to launch next year to end fragmentation.

deb_ex.t: our publicly owned railways should work in the service of passengers, and these extra trains would be a great example of that
deb_ex.sum: Praises the hon. Member's campaigning, welcomes West Midlands Trains' proposals for a trial, and backs the call for extra evening services to Lichfield.

deb_ex.t: It is for the new Welsh Government to confirm their own contribution to this project, so that we can get on and deliver it as quickly as possible.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms no Welsh Government contribution has yet been provided, praises the hon. Member's campaigning, and celebrates the government's own Budget commitment to Cardiff Parkway.

deb_ex.t: This Government are investing considerably in improving rail services and public transport connections in Cambridgeshire.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to follow up on the light rail proposal and highlights existing government investment in Cambridgeshire rail, including East West Rail and Cambridge South station.

deb_ex.t: we are prioritising improvements in the Yorkshire region, such as services from York to Leeds, and between Sheffield, Bradford and Leeds
deb_ex.sum: Sets out Northern Powerhouse Rail priorities in Yorkshire and acknowledges the York area capacity case, promising to keep all options under review.

deb_ex.t: I would be happy to continue those conversations about phase 2 as we head into the next spending review.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the government's phase 1 investment and agrees to continue discussions about phase 2 ahead of the next spending review.

deb_ex.t: We need to get the basics right on South Western to provide the service that she and her constituents deserve.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to discuss options with South Western for Hampton and Whitton, highlights benefits of renationalisation including new Arterio trains and reduced cancellations, while acknowledging more work is needed.

deb_ex.t: cancellations across publicly-owned operators were 3.9% compared to 4.9% for operators yet to transfer and still in private ownership
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the need for improved punctuality and reliability but defends the government's record by citing lower cancellation rates and higher punctuality among publicly owned operators compared with those still in private hands.

deb_ex.t: Value for money and affordability will be central to the decisions we make on those procurements.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the TransPennine Express fleet investment by noting the figure includes maintenance costs, and confirms that value for money and affordability will guide upcoming rolling stock procurements for Southeastern and Northern trains.

deb_ex.t: we continue to deliver step-free access through the Access for All programme. Since July 2024, we have completed improvements at 31 stations
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress on the Access for All programme, citing completions at 31 stations, 22 under way, and a new level boarding commitment.

deb_ex.t: Chepstow was nominated for Access for All funding in 2022, but was not selected for funding by the previous Government.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges Chepstow's case and explains it was not selected under the previous government, promising to work with the MP to raise it at the next spending review.

deb_ex.t: A full lift replacement is planned for 2028, but I realise that that will sound like a long way off to his constituents.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the Bishop's Stortford lift problems, notes a full replacement is planned for 2028, and commits to asking officials to meet Greater Anglia to reduce short-term disruption.

deb_ex.t: matters relating to the railways are devolved, but I will look into the accessibility issues at the station he refers to
deb_ex.sum: Notes that Scottish railway matters are devolved but commits to look into Kirkconnel's accessibility issues and liaise with the Scottish Government.

deb_ex.t: I would be happy to look at the details and discuss with him whether future improvements could come forward as part of the next spending review.
deb_ex.sum: Points to the existing national programme and offers to discuss future improvements for Woking and West Byfleet at the next spending review.

deb_ex.t: We are investing in the rail network in the Greater Manchester area, including the Bolton-Manchester line and services to Blackburn.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government investment in Greater Manchester rail, including the Bolton-Manchester line, longer trains, and station upgrades at Salford and Manchester Victoria.

deb_ex.t: early planning work is under way to purchase up to 450 new trains for Northern, which could include the replacement of the ageing units on the Clitheroe-Bolton line.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges Northern Rail's unacceptable performance, confirms the Rail Minister has demanded an improvement plan, and outlines plans for additional trains and up to 450 new trains including for the Clitheroe-Bolton line.

deb_ex.t: My Department regularly discusses roadworks and other highways matters with the Northern Ireland Executive through the UK Roads Leadership Group.
deb_ex.sum: The Secretary of State confirms that her Department regularly engages with the Northern Ireland Executive on roadworks matters through the UK Roads Leadership Group.

deb_ex.t: I completely understand why the hon. Gentleman raises these matters. Whether it is people travelling on the roads or businesses that are impacted by roadworks, the impacts are felt
deb_ex.sum: The Secretary of State sympathises and notes that a code of practice has been published through the UK Roads Leadership Group encouraging better co-ordination including overnight works to minimise disruption.

deb_ex.t: I will certainly pursue discussions with the Northern Ireland Executive about lane rental, because I know it could make a real difference in that part of the UK as well.
deb_ex.sum: The Secretary of State confirms she will pursue discussions with the Northern Ireland Executive about lane rental, drawing on her experience as Deputy Mayor of London to endorse its benefits.

deb_ex.t: The fact that Great Western Railways will come into public ownership on 13 December presents an opportunity
deb_ex.sum: Points to Great Western Railways entering public ownership as an opportunity to improve connectivity and signals more announcements on wi-fi are forthcoming.

deb_ex.t: In addition to the extension of the temporary 5p cut to fuel duty, we are also maintaining the road tax holiday for heavy goods vehicles until summer next year
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's package of motoring cost measures including the 5p fuel duty cut extension, road tax holiday for HGVs, cheaper public EV charging and discounts on electric cars.

deb_ex.t: we are very keen to make progress on better wi-fi connectivity on Great Western services, and I hope to say more on that in the coming months
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms commitment to better wi-fi on Great Western services and promises further announcements in coming months.

deb_ex.t: We are not publishing a separate rail freight strategy, as I will put that target in the long-term rail strategy when it is published
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the 75% by 2050 and 40% by 2040 freight targets and explains that rather than a separate strategy, rail freight goals will be embedded in the long-term rail strategy and Great British Railways' first business plan.

deb_ex.t: I can assure my hon. Friend that we look at these issues in the round. He mentions charge point infrastructure. Only this week, I had a roundtable with the main operators of charge
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House the Government looks at EV issues in the round, cites recent roundtables with charge point operators and manufacturers, and confirms the Chancellor will respond to the ZEV mandate review by Christmas.

deb_ex.t: Let me thank the hon. Gentleman for his question. Air quality in relation to both pilot and passenger safety is of real concern to the Department for Transport. We undertake work c
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member and confirms the Department constantly monitors the impact of cabin air quality on pilots and passengers, offering further direct engagement.

deb_ex.t: we need a framework that is flexible enough to adapt to change, support innovation and keep passengers at its heart. The Bill will help deliver that framework
deb_ex.sum: Opens the government wind-up, defending the six-month CAA reporting timeline and explaining how the Bill has been strengthened since the Lords, while acknowledging points raised across the debate.

deb_ex.t: I will just finish my point. I am, however, more than happy to come and answer any questions the Secretary of State may have in this place. The shadow Minister made an important po
deb_ex.sum: Defends the six-month timeline as faster than the two-year response to the 2023 outage, confirms the Government is open to a review of drop-off charges, and acknowledges the transport connectivity concerns raised by Members.

deb_ex.t: If the shadow Secretary of State is of the opinion that I have mischaracterised what he said, I will of course withdraw that statement, but I suppose we should let the usual channe
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government is open to a review of drop-off charges, recognising transparency and fairness concerns, while noting charges serve congestion management and infrastructure funding purposes.

deb_ex.t: I give way to my hon. Friend the Member for Hitchin
deb_ex.sum: Invites a further contribution from his hon. Friend on Luton airport drop-off and transport alternatives.

deb_ex.t: we want to promote the use of public transport to reach our airports by as many people as possible
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the suggestion about subsidised bus travel to airports and affirms the government's aim to promote public transport access to airports.

deb_ex.t: people with disabilities are disproportionately more likely to use drop-off services at airports than other customers, so it is for airports to facilitate that
deb_ex.sum: Agrees disabled passengers disproportionately rely on drop-off services and says robust free drop-off procedures are mostly in place but need wider adoption across the sector.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right to say that that should be our focus. All four of the tests that we have set out on which a development consent order for Heathrow expansion would be grante
deb_ex.sum: Affirms that all four tests for Heathrow development consent depend on adequate surface access and commits to considering this now the consultation has closed.

deb_ex.t: the DFT takes this matter incredibly seriously and is progressing work across the Government to think about how we can become more adaptive
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House that DfT takes climate resilience at airports seriously and is working across government and with the private sector to improve adaptive capacity.

deb_ex.t: disruption of this kind is absolutely unacceptable
deb_ex.sum: Apologises to affected passengers, explains the technical cause of the NATS outage, and outlines the Government's response including a report by 16 September and a six-month CAA review.

deb_ex.t: A six-month timeframe to get to the bottom of what is a highly technical matter and an incident of disruption is proportionate and timely
deb_ex.sum: Defends the six-month CAA review timeline by reference to the 2023 outage, explains the technical cause, and affirms the Government is exercising effective ministerial oversight on behalf of passengers.

deb_ex.t: I am confident that the fantastic teams of people working at NATS responded with all possible haste and diligence to the disruption
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the staff at NATS and affirms the Government will look closely at NATS's resilience and the technological transformation needed to keep air traffic control fit for purpose.

deb_ex.t: we will do so with passenger safety at its heart, and effective oversight of NATS must run to the core of that
deb_ex.sum: Defends NATS's general safety record while acknowledging the seriousness of repeated disruptions, and commits that any airport expansion will have passenger safety at its heart alongside effective NATS oversight.

deb_ex.t: this is a useful opportunity to ask ourselves questions about where we can encourage NATS to go further and push the boundaries
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the disruption is an opportunity to push NATS further and faster on technological innovation and to build greater resilience across UK aviation.

deb_ex.t: Parliament must have its say on how the lessons that we learn from this incident can inform the Bill
deb_ex.sum: Defends the six-month timeline and agrees Parliament must engage with lessons learned, linking the incident to the Civil Aviation Bill which will strengthen passenger rights and CAA powers.

deb_ex.t: I am resolute in my belief that all the staff at NATS responded with all the haste and diligence that we would expect to protect passengers
deb_ex.sum: Thanks NATS staff across the UK and affirms his belief that all staff responded with haste and diligence to protect passengers and enable aviation to restart safely.

deb_ex.t: Passengers whose flights have been cancelled are entitled to assistance from their airlines, including either a refund within seven days or a rerouting
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the significant economic impact and sets out passengers' existing rights to refunds and rerouting, while noting the failure of airport capacity to handle disrupted passengers as a key lesson.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for his determined advocacy for passengers with disabilities in both our aviation sector and the wider UK transport system. He is right that the Bill will en
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the Civil Aviation Bill will enable a review of enhanced passenger rights for those with disabilities and commits to examining how the most vulnerable are affected by disruption.

deb_ex.t: The Secretary of State puts together a priorities letter that sets out very clearly her expectations of our air traffic control system
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the House that the Secretary of State's priorities letter to NATS emphasises technological transformation, and that the incident makes completing that change with all possible haste even more pressing.

deb_ex.t: The Department needs to ensure that it is doing its bit, and we will never be shy of fighting for passengers and their rights

deb_ex.t: resilience is clearly not where it needs to be. We need our technological systems to be more adaptive and more reactive.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges that resilience is not where it needs to be and states that the Secretary of State has made technological agility and resilience top priorities for the CAA and NATS.

deb_ex.t: The Transport Secretary and I met Martin Rolfe on Wednesday, and expressed our concern about the scale of disruption on behalf of passengers and the industry.
deb_ex.sum: Reports that the Transport Secretary and Minister met the NATS chief executive to express concern, and confirms the Department will keep scrutiny of NATS leadership and technology at the forefront.

deb_ex.sum: Reassures the hon. Member that civil and military air traffic control systems are separate, while acknowledging that aviation resilience is critical to economic growth and that lessons must be learned.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Lady for her work representing her constituents who are employees of NATS. Let me use this opportunity to thank them again for the hard work that they do. However,

deb_ex.sum: States NATS has confirmed the incident was technical not cyber-related, and reassures the House that CAA, NATS and DfT work closely together to defend against cyber threats.

deb_ex.t: Aviation connectivity is perhaps nowhere more important than from Northern Ireland to the rest of the United Kingdom. It is an economic and a social lifeline
deb_ex.sum: Affirms that aviation connectivity from Northern Ireland is an economic and social lifeline and commits to discussing how to strengthen those links further with the hon. Member.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government's commitment to a sustainable UK steel sector and its encouragement of lower-carbon materials, noting Wales will account for around half of future UK steelmaking capacity.

deb_ex.t: I will ensure that I facilitate a meeting with the Rail Minister on the topic he raises.

deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms government commitment to regional airport connectivity through Heathrow expansion consultations, PSO routes, airspace modernisation and jet fuel cost protections, directly addressing concerns about airports like Exeter and Newquay

deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government approved the development consent order and says it is now a privately funded project for Gatwick to progress, while pledging continued official engagement.

deb_ex.t: I expect all its members to contribute in meaningful ways to find practical, local solutions to these challenges, and we will of course keep options under advisement
deb_ex.sum: Praises progress of the cross-Solent group and says the Government will keep options under advisement, maintaining that locally led solutions are preferred.

deb_ex.sum: Expresses personal interest in rail connectivity to ports and electrification for freight efficiency after visiting Immingham, and commits to taking the conversation forward.

deb_ex.t: the Government have committed to undertake a review to ensure that travel remains accessible and passengers are treated fairly.

deb_ex.sum: Responds that the government works internationally and through Commonwealth relationships to counter China's influence in affected regions.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms the £21 million three-year fund to advance LGBTQ rights internationally and pledges the Government will always support the international rights of LGBT people.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms ICBs are being asked to assess priority needs across their areas, with an emphasis on ensuring rural communities are not overlooked.

deb_ex.sum: Points to £29 billion additional NHS investment, thousands of new staff recruited, and the £6.75 billion estate safety fund as evidence the Government is addressing hospital capacity and facility needs.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that under-investment since 2009 has undermined safety and performance, and points to the estate safety fund and local capital improvement processes as the Government's response.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the point and outlines the £1.5 billion announced for 950 NHS projects, stressing each area must address infection control and building repairs within the funding allocated.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the Education Secretary already takes the issue seriously and asserts that public buildings across the country must be made resilient to changing weather and climate.

deb_ex.t: It does feel unthinkable that any staff member should deliberately harm a child, but we have a responsibility to be prepared to think the unthinkable.

deb_ex.sum: Thanks all speakers, acknowledges the grief of bereaved families, announces action on hospital remains for bereaved parents, and outlines government commitments including Martha's rule expansion and family hubs.

deb_ex.t: we have to give much greater priority to maternal and neonatal care
deb_ex.sum: Outlines government plans including expanding Martha's rule to all maternity and neonatal services and restoring Sure Start family hubs to deliver co-ordinated early support.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's commitment to bring forward comprehensive proposals to regulate the funeral sector and ensure dignity for the deceased.

deb_ex.sum: Deflects the question on proportional representation by attacking the Green party over racist language used by one of their councillors.

deb_ex.sum: Praises the local railway and confirms Great British Railways will work with local authorities and businesses to drive investment and improve services.

deb_ex.sum: Points to ongoing budget discussions and cites the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 as evidence of the Government's commitment to tackling welfare fraud.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the profound debt owed to Gurkhas and confirms constructive ministerial discussions on pensions with veterans and the Nepalese government are continuing.

deb_ex.t: We saw the practical benefits of the Union with the Minister’s swift action on military personnel coming to deal with the wildfires. Will he join me in paying tribute to the farmer
deb_ex.sum: Praises the swift military response to Welsh wildfires, pays tribute to farmers and firefighters, and calls for a long-term plan given the increasing frequency of wildfires due to climate change.

deb_ex.t: anyone who sets their face against the deal that I hope he pushes over the line on 20 November is in favour of adding costs to businesses and households
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the concrete gains already negotiated with the EU and argues that anyone opposing the deal is in favour of adding costs to businesses and households.

deb_ex.t: Only on Friday, I spoke to a constituent who gave notice of retirement in March and still has not had his pensions quote. I commend the Minister very much on the very hard work she
deb_ex.sum: Former minister who initiated action on Capita shares a fresh constituency case still awaiting a pension quote after giving notice in March, and asks the Minister to direct officials to prepare viable insourcing options for the House.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Gentleman for his questions and will try to do them justice in the short time available. The Chancellor said this morning that Brexit has hammered British exports.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees Brexit harmed exports and defends the Government's EU reset approach, including the SPS agreement, while rejecting single market membership and defending the fiscal rules.

deb_ex.t: this Government will drive good growth in every postcode
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government's commitment to good growth in every postcode, acknowledging high poverty in parts of London including Barking.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right to raise this matter. The cost of energy for UK businesses is higher than for those elsewhere. That is why the Business Secretary, working hand in hand with
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges UK business energy costs are too high and points to the British industrial competitiveness scheme as the Government's response for key growth sectors.

deb_ex.t: fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our economic security and national security. That is why we have committed to meeting those fiscal rules
deb_ex.sum: Responds that rising borrowing costs underline the necessity of sticking to the fiscal rules, and notes the Government is meeting one rule early.

deb_ex.t: I can reassure her that that will be for mayoral strategic authorities to take forward
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that mayoral strategic authorities will lead local industrial strategy and expresses confidence her hon. Friend's area will thrive under the Government.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman invites me to write the next Budget, and I am not going to do that
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the question, declining to preview Budget decisions on national insurance and business rates.

deb_ex.t: we will work across Departments to ensure that we open up public procurement to smaller and start-up businesses, so that they stay here
deb_ex.sum: Commits to opening public procurement to smaller and start-up businesses across Departments to keep scaling companies in the UK.

deb_ex.t: Sometimes it is necessary, in order to fund improvements in our national health service and to fill the £22 billion fiscal black hole that we inherited
deb_ex.sum: Defends tax rises as necessary to fund the NHS and address the fiscal black hole inherited from the previous Government.

deb_ex.t: Being from Wolverhampton, I agree with my hon. Friend that the midlands is a very important part of the country
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the midlands' importance and points to the ceramics support package as evidence the Government is delivering for the region.

deb_ex.t: As the Chancellor set out this morning, we are determined to speed up infrastructure provision. Frankly, compared to other countries, we are just too slow at building high-speed ra
deb_ex.sum: Affirms the government's commitment to speeding up infrastructure provision and notes her own interest in the Cambridge-Oxford corridor.

deb_ex.t: The Attorney General will provide guidance to Ministers, so that we can make quicker decisions
deb_ex.sum: Shares the impatience for faster delivery and points to Attorney General guidance that will help Ministers make quicker decisions with less consultation.

deb_ex.t: We have to get local government reorganisation right, so I make no apology for the Secretary of State coming to the House
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Secretary of State's pause as necessary to get reorganisation right, making no apology for updating the House.

deb_ex.t: there was a discussion about global trade imbalances, and that is something that we are considering putting on the agenda
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the trade deficit matters and reports it was discussed at the G20, with a view to placing global trade imbalances on the UK's G20 presidency agenda.

deb_ex.t: Scotland has rightly had plenty of devolution, but that does not mean that the two decades of SNP Government have been successful
deb_ex.sum: Gently rebuffs the SNP by noting Scotland has had substantial devolution but that two decades of SNP government have not delivered success.

deb_ex.t: We are proud to be the Labour Government who lifted the two-child limit and lifted 450,000 children out of poverty.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the government's record in lifting 450,000 children out of poverty by removing the two-child limit.

deb_ex.t: We are supporting automative with £4 billion in capital and research and development funding to manufacture zero-emission vehicles
deb_ex.sum: Outlines government support for Jaguar Land Rover and the automotive sector, including £4 billion for zero-emission vehicles, and expresses sympathy for the workforce.

deb_ex.t: We can deliver good infrastructure and good jobs and limit the number of consultations, and have an eye to the impact on the environment
deb_ex.sum: Argues good infrastructure, jobs and environmental care can be delivered together and promises a specific reply to the BioYorkshire question.

deb_ex.t: The Government are on the side of young people—both young graduates and those who pursue technical education
deb_ex.sum: Pledges government support for both graduates and those in technical education, reaffirming the aim of parity and growth in every postcode.

deb_ex.t: We are holding a consultation, which will be a quick one.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges constituent concerns, confirms personal engagement with the Business Secretary, and promises a quick ZEV mandate consultation.

deb_ex.t: building societies often offer more innovative products—to first-time buyers in particular—and do sterling work
deb_ex.sum: Warmly endorses the co-operative and mutual sector's role, citing building societies' innovative products for first-time buyers from her time as Economic Secretary.

deb_ex.t: if we want to tackle climate change, we cannot stop every renewable project from going ahead, which is what the Greens would have us do
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the charge of ignoring the environment and turns the attack on the Greens, accusing them of blocking renewable and nuclear projects.

deb_ex.t: One of our trailblazer projects in the place-based business cases is with Birmingham, which is obviously the beating heart of the west midlands.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the MP that Birmingham is already part of a trailblazer place-based business case, signalling midlands engagement.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member will know that rural communities are close to my heart, given my previous ministerial role and because I have a semi-rural constituency. There is huge potential in
deb_ex.sum: Affirms commitment to rural communities, citing bus fare caps and local transport improvements as evidence the Government is acting.

deb_ex.t: The Government are intent on driving good growth and job creation opportunities across the country—in the north, the south, the midlands and every other part, too.
deb_ex.sum: Gives assurance that the Government is committed to driving growth across all regions of the country.

deb_ex.t: The Green Book discount rate is a tool of economic analysis. It does not change the cost of the deal.
deb_ex.sum: Rebuts the Conservative claim, clarifying that the Green Book discount rate is an analytical tool and does not alter the actual cost of the deal.

deb_ex.t: We are working with the mayor on that issue. Our colleagues will get back to you on that.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government is working with the mayor on the West Yorkshire mass transit project and commits to a follow-up response.

deb_ex.t: Earlier this summer we announced the business rate reductions for pubs, social clubs and live music venues, and we will go further in the Budget.
deb_ex.sum: Points to business rate reductions already announced for pubs and live music venues and signals further action at the Budget.

deb_ex.t: I will convey that message to the Chancellor, but I will not be writing the Budget right now.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to pass the fuel duty message to the Chancellor while declining to pre-empt Budget decisions.

deb_ex.t: we take the economic success of rural communities really seriously. We are improving connectivity, whether digital connectivity or local transport connectivity
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates the Government's commitment to rural economic success through improved digital and transport connectivity.

deb_ex.t: we have given strategic steers to the public financial institutions to ensure that they are focusing on regional growth, and that is also about opening up opportunities
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern and points to strategic steers given to public financial institutions to support regional growth and smaller businesses.

deb_ex.t: The sanitary and phytosanitary agreement that we are negotiating with the EU will help to reduce that friction.
deb_ex.sum: Points to the SPS agreement being negotiated with the EU as the Government's route to reducing trade friction in Northern Ireland.

deb_ex.t: It is money that already sits with the British Business Bank, but the change is the focus on the north, on scale-up businesses, to ensure that we unleash their growth potential. We
deb_ex.sum: Concedes the money already existed within the British Business Bank but says the new element is the explicit focus on northern scale-up businesses.

deb_ex.t: The trade deals that we are doing, and also the reset of the relationship that we are taking forward with the EU, will bring down barriers with our biggest and closest market.
deb_ex.sum: Points to trade deals and the EU relationship reset as the Government's strategy for reducing barriers with Britain's biggest market.

deb_ex.t: UKRI—UK Research and Innovation —invests in that sort of research, and the Government will continue to do that through UKRI.
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House that UKRI invests in frontier research and the Government will continue to support it.

deb_ex.t: I can reassure the hon. Gentleman; the east midlands and the west midlands are really important. The changes that the Chancellor outlined to the discount rate today will benefit pl
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the Member that changes to the discount rate will benefit regional investment projects and that the Government aims to drive growth in every postcode including his constituency.

deb_ex.t: the mayoral strategic authorities are about local authorities coming together in a combined authority and working together across the borders of the west midlands
deb_ex.sum: Disagrees that the arrangement is anti-devolution, explaining that mayoral combined authorities represent local councils working together across boundaries to drive regional growth.

deb_ex.t: We are working in close partnership with business, and the hon. Gentleman is right to say that we have to unleash talent and business investment in his own constituency and elsewhe
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that local talent and business investment must be unlocked, and explains that public financial institutions independently assess projects before backing them within government-set strategic priorities.

deb_ex.t: we will publish plans for further fiscal devolution, including greater retention of business rates revenue for local councils and strategic authorities.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's commitment to supporting growth in every area, including plans for fiscal devolution and greater business rates retention to be announced at the Budget.

deb_ex.t: All strategic authorities, including those without a mayor, will benefit from greater powers over skills, transport and housing.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that all strategic authorities, including those without a mayor, will benefit from greater powers over skills, transport and housing under the Government's devolution plans.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is a doughty champion for his area. As he said, the Prime Minister has been engaging with Cornwall—including, importantly, with its six MPs, including my hon. Friend
deb_ex.sum: Outlines the Government's devolution agreement with Cornwall, including statutory powers on transport and housing, an overnight visitor levy, and the £30 million Kernow industrial growth fund.

deb_ex.t: this Government of course care about driving growth in rural areas. There is great potential there, which is why we are supporting our farmers
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the Government cares about rural growth, pointing to the £2.7 billion sustainable farming budget and improved rural connectivity as evidence.

deb_ex.t: there are opportunities for areas that do not opt to have a mayor, but set up as foundation strategic authorities to gain the benefit of retaining more business rates
deb_ex.sum: Disagrees with the Lib Dem's assessment, reiterating that areas without a mayor can set up as foundation strategic authorities and benefit from greater business rates retention and new powers.

deb_ex.t: NHS delivering 3.5% productivity growth in 2025-26, beating its 2% target. The Government will continue to drive public sector efficiency
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress on public sector productivity, citing NHS growth and AI investment to deliver £14 billion in efficiencies by 2028-29.

deb_ex.t: I am proud to be part of a Government who have avoided strikes that impact on public spending.
deb_ex.sum: Deflects Hunt's criticism with humour and defends the government's pay settlement by highlighting it avoided costly strikes affecting public spending.

deb_ex.t: we are driving efficiencies, faster service delivery and using AI in the NHS to really drive improvements in care, as well as delivering more bang for buck.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with Malhotra and outlines two benefits of driving productivity: better value for taxpayers and faster, improved service delivery including NHS care.

deb_ex.t: we are focused on driving public sector productivity to reach the efficiency targets I talked about. We are holding each Department to account on that.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the House that the government is holding departments to account on efficiency targets and points to NHS progress as evidence of productivity gains.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Lady for raising this important issue. I would be very happy to meet her.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member for raising the issue and agrees to meet her.

deb_ex.t: We are improving funding for local government as a result of the spending review, and I would be happy to meet the hon. Gentleman to discuss that further.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms funding for local government is improving following the spending review and offers to meet the MP to discuss further.

deb_ex.t: We need to make sure that a budget is set for Northern Ireland so that the Executive can continue to deliver vital local public services.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the MP that she is working closely with the Secretary of State for Northern Ireland and that a budget must be set to protect vital local public services.

deb_ex.t: I reassure my hon. Friend that I am working extremely closely with the Health Secretary and discussing overall levels of NHS spending—of course, the Department has the biggest budg
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the MP she is working closely with the Health Secretary on NHS spending levels and commits to taking back the specific compensation issue raised.

deb_ex.t: We need to take action at every level. For example, the person who does a weekend job for their friend, transporting half a skip of old kitchen waste that suddenly ends up on a lay
deb_ex.sum: Explains that the new regime targets the whole chain from minor transporters to organised crime, including penalty points, permit revocation and up to five years' imprisonment.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right. We are acutely conscious of the issue that farmers face. There is innovative work being done with drones, and I met one farmer who told me that his neighbo
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges farmers' plight, notes work with insurers and drone monitoring, and confirms broader waste crime action plan measures including tightening exemptions.

deb_ex.t: Under the current system, checking the paperwork is all that the Environment Agency can do; that is the problem. Under the managing public money rules, the Environment Agency is no
deb_ex.sum: Explains Treasury constraints that prevent using legitimate operators' fees to fund criminal enforcement and outlines the cross-government multi-agency action plan.

deb_ex.t: my risk appetite for not granting permits to people who may be questionable is very high
deb_ex.sum: Declines to set prosecution targets but asserts a high risk appetite for refusing permits and outlines a risk-based, intelligence-led enforcement approach.

deb_ex.t: I am responsible for many things, from forests and international biodiversity to peat and trees; I am afraid the courts are slightly outwith my jurisdiction, but I will pass that p
deb_ex.sum: Notes courts are outside her remit but highlights the doubled Environment Agency enforcement budget and 18 prosecutions since March as evidence of progress.

deb_ex.t: I will be brief and try not to detain the House for too long, but what a rich and insightful debate we have had. Let me begin by addressing the question of costs, which was raised
deb_ex.sum: Responds to all contributions, defends the cost-benefit balance, confirms an independent evaluation by 2029, and expresses sympathy for constituents suffering near illegal sites.

deb_ex.t: Since publishing the waste crime action plan in March, we have started clearing illegal waste at Kidlington, and we are investigating clearing up sites in Wigan, Sheffield and Hynd
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress including arrests, site clearances, digital tracking and new legislation to tackle waste criminals.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right that, under the previous Government, there was a large amount of illegally dumped waste—about 30,000 tonnes between 2018 and 2022. Enforcement action is bei
deb_ex.sum: Outlines enforcement action being taken at Brambletree wharf by Medway council and the Environment Agency, contrasting the current government's action with inaction under the previous government.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member is absolutely right that fly-tippers are despoiling our countryside, and I pay tribute to his local group for taking such great action to keep the beaches and count
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to the Eastbourne community group and outlines new penalties including up to nine penalty points on fly-tippers' driving licences, warning that fly-tippers are often linked to serious organised crime.

deb_ex.t: I was pleased to meet the hon. Gentleman and my hon. Friend the Member for Carlisle (Ms Minns) to talk about the activities at these waste sites. Unpicking the work happening there
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the complexity of tackling illegal waste sites and highlights a significant increase in waste crime enforcement funding, from £10 million to £30 million.

deb_ex.t: Our waste collection systems are completely different from those in Germany and France, where they have a wide network of bring banks for glass. We have the privilege of having gla
deb_ex.sum: Explains the difference in waste collection systems between the UK and Europe and says officials are working at pace to find a solution for the dual burden falling on pubs.

deb_ex.t: As we push the waste criminals out of the sector, there will be more business for legitimate operators. That also means that the carrier registration number has to be carried on th
deb_ex.sum: Explains the new regime will require carrier registration numbers on all advertising and vehicles, introduce criminal record and identity checks, and push waste criminals out of the sector.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right about our tree cover, which is why I am delighted to tell him that tree planting is at its highest rate for 20 years. As we endure our second heatwave this
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the point and announces tree planting is at its highest rate for 20 years, with funding through the trees outside woodland fund doubled to £2.5 million.

deb_ex.t: We have been around the houses on this. The document that has been released talks about coral collapse by 2030 and mangrove collapse by 2050. I would say that there is enough to wo
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the question by pointing to the contents already released, suggesting there is sufficient alarming information in the published document without seeking further versions.

deb_ex.t: With permission, I would like to make a statement about the nature and climate crisis. Nature is the monopoly provider of everything we need to live. We are living through the Anth
deb_ex.sum: Minister sets out the Government's commitment to tackling the nature and climate crisis, citing record investment in flood resilience, nature recovery, and carbon reduction targets.

deb_ex.t: I am disappointed by the nature and tone of the hon. Gentleman’s response to our attempts to right some of the wrongs left behind by the previous Government. The hon. Gentleman ask
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends the Planning and Infrastructure Act, peatland investment and farming schemes, arguing they deliver better environmental outcomes than the previous fragmented approach.

deb_ex.t: Through some of our landscape recovery projects we are seeing farm clusters get behind the new idea of leveraging in private finance to work alongside public investment, but it is
deb_ex.sum: Minister outlines investment in natural flood management and landscape recovery projects, and confirms the fourth national adaptation programme is planned for 2028.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member asked about a range of policies. I will talk about natural flood management. We will invest £300 million in natural flood management over the next 10 years—the high
deb_ex.sum: Minister outlines £300 million for natural flood management, support for farmers to hold water naturally, and widened eligibility criteria for flood management funding.

deb_ex.t: we have worked to set nature standards so that when nature projects and large financial funds want to invest in nature, they have the confidence to do so
deb_ex.sum: Minister highlights work with BSI to set nature standards and progress on carbon and nature markets to give investors confidence and prevent greenwashing.

deb_ex.t: I was discussing that very issue with Natural England this morning. Land covering about 32% of England is already likely to, or has the potential to, contribute to the 30 by 30 tar
deb_ex.sum: Minister responds that 32% of England's land already contributes to 30 by 30 and outlines a tiered bronze-silver-gold route to meeting the target through nature reserves and landscape recovery.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right: we have an army of citizen scientists and naturalists, and we are certainly looking forward to celebrating some of them tomorrow at RHS Garden Wisley for B
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges citizen scientists' vital role but explains that river clean-up volunteers need Environment Agency permits to avoid unintended consequences to habitats and flood defences.

deb_ex.t: it is essential that we have a climate transition that is fair to those workers in the North sea
deb_ex.sum: Minister declines to comment on individual licences but agrees the UK must move off the fossil fuel rollercoaster and ensure a fair transition for North sea workers.

deb_ex.t: The Water Minister, my hon. Friend the Member for Kingston upon Hull West and Haltemprice (Emma Hardy), is only too happy to meet my hon. Friend to discuss bottom trawling. I belie
deb_ex.sum: Minister explains marine protection depends on appropriate site-specific measures and directs the MP to the Water Minister for detailed discussion on bottom trawling.

deb_ex.t: By publishing that incineration capacity strategy, we set out clearly the standards that we are looking for on new incineration permits. We have a problem—an epidemic—with abandone
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends the incineration capacity strategy, arguing energy from waste is preferable to illegal or abandoned landfill and forms part of the clean power transition.

deb_ex.t: I remember when I was Chair of the Environmental Audit Committee doing an inquiry into heatwaves that started during the “beast from the east”, so nobody gave us any evidence, and
deb_ex.sum: Minister expresses sympathy for Walthamstow constituents and outlines Network Rail tree clearance action, while stressing the need for local government mutual assistance planning and reviewing vegetation suitability.

deb_ex.t: The North Sea Transition Authority is equipped to support a fair, managed and prosperous transition, including through a new statutory objective to consider workers, communities an
deb_ex.sum: Minister highlights the North Sea Transition Authority's role in a fair transition, extended offshore worker rights, and the Government's plan to secure clean energy jobs, without addressing the specific Scottish pipeline concern.

deb_ex.t: which Conservative party are the voters supposed to believe: the one that legislated for net zero or the one that now instructs its MPs to vote against it?
deb_ex.sum: Minister attacks Conservative inconsistency on net zero, contrasting their 2019 legislation with the current leader's claim the target is impossible.

deb_ex.t: Schools cover a land mass the size of Birmingham, and they need to play their part in educating pupils about the climate and nature crisis
deb_ex.sum: Highlights solar panels for schools, DfE building investment, and the government estate nature plan as ways schools are contributing to climate and nature goals.

deb_ex.t: I always like to go and see trees being planted, and my hon. Friend is right to talk about the importance of trees, both for shading our streets and as part of the three new nation
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the doubling of the Trees Outside Woodland grant and the three new national forests, stressing the need for the right trees in the right places for long-term survival.

deb_ex.t: I have been in discussion with officials in the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs about how we can align and spatially target funding towards those areas in particular
deb_ex.sum: Makes a joke about Conservative absences, then confirms discussions with DEFRA officials and the West Midlands combined authority on aligning funding with local nature recovery strategies.

deb_ex.t: I look after many things, but sadly I do not yet control the broadcast schedules of any national broadcasters. The point of the National Emergency Briefing is to get people togethe
deb_ex.sum: Declines to control broadcast schedules but praises community gatherings like People Planet Pint as positive ways for people to engage locally with the climate crisis.

deb_ex.t: We have the biodiversity net gain framework, which is all about making sure that there is a biodiversity uplift of 10% in every planning policy
deb_ex.sum: Points to the biodiversity net gain framework requiring a 10% biodiversity uplift in planning and notes the government has refined it to work better in practice.

deb_ex.t: her suggestion is an excellent topic for the Youth Parliament—or local youth panels could be organised through schools
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the suggestion is beyond her brief but endorses the idea of local youth panels through schools or the Youth Parliament as a way to drive local accountability.

deb_ex.t: Global ecosystem degradation and collapse threaten UK national security and prosperity…Without major intervention…this is highly likely to continue to 2050 and beyond.
deb_ex.sum: Quotes the already-public biodiversity security report warning of ecosystem collapse threatening UK national security and directs the member to the Secretary of State for Energy Security for details on the climate security taskforce.

deb_ex.t: it is vital that children in Ashford have the protection of shade from trees. Academy trusts should be making funds available for adaptation, to mitigate impacts in their schools
deb_ex.sum: Stresses the importance of shade trees in schools during heatwaves, urges academy trusts to fund adaptation, and commends the students for their environmental efforts.

deb_ex.t: We are having a triple-COP year. We will be setting out our approach and our achievements as we move towards the biodiversity COP in Armenia and the climate COP in Turkey. There is
deb_ex.sum: Outlines the triple-COP year ahead and commits to ensuring every pound invested in climate also delivers for nature, signalling an end to siloed government spending.

deb_ex.t: We are building nine new reservoirs, but further to what my hon. Friend says, I have had messages from Severn Trent Water, who advise me to put a bucket in the bath, get a hosepipe
deb_ex.sum: Confirms nine new reservoirs are being built and notes existing hosepipe bans in three areas, warning there may be more, while sharing practical water-saving advice from Severn Trent.

deb_ex.t: I will be travelling to Fylingdales this week to make an announcement about what we are doing to help those brave farmers who are on the frontline of that wildfire.
deb_ex.sum: Signals an imminent announcement on support for farmers dealing with wildfires, confirming she will travel to Fylingdales this week.

deb_ex.t: As I mentioned before, we are more than doubling the funding for tree planting through the trees outside woodland fund. Climate change is sexist: it seems to be that women are part
deb_ex.sum: Minister outlines tree planting funding increases and highlights the disproportionate impact of heat on vulnerable groups including women, the young, and the elderly, stressing hospitals must not overheat.

deb_ex.t: I pay tribute to everyone who is helping with the restocking. My hon. Friend is lucky to have a river so close to London that has such a sensitive and rare species as the European
deb_ex.sum: Minister praises restoration efforts and agrees perpetrators of environmental crimes must be brought to justice, while stressing the need for a watertight legal case.

deb_ex.t: We know that we need to experiment with agroforestry, and that we need to do farming differently in this country, but sometimes it is about going back to the old ways of farming, w
deb_ex.sum: Minister agrees on the need to adapt farming practices through agroforestry and traditional mixed farming methods, and emphasises growing domestic fruit and veg to reduce reliance on Spain.

deb_ex.t: We need to reduce the urban heat island effect, with more tree planting and soft planting, and moving away from the grey concrete.
deb_ex.sum: Minister outlines a whole-city approach to reducing the urban heat island effect through tree planting, soft planting, and reducing front-garden concreting to tackle both heat and flooding.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right to raise the subject of peatlands and their role in hydrological protection. He raises the same point as the hon. Member for Keighley and Ilkley
deb_ex.sum: Minister agrees on the hydrological importance of peatlands, describing them as the country's Amazon rainforest, and affirms the Government's commitment to protecting them.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend’s year 2s at St Michael’s show that you are never too young to start caring about the environment, but it is important that we nurture and protect that climate aware
deb_ex.sum: Minister congratulates the schoolchildren and highlights the new GCSE in natural history as a way of nurturing climate and eco awareness into secondary school age.

deb_ex.t: I commend my hon. Friend on getting through that quickly. She tempts me to go beyond my brief, and on to the subject of battery and solar energy. Solar installations can result in
deb_ex.sum: Minister highlights biodiversity net gains from solar installations and the compatibility of solar with sheep grazing, but defers battery energy storage questions to the Energy Secretary.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend asks a great question. I said earlier that climate change is sexist; it also hits the poorest harder—a point he makes well. As we look towards the future, as well as
deb_ex.sum: Minister agrees climate change hits the poorest hardest and says the Government must look beyond warm spaces to providing cool, air-conditioned places for relief during heatwaves.

deb_ex.t: We must never again be in the position of having more prisoners than prison places. Can he reassure the House that, as he looks at the use of prison capacity
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the steps taken to reduce prison populations while excluding dangerous offenders and asks for assurance that workshops and training areas in prisons will be protected.

deb_ex.t: Will the Minister take every possible step to protect the pension prosperity of those who will face voluntary or compulsory redundancy at the global headquarters of JLR at Whitley
deb_ex.sum: The Lab MP contrasts current action with Tory-era closures and urges the Minister to take every possible step to protect the pension rights of workers facing voluntary or compulsory redundancy at JLR.

deb_ex.t: Will she say what more respect orders can do to tackle this level of low but persistent antisocial behaviour that blights our streets?
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Minister for visiting Coventry and asks how respect orders can build on existing local partnership work to tackle persistent low-level antisocial behaviour on the streets.

deb_ex.sum: Drawing on experience of South East Water outages, urges the Minister to ensure local authorities, water companies and energy firms work with NHS and nurseries to proactively register the most vulnerable on the priority services register.
