deb_ex.t: On international law, my new guidance makes it clear that domestic law and international law should be treated in the same way.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the revised legal guidance, arguing it treats domestic and international law equally and still requires adherence to both.

deb_ex.t: The military base at Diego Garcia is critical for our national security, and for keeping people safe here in Britain.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Chagos negotiations as driven by the need to secure Diego Garcia's long-term operation for national security, not by any legal obligation.

deb_ex.t: The courtrooms will transform how the justice system treats survivors of some of the most serious crimes, and will ensure a victim-focused, trauma-informed approach.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's plans to roll out specialist rape and serious sexual offences courtrooms in every Crown court, designed to support survivors and increase victim participation.

deb_ex.t: I would, of course, be happy to raise this matter with my ministerial colleagues and get back to him.
deb_ex.sum: Expresses sympathy for Harshita's family and commits to raising the case with ministerial colleagues.

deb_ex.t: The CPS will publish a dedicated action plan on tech-facilitated violence against women and girls, building on its VAWG strategy, which was published last November.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the rise in tech-facilitated abuse and outlines Government action including a roundtable and a forthcoming CPS action plan on the issue.

deb_ex.t: victims of domestic abuse will be provided with a dedicated victim liaison officer, providing better support from charge to trial.
deb_ex.sum: Announces the national roll-out of enhanced services for domestic abuse survivors, including a dedicated victim liaison officer to support victims from charge to trial.

deb_ex.t: This is a Government who are committed to halving violence against women and girls in a decade, and we are getting on with the job.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's record on domestic abuse, citing enhanced services, pre-trial meeting pilots, and the commitment to halve violence against women and girls within a decade.

deb_ex.t: The Government are clear that it is firmly in the UK’s interests to remain a member of the European convention on human rights. The ECHR has allowed people to object when “do not r
deb_ex.sum: Defends UK membership of the ECHR, citing its practical benefits for individuals and the UK's active role in modernising it through the Chiinău declaration.

deb_ex.t: It plays an important role in all aspects of our life, including in the Good Friday agreement, for example, which would unravel without it.
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the government's steadfast commitment to the ECHR, noting its importance for the Good Friday agreement while acknowledging the need for modernisation.

deb_ex.t: Stalking in all its forms is a horrendous, life-shattering crime. In September, I spoke at the national multi-agency conference, at which the Government and the third sector came t
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government action on stalking including a legal review, a national conference, and widened stalking protection orders.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for her question, and I am deeply sorry to hear of Jodie and Julie’s experience. As part of our strategy to halve violence against women and girls in a decad
deb_ex.sum: Responds with details of forthcoming statutory multi-agency guidance on stalking and offers to raise the constituents' specific case with the CPS.

deb_ex.t: every domestic abuse victim will have a dedicated victim liaison officer, who will remain a point of contact from charge through to trial.
deb_ex.sum: Announces the national roll-out of the CPS victim transformation programme, including dedicated victim liaison officers for domestic abuse victims and an enhanced service for rape victims.

deb_ex.t: We have invested an additional £96 million in the CPS, increasing its funding by more than 10% between 2026 and 2029.
deb_ex.sum: Offers to raise the constituent's case with the CPS directly and outlines government investment of £96 million to increase CPS capacity and deliver faster justice.

deb_ex.t: in three CPS areas, we are piloting offering victims of domestic abuse in the Crown court a pre-trial meeting with the prosecution team
deb_ex.sum: Describes the enhanced CPS service for domestic abuse victims including dedicated liaison officers and pilot pre-trial meetings with the prosecution team in Crown court cases.

deb_ex.t: It is part of the conversations that victim liaison officers are having, so that every victim and survivor is able to shape the support around them
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary confirms that victim liaison officers discuss protective support with each victim to ensure they feel safe.

deb_ex.t: I hope they have got the message from the changes in the law that have happened, and the changes that we have now been able to make
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary acknowledges the policing family's scrutiny, expresses hope that the legislative changes signal the Government's commitment, and promises to work with police on long-term system improvement.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Lady will know of the significant increase in funding to our police that we have already made. Through the National Police Chiefs’ Council, representations have been
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary points to increased police funding already provided and says conversations about additional resourcing through the NPCC are ongoing.

deb_ex.t: I hope that my hon. Friend takes comfort from what both the Prime Minister and I have said about ensuring that the right support is in place for those who are paroled to stay out o
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary commits to ensuring the right support is in place for IPP prisoners to progress through the Parole Board, with public safety as the overriding consideration, and invites ongoing dialogue.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Lady hits on an important point: what are we using our facilities for if not to rehabilitate people, particularly our young people? That is a symptom of what happens when
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary agrees that rehabilitation, especially for young people, is undermined by an overcrowded estate and says the investment and capacity programme is aimed at creating conditions for proper release preparation.

deb_ex.t: First, I recognise my hon. Friend’s work in the Department, which we are building out from, particularly on the hotline. That is why we have brought it forward. I am pleased that s
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary praises restriction zones as world-leading, commits to maximum engagement with campaigners to ensure they are implemented effectively, and thanks Atkinson for enabling him to highlight them.

deb_ex.t: I will undertake to look at that specific case and get back to her as soon as possible.
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary briefly notes the exclusions already announced and undertakes to look into the specific case Kearns raised and respond as soon as possible.

deb_ex.t: we have taken death by dangerous driving out of scope of the progression model, so anybody whose sentence was being reduced from two thirds to a half
deb_ex.sum: Confirms death by dangerous driving has been removed from the progression model and promises to clarify the release date for the specific case raised.

deb_ex.t: rape has been excluded from the progression model, but I will look at that case as a matter of urgency and come back to him
deb_ex.sum: Confirms rape is excluded from the progression model and promises to look at the specific case urgently, directing the victim to their liaison officer.

deb_ex.t: The answer to that question is no. When the system is running as hot as it is, it becomes a self-defeating cycle
deb_ex.sum: Concedes the current system is not doing enough to prevent reoffending and points to the Prime Minister's housing commitments as grounds for optimism.

deb_ex.t: I hope that there will be a degree of recognition that it was done in the noble cause of wanting to go further, but I still recognise everything he says
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the criticism of victim communications, acknowledges they were sent with good intentions, and commits to ensuring future correspondence is trauma informed.

deb_ex.t: I hope she heard what I said about our enthusiasm for those things that prevent reoffending. The Prisons Minister is looking closely at that in our estate plans
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the government's commitment to rehabilitation provision within prisons and confirms the Prisons Minister is examining estate plans to protect those areas.

deb_ex.t: these sentences have more than had their time—let us work together to bring them to an end
deb_ex.sum: Rejects a binary choice, acknowledges the difficulty of supporting long-term IPP prisoners back into society, and calls for cross-party work to end these sentences.

deb_ex.t: there must always be places for people to go to prison when they have committed serious offences; the worst-case scenario would be either trials collapsing or people being rebailed
deb_ex.sum: Agrees there must always be prison places for serious offenders to prevent trials collapsing or suspects being rebailed into situations where they were offending.

deb_ex.t: court delays are often a factor in the size of the remand population. There is important legislation on that making its way through this House
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the remand population as a significant factor and links its size to court delays, pointing to forthcoming legislation as the vehicle for addressing it.

deb_ex.t: I ask them, as I ask my hon. Friend, to judge us by our actions. We want to get to the same place as them
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the speaker's policing background, asks to be judged by actions, and commits to working with the policing family to ease pressure caused by an overstretched criminal justice system.

deb_ex.t: the MOJ produces a wide range of statistics quarterly, and it will continue to do so. I will, of course, have a look at the important suggestion
deb_ex.sum: Points to the Ministry of Justice's existing quarterly statistics and says he will consider the suggestion, emphasising the public's right to full information.

deb_ex.t: what we are doing to close that gap—is to bring more support forward to ensure that there is direct support, whether through the victims hotline
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the government wanted to go further on exemptions and sets out the support measures, victim hotline and community sector engagement designed to protect survivors.

deb_ex.t: Like pretty much every Lord Chancellor for a number of years now, the first thing in my inbox on day one was a note saying, “By the way, we are going to run out of prison places”—m
deb_ex.sum: Reveals he inherited an imminent capacity crisis on day one, confirms the Sentencing Act has pushed the saturation date back, and commits to a 10-year plan for prison capacity.

deb_ex.t: we are making changes as part of this process. The presumption of tagging eliminates a point of failure, and tagging in prisons—a pilot that is developing—also reduces failure
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the substance of concerns about tagging reliability and outlines improvements including presumption of tagging and prison-tagging pilots, committing to challenge work to demonstrate impact.

deb_ex.t: someone who went to prison for a one-and-a-half-year sentence is still there 18 and a half years later. All of us should feel discomfort about that.
deb_ex.sum: Expresses strong agreement and discomfort at the injustice described, committing to best possible support for IPP prisoners through Parole Board processes and to finding a way to bring IPP to a close.

deb_ex.t: Vetting must be done properly, and my hon. Friend the Prisons Minister and I are working with the Cabinet Office to improve it.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the seriousness of vetting delays and attrition, explains work with the Cabinet Office to improve vetting, and promises to revert directly on the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough question.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend makes a really important point. I think we could say unanimously across this place that if an individual out on licence contacted their victim, that would be a signi
deb_ex.sum: Distinguishes serious licence breaches from more technical non-compliance, defends the principle of attendance at meetings, but agrees to look at the recall system to ensure it is effective.

deb_ex.t: I have been having conversations with my right hon. Friend the Secretary of State for Education very recently on that point.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees fully, citing recent conversations with the Education Secretary and reflecting on his own experience as a local councillor acting as corporate parent to children in care.

deb_ex.t: Deflating it in the ways that I have talked about will help us to build a more stable regime and a better place to work.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges retention and attrition challenges and argues that deflating the prison population will stabilise the regime and make the estate a better place to work.

deb_ex.t: the critical thing is high-quality engagement with victim liaison officers so that those individuals have certainty about what is happening
deb_ex.sum: Points to the victims helpline, funding for local organisations and high-quality victim liaison officer engagement as the key mechanisms to support survivors through early release.

deb_ex.t: We of course want to have effective workload management tools in place. That is what myself and my hon. Friend the Prisons Minister are working closely on
deb_ex.sum: Explains the old system is being replaced because it is 15 years old and outlines ambitions for better technology including AI transcription, pledging effective workload management tools in the new model.

deb_ex.t: That is an excellent suggestion by my right hon. Friend; I will be in touch with Bob. We do not intend for this to be a long, drawn-out process. We want to build from the best evid
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the suggestion enthusiastically, commits to contacting Bob Neill and emphasises that the process will not be drawn out but will build on the best available evidence.

deb_ex.t: I again recognise the impact of the uncertainty across the summer. On the point about victim support, it is about high-quality engagement through victim liaison officers
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the appalling case and the uncertainty victims faced over the summer, and points to victim liaison officers, local support services and augmented funding for the victims helpline as ongoing support.

deb_ex.t: Traditionally, victims and survivors have lived their lives around the licence conditions of their perpetrator. We need to flip that, and restriction zones give us that chance.
deb_ex.sum: Argues restriction zones represent a significant shift by flipping the dynamic so victims no longer have to organise their lives around their perpetrator's licence conditions.

deb_ex.t: I was with staff on Friday and I was tagged, as colleagues may have seen. I have to say it worked very effectively in that case.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges points of failure but highlights improving technology and compliance, and describes personally being tagged to underline the government's commitment to making the system work.

deb_ex.t: I really recognise the importance of that question, and indeed the anxiety caused for survivors of domestic abuse as a result of the changes. We need clearer, earlier flagging. Tha
deb_ex.sum: Norris acknowledges anxiety for domestic abuse survivors and outlines government commitments to earlier flagging, better investment, and improved victim liaison engagement.

deb_ex.t: my priority is to reduce the Crown court waiting list and enable victims to have their day in court more quickly.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Courts and Tribunals Bill will return on 13 October and frames the government's priority as reducing Crown court waiting lists to help victims.

deb_ex.t: I would always caution the hon. Gentleman about believing reports. When there are things to be said, they will be said from the Dispatch Box.
deb_ex.sum: Deflects speculation from press reports, signals the new Lord Chancellor will review all aspects of MoJ business, and invites Parliament to engage when the Bill returns.

deb_ex.t: legislation very rarely looks the same at the beginning of the process as it does at the end.
deb_ex.sum: Declines to give a guarantee at this stage, stresses that legislation evolves through parliamentary scrutiny, and offers to engage with colleagues who have concerns.

deb_ex.t: the Opposition do not know how to deal with either the new Prime Minister or the new Government.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the Opposition's framing and reiterates the government's intention to work collectively in the country's interest, deflecting personal criticism.

deb_ex.t: if people have an interest in the legislation and want to discuss it, our door is open.
deb_ex.sum: Following the Speaker's intervention, reiterates the open-door offer to colleagues who wish to engage with the legislation.

deb_ex.t: I assure the hon. Lady that we will consider all evidence that is submitted, and certainly evidence submitted by those experts who I talked about in my opening answer. I am afraid
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House that expert evidence will be considered, rejects the critique of the government's approach, and argues that the status quo itself is unjust given trial waiting times stretching to 2029-30.

deb_ex.t: The Government have increased foreign national offender returns by 41%, with more than 3,000 foreign national offenders removed directly from prison last year through the early rem
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress on foreign national offender removals, citing a 41% increase and announcing new post-sentencing deportation powers and a cross-government taskforce.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Gentleman may well have seen that I set out the Government’s approach in this regard from this Dispatch Box in July. He will know, and it is important to reiterate t
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach, explaining that changes to the Immigration Act 1971 are not merely technical and that negotiations with receiving countries are ongoing but not publicly reported.

deb_ex.t: I congratulate my hon. Friend on her new position. I have a double degree of anxiety: as a former Justice Minister, she will know very well of what she speaks, but she is also a De
deb_ex.sum: Responds to the question by affirming the government's commitment to go further on removals and confirms joint working with the Home Office and Foreign Office to share information with receiving countries.

deb_ex.t: the answer to justice delayed cannot be justice diminished. We are looking again at the proposals, considering the evidence and listening to experts
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's position on the Crown court backlog, citing inherited figures and outlining investment, modernisation and the forthcoming Courts and Tribunals Bill as the means to fix it.

deb_ex.t: the Milton Keynes MPs are hunting in a pack on this matter. I think I have already committed to a visit, which I am sure I will make shortly.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges local ambition for a Milton Keynes justice quarter, confirms ongoing ministerial engagement with MPs, and signals a personal visit is planned.

deb_ex.t: I give the hon. Gentleman the assurance that I have no concerns in that regard. The device we used was the commencement order.
deb_ex.sum: Gives assurance that the government's legal position is sound, explaining that commencement orders were used to activate provisions selectively, and hints at tidying up the statute book through future primary legislation.

deb_ex.t: there are individuals with tariffs of 18 months who have served 18 years on those sentences. This has been a matter of consensus for a long period of time
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach to IPP sentences, citing the injustice of long over-tariff detention and noting cross-party consensus, while committing to proceed safely.

deb_ex.t: Our Government will bring forward legislation to end the IPP sentence by the end of this Parliament.
deb_ex.sum: Announces the government will legislate to end IPP sentences before the end of this Parliament, noting complexity and the need for cross-party engagement.

deb_ex.t: these sentences have been discontinued for a very good reason. That is a long-standing cross-party position, and it is time that we move forward.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the mental health challenges faced by IPP prisoners, highlights immediate support measures including the new Phoenix unit, and reaffirms the government's commitment to balanced reform.

deb_ex.t: I am grateful to the hon. Gentleman for the question, and the spirit in which it was asked. I will not be drawn on that individual case if it is with the Attorney General, because
deb_ex.sum: Declines to comment on the individual case before the Attorney General but acknowledges the tension between public protection and the injustice of holding prisoners long beyond their original sentences.

deb_ex.t: I am grateful for that question. It should discomfit colleagues that, in many cases, lots and lots of people across our communities have served long beyond their sentence and have
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges the injustice of IPP sentences, confirms forthcoming legislation, and agrees that those released must receive strong support to sustain their freedom.

deb_ex.t: The Bill has victims at its heart. Its purpose is urgent and long overdue: to ensure that justice in this country is fast and fair
deb_ex.sum: Moves Third Reading, crediting contributors and victims who shaped the Bill, and defends the Government's reform programme to tackle the 81,000-case Crown court backlog through investment, modernisation and structural change.

deb_ex.t: I will say two things. First, we are absolutely clear that tackling the climate crisis is an absolute priority for the Government. It is vital for our national security, our energy
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the Jackdaw decision is a transitional measure and that the Government's clear direction remains breaking dependence on fossil fuels and building home-grown clean energy.

deb_ex.t: the £2 billion we have set up today will be part of that picture and ensure that we can invest in projects in Northern Ireland
deb_ex.sum: Notes energy policy is devolved but confirms the interconnector with Ireland will benefit from the decision and that the new £2 billion fund will invest in Northern Ireland projects.

deb_ex.t: it is important that people understand that the Government are taking the issue seriously and are determined not to only tackle climate change at home
deb_ex.sum: Stresses the Government is taking climate change seriously and urges people to seek factual information about the progress being made towards decarbonising the energy system.

deb_ex.t: Let me be clear that that is a separate consenting decision. I am not making any comment at all today on the Rosebank decision, which will be made in due course. We are absolutely
deb_ex.sum: Makes clear Rosebank is a separate future decision and reaffirms the Government's commitment to the clean power mission, while defending Jackdaw on energy security and revenue grounds.

deb_ex.t: workers have to be right at the centre
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates GMB members and the skilled workforce that operates the gas transmission system, agreeing workers must be at the centre of the transition.

deb_ex.t: our long-term energy security and resilience cannot come from our being dependent on a fossil fuel that we will always be a net importer of
deb_ex.sum: Frames the Jackdaw decision as essential for winter energy security and argues long-term resilience must come from clean power, not continued fossil fuel dependence.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right that the North sea is a declining basin—I have said that on a number of occasions. That is not going to be turned around by decisions that we make, but none
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the North Sea is a declining basin but defends the Jackdaw decision as consistent with the manifesto commitment not to license new fields, arguing revenues bridge the transition.

deb_ex.t: we have always been clear that a strategic reserve will be necessary for particular industries and parts of the power system
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges more needs to be done on industrial gas costs, signals a strategic gas reserve for certain industries, and commits to working with the hon. Member to support those sectors.

deb_ex.t: if we do not fix the fundamental problem, we will have to bail people out every time there is another fossil fuel price spike
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the affordability crisis, points to VAT removal and previous bill reductions, and argues that only the clean energy transition will permanently end fossil fuel price spikes.

deb_ex.t: Your points have been noted, and I will absolutely take them back to the Department.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister accepts the Speaker's rebuke and undertakes to take the concerns back to the Department.

deb_ex.t: the Energy Secretary has decided in favour of the project and that the regulator, the North Sea Transition Authority, has now granted consent for gas to be produced
deb_ex.sum: The Minister announces the Energy Secretary has approved the Jackdaw gasfield consent, outlines the environmental considerations made, and sets out the North Sea energy wealth fund and transitional energy certificates as part of a managed g

deb_ex.t: the Conservative party left Britain with an energy system that was less secure, more exposed to international shocks and slower to invest than it should have been
deb_ex.sum: The Minister rebuts Conservative criticism, defends the consenting process, and argues the long-term priority is clean power and nuclear rather than fossil fuels, accusing the Conservatives of leaving Britain's energy system less secure.

deb_ex.t: it would be irresponsible not to make the investment needed in clean power and the long-term future of jobs. We are seeking to do both.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister agrees that retaining oil and gas supply chain workers is vital for building the renewables sector, and outlines how revenues from Jackdaw will be invested in clean power.

deb_ex.t: the Secretary of State was very clear that her assessment is that the decision does not prevent the UK from meeting legally binding limits on carbon emissions
deb_ex.sum: The Minister defends the decision as consistent with net zero obligations, argues a managed transition requires balancing climate goals with short-term energy security, and criticises the Lib Dems' record on nuclear.

deb_ex.t: A few years ago, 90% of the electricity price was set by gas. The figure is now 60%, and is going down all the time
deb_ex.sum: The Minister agrees Jackdaw will not cut bills directly but argues it matters for security, and sets out progress on breaking the electricity-gas price link through the warm homes plan and clean power mission.

deb_ex.t: the process will be just consideration of individual applications, rather than us having to go through all that again
deb_ex.sum: The Minister confirms the consenting process has been updated following the court judgments so future applications will be decided on individual merits without repeating the whole process, and calls for cross-party support for supply chain

deb_ex.t: The real prize of the energy transition, if we get it right, is tackling the climate crisis while creating jobs in every single part of the country.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister praises the hon. Member's championing of her community and argues that getting the energy transition right will create the next generation of sustainable jobs in renewables, carbon capture and hydrogen.

deb_ex.t: Just to be clear, I said that there was no time delay because the projects were not ready to extract in any event. It is for the developer to speak to the details, but my understan
deb_ex.sum: The Minister clarifies that Jackdaw development continued at the developer's risk during the consenting period, and declines to comment on the separate Rosebank regulatory process.

deb_ex.t: It is our duty to ensure that there is a long-term legacy for that workforce in oil and gas, in decommissioning and in other technologies
deb_ex.sum: The Minister pays tribute to North Sea workers, endorses the ambition of a clean energy supply chain reaching every postcode, and affirms the government's duty to secure long-term jobs in decommissioning and new technologies.

deb_ex.t: When we see big industry leave towns—I am a Lanarkshire MP, and I know the impact of coalmine closures and steel closures in my constituency
deb_ex.sum: The Minister sets out 27 direct and 273 safeguarded jobs from the project, and defends counting wider economic impacts by drawing on his own experience of industrial decline in Lanarkshire.

deb_ex.t: the determination made by the Secretary of State is that we are able to do that while meeting the climate objectives
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House that Jackdaw represents only around 5-6% of UK production, that the decision meets climate objectives, and that £2 billion in revenues will accelerate clean energy investment.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Lady speaks about 50 years; I am not quite sure what the SNP’s energy policy is right now. It changes from minute to minute, and it changes depending on whether the First
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's decision and investment in renewables, while attacking the SNP's inconsistent energy policy and dismissing criticism of Great British Energy.

deb_ex.t: I will always agree about high-quality jobs in Lanarkshire. It was a pleasure to visit my hon. Friend’s constituency to see the opening of the RES facility in Bellshill. It is an i
deb_ex.sum: Agrees jobs in Lanarkshire matter, cites the RES facility as an example of transition employment, and frames reindustrialisation as central to the Government's agenda.

deb_ex.t: I said in my statement that in the transition to clean energy, we will continue to need oil and gas. The UK continental shelf continues to be an important source of that, but we ha
deb_ex.sum: Defends the pragmatic decision as consistent with being a net importer, and criticises the Conservatives for abandoning their previous cross-party consensus on renewables.

deb_ex.t: One of the things we will launch soon is the future jobs service, which will support workers all the way through that process, giving them the necessary retraining
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the 27 direct jobs plus wider supply chain safeguards, and outlines the forthcoming future jobs service to retrain workers through the energy transition.

deb_ex.t: the Greens oppose the very infrastructure—they oppose wind farms, they oppose pylons, they oppose solar farms, they oppose nuclear—that gets us off fossil fuels
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the Green critique, arguing the Greens themselves block the renewable infrastructure needed to exit fossil fuels, and defends the Government's pragmatic approach.

deb_ex.t: I had a great visit to my hon. Friend’s constituency recently to see the importance of solar panels in a project there. We need to see much more of that investment, because our ene
deb_ex.sum: Argues energy sovereignty requires both building clean energy infrastructure now and maintaining gas supply through the transition, and says the Government is focused on both simultaneously.

deb_ex.t: geothermal is a huge opportunity and I know that there are projects starting to come much closer to delivery. We want to see much more of that
deb_ex.sum: Agrees geothermal is a huge opportunity and welcomes the hon. Member's championing of it, but declines to ring-fence funds and offers instead to have further discussions.

deb_ex.t: The real drive behind this is the clean energy transition for our energy security, but reindustrialisation off the back of that will create good jobs in every single part
deb_ex.sum: Points to Ayrshire supply chain opportunities, promotes the case for new nuclear at Hunterston, and frames reindustrialisation as central to delivering good jobs across the country.

deb_ex.t: the Scottish Government have the ScotWind fund, which they are currently drawing down to meet the deficit in their own spending. That is not building a legacy for the future
deb_ex.sum: Defends support for Acorn and welcomes SNP backing for Jackdaw, but criticises the Scottish Government for drawing down the ScotWind fund and for slow consenting decisions on renewables projects.

deb_ex.t: I agree with my hon. Friend. I have visited Torness and met the incredibly skilled workforce there. What I find difficult about the Scottish Government’s position on jobs in Scotla
deb_ex.sum: Strongly endorses nuclear power as essential to Scottish energy security, criticises the SNP for abandoning skilled nuclear workers, and calls on them to drop their anti-science position.

deb_ex.t: We had to design that process, consult on it with industry, get to a place where it was a practical process and then consider the applications. We have done that
deb_ex.sum: Declines to comment on the promotion but defends the consenting process as necessary following the Court of Session judgment and says it was completed as quickly as possible.

deb_ex.t: The pathway to net zero by 2050 has to accommodate the fact that we will require oil and gas, one way or another, while we are in that transition. The choices open to the Governmen
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Jackdaw consenting decision by explaining the trade-off between domestic extraction and higher-carbon LNG imports, framing it as consistent with carbon budgets and the net-zero pathway.

deb_ex.t: It is a great pleasure to see the hon. Gentleman back and looking so well. He is genuinely an hon. Gentleman and it is always a pleasure to speak with him. I completely agree with
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the hon. Member's support and highlights that the Lib Dem leader has personally endorsed Jackdaw, suggesting the party broadly backs the decision.

deb_ex.t: We have set up Great British Energy as a publicly owned energy company. It is already investing in supply chains, in supporting the North sea transition
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the difficulties faced by the hon. Member's constituency but defends Government investment in workforce transition, Great British Energy and supply chain support as evidence of meaningful action.

deb_ex.t: although this decision is important for energy security reasons, it will do nothing to bring down prices. Prices are set on an international market
deb_ex.sum: Corrects the claim that the Prime Minister promised lower prices, reaffirms prices are set internationally, and attacks Reform UK for championing maximum extraction while ignoring offshore wind jobs.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right on his point about jobs, although I reiterate that direct jobs are often not the whole story with such projects, as there is a whole ecosystem around jobs.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms joint UK-Scottish Government funding for skills and worker transition, while raising concern about the hollowing out of further education in Scotland and the need for more investment in colleges.

deb_ex.t: the North sea future jobs service should launch early next year.
deb_ex.sum: Assures the hon. Member that retraining funding is already committed via the North Sea future plan, which centres workers and recognises skills transferability into other energy, defence and manufacturing sectors.

deb_ex.t: the long-term energy security and our energy independence do not come from oil and gas, which we will always be a net importer of at this point on

deb_ex.t: every single individual application is considered on its own merits, with its own evidence base and its own consultation process. The Rosebank decision is separate from the Jackdaw decision.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms that every consenting application is assessed individually on its own evidence and that the Rosebank decision remains separate from today's Jackdaw decision.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees the climate emergency is real and urgent, rejects the adaptation-only argument, and defends the warm homes plan as the route to reducing household energy demand.

deb_ex.t: I will not comment on future decisions, but the decision I am outlining today is clearly taking into consideration environmental impact, and all other decisions will do likewise. T
deb_ex.sum: Declines to pre-judge future decisions but defends Labour's environmental record, pointing to the Climate Change Act, coal closure and world-leading targets as evidence of commitment to tackling climate change.

deb_ex.t: the Prime Minister has committed to working through how we can make the standing charge fairer and encourage people to make decarbonisation choices for affordability reasons.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges public frustration with standing charges, explains the funding challenge behind them, and confirms the Prime Minister has committed to making the charge fairer as part of a broader effort to reduce bills.

deb_ex.t: We have worked not just to create new jobs in the clean power of the future, but to make sure those are good jobs.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Jackdaw decision by stressing the importance of the clean energy transition and the Government's commitment to creating good, well-paid jobs in offshore wind and clean power.

deb_ex.t: On the international point and the message this decision sends about the climate emergency, I cannot be clearer about how central tackling climate change still is to the wider agen
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Jackdaw decision as consistent with the climate agenda, explains Rosebank is a quasi-judicial regulatory decision not subject to parliamentary debate, and reassures that environmental impacts will be central.

deb_ex.t: this Government take the climate emergency very seriously and are taking action right now to tackle it, whether that is building the clean power that gets us off fossil fuels
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the Government takes the climate emergency seriously, highlighting clean power investment and home insulation, and encourages young people to see clean energy jobs as real opportunities.

deb_ex.t: we are making it as attractive as possible to invest in clean energy sectors. That is why we have seen more than £100 billion-worth of private investment
deb_ex.sum: Points to over £110 billion of private investment in clean energy since Labour took office and urges pension funds to seize the economic opportunity of the clean energy transition.

deb_ex.t: I cannot just click my fingers and make that happen overnight. We have to build this infrastructure over time, and there is a transition period
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the claim that Jackdaw approval contradicts climate action, arguing gas is needed during a transition period and inviting ideas on how to accelerate electrification of heating.

deb_ex.t: Pragmatism means being clear that oil and gas will be important for decades to come and that we have to invest now in the jobs of the future
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that oil and gas jobs exist right across the UK, defends a managed transition supporting workers into new nuclear and renewables, and criticises politicians who claim pragmatism but refuse to acknowledge ongoing gas needs.

deb_ex.t: I or the Minister for the Middle East will take that up

deb_ex.sum: Miliband offers condolences and commits to discussing with Kirkham and the Middle East Minister what further action might be possible on accountability.

deb_ex.t: It is the coalition of countries that we have, as well as our actions, that gives us hope that we can actually make a difference
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that a coalition of countries acting together, alongside UK sanctions, offers the best hope of making a difference on both settlements and humanitarian issues.

deb_ex.t: it has been obvious that there has been collusion for a long time and the collusion has been allowed to continue
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the government continues to urge Israel to end army collusion with settler extremists, acknowledging with sorrow that collusion has long been evident and tolerated.

deb_ex.t: we need to work with our international partners—at this time of all times—to uphold international law in Gaza, in the west bank
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that the UK must work with international partners to uphold international law in Gaza, the West Bank and beyond.

deb_ex.t: this occupation has become entrenched over a long period. We have to work to unwind it and find ways in which we can get back
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the urgency of acting, noting the occupation has become entrenched over a long period and the government must work to unwind it and restore the path to a two-state solution.

deb_ex.t: The immorality of what is happening has stirred the conscience of millions of people across our country, and it is right that we act
deb_ex.sum: Notes that the issue has mobilised millions of ordinary British people whose moral conscience has been stirred, affirming that action is right and necessary.

deb_ex.t: E1 crossed a long-standing red line for the international community, which is why we saw such an outpouring from our allies
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that E1 crossed a long-standing international red line and affirms the urgency of acting in response.

deb_ex.t: the most important thing is upholding the role of both the ICC and the ICJ in these processes
deb_ex.sum: States that the UK works with the ICC and ICJ, which the government regards as incredibly important institutions for upholding accountability.

deb_ex.t: We are very clear that we do not want to see illegal settlement expansion, so I promise to look at this
deb_ex.sum: Undertakes to look at the gift aid issue, reiterates the government's opposition to illegal settlement expansion, and thanks all Members for their contributions.

deb_ex.t: We are doing everything in our power to stop the prospect of a two-state solution being destroyed by the expansion of illegal settlements.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's new sanctions measures announced on 8 September targeting illegal settlement activity and affirms commitment to protecting the two-state solution.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend asks an important question. The UK has stepped in to support Palestinian farmers who lost their work permits in green line Israel, but her broader point is the most
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges support for Palestinian farmers who lost work permits and expresses hope of working with whichever Israeli government is elected to counter settler terrorism.

deb_ex.t: Let me join you, Mr Speaker, in wishing my hon. Friend a happy birthday. May I say how well informed you are? I credit your staff, myself. In all seriousness, the situation in the
deb_ex.sum: Describes the situation in the West Bank as horrifying and confirms new legislation expanding the global human rights sanctions regime to target those responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend raises a really important issue that we have discussed in this House before. The E1 development is a direct threat to the prospect of a two-state solution. I want to
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms that the E1 development threatens the two-state solution and warns that individuals and businesses bidding for E1 construction tenders risk facing the full force of UK sanctions.

deb_ex.t: the very important finding we have made is that the occupation, not just the settlements, is illegal.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with his hon. Friend, reiterates that the occupation itself is illegal, and confirms action will be taken on economic relationships to advance the two-state solution.

deb_ex.t: we are determined to do all we can to prevent the settlement building in E1 from happening.
deb_ex.sum: Declines to speculate on specific future designations but confirms the expanded sanctions regime is in place precisely to enable swift action to prevent E1 settlement building.

deb_ex.t: the hon. Gentleman should be in no doubt about the purpose of our sanctions regime—to prevent the growth of illegal settlements, which is destroying the prospect of a two-state solution.
deb_ex.sum: Declines to comment on specific companies before sanctions action is taken but reaffirms the purpose of the sanctions regime is to prevent illegal settlement growth and protect the two-state solution.

deb_ex.t: I do not think that the response of the international community as a whole has been sufficient, which is why I made the statement I did on 8 September.
deb_ex.sum: Honestly acknowledges the international community's response has been insufficient, outlines steps taken since 8 September, and commits to using all powers including engagement with the incoming Israeli government to end settler terrorism.

deb_ex.t: I have seen that report, and I undertake to read it comprehensively. The reason we took the actions we did on 8 September was precisely to say that we will not stand by in silence
deb_ex.sum: Confirms he has seen the UN report and will read it fully, reaffirms the Government's actions of 8 September calling out war crimes and ethnic cleansing, and pledges maximum action to achieve peace and dignity for both peoples.

deb_ex.t: I am glad that my hon. Friend has raised this case, because we are obviously deeply concerned about the denial of entry to the west bank to two Members of Parliament and, I believe
deb_ex.sum: Expresses deep concern about MPs being denied entry to the West Bank, confirms the issue has been raised with Israeli authorities, and affirms the importance of MPs having free international access to carry out their duties.

deb_ex.sum: Assures the hon. Member that the work of tracking potential breaches of international humanitarian law continues and that the Department takes these issues incredibly seriously.

deb_ex.t: we are absolutely clear about the need to counter the Russian hybrid threat.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the UK does not engage with Russian officials and reiterates the government's clear commitment to countering the Russian hybrid threat.

deb_ex.sum: Declines to add anything further to previous answers on the appointment of Jonathan Powell.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that Ryan Cornelius should be released and confirms the issue is being raised with UAE counterparts.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that blocking of aid is outrageous and reaffirms the government's commitment to unblocking it, while declining to speculate on the use of the sanctions regime.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman raises an important issue. The role we will play is to bring home some of the lessons we have learned from taking action with allies, for example in relation to
deb_ex.sum: Explains the department will contribute lessons learned from countering disinformation with allies, citing the Moldova example, to strengthen the UK's own information defence.

deb_ex.sum: Outlines discussions at the Warsaw security forum and announces the establishment of a national centre for information defence to counter foreign interference.

deb_ex.t: He is absolutely right about countering all the threats we face from AI, as well as taking advantage of the opportunities.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the importance of countering AI-related threats and says the new national centre announced by the Prime Minister will address them.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms acceptance of the Brexit referendum result while stressing that Russia's ongoing attempts to interfere with and destabilise democracy must be recognised across the House.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the question and asserts that the Government will speak out firmly in favour of democratic norms wherever they are threatened, framing the current threat as the gravest since World War Two.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the hon. Lady to her place. She talks eloquently about the threats we face from across the world, whether that is Russia, Iran or China. It is incredibly important, and t
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the question's substance and asserts the Government will be resolute in countering threats from Russia, Iran and China, emphasising hybrid warfare as the modern challenge.

deb_ex.sum: Affirms determination to act on the Chelsea proceeds while citing legal constraints, and signals plans to push EU partners to move on Russian sovereign assets to support Ukraine through winter.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's engagement with European allies, emphasising commitment to Ukraine and a stronger NATO as guarantors of peace.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms a defence and security partnership with the EU and signals more work on countering disinformation is coming, while stressing the breadth of hybrid warfare threats.

deb_ex.sum: Rejects the accusation, citing a phased ban on maritime services for Russian gas expiring in January, and reaffirms the government's aim to ratchet up economic pressure on Russia.

deb_ex.sum: Stops short of endorsing single market membership but signals the government will use the upcoming EU summit to improve on the current Brexit deal across trade, defence and security.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's response to the RAF Fairford incident, noting IRGC designation, sanctions, and diplomatic pressure on Iran at the Istanbul E4/R4 Foreign Ministers meeting.

deb_ex.sum: Asserts the Commons' primacy, defends adherence to international law under global threat, and maintains that the Diego Garcia base is consistent with that legal framework.

deb_ex.sum: Praises pupils at Brompton Community primary school for their democratic campaigning on a 20 mph speed limit and asks the Minister to join in recognising them as an inspiring example.

deb_ex.sum: Reminds the hon. Member that Mersey Gateway tolls are Halton council's responsibility and highlights existing resident benefits, defending the current government position.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's commitment to better bus services, citing over £3 billion of funding and new powers under the Bus Services Act 2025.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out government funding of £45 million for Hampshire and highlights new powers under the Bus Services Act 2025 to help local leaders improve services.

deb_ex.sum: Points to the £165 million growth and housing accelerator fund as a mechanism for joint working and offers to ask National Highways to contact the hon. Member directly.

The NHS modernisation Bill will clarify and strengthen accountability in the NHS. It ends the fragmented accountability that we inherited on coming into government, and the reforms

corridor care is not an acceptable standard of care, and it must not become normalised

deb_ex.t: I wish at the start to take a moment to thank the Members on both sides of the House who served on the Public Bill Committee during what was a very hot end of June and July—if we c
deb_ex.sum: Thanks Committee members and sets out government new clauses on visiting rights and ICB local authority representation, then announces plans to table an amendment in the Lords to establish a statutory maternity and neonatal commissioner.

deb_ex.t: amendments 60 to 62 will re-establish a requirement for ICBs to have at least one board member jointly nominated by local authorities in their area
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms government commitment to listening and outlines the re-established requirement for ICBs to have a local authority board member, then confirms plans for a statutory maternity and neonatal commissioner to be tabled in the Lords.

deb_ex.t: we want to be ambitious. We are determined to make a real and positive change for people up and down the country who use the NHS
deb_ex.sum: Responds for the Government, acknowledging the breadth of debate and restating that the Bill's ambitions are to strengthen democratic accountability, strip back bureaucracy and empower patients.

deb_ex.t: reducing health inequalities remains a priority for this Government
deb_ex.sum: Minister responds to a range of amendments on carers, health inequalities, sickle cell, women's health and maternity, confirming government priorities and committing to follow-up letters while declining to accept new clause 91.

deb_ex.t: Contracts involving NHS data and digital services must be subject to proper scrutiny
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends existing legal tools for NHS data and procurement scrutiny, outlines how current legislation covers ethical standards and supplier exclusions, and signals a government-wide review of strategic procurement pipelines.

deb_ex.t: I thank Members in all parts of the House for their contributions to what has been an interesting and helpful discussion
deb_ex.sum: Minister thanks Members for their contributions and closes debate on the Bill, noting their expertise and scrutiny have strengthened it.

deb_ex.t: I spoke from the Opposition Benches for many years about the lack of accountability of our local systems to local members of Parliament
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges longstanding concerns about NHS accountability to local MPs, noting this drove her into politics and that she has worked to address it in her ministerial role.

deb_ex.t: the Bill is about returning that democratic accountability directly to the Secretary of State
deb_ex.sum: Minister rebuffs opposition interruptions, asserts the Bill returns democratic accountability to the Secretary of State, devolves delivery responsibility and empowers patients, and commends the new clause to the House.

deb_ex.t: I know that many hon. Members want to talk about the provisions in the Bill covering many important issues. I will therefore speak briefly about two Government amendments relating
deb_ex.sum: Minister introduces government new clauses on medical device licensing and information sharing, arguing they future-proof the regulatory framework and protect patients without weakening data safeguards.

deb_ex.t: As the hon. and learned Gentleman knows—we have spent many long hours in this place discussing the arrangements with regard to our leaving the European Union—there are different re
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends the Northern Ireland arrangements as a necessary consequence of Brexit and the Windsor framework, and explains that the new information-sharing clauses clarify MHRA powers without weakening patient data protections.

deb_ex.t: we are committed to devolving responsibility and to empowering leaders in the NHS, while also holding them directly accountable
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's approach, commits to reviewing Healthwatch provisions in the Lords, and reaffirms dedication to patient voice, health inequalities and eradicating corridor care.

deb_ex.t: I can give the House the assurance that we will work with the executive of HSSIB and the CQC to ensure that their operating model upholds this operational independence.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the transfer of HSSIB functions to the CQC, commits to operational independence for the investigation arm, and promises a reply to Sir Bernard Jenkin's letter.

deb_ex.t: I apologise, but I am going to press on. There is a lot to get through. We are committed to tackling health inequalities wherever they arise. There are strong duties on both ICBs a
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the Government's commitment to the national cancer plan and mental health strategy, noting record investment and ICBs meeting the mental health investment standard.

deb_ex.t: corridor care is one of the most visible and distressing symptoms of systemic pressures across the urgent and emergency care pathway
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's approach of avoiding condition-specific statutory duties and outlines action being taken to reduce and eradicate corridor care.

deb_ex.t: I can commit to the report being published in this Parliament, with a full Government response issued within three months of publication.
deb_ex.sum: Responds to points on corridor care, child health support and funeral regulation, committing to the Hugh Menai-Davis report being published this Parliament with a government response within three months.

deb_ex.t: We are undertaking urgent work to develop comprehensive proposals, including formal regulation of the funeral sector to drive out rogue operators
deb_ex.sum: Defends existing controls on puberty-suppressing hormones, rejects new clauses 142 and 143 as unnecessary, and commits to developing comprehensive funeral sector regulation proposals.

deb_ex.t: the Government do support well-designed research into innovative treatments using controlled drugs, where this is conducted safely and appropriately
deb_ex.sum: Confirms support for psychedelic therapy research, commits to writing to the Member on ACMD recommendations, and notes capital planning improvements for local infrastructure.

deb_ex.t: I commit to getting back to hon. Members. I know that my noble Friend Baroness Merron is committed to working co-operatively with all Members
deb_ex.sum: Closes the Report stage debate by committing to follow up on any missed points and noting the Lords Minister's cooperative approach.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend makes an excellent point about the importance of intermediate care, which is a key component of supporting patients into discharge to recover outside of hospitals. C
deb_ex.sum: Minister affirms intermediate care is a key government priority, stressing home-based care as the default pathway and commitment to working with the system to deliver it.

deb_ex.t: all changes to services should be based on clear evidence that they deliver better outcomes for his constituents and people across the country.
deb_ex.sum: Minister agrees to meet the Member and reaffirms that service changes must be evidence-based and deliver better outcomes, consistent with the government's aim of care closer to home.

deb_ex.t: We want to support frail people in their homes before they even get into hospital. I am working with the integrated care board to make sure that all that happens.
deb_ex.sum: Minister agrees with the principle of more care closer to home, confirms she is working with integrated care boards, and offers to meet the Member to discuss further.

deb_ex.t: As the hon. Gentleman knows, the situation deteriorated massively under the 14 years of Conservative government. He is well aware of the fragmentation of all our services. He knows
deb_ex.sum: Minister deflects blame onto fourteen years of Conservative fragmentation of services, reaffirms the government's three-shift strategy and social care ambitions, and claims the Opposition's challenge as endorsement of the government's direc

deb_ex.t: I am keen to discuss the new hospital programme and its progress with all Members
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the correspondence and encourages continued local discussions about the renal service, offering to stay in touch with the member.

deb_ex.t: We are moving the system governing hospitals such as Blackpool away from deficit funding so that it becomes well governed and managed
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern and says the system is moving away from deficit funding towards fair-shares allocation, offering further discussion.

deb_ex.t: I have met the hon. Member for Torbay (Steve Darling) to discuss this matter. Obviously, money has been allocated. We are well aware of the hospital’s position, and it is also part
deb_ex.sum: Notes she has already met the Torbay MP and that money has been allocated, offering to provide further information to the hon. Lady.

deb_ex.t: The movement of services is now firmly part of the programme, and the people of Watford will have the services that they deserve.
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to local campaigners and affirms that Watford will receive the services it deserves, promising an update once a final decision is made.

deb_ex.t: Food in hospitals is really important, and we would be very happy to meet Audrina. Well done to her.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes Audrina's campaign, affirms the importance of food in hospitals, and agrees to a meeting.

deb_ex.t: We are investing unprecedented amounts in capital and giving greater certainty, and I would be happy to meet my hon. Friend to discuss the proposal from Ipswich.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the poor state of NHS buildings inherited from the Conservatives, highlights record capital investment, and offers to meet to discuss the Ipswich proposal.

deb_ex.t: it is the responsibility of the commissioners to look holistically at the provision of services. We want more services closer to home
deb_ex.sum: Agrees commissioners should look holistically at service provision and encourages the Member to keep campaigning on transport between the two hospitals.

deb_ex.t: we are absolutely committed to working with the local system to do that. I absolutely commit to updating him as soon as possible
deb_ex.sum: Minister commits to working with the local system on the Torbay hospital crisis and promises a swift update to the hon. Member.

deb_ex.t: I am always keen to discuss and visit places in Dorset with my hon. Friend. I am happy to look, with him, at the integrated care board’s overall plan for the provision of all those
deb_ex.sum: Minister offers to look with the Member at the integrated care board's overall service provision plan for Dorset.

deb_ex.t: It is up to local systems to decide on the clinical pathways across the whole patch. Those decisions must be clinically led, and there must be consultation with local people
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges the local hospital issues, insists decisions must be clinically led with local consultation, and offers to continue monitoring and discussing with the Member.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely endorse your comments about our colleague, Mr Speaker. I know that my hon. Friend and many other colleagues are deeply concerned about the issues at Northern Care Alli
deb_ex.sum: Minister confirms the trust is under the highest level of regional oversight and stresses the need for rapid improvement in governance and patient care.

deb_ex.t: further action is available to NHS England and the Care Quality Commission. We want to ensure that the focus now is on supporting and challenging the trust
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges the scale of failures, confirms further regulatory action remains available, and encourages MPs to work closely with the trust to drive sustained improvement.

deb_ex.sum: Outlines the Government's commitment to safe, high-quality maternity care, updates the House on recruitment progress and trust reopening criteria, and confirms ministerial priority status for maternity services.

deb_ex.t: I am glad to see that SNP Members are staying classy, as usual. On the matter of personnel choices, I am not sure that my first go-to source would be the First Minister, because of
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the independence question by attacking the SNP's record on NHS waiting times and governance, dismissing the call for a referendum.

deb_ex.t: The Chair of the Scottish Affairs Committee speaks with her characteristic wisdom and authority on these matters. It seems that the only output that is rising on the SNP’s watch is
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the previous speaker's point and takes a further dig at SNP legal difficulties, continuing to deflect from the independence question.

deb_ex.t: for them, government is simply a way station on the route to independence, so they are not interested in delivering truthfully for the people of Scotland
deb_ex.sum: Agrees devolution provides tools but argues the SNP has squandered them because independence, not delivery, is their true goal.

deb_ex.t: I have always believed that to be pro-Scottish, you do not need to be anti-English. We should be bigger and more generous than that.
deb_ex.sum: Responds warmly to the football question and uses it to reinforce his view that being pro-Scottish does not require being anti-English or anti-Union.

deb_ex.t: We had a manifesto commitment not only opposing independence, but opposing a further referendum, and we stand by that mandate.
deb_ex.sum: Gives a clear one-word affirmation and reiterates the government's manifesto commitment against both independence and a further referendum.

deb_ex.t: there are ways that we can improve the working of our democracy within the United Kingdom, without leaving and separating ourselves from the United Kingdom
deb_ex.sum: Recalls campaigning for the alternative vote alongside the Lib Dems and expresses openness to democratic improvements within the Union, while opposing separation.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the hon. Member to her place and congratulate her on her recent by-election victory. This Government’s focus is to make the existing devolution settlement work effectivel
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the new Member and defends the government's position that the existing devolution settlement should work effectively, criticising SNP centralisation at Holyrood.

deb_ex.t: The SNP seems to respect every vote, apart from the constitutional referendum, in which 84% of the Scottish people exercised their democratic choice. The hon. Member she says that
deb_ex.sum: Defends the UK Government's retention of energy policy and deflects by attacking SNP centralisation at Holyrood, referencing the 1998 independence referendum result.

deb_ex.t: After 19 years in power, they must account for their record on public services, from NHS waiting lists to declining school standards.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the previous contribution, criticising the SNP's record on NHS and education after 19 years in power and calling for delivery over division.

deb_ex.t: It is perfectly possible to drive a Ferrari into a ditch, which is pretty much what we have seen over the last 19 years.
deb_ex.sum: Rebuffs the suggestion that SNP mismanagement should discredit devolution itself, implying the fault lies with the SNP rather than the settlement.

deb_ex.t: An awareness of all those issues is not simply for the incoming Prime Minister, but for anybody who reads a newspaper in Scotland. What we have witnessed is a travesty of the poten
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that the SNP has squandered the potential of devolution through failure across devolved policy areas including ferries, hospitals and schools.

deb_ex.t: Scotland possesses land areas with high potential for new nuclear development. Such projects could deliver significant investment and thousands of high-quality, unionised, skilled jobs.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms Scotland has high potential for new nuclear development and says the Government is open to discussions with the Scottish Government to boost growth and energy security.

deb_ex.t: Whether it is Hunterston in my hon. Friend’s constituency or Torness in my own constituency, Scotland has a proud history of harnessing civil nuclear power to bring jobs and growth
deb_ex.sum: Praises Scotland's civil nuclear history and sharply criticises the SNP's anti-nuclear position as anti-scientific, warning it will cost Scotland high-skilled jobs and investment.

deb_ex.t: Yes. On that there is cross-party consensus. I can attest to that as the constituency Member of Parliament in Lothian East, where we have had decades of not just sustainable power
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the Conservative member, cites Torness as evidence of nuclear's economic and skills benefits, and expresses the Government's desire to see nuclear continue beyond 2029-30.

deb_ex.t: City region and growth deals are having a visible and transformative impact on regional economies across Scotland.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's position that city region deals are having a transformative impact on Scottish regional economies, backed by over £1.5 billion of UK Government investment.

deb_ex.t: In the words of the incoming Prime Minister, we’re up for it, as far as devolving power from Holyrood is concerned. Alas, many of the powers rest with the Scottish Government. We n
deb_ex.sum: Signals the government's support for devolving power from Holyrood to city regions and criticises centralisation, calling for a renewed focus on Scotland's city regions.

deb_ex.t: West Dunbartonshire is presently benefiting from over £500 million through the Glasgow city region deal, as well as money from our new local growth fund.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the Member that the government is committed to unlocking the economic potential of sites like the ExxonMobil terminal, noting West Dunbartonshire is already benefiting from over £500 million through the Glasgow city region deal.

deb_ex.t: Scotland remains at the very heart of the UK’s energy system. Just last week, I was at St Fergus alongside the Energy Secretary to approve the Jackdaw gasfield, paving the way for
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's record on Scottish energy, citing the Jackdaw gasfield approval and clean electricity generation statistics, and argues this supports jobs, climate goals and energy security.

deb_ex.t: because of the policy of the Scottish National party in Edinburgh, we are forgoing millions of pounds of investment, energy security, and good, well-paid, unionised jobs for decades to come.
deb_ex.sum: Echoes the previous point from personal experience at Torness, arguing SNP policy costs Scotland millions in investment, energy security and good unionised jobs.

deb_ex.t: the measure of the effectiveness of GB Energy was never the number of officials working in the headquarters in Aberdeen; it was how many jobs are created in the north-east
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the Conservative critique by arguing GB Energy's success should be measured by jobs created across the UK rather than headcount at Aberdeen HQ, and points to Jackdaw consent as evidence of progress.

deb_ex.t: domestic oil and gas will continue to play an important part in our energy mix for decades to come.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's pragmatic approach to the North Sea, citing the approval of the Jackdaw gasfield and affirming the continued importance of domestic oil and gas.

deb_ex.t: over the decade preceding July 2024 and the election of the Labour Government, alas 70,000 jobs were lost.
deb_ex.sum: Rebuts Conservative criticism by noting 70,000 jobs were lost under the previous government and stresses the need for a credible transition plan.

deb_ex.t: it left an energy system in 2024 that was less secure, more exposed to international shocks, and slower to invest.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses Conservative criticism as hypocritical given the energy insecurity they left behind, and points to the Jackdaw approval as evidence of the government's pragmatic approach.

deb_ex.t: The reason we took the decision on Jackdaw last week was that the Conservative Government so messed up the process that we ended up in court.
deb_ex.sum: Blames Conservative mismanagement of the North Sea approval process for forcing the government into court, justifying the delayed Jackdaw decision.

deb_ex.t: The point that my hon. Friend makes is well taken. The supply chain supporting oil and gas, and the energy sector more generally, is not limited to the north-east but stretches rig
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the breadth of the supply chain across Scotland and signals that the Chancellor's forthcoming statement will be relevant.

deb_ex.t: The SNP-led Government in Edinburgh are not short of opinions on anything, apart from their view on the Jackdaw decision that we reached last week. The First Minister opposed the d
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the SNP's inconsistent positions on North Sea oil and gas transition while defending the government's Jackdaw decision.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend speaks with great authority because a number of North sea workers are based in the Western Isles. For many years, people have argued for the establishment of an ener
deb_ex.sum: Defends the energy wealth fund as a genuine commitment to North Sea workers and contrasts it with the SNP's failure to deliver a publicly owned energy company.

deb_ex.t: there is a process that needs to be followed, following the evidence and reaching a determination. Alas, that was not a process that the Conservatives chose to follow.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's cautious, evidence-based approach to Rosebank while criticising the Conservatives for failing to follow due process on previous decisions.

deb_ex.t: I get the impression that that question was drafted before the Jackdaw decision was issued just last week.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the previous question as pre-drafted before the Jackdaw approval, implying the criticism is already out of date.

deb_ex.t: The UK Government are committed to deepening devolution across Scotland, working in partnership with the Scottish Government to push power out from Holyrood and into the hands of l
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's commitment to deepening devolution in Scotland by pushing power from Holyrood into local communities, citing the Prime Minister's offer of a collaborative new model of regional economic empowerment.

deb_ex.t: The Prime Minister on these Benches was making a very basic and clear comparison, which is that there is no consensus in favour of a border poll in Northern Ireland, and there is c
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the SNP's call for independence referendum legislation by arguing that the Prime Minister was simply noting there is no consensus for either a border poll in Northern Ireland or a referendum in Scotland.

deb_ex.t: Scotland is the most devolved nation in the United Kingdom, but still one of the most centralised nations in Europe. We believe that should change.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that power should flow beyond Holyrood into communities, invoking Donald Dewar's vision, and criticises the current situation where Scotland is simultaneously the UK's most devolved nation yet one of Europe's most centralised.

deb_ex.t: There is a certain irony in being told how devolution operates by a Conservative party that was deeply resistant to devolution when we established it; and I voted for the Scotland
deb_ex.sum: Rebuffs the Conservative critique by noting the irony of lectures on devolution from a party that opposed the Scotland Act 1998, and clarifies that the Prime Minister's deeper devolution agenda is about decentralisation across the whole UK,

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right, and we have expressed an interest in taking part in the PISA financial literacy assessment in 2029. We recognise the importance of financial edu
deb_ex.sum: Confirms UK interest in the 2029 PISA financial literacy assessment and signals that financial education will be strengthened in the maths and citizenship curricula, agreeing to meet.

deb_ex.t: I am absolutely with the hon. Member on the importance of residential activities, and for every young person to have access to them.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the importance of residential activities for young people and begins to reference a personal connection to a facility in the hon. Member's constituency.

deb_ex.t: It is a fantastic facility, and my ambition is that every child has the opportunity to go somewhere as fantastic as that.
deb_ex.sum: Shares a personal experience of Ghyll Head outdoor centre and expresses ambition that every child should have access to such opportunities, offering to work with the hon. Member.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend has already spoken to me a number of times about these issues, because he is a very good chair of the APPG on classics. I thank him for his question, and he is absol
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the curriculum has narrowed under the EBacc and commits to ensuring all young people can access great academic subjects including classics alongside technical ones.

deb_ex.t: If the hon. Gentleman can find where I said that I wanted to bring back coursework then he can bring it to me, because I did not say that.
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the opposition's characterisation, denies having said she wanted to bring back coursework and challenges them to produce evidence.

deb_ex.t: They send their kids to private school, where they all come out really confident in speaking. I want that for every child.
deb_ex.sum: Defends her record, accuses the Opposition of narrowing the curriculum and refusing accountability, and champions oracy, computing and PE as core curriculum priorities for all children.

deb_ex.t: The student loans system we inherited is broken and unfair, and some graduates feel the weight of it more strongly.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the student loans system inherited is broken and unfair and signals reform is her top priority.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Lady has put that really well. I reassure her that we absolutely keep these things under review. I have said that this issue is at the top of my in-tray, and that remains
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the questioner that she keeps these issues under review and acknowledges cost of living pressures on plan 2 graduates, promising more to say soon.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for his question and for all his campaigning on this issue, which I have followed closely. He is absolutely right, and in response to the excellent report of
deb_ex.sum: Highlights government actions including clearer pre-university guidance, capping maximum interest rates and reintroducing maintenance grants.

deb_ex.t: As I have said, I am determined that we get these things right. Two things can be true at the same time: I feel the system is unfair and in need of reform, but we also have to put
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's position by arguing reform must be balanced against wider public finances, while attacking the Conservatives for introducing the plan 2 system and freezing the threshold multiple times.

deb_ex.t: making it tastier and healthier and giving over half a million more children free school meals
