deb_ex.sum: Suggests that domestic oil and gas production would boost Exchequer revenues which could then be used to reduce consumer bills.

deb_ex.t: The definition of a Scotch single malt whisky is that it must be mashed, fermented and distilled at a single distillery in Scotland, but for English single malt, some of those step
deb_ex.sum: Lumsden argues that consistency in the definition of single malt across UK nations would be clearer for consumers and better for the industry.

deb_ex.t: The parties that are talking down the North sea oil and gas workers are the Labour Government here and the SNP Government in Holyrood. The Conservative party is standing up for the
deb_ex.sum: Lumsden accuses the Labour government of delaying Jackdaw and Rosebank approvals to protect its position in a London by-election, argues the Prime Minister promised a pragmatic approach, and demands approval as a matter of urgency for natio

deb_ex.t: Will the Minister tell us whether the Government have a role in consenting new drilling in the Falklands—yes or no?
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Minister for a direct yes-or-no answer on whether the UK Government has a role in consenting new drilling in the Falklands.

deb_ex.t: while Labour dithers on approving Rosebank and Jackdaw, thousands of my constituents in Aberdeen South are losing their jobs
deb_ex.sum: Argues domestic oil and gas production is preferable to importing dirtier hydrocarbons and presses the Minister for a timetable on Rosebank and Jackdaw decisions, citing job losses in his constituency.

deb_ex.t: Before recess, senior officials from Ofcom gave a dreadful performance at the Scottish Affairs Committee as they failed to justify why my constituents were denied bespoke news prog
deb_ex.sum: Criticises Ofcom for failing to justify the removal of bespoke STV North news coverage to the Scottish Affairs Committee and calls for a Government-time debate on whether Ofcom can still fulfil its legal responsibilities.

deb_ex.t: the SNP Government need to play a role in this? So far, they have been silent on the subject
deb_ex.sum: Calls on the SNP Scottish Government to play a role, noting their silence on the matter so far.

deb_ex.t: Will this decision streamline the process for other North sea developments? We need a pipeline of projects coming through to protect jobs and to keep the lights on.
deb_ex.sum: A Conservative MP, also noting his frustration at the Secretary of State visiting his constituency without notice, welcomes the Jackdaw decision and asks whether it will streamline approval of other North Sea projects to protect jobs.

deb_ex.t: The Labour Government’s answer to energy independence was to create GB Energy, which we were told was going to create 1,000 jobs in Aberdeen. Two years in, it has just 132 employee
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the government's record on GB Energy, noting far fewer jobs than promised in Aberdeen, and calls for a return to domestic drilling to boost employment.

Brexit continues to put up barriers to business and trade, including through labour shortages, trade friction and long-term uncertainty over subsidies.
deb_ex.sum: Bird highlights Brexit's severe impact on Scottish farmers, citing lost revenue, trade barriers and labour shortages, and urges the Minister to do more to support them.

deb_ex.t: The Energy Secretary says that he supports green jobs, yet there is growing concern that only two of the six National Energy System Operator pipelines will support the Scottish win
deb_ex.sum: SNP MP raises concern that only two of six NESO pipelines support Scottish wind pathways, warning this could cost Scotland £100 billion of renewables investment and thousands of jobs.

deb_ex.t: I apologise in advance to those on the Opposition Front Bench, because I, too, am going to ask a question about Brexit. A study last month showed that the Scottish economy has been
deb_ex.sum: SNP MP welcomes limited aspects of the deal but argues it does little to offset the £30 billion annual cost of Brexit to Scotland, particularly for food, drink and farming sectors, and asks what the government says to overlooked Scottish fa

deb_ex.t: Whether he has had recent discussions with Cabinet colleagues on the devolution of further powers to Scotland.
deb_ex.sum: Asks whether the Secretary of State has discussed devolving further powers to Scotland with Cabinet colleagues.

deb_ex.t: Devolution appears to be all the rage at the moment, and the Secretary of State will know fine well that the Scottish Parliament recently voted to devolve energy powers back to Sco
deb_ex.sum: Calls on the UK Government to respect the Scottish Parliament's vote and devolve energy powers to Scotland.

deb_ex.t: Scotland is not a region, and nor should it be treated as one. Those in Scotland are hurt and frustrated at the way the Prime Minister has conducted the conversation around devolut
deb_ex.sum: Bird accuses the Prime Minister of arrogantly dismissing Scotland's pro-independence mandate and treating Scotland as a region rather than a nation.

deb_ex.t: Monifieth in my constituency is home to over 9,000 people and is the central connection point for a vast rural community across Angus. Despite an application in 2023, a banking hub
deb_ex.sum: Raises Monifieth's failed banking hub application and argues current regulations are unfit for rural communities, asking the Minister to meet to resolve the situation.

deb_ex.t: how many Palestinian lives could have been spared if the UK Government 25 years ago had acted on the information and the facts that were in front of them
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes last week's statement but criticises successive UK Governments for decades of inaction despite knowing the scale of Palestinian suffering, and grieves the murder of her friend Awdah Hathaleen by an Israeli settler.

deb_ex.t: the Prime Minister is already abandoning his promises to WASPI women. How can pensioners, WASPI women and the public in general trust the DWP
deb_ex.sum: Accuses the Labour Government of abandoning WASPI women and breaking Prime Ministerial promises, questioning how pensioners can trust the DWP.

deb_ex.t: the UK Government spend seven times more on defence in south-east England than in the whole of Scotland combined
deb_ex.sum: Argues that Scotland faces real threats but receives disproportionately low defence spending, and calls for a permanent Royal Navy surface vessel on Scotland's north coast.

deb_ex.t: the rules and requirements to use the protected name for English whisky and its sub-categories, including the single malt, are determined by product specification.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister explains that the English whisky product specification was produced by the English Whisky Guild reflecting its sector's traditions and complies with all applicable legislation.

deb_ex.t: It is not a binary choice. We can support English whisky and Scotch whisky, and I stress that we are supporting the growth of the whisky industry.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister rejects the binary framing, arguing the government supports both English and Scotch whisky and points to trade agreements with India, the US and China as evidence.

deb_ex.t: we introduced the new rule that each farm business could have only one SFI26 agreement, which cannot exceed £100,000 per year.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government improvements to SFI26, including a £310 million allocation across two windows and commitments to reform for SFI27.

deb_ex.t: I am not going to claim that this scheme is perfect or working as we want it to work, but we inherited this scheme from the previous Government, and we are fixing it. Under them, j
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's record, blaming the inherited scheme for its flaws, rejects the claim that first-come-first-served was a Labour innovation, and refuses to accept the shadow minister's criticism.

deb_ex.t: it was Michael Gove who I think first introduced the first come, first served approach. I also pay tribute to those at the RPA.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the previous minister's contributions, endorses his point about Conservative hypocrisy on SFI, and pays tribute to RPA staff.

deb_ex.t: I mentioned some of the funding that we have put into sustainable funding—£11.8 billion over this Parliament.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Liberal Democrat spokesperson, highlights £11.8 billion in farming funding over Parliament, and commits to reflecting on her points in designing next year's scheme.

deb_ex.t: I am really keen to work in partnership with others to design a scheme that works for all farmers next year.
deb_ex.sum: Encourages the hon. Member to write with farmers' concerns and reaffirms the government's commitment to designing a better scheme for next year.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Chair of the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee for his measured intervention, and look forward to being before his Committee later this month. We obviously
deb_ex.sum: Explains that high demand was anticipated and the government increased funding to £310 million, and welcomes the committee chair's scrutiny ahead of an upcoming appearance.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for the way he has engaged with me on thinking through the design for the scheme next year. He is right to say that some farmers reported technical issues wi
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges technical issues were reported and confirms the RPA is working through valid cases, inviting the hon. Member to share specific examples.

deb_ex.t: We are publishing the figures for applications across counties and constituencies, so I can certainly make that information available to the right hon. Member.
deb_ex.sum: Promises to share county-level figures with the Member and points to the 25-year farming road map as the government's commitment to farm resilience.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is a real champion for farmers in his constituency, as is very evident from the contributions that he makes in this House, which are so informed. He is absolutely ri
deb_ex.sum: Praises the hon. Member as a champion for farmers, endorses the call-out of Opposition inaction, and offers a meeting to inform next year's scheme design.

deb_ex.t: our annual report sets out how we spend the farming budget, and if he has not yet had a chance to see that, I encourage him to do so.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member for his constructive engagement, points to the annual report on farming budget spending, and agrees to take RPA frustrations back to the Department.

deb_ex.t: It was a real pleasure to meet my hon. Friend recently to discuss some of the particular challenges her constituency is facing, and wider issues including bluetongue. I will certai
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member following a recent meeting and commits to bearing her constructive points about less-favourable land in mind when designing SFI27.

deb_ex.t: I am keen to open SFI27 as early as possible, and I gave that assurance from the Dispatch Box earlier.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the difficult year for farmers, reaffirms commitment to opening SFI27 as early as possible, and highlights £2.3 billion available for farming this year.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend will know that we were responding to our settlement from the Treasury. There is always more we can do. That is why we published our farming road map earlier this yea
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges Treasury constraints but points to the farming road map as evidence of the government's commitment to a resilient, nature-friendly farming sector.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely recognise the human difficulties for farmers who have not been able to apply for the scheme this year.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the human difficulties for unsuccessful applicants, invites the Member to share specific examples, and signposts wider support available via the DEFRA website.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for the way in which he has been engaging with me already so that we can learn lessons from SFI26, and for convening colleagues in the process. Uplands are a
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member for engaging constructively, confirms uplands are a priority, and commits to extending nature-friendly upland farming models across the country.

deb_ex.t: The scheme was what it was; we inherited a mess from the previous Administration. I am keen to learn lessons from what worked.
deb_ex.sum: Declines to apologise, blames the inherited scheme design, acknowledges the heartache caused and says lessons will be learned.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member will have heard what I said at the outset with regard to our farming road map, which sets out the long-term vision for delivering a more nature-friendly farming sec
deb_ex.sum: Points to the farming road map and the £2.3 billion farming budget as evidence of long-term commitment, and directs the Member to other available schemes on the DEFRA blog.

deb_ex.t: I will take no lectures from the Conservatives; they had a scheme that was half-baked and did not deliver anything nor put money in the pockets of farmers.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects Conservative criticism by blaming the previous government for a half-baked scheme that failed farmers.

deb_ex.t: That is a little rich coming from the right hon. Member, who served in the previous Conservative Government, which designed the scheme.
deb_ex.sum: Deflects criticism by noting the questioner served in the government that designed the scheme and invites constructive engagement on improvements.

deb_ex.t: I said at the outset that it has been a brutal year for farmers across our country, with drought, rising input costs and various other factors. I hear those messages loud and clear
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the brutal year farmers have faced, says lessons must be learned, but again attributes the scheme's faults to the previous government.

deb_ex.t: I said at the outset that there are lessons that need to be learnt from the scheme this year, so I hope that the hon. Member has heard that message loud and clear. If the hon. Memb
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates that lessons will be learned from this year's scheme and invites the Member to share specific constituency examples to inform improvements for next year.

deb_ex.t: I am engaging all the time with farmers across the country and their representatives. They are at the heart of our redesign of the scheme for next year. Workshops are starting toda
deb_ex.sum: Insists he is continuously engaging with farmers and their representatives, that redesign workshops have already begun, and reaffirms commitment to improving the process.

deb_ex.t: I do not accept that we have not learned lessons from the past. That is why we made a number of changes for SFI26, as I set out at the outset of my statement. Of course I am sorry
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the claim that no lessons were learned, lists changes made for SFI26, and offers a qualified apology to unsuccessful applicants while pledging to improve the scheme.

deb_ex.t: I thank the right hon. Member for his question. As I said at the outset, it is worth noting that £2.3 billion has been made available for the farming budget this year, with £11.8 b
deb_ex.sum: Points to the £2.3 billion farming budget and the first-ever farming road map as proof of the government's commitment, and invites the Member to share specific cases of unsuccessful applicants.

deb_ex.t: food security is national security, and we are working through what that looks like in the Department
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges farmers' difficulties but affirms the government's food security commitment and its road map for future certainty in the sector.

deb_ex.t: I thank the right hon. Lady for her question. As I mentioned at the outset, it was her Government who introduced the “first come, first served” approach. We are absolutely keen to
deb_ex.sum: Deflects criticism by noting the previous government introduced the first-come-first-served approach and invites practical suggestions for improvement.

deb_ex.t: I have met the RPA on the lessons learned from the scheme and what worked well this year
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House that he has already met the RPA to review lessons learned and will analyse application data.

deb_ex.t: we are keen to open SFI27 as early as possible into the new year
deb_ex.sum: Promises further information on future rounds in due course and points farmers to other available DEFRA funding schemes.

deb_ex.t: I am very happy to meet the hon. Gentleman to discuss those issues
deb_ex.sum: Offers to meet the hon. Member to discuss the concerns raised about farmers on the levels.

deb_ex.t: We will continue to be as transparent as we can beyond the figures available for farmers
deb_ex.sum: Points to the annual report as evidence of transparency and commits to continuing to publish budget information for farmers.

deb_ex.t: he knows my commitment to working in partnership with the Northern Ireland Government. I have already met with my counterparts in Northern Ireland
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges farming is devolved but confirms he has already met Northern Ireland counterparts and is committed to working in partnership with them.

deb_ex.t: Demand substantially exceeded the funding available, and we must learn from that experience as we work with the sector in partnership on SFI27.
deb_ex.sum: Responds for the Government by defending the farming road map and record £11.8 billion allocation, acknowledging frustration at the SFI window closing speed, committing to scrap first-come-first-served and to bring forward SFI27 as early as

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Gentleman for that intervention. He will know that we made a number of changes to improve the scheme this year. He briefly mentioned those in his opening remarks,
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms commitment to scrapping first-come-first-served and bringing forward SFI27 early, defends new trade deals as protecting food standards, and highlights the SPS agreement with the EU as benefiting British farmers.

deb_ex.t: the Government went further to protect more farms and businesses, while maintaining the core principle that the most valuable agricultural and business assets should not receive unlimited relief
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's reforms to agricultural property relief, arguing the previous Chancellor listened to industry concerns and acted to protect more farms while maintaining the principle that the most valuable assets should not receive

deb_ex.t: On these matters the Government’s view is now settled. I recognise that the previous Chancellor made the changes as a result of the engagement that she and others had with the farm
deb_ex.sum: Minister closes the debate by defending the Government's settled position on farm inheritance tax and reaffirming its commitment to backing British farming through the farming road map.

deb_ex.t: its protected status and production requirements remain unchanged following the registration of English whisky geographical indication.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures the House that Scotch whisky's protected status and production requirements are unaffected by the registration of the English whisky GI.

deb_ex.t: Other whisky definitions, including Welsh, Irish and EU definitions, already co-exist with the Scotch whisky definition without affecting its protected status.
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates that the English whisky GI does not affect Scotch whisky's definition and notes that other whisky definitions already co-exist without undermining Scotch whisky's protected status.

deb_ex.t: due process has been followed, and rigorous scrutiny processes have been adhered to.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the process, noting the Scotch Whisky Association has appealed to the first tier tribunal and asserting that due process and rigorous scrutiny have been followed.

deb_ex.t: The wine sector is a British success story and we want to grow it further.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government support for the wine sector including innovation, labour access and export promotion via agrifood attachés.

deb_ex.t: DEFRA recognises the growth potential of the wine tourism industry, including its contribution to rural jobs and rural communities.
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms government commitment to the wine industry and acknowledges wine tourism's rural economic potential, while deflecting the duty relief question to the Treasury.

deb_ex.t: An SPS agreement could increase the volume of UK exports of major primary agricultural commodities to the EU by around 16%.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's position that the SPS agreement will reduce trade barriers and could increase UK agricultural exports to the EU by around 16%.

deb_ex.t: I can confirm that the UK has been clear about the importance of being able to support the use of new and innovative technologies.
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms commitment to the Precision Breeding Act and states the UK has made clear to the EU the importance of supporting new and innovative technologies in negotiations.

deb_ex.t: The CropLife UK report is clear that the numbers presented are a worst-case scenario. We are building a new pragmatic relationship with the EU, markedly different to what has gone
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the CropLife UK figure as a worst-case scenario and defends the government's approach as pragmatic and beneficial, while declining to give further detail before negotiations conclude.

deb_ex.t: We recognise the importance of access to high-quality genetic material for maintaining healthy breeding populations.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the importance of access to genetic material for breeding populations and states that zoo technical arrangements facilitate such trade, with details subject to ongoing negotiations.

deb_ex.t: we have been clear that we will only pursue an SPS agreement that has British interests at its heart.
deb_ex.sum: Hits back at the shadow Minister over the previous government's record and insists the government will only conclude an SPS agreement with British interests at its heart.

deb_ex.t: As a Member of Parliament who represents a coastal community, engaging with our fishing community is a priority of mine. That is why I have visited Cornwall and the south-west on a
deb_ex.sum: Emphasises personal engagement with coastal fishing communities and commits to working with the fishing and seafood sector towards a viable and sustainable future.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Member will have heard what I said about the value of the sanitary and phytosanitary agreement, but more broadly, Seafish obviously has a role in promoting seafood a
deb_ex.sum: Notes Seafish's role in promoting seafood globally and highlights the Minister's attendance at a Paris food expo promoting British products including oysters.

deb_ex.t: Fertiliser CBAM liabilities are expected to be below 1% of current prices, with impacts on farmers very limited.
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that fertiliser CBAM liabilities will be below 1% of current prices with limited impact on farmers, and that CBAM will support transition to low-carbon supply chains alongside domestic farming policy.

deb_ex.t: I will ensure that a Minister meets the hon. Lady to discuss that proposal, because I find myself in agreement with it.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the proposal for mandatory suicide prevention training, acknowledges the devastating case of Matilda, and commits to arranging a meeting with a Minister.

deb_ex.t: I recognise that Ian is obviously in a very difficult position. I am pleased to say the Exchequer Secretary has announced that we will bring forward a new approach to this issue. W
deb_ex.sum: Announces a new permanent approach removing VAT as a barrier to free-of-charge donations of innovative medicines, backdated to June, and commits to a ministerial meeting.

deb_ex.t: The second round of auditions, Mr Speaker! I saw Essex got a mention this week, but it was still a question about London. I did increase police numbers in my time as Mayor of Great
deb_ex.sum: Credits his own record on police numbers in Greater Manchester but argues central government support is essential, turning the question back on the former Home Secretary's own responsibility for the Met's decline.

deb_ex.t: I will. Marie Lyon has been an incredible, indomitable fighter for women affected by Primodos. I pay full tribute to her. I was so sorry to hear about her recent illness, but I can
deb_ex.sum: Praises Marie Lyon's campaign, expresses sorrow at her illness, and commits from the Dispatch Box to work with her and the MP to secure justice for Primodos victims.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman and colleagues will know that I did go to Northern Ireland shortly after coming into office to speak to all parties, including on this very important issue of th
deb_ex.sum: Confirms he found extra money for Northern Ireland despite fiscal pressures, but calls on all Stormont parties to take responsibility and set a budget rather than relying solely on Westminster.

deb_ex.t: My hon. and learned Friend is doing a sterling job in speaking up for his constituents. I agree that Lindsay and Craig’s sentence is appalling and unjustifiable. That is why the Fo
deb_ex.sum: Condemns Craig and Lindsay's sentence as appalling and unjustifiable, confirms the Foreign Secretary has raised the case directly with his Iranian counterpart, and pledges to pursue it relentlessly.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Lady makes a very strong point. Getting energy bills down, gas and electric, is at the very top of my list of priorities. It matters for households. She described the numb
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the scale of energy debt and says cutting gas and electricity bills is a top priority, confirming further measures beyond the VAT cut will be set out in due course.

deb_ex.t: I know how important this issue is. Child trust funds for disabled children are crucial, and they need to be unlocked quickly. I will ensure that Treasury Ministers are working wit
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the importance of unlocking child trust funds for disabled children and commits to ensuring Treasury Ministers work with colleagues to make rapid progress.

deb_ex.t: I would like to see a fully devolved south-west of England. I know Cornish Members were in No.10 North this week to discuss a devolution deal.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the idea of a Wessex mayor and commits to pursuing full devolution for the south-west of England, inviting Wessex Members to engage quickly.

deb_ex.t: I was sorry to hear about the potential job losses, and we will see what we can do to support my hon. Friend and his constituents.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to meet the Member to discuss the brewery closure and expresses regret at the potential job losses, pledging to see what support can be offered.

deb_ex.t: I will ask the Justice Secretary to look at those rules and come back to her.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees action is needed to support Probation Service staff and commits to asking the Justice Secretary to review the visa rules.

deb_ex.t: It is incumbent on all parties represented in this House to root out the politics of poison, which has seeped far too far into our politics.
deb_ex.sum: Condemns racist and discriminatory comments and calls on all parties to root out the politics of poison, noting that firm action is still awaited from the Opposition.

deb_ex.t: There is no diminution in our strong support to keep the Falkland Islands British.
deb_ex.sum: Firmly reaffirms the Government's commitment to the Falkland Islands and islanders' right to self-determination, citing diplomatic and defence-level engagement including with President Trump.

deb_ex.t: We should commit to ensuring that they are clearly and publicly available in all communities—something that I have long called for
deb_ex.sum: Strongly backs improved defibrillator access and CPR training, linking it to the 10-year health plan's shift from hospital to community care.
